A data-driven intelligent framework for silver carp (Hypophthalmichthys molitrix) surimi gel properties prediction and quality improvement.
abstract: This study developed a data-driven framework linking silver carp surimi gelling properties prediction with process optimization using raw-material characteristics and controllable processing parameters. A dataset of 1571 processing records spanning regions, seasons, fish-size grades, and key processing conditions was established. Target-specific stacked ensemble models predicted gel strength, breaking strain, and whiteness, with test set R2 values of 0.95, 0.82, and 0.93, respectively. SHAP analysis identified salt-soluble protein content and surimi moisture content as the most influential predictors of gel strength; region and season were most influential for breaking strain, whereas whiteness was more closely associated with season and the moisture-protein balance. The models were coupled with desirability-based optimization to generate raw-material-specific processing recommendations. Independent validation using six newly collected raw-material lots representing three regions and two seasons showed that the optimized schemes increased mean gel strength by approximately 25-107% relative to the conventional empirical process, with no significant differences detected in breaking strain; whiteness responses varied with raw-material and seasonal conditions. Overall, these results show that incorporating raw-material properties into interpretable multi-target prediction can support batch-specific process recommendations, and the desirable quality control.

How food structure and processing govern metabolizable energy: a critical review of the food-matrix determinants of energy availability and the limits of the Atwater accounting.
abstract: Food energy is usually reported using Atwater factors: composition-based coefficients that treat metabolizable energy as a function of macronutrient mass rather than food structure. Yet a growing food-science literature shows that metabolizable energy can diverge materially from Atwater predictions according to the integrity of the food matrix and the processing applied to it. This review brings energy-accounting and food-structure science into direct contact. It defines where the Atwater system remains useful and where its structural blind spot becomes consequential; clarifies the frequent conflation of digestibility, bioaccessibility, bioavailability and metabolizable energy, and distinguishes physical resistance from chemical inhibition of digestive enzymes while treating the two as coupled rather than independent. It then maps major processing operations to their structural and energetic consequences, and compares methods used to quantify metabolizable energy and nutrient release, including human balance studies, ileostomy and intubation studies, standardised in vitro digestion, dynamic models and in silico approaches. Tree nuts provide the strongest empirical case. Measured metabolizable energy ranges from about 5% below the Atwater value for pistachios to more than 30% below for whole almonds, a divergence that is explained by matrix integrity and lipid encapsulation. Four energetic consequences of matrix disruption are considered: net metabolizable energy, rate of energy release, thermic effect of feeding and colonic salvage. The review concludes that energy values based on composition alone are insufficient for foods whose structure strongly constrains digestion, and that food-composition data, labelling, feeding research and reformulation would benefit from structure-aware measures of delivered energy.

title: Starch-derived oligosaccharides as prebiotics in innovative functional foods.
abstract: Driven by the escalating demand for innovative functional foods, starch-derived oligosaccharides (SDOs), particularly low-degree-of-polymerization fractions, have emerged as prominent functional carbohydrates, with selected SDO fractions exhibiting prebiotic properties. Their digestive behavior and gut microbial utilization depend strongly on degree of polymerization, glycosidic linkage, and molecular structure. Findings from in vitro and cell-based studies, animal models, and selected human intervention trials further indicate structure-dependent microbial and physiological responses. Herein, the structural characteristics, underlying prebiotic mechanisms, and traditional biocatalytic synthesis strategies of diverse SDOs are systematically summarized and discussed. Currently, enzymatic transglycosylation dominates the industrial production of SDOs; however, this process is fundamentally bottlenecked by the inherent hydrolytic propensity and poor regioselectivity of wild-type glycosidases or transglycosidases, leading to heterogeneous product profiles and limited thermodynamic yields. To overcome these natural biocatalytic constraints, customizing robust enzymes via artificial intelligence (AI) and computational structural redesign has become an important research direction. By integrating deep learning algorithms with structure-based de novo design and multidimensional kinetic prediction, the architecture of native catalytic clefts can be rationally remodeled. Such computational strategies facilitate favorable orientation of carbohydrate acceptor substrates and enhance transglycosylation selectivity toward targeted SDOs promoting innovative functional food applications.

title: IoT and UAV Integration for Wheat Disease Monitoring: A Review of Multimodal Sensing and Analytical Frameworks With Perspectives on Cereal Crop Stress
abstract: Cereal productivity is increasingly threatened by both biotic stresses, such as fungal diseases including yellow rust and Fusarium head blight (FHB), and abiotic stress factors which cause substantial yield and quality losses worldwide. Conventional monitoring remains time-consuming, labor-intensive, and spatially constrained, motivating automated, and scalable disease surveillance. Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms provide high-resolution, field-scale canopy observations for detection and severity mapping, while Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks deliver continuous microclimate measurements that are critical for forecasting disease risk. Importantly, integrating these modalities supports not only detection but also interpretation of plant–pathogen–environment interactions by linking microclimatic drivers to physiological stress responses in wheat. In contrast to prior reviews that focus on individual sensing modalities, this study synthesizes UAV imaging, IoT-based environmental monitoring, and physiologically grounded interpretation into a unified perspective. We compare sensing technologies, datasets, and analytical pipelines, and identify key gaps in interoperability, data fusion, and communication efficiency. To address these limitations, we propose a three-tier IoT–UAV conceptual framework that couples short-range IoT sensor clustering with long-range, delay-tolerant UAV data collection and edge/cloud analytics. This architecture enables scalable, energy-aware monitoring and serves as a reference model for biologically informed, data-driven early warning systems that connect environmental risk signals with observable disease expression. In addition, the reviewed approaches provide perspectives for extending wheat-focused disease monitoring frameworks to broader cereal crop stress analysis, including the integration of abiotic stress factors and their impact on crop resilience.

title: Trustworthy Collaborative Agents for Industrial IoT: A Multimodal Mixed Reality Framework for Human-Centric Precision Assembly
abstract: In the evolving industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), the complexity of assembly tasks requires intelligent agents capable of augmenting human capabilities through real-time perception and decision-making. However, deploying such agents on edge devices faces challenges in spatial alignment accuracy and computational efficiency, which compromise their trustworthiness in high-risk environments. To address these issues, this article proposes a human-centric collaborative agent (HC-CoAgent), a lightweight mixed reality (MR) framework tailored for precision circuit assembly. Unlike traditional static systems, HC-CoAgent functions as a “cognitive peer”—an AI partner that dynamically shares the operator’s cognitive load by fusing visual object recognition, gesture tracking, and gaze input. Crucially, to bridge the “reality gap,” we introduce a novel human-in-the-loop (HITL) spatial alignment mechanism utilizing a threshold-controlled 3-D pointing strategy. The theoretical rigor of this mechanism is validated via a support vector machine (SVM) analysis, which defines the precise trustworthiness boundaries for safe interaction. Furthermore, visual attention analysis reveals that the agent functions as a cognitive anchor, significantly reducing visual entropy and aligning novice gaze patterns with expert baselines. Experimental results from industrial wiring scenarios demonstrate that HC-CoAgent improves task efficiency by 33% and reduces error rates significantly compared to both traditional paper-based methods and uncalibrated MR baselines. The system also exhibits low cognitive load and high usability, validating its potential as an effective and efficient edge AI agent for empowering the IIoT workforce.

title: A Content-Adaptive JPEG-Based Encryption Framework for Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Remote sensing images (RSIs) are characterized by high data redundancy and strong sensitivity, posing significant challenges for secure transmission in bandwidth- and storage-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) environments. Existing RSI encryption schemes primarily emphasize security, while often overlooking compression efficiency, leading to substantial bit expansion and limited practicality in real-world IoT applications. To balance image privacy against storage capacity, we propose a JPEG-compatible RSI encryption algorithm based on content-adaptive criteria, which integrates reversible data hiding (RDH) to guarantee data integrity during transmission. Based on the structural characteristics of RSI, a block-separation strategy of varying block sizes employing content-adaptive criteria is introduced to replace the equal-size block separation in the block decomposition stage of JPEG compression. Following the quantization stage, the DC differences of variably sized blocks are encrypted according to their statistical characteristics, thereby significantly reducing bitstream expansion (BE) while enhancing computational efficiency. Moreover, to degrade the encryption overhead and reinforce the security of RSIs, we introduce both local and global confusion algorithms. The local algorithm employs circular distortion to encrypt blocks, while the global algorithm utilizes cross-disturbance to secure run/size (RS) pairs. Furthermore, an improved RDH algorithm based on histogram shifting (HS) tailored for RSI encryption is given to balance embedding capacity with bit increment. Extensive experimental evaluations and detailed security analyses reveal that the proposed algorithm decreases the bit expansion rate by 22.84%–56.83% compared with state-of-the-art schemes while maintaining strong resistance to statistical and structural attacks.

title: Reliable Hyperspectral Image Classification via Deviation-Guided Domain Adaptation
abstract: With the increasing deployment of hyperspectral sensors on IoT-enabled remote sensing platforms, massive hyperspectral image (HSI) data are continuously acquired from multiple sensors under varying imaging conditions and across different geographic regions. However, continuously acquired data may exhibit distribution shifts and contain unknown categories, which can result in ineffective knowledge transfer or even negative transfer. To this end, we propose a deviation-guided domain adaptation framework (DGDA) for reliable open-set HSI classification. Specifically, a Mamba-enhanced spectral–spatial encoder first learns transferable representations by jointly modeling local spatial patterns and long-range spectral dependencies, providing a reliable feature space for target-structure discovery. On this basis, dynamic virtual-unknown prototypes (DVUPs) are constructed from unmatched target clusters to explicitly characterize target-private structures. Finally, a deviation-guided selective alignment and unknown routing (DG-SAUR) mechanism uses source-known and virtual-unknown structures to align reliable known-like samples and route high-deviation samples toward the unknown space, thereby achieving shared-class transfer and unknown-sample rejection. Experiments on four cross-scene and cross-sensor adaptation tasks show that DGDA achieves the best HOS on all tasks and outperforms the strongest competing methods by an average of 11.6 percentage points. These results demonstrate its potential to reliably interpret unlabeled imagery from multiple IoT remote sensing platforms while preventing source-unseen observations from contaminating downstream monitoring and decision-making.

title: Hybrid Stackelberg Game and Diffusion-Based Auction for Two-Tier Agentic AI Task Offloading in Internet of Agents
abstract: The Internet of Agents (IoA) not only provides a foundational architecture for collaborative reasoning among artificial intelligence (AI) agents but also brings new challenges to task offloading. Unlike traditional task offloading, agentic AI tasks involve sustained multistep reasoning, planning, and context maintenance, thereby imposing coupled pressure on memory occupancy, inference latency, and energy consumption. To address these issues, we propose a two-tier agentic AI task offloading framework within the IoA scenarios. In the first tier, resource-requester agents (RRAs), e.g., autonomous vehicles (AVs), offload inference-intensive tasks to nearby resource providers. Such resource providers can be mobile resource agents (MRAs), e.g., neighboring vehicles, and infrastructure resource agents (IRAs), e.g., roadside units (RSUs). In the second tier, overloaded IRAs further procure supplementary inference resources from aerial resource agents (ARAs), e.g., uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs), to handle overflow workloads caused by limited residual video RAM (VRAM) and key-value (KV)-cache accumulation. We formulate the first-tier pricing and offloading interaction as a Stackelberg game, where MRAs/IRAs act as leaders and RRAs act as followers. Moreover, we model the second-tier IRA-ARA resource trading as a double Dutch auction (DDA). To solve the proposed hierarchical model, we develop an iterative best-response algorithm for the first-tier Stackelberg game and a diffusion-based deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm for the second-tier DDA process. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed framework can improve agentic task-offloading efficiency, auction reward, and social welfare while reducing information-exchange cost.

title: Toward IoT-Enabled UAV Swarms for Air-Quality Monitoring: A Comprehensive Survey on Technologies, Methods, and Optimization Strategies
abstract: Air-quality monitoring has become a significant global concern because poor air quality adversely affects human health and the environment. Recent advances in uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs), when integrated into Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures, offer a flexible and scalable solution for acquiring high-resolution air-quality data, especially in under-monitored or hard-to-access regions. UAVs can complement land-based monitoring by collecting measurements in remote, dangerous, or difficult-to-access locations. Because air-quality monitoring is conducted in uncertain and complex physical environments, UAV systems increasingly require swarm-based, autonomous, and intelligent capabilities. However, several technical challenges must be addressed for large-scale UAV-enabled air-quality monitoring, including reliable wireless communication, scalable multi-UAV networking, distributed control, and safe system operation. This survey discusses the enabling technologies of UAV-based IoT systems, including communication, networking, computation, trajectory planning, cooperation, and coordination, together with relevant optimization strategies. It then analyzes key operational and management considerations, including movement, connectivity, energy, safety, security, and privacy protection. Finally, it summarizes existing air-quality datasets, their roles in UAV-based sensing, and the challenges of UAV-based data collection. The survey concludes by identifying open challenges and discussing future research directions for advancing air-quality monitoring.

title: Internet of Agents (IoA): Sensing, Communication, Decision-Making, and Execution
abstract: Advances in sensing, communication, and reasoning are driving deeper integration of AI into IoT systems. However, progress remains siloed across two communities: agent research centers on task decomposition, semantic planning, and coordination, whereas IoT research prioritizes sensing, communication, and edge computing. Bridging these perspectives and integrating semantic reasoning with system foundations remains a key challenge. Therefore, we present the Internet of Agents (IoAs), a framework that reorganizes existing AI agent research from a systems perspective, following the classical IoT paradigm of sensing, communication, decision-making, and execution. IoA reconceptualizes system nodes as agents rather than traditional IoT endpoints. For sensing, IoA broadens awareness to include reasoning depth, knowledge gaps, and external tool capabilities. In communication, IoA adopts a three-layer architecture (environment, interaction, and semantic), designed to align with the five-layer Internet protocol stack. In decision-making and execution, IoA frames the shift from rule-based control to semantic planning and from reactive execution to proactive execution. We further identify open challenges and future research directions across the four modules of IoA.

title: Uncovering Delay Paths and Hidden Latency in Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: End-to-end latency is a key requirement for intelligent transportation systems (ITSs), particularly for safety-critical applications such as vulnerable road user (VRU) protection, cooperative perception, and remote driving. Existing studies typically evaluate latency from a communication perspective, implicitly assuming that network transmission dominates the end-to-end delay. However, measurements collected from operational ITS deployments reveal a different picture. In this letter, we introduce a structured framework for experimentally decomposing end-to-end latency into its main functional contributions across sensing, processing, communication, and visualization stages. The framework is validated through measurement campaigns conducted in the Modena Automotive Smart Area (MASA), a real-world ITS living lab supporting heterogeneous vehicular services. Experimental results consistently show that sensing and processing frequently dominate the overall latency budget, while communication contributes only a small fraction of the end-to-end delay. These findings highlight the importance of adopting holistic latency evaluation methodologies when designing latency-sensitive ITS applications.

title: A Data-Driven Probabilistic Harmonic Current Forecasting for Aggregated Harmonic Sources
abstract: With the increasing deployment of non-linear power electronic devices in distribution networks, the issue of excessive harmonics has become increasingly prominent. Accurate analysis and forecasting of harmonic currents are essential to better understand and mitigate harmonic-related problems. Common harmonic sources in power grids include various types of loads and renewable energy generation equipment, such as wind and photovoltaic systems. Accordingly, this paper focuses on forecasting harmonic currents for different types of aggregated harmonic sources. Considering the strong randomness, high time-variability, and coupling characteristics of harmonic currents, a data-driven probabilistic harmonic current forecasting method is proposed. First, the raw data are decomposed into deterministic and stochastic components. Next, a radial basis function autoregressive exponential model is employed to perform point forecasting of the deterministic component, accommodating multiple input factors and simultaneous multi-harmonic outputs while preserving model partial interpretability. Subsequently, the proposed multi-Gaussian fitting method and an improved Markov chain Monte Carlo approach are used for probabilistic forecasting of the stochastic component. Finally, the deterministic and stochastic component predictions are combined to yield the final probabilistic harmonic current forecast. Using actual harmonic measurement data, comparative analyses with multiple intelligent models are conducted to validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed forecasting method. Furthermore, the harmonic current predictions are applied to forward probabilistic harmonic power flows, and corresponding forward and new probabilistic harmonic mitigation measures are proposed, demonstrating practical engineering applicability.

title: Learning-Free Laplacian Kernel Modeling for Joint Imputation of Multi-Energy Load Data in Integrated Energy Systems
abstract: The reliability of data-driven applications in integrated energy systems (IESs), such as multi-energy load prediction, relies on the availability of complete and high-quality load data. However, real-world multi-energy load data can suffer from missing records, and accurate recovery remains challenging due to heterogeneous missing patterns and strong yet nontrivial coupling among different energy loads. To address this issue, this paper proposes an efficient learning-free Laplacian kernel framework for joint multi-energy load imputation, in which missing entries are directly treated as decision variables and the complete load matrix is reconstructed through a unified convex optimization formulation without requiring any training data. The proposed framework captures both the intra-load structure and cross-load coupling of multi-energy load data. This is achieved by combining a circulant Laplacian kernel-based temporal regularizer and a circulant tensor nuclear norm for local continuity and global periodicity, respectively, together with a correlation-based signed Laplacian regularizer for inter-load coupling relationship modeling. To efficiently solve the resulting optimization problem, an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is derived, where the dominant updates are implemented in the frequency domain via the fast Fourier transform (FFT) by exploiting the underlying circulant structures. This enables fast and scalable imputation of long-horizon and high-resolution load data with low computational overhead. Numerical experiments on real-world multi-energy load datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework not only consistently outperforms state-of-the-art imputation baselines under different missing patterns but also yields superior performance in downstream load forecasting tasks. The source code is available at: https://github.com/zhaopengfei12345/data-imputation

From AI boyfriends to AI shopping agents? The emerging convergence of relational AI and AI-assisted commerce
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is becoming both relational and agentic. AI boyfriends are treated as a visible romantic exemplar within the broader theoretical and empirical domain of relational AI. This paper examines whether relational AI, including AI boyfriends, is emerging alongside AI-assisted commerce, and whether functional integration keeps pace with attention and market growth. Study 1 analyzes Google Trends data (2020–2026, six markets): relational-AI attention rises significantly in five countries, AI-commerce attention rises in all six, with substantial but non-invariant temporal co-movement in attention. Study 2 examines 44 AI-companion apps on Google Play: the category shows substantial downloads and spending, romantic positioning (e.g., AI boyfriends) shows no observable adoption penalty, in-app purchasing is universal, yet no app positions shopping as a core feature. Study 3 analyzes 181,226 Reddit posts from relational-AI communities: design-weighted coding estimates 9.1% of corpus posts contain commercial discourse, but only 0.3% involve the companion itself in consumer or purchasing decisions. We conceptualize this as an attention-market-integration gap, where attention and market realization outpace functional commerce integration. The study equips managers and researchers with guidance for engaging with the emerging AI boyfriend trend.

title: AP2/ERF transcription factors in plant stress adaptation: evolutionary expansion, functional diversification and hormone crosstalk.
abstract: APETALA2/ethylene response factor (AP2/ERF) transcription factors constitute a plant-specific regulatory family that coordinates plant development, environmental stress responses, and hormone signaling. However, the contribution of AP2/ERF family expansion and functional diversification to environmental adaptation has not been fully integrated across evolutionary and mechanistic scales. This review synthesizes classical findings and representative advances from the past five years in structural classification, duplication-driven expansion, functional diversification, stress adaptation, and hormone crosstalk, with particular emphasis on how post-duplication divergence shapes regulatory function. Across these studies, AP2/ERF proteins emerge as context-dependent nodes that connect environmental or hormonal signals with direct target genes and downstream physiological responses. This perspective distinguishes family expansion from demonstrated adaptive function and helps explain why closely related AP2/ERFs can produce contrasting outcomes in different biological contexts. We further discuss priorities for functional validation in non-model species, multi-stress experiments, multi-omics integration, field phenotyping, and gene-editing-based breeding, highlighting AP2/ERF regulators with potential for engineering stress-resilient crops.

title: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO 2
abstract: Predicting boreal forest growth is hindered by limited experimental tests on the compounding effects of climate change and atmospheric CO 2 . We integrated regional tree‐ring data with a peatland warming and CO 2 manipulation experiment, including 45 trait measurements, to assess growth responses of two widespread boreal conifers, Larix laricina and Picea mariana , to temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), soil moisture, and elevated CO 2 . L. laricina growth was consistently more climate‐sensitive than P. mariana , increasing strongly with soil moisture and declining slightly with VPD at the regional scale, but responding positively to VPD and temperature—not soil moisture or CO 2 —at the experimental peatland. L. laricina 's acquisitive strategy enhanced water and nutrient uptake, sustaining growth but reducing hydraulic safety. By contrast, P. mariana 's conservative strategy maintained water‐use efficiency and hydraulic resilience without compromising growth. Our results challenge projections of widespread CO 2 fertilization in boreal forests and highlight conservative conifers as potential winners under warming and drying, sustaining growth while maintaining low mortality risk. This dynamic could reshape projections of the boreal carbon sink and its role in global climate feedback.

title: Biodegradable and Non‐Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil–Plant Systems
abstract: The accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in soils worldwide has raised concerns about their potential impacts on microbially mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling. However, whether biodegradable and non‐biodegradable MPs differently affect microbial C and N metabolism and coupling, and whether these responses are modulated by co‐occurring plant identity remain uncertain. We combined a meta‐analysis with a controlled pot experiment comparing soil responses under two congeneric plant species exposed to two biodegradable and two non‐biodegradable MPs at doses ranging from 0% to 2% (w/w). In the meta‐analysis, MPs generally increased CO 2 emission and microbial biomass N (MBN), but had no significant overall effect on microbial biomass C (MBC). In the pot experiment, MPs likewise increased CO 2 emission, whereas overall effect sizes of MBC and MBN were nonsignificant. Nevertheless, these overall responses did not capture the distinct patterns of microbial C–N metabolic coordination between MP types. Under biodegradable MPs, tighter MBC–MBN coupling with a dose‐dependent shift toward greater respiratory C loss relative to MBC collectively indicated a maintenance‐associated metabolic pattern. In contrast, MBC–MBN decoupling and stronger MBC–CO 2 coupling under non‐biodegradable MPs indicated a biomass‐linked metabolic pattern. In addition, plant identity modulated these microbial metabolisms in an MP‐type manner, particularly in N‐related processes. These metabolic responses were accompanied with changes in soil property conditions and substrate availability, weakened DOC–DON coupling, and shifts in microbial community structure and life history strategy. RDA‐based hierarchical and variation partitioning and SEM further indicated that modeled soil property pathways were more prominent under non‐biodegradable MPs, while substrate‐related pathways were prominent under biodegradable MPs. Together, the meta‐analysis reveals the general microbial metabolic patterns under MP type, and the pot experiment further reveals how MP type and plant identity jointly influence microbial C–N metabolism through contrasting associations with soil substrates and property conditions.

title: "Dump my brain so it remembers for me": An AI-Augmented External Autobiographical Memory for Aphantasia and SDAM
abstract: I have aphantasia (no voluntary mental imagery) and severely deficient autobiographical memory (SDAM): I cannot relive my past or picture it. The deficit falls less on daily survival than on knowledge work — holding a project’s history, knowing what a colleague last said and cares about, assembling the context to send a message. Conventional memory aids fail this profile: built around images I cannot form (and, rarely photographed, do not capture), assuming a user who returns to review their own store. I report a one-month autoethnographic deployment of a memory prosthesis I do not operate: an AI agent over a continuously and automatically ingested personal knowledge base. I supply intent; the agent owns the rest of the memory loop — it gathers across my tools, connects scattered sources into the context an action needs, organizes and indexes the store, and surfaces proactively because I will not pull. I introduce AI-augmented external autobiographical memory as a cognitive prosthetic for this overlooked, non-clinical profile, derive design principles from daily use, and argue that the function the prosthesis must own is connection — reconnecting dispersed context across sources and time — which for this profile is not merely effortful but structurally unsupported. This works for someone with an unusually high digital footprint; capturing a low-footprint life remains open.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility

title: Auxel: A Multi-Agent Conversational Data-Analysis Assistant for Blind and Low-Vision Users
abstract: Blind and low-vision (BLV) users increasingly have access to AI-powered data analysis tools such as Excel Copilot, ChatGPT Advanced Data Analysis, Claude for Excel, and Gemini in Sheets. While these systems can successfully analyze tabular data, they largely assume a sighted interaction model in which users inspect visual tables, charts, and formatted outputs. As a result, the final presentation of results—and the interaction required to explore them—remains a significant accessibility barrier. To address this, we developed Auxel, a web-based conversational data assistant that enables BLV users to interact with spreadsheet data via natural-language speech or text, while a multi-agent pipeline performs ambiguity resolution, intent classification, code generation, and response synthesis. Rather than simply returning visual outputs, Auxel generates multimodal, screen-reader-optimized responses, including concise spoken summaries, accessible tables, and interactive grid views designed for efficient exploration with assistive technologies. This demo presents Auxel running live in a web browser with both JAWS and VoiceOver. We also discuss implementation insights gained while engineering a highly interactive web interface for screen-reader users, including undocumented differences in JAWS and VoiceOver behavior, practical limitations of current WAI-ARIA guidance for complex data interfaces, and the design trade-offs required to support consistent accessible interactions across assistive technologies.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility

title: Voice Over Persona: Dialogue Modality Drives Player Engagement and Immersion in LLM-Driven AI Agents in Games
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled Non-Player Characters (NPCs) in video games to generate context-aware, real-time dialogue, opening new possibilities for designing richer and more immersive player experiences [14]. However, the effects of specific NPC design variables on player experience remain empirically underexplored. This paper presents a work-in-progress study examining how NPC persona (Empathic/Supportive vs. Low-Empathy/Task-focused) and dialogue modality (Text vs. Voice) influence player emotional response, engagement, and immersion in an AI-driven game environment. A Unity-based first-person detective game prototype was developed, in which an AI-driven NPC mentor guides players through a fictional investigation. Using a 2 × 2 within-subjects factorial design, 23 adult university students each completed four gameplay scenarios representing all combinations of persona and modality. Player experience was measured after each scenario using the Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM), the User Engagement Scale Short Form (UES-SF), and two subscales of the Immersive Experience Questionnaire (IEQ). Results indicated that dialogue modality had a consistent and significant effect on player experience, with voice-based interaction producing significantly higher scores on IEQ Emotional Involvement and UES Focused Attention compared to text-based interaction, and marginal trends in the same direction across all remaining measures. NPC persona did not produce significant differences in any measure; a result interpreted as reflecting the brief scenario duration and inherent variability of real-time LLM-generated dialogue rather than the absence of any persona effect. No significant interaction between persona and modality was found. These findings suggest that the modality through which players communicate with an AI-driven NPC is a more immediate impactful design decision, offering practical guidance for developers designing LLM-driven NPC systems in narrative games. Future work will include studies to investigate how specific NPC communication styles impact player experience in prolonged multiple round game levels.
journal: Companion Proceedings of the Annual Symposium on Computer-Human Interaction in Play

title: Serving the Player or Shaping Them? Game-Embedded AI Companions and the Rewiring of Well-being
abstract: AI companions are increasingly embedded in games. Prior work highlights the benefits of companions in games for improved mental-health; however, these systems raise concerns around dependency, safety, and ethical responsibility. In this provocation, we argue game-embedded AI companions must be critically reframed as neuropsychologically adaptive agents capable of shaping players’ cognitive and emotional processes over time, often in ways that may be opaque to players or difficult to meaningfully consent to. Drawing on psychology, cognitive neuroscience, ethics, HCI, and game design, we call for a shift from short-term outcomes toward understanding how AI companions may actively rewire well-being through play.
journal: Companion Proceedings of the Annual Symposium on Computer-Human Interaction in Play

title: Knowing When to Trust Cheap Retrieval: A Calibration and Cost-Aware Decision Layer for Open-Vocabulary Temporal Change Retrieval
abstract: Multimodal information retrieval in remote sensing increasingly poses free-text questions about time: given co-registered image pairs (T1, T2) of one location at two acquisition times, the task is to retrieve the pairs in which a described change — for example, “low vegetation became bare ground” — has occurred. The efficient way to serve this is to keep a large vision–language model frozen, embed each pair once, cache the result, and answer queries by vector arithmetic. We study what such a cheap, training-free pipeline can and cannot deliver, and contribute the decision machinery that makes it deployable. Under a pre-registered protocol on a public bi-temporal benchmark, with queries posed as templated transitions over six land-cover classes, a frozen encoder carries genuine ranking signal: 18 of 22 supported change transitions are forward-reliable at a false-discovery rate of q ≤ 0.05. As a per-item decision, however, it only ties a base-rate predictor on a coverage-fair selective-risk metric. Across three frozen encoders it never beats that predictor: it ties on two and is significantly worse on the third — the one whose ranking map is the strongest — so ranking quality does not purchase per-item decision quality. Re-pricing the same decisions under asymmetric misclassification costs recovers an operating envelope in which acting on the cheap signal is cheaper than following prevalence, and this advantage appears only where the ranking signal is genuine. The contribution is a near-zero-compute calibration-and-cost decision layer, evaluated jointly for effectiveness and serving cost, that tells an operator when a frozen, cache-once retriever is worth trusting, rather than a new backbone or a leaderboard number.

title: SUSTAINABLE E-LEADERSHIP AND ORGANIZATIONAL TRANSFORMATION: THE ROLES OF FLEXIBILITY, DIGITALIZATION, AND CULTURE IN ENHANCING OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY
abstract: The given paper analyzes the contribution of sustainable e-leadership (SEL) to the efficiency of operations with the help of the mediating variables, such as organizational flexibility (OF) and digitalization (DIG), and the moderating role of digital organizational culture (DOC). Based on the Resource-Based View (RBV), the conceptual framework of the study is sustainable eleadership that is a crucial intangible asset that helps organizations transform flexible structures and digitalized operational processes to effective and reliable performance results in dynamic and highly regulated environments. Data were collected from 300 senior and middle managers across 15 Jordanian commercial banks—a highly regulated sector undergoing intensive digital pressure in an emerging-economy context—using an online survey. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) provided by SmartPLS 4.0 was imposed on the proposed research model. The results indicate that sustainable e-leadership affects both flexibility and digitalization of organizations significantly in a positive manner that leads to improvement in operational efficiency. Besides, organizational flexibility and digitalization can work as independent and sequential mediators exposing a multistage process of capability development in which leadership initiatives are transformed into effective everyday operations. The findings show as well that digital organizational culture reinforces the effect of sustainable e-leadership on flexibility and digitalization, which determines the degree to which digital initiatives are institutionalized into consistent operating patterns, instead of being a solitary technological endeavor. Focusing on the organizational change as the process of increasing efficiency in operations under the leadership, flexibility, digitalization and cultural fit, this research adds the RBV knowledge to the operational segment of digital leadership. The paper makes theoretical contributions by explaining how e-leadership-facilitating capabilities contribute to efficiency-oriented change and offers practical implications to the banking managers looking to increase flexibility, instill digitalization in their operations, and promote a culture that encourages sustainable operational excellence.

title: From naïve to vigilant: how inflammatory and metabolic cues shape human T cells
abstract: CD4⁺ T cells are essential regulators of adaptive immunity and can differentiate into distinct helper T cell subsets depending on signals from their environment. Among these subsets, T helper 17 (Th17) cells play a crucial role in protecting against bacterial and fungal infections but are also implicated in chronic inflammatory and autoimmune diseases. This thesis investigates how environmental and metabolic factors influence human Th17 cell differentiation and function. Using a defined human in vitro model, we demonstrate that Th17 development is shaped by a combination of signals, including TGF-β, extracellular lactate, and hypoxia. These factors modify cellular transcriptional programs and converge on key regulatory pathways, particularly STAT3. We further show that mitochondrial activity is closely linked to Th17 differentiation. Cells with high mitochondrial membrane potential are more likely to develop into Th17 cells, but also display characteristics associated with functional exhaustion. The clinical relevance of these findings was explored in osteoarthritis, where synovial T cells were found to remain activated and responsive despite longstanding disease. Together, the results show that T cell differentiation is highly dynamic and determined by interactions between environmental cues, metabolism, and tissue context. Understanding these interactions may provide new therapeutic opportunities for chronic inflammatory diseases.

title: Gis and Artificial Intelligence-based Forecasting of Regional Sustainable Development
abstract: Ensuring the sustainable development of the regional economy has become the most important issue on a global scale. In 2024-2026, growth rates in the countries that account for more than 80% of the world's population and global GDP remain below those of the decade preceding the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2025, the German geospatial analytics (Geospatial Analytics) market is valued at USD 1.45 billion, and it is expected to reach USD 2.55 billion by 2030. Therefore, using GIS technologies as a lever for forecasting regions, and studying their structural components and their impact on the formation of regional economic policy, is a pressing scientific problem.

title: Estimating healthcare cost savings from greenspace in Washington
Death of the Author, Birth of the Algorithm? Reimagining Literary Meaning- Making in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced new possibilities for literary interpretation, challenging traditional assumptions about authorship, readership and textual meaning. While Roland Barthes’ concept of the “Death of the Author” displaced authorial intention as the primary source of meaning, contemporary AI technologies raise questions about whether algorithms are becoming active participants in interpretive processes. This study explores how generative AI reshapes literary meaning- making and examines the implications of AI- generated interpretations for literary studies in the digital age. This qualitative exploratory study was conducted among 20 undergraduate students enrolled in a BA English programme at a private university in Sri Lanka. Drawing on Barthes’ notion of the Death of the Author, Michael Foucault’s concept of the author function, and reader- response theories advanced by Wolfgang Iser and Stanley Fish, the study critically examines the role of generative AI in the production and mediation of literary interpretations. Relevant scholarly literature on AI- assisted reading and digital textuality is analysed to develop a theoretical framework for understanding algorithmic participation in literary meaning- making. The analysis suggest that generative AI complicates traditional distinctions between author, reader, and text. Rather than functioning as an author in the conventional sense, AI appears to operate as an interpretive agent capable of generating multiple readings based on patterns derived from vast textual corpora. This development extends reader- centred approaches to literary interpretation while simultaneously raising concerns regarding originality, authority, and the pedagogical use of AI-generated analyses. The study argues that AI- generated interpretations should be viewed not as replacements for human reading but as additional voices within broader interpretive communities. The paper proposes that literary studies must reconsider established theories of authorship and interpretation in response to emerging AI technologies. By positioning AI as a participant in, rather than a determinant of, meaning- making, the study contributes to ongoing discussions in literary theory, semiotics, and digital humanities. The findings offer insights for educators, researchers, and students navigating literary interpretation in increasingly AI- mediated learning environments.

title: Transformation of the Kohombayo Folk Belief: A Study on Daduru Oya Valley in Sri Lanka
abstract: The belief in Kohombayo is an ancient folklore tradition associated with paddy cultivation. The Kohombayo were believed to be invisible beings who steal a portion of harvest, a series of ritualistic practices were performed at threshing floor to prevent loss. This research aims to identify history of Kohombayo belief, rituals associated with them, and how modern farming methods have influenced this. Drawing on Walter Benjamin’s theory of mechanical and digital reproduction, this study explores, how agriculture modernization and digitalization have transformed to influence of this belief. The research was conducted through qualitative research methodology with Bandarigalgoda village in Daduru oya valley serving as study area. Data were collected from 55 residents through non participant observation. Library study incorporated with books and research articles, field study incorporated with interviews and questionnaires. Thematic analysis was adopted to interpret. Findings reveal that, while the Kohombayo belief and rituals like spilling milk, hiding salt in threshing floor, drawing symbol called Alu yantharaya on threshing floor to prevent harvest from Kohombayo , is largely declined due to introduction of machine harvesting, it has not completely vanished. Only four adult participants were familiar with term Kohombayo and limited knowledge was preserved, mainly among the oldest generation. They still maintain Kohombayo faith in belief, communicate through dreams, practicing divine remembrance while offering alms and planting Kohombo trees, as symbolic acts of protection for their harvest. The study concludes that the last bearers of Kohombayo knowledge are fading with rise of the digital era, as younger generation increasingly rely on technological and digital knowledge rather than traditional beliefs. Preserving vanishing folk heritage must be prioritized before it is lost to modern agriculture and digital influences.

title: Africa-Papers: A 10-Billion-Token Multi-Domain Academic Corpus for African Foundation Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) depend fundamentally on the diversity, depth, and factual rigor of their pre-training corpora. However, contemporary foundational pre-training datasets (such as The Pile, S2ORC, and Dolma) exhibit a severe structural omission: African scientific, medical, legal, and agricultural scholarship constitutes less than 0.5% of global pre-training tokens. Consequently, state-of-the-art models suffer from systematic failure modes when reasoning about tropical epidemiology, localized smallholder agro-ecologies, regional economic governance, and indigenous linguistic structures. To resolve this representation deficit and advance African intellectual sovereignty in artificial intelligence, we introduce Africa-Papers, the largest curated multi-domain Pan-African academic pre-training corpus to date. Comprising over 844,807 full-text papers spanning 10.15 billion tokens across 879 Parquet shards, Africa-Papers unifies four primary scientific streams: (1) continental peer-reviewed journals indexed in DOAJ across 31 African nations, (2) the CGIAR CGSpace agricultural repository, (3) African-authored and African-focused STEM/AI preprints on arXiv, and (4) open-access international publications by scholars affiliated with African institutions indexed via OpenAlex. The entire corpus is processed into layout-aware, clean Markdown preserving section hierarchies, mathematical equations, and tabular data, accompanied by exact BPE token counts and a standardized 8-domain taxonomy. We release Africa-Papers openly on the Hugging Face Hub under the AfriSpeech organization to accelerate continual pre-training and domain evaluation for foundation models globally.

title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation. METHODS The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report. RESULTS On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions. CONCLUSIONS This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

title: Morphology guided hybrid deep learning for species identification of root knot nematodes
abstract: Root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.) are a major global constraint on crop productivity. The second-stage juvenile (J2) is the infective stage of nematode that actively seeks out and infects plant roots; thus, accurate identification at this stage is important for effective nematode management and control. However, current identification practices remain challenging and is time-consuming, due to their reliance on expert-dependent microscopic examinations. This challenge creates significant barriers to scalability and rapid decision-making. To address this, we propose a morphology guided hybrid deep learning framework for identifying Meloidogyne graminicola and M. incognita at the J2 stage. The proposed framework integrates biologically relevant shape descriptors with deep visual representations to improve species discrimination. Standardized morphological features are fused with convolutional embeddings via a modified MobileNetV2 classifier head, to enable joint and discriminative representation learning. The proposed approach was evaluated against morphology-based machine learning models and end-to-end deep learning baselines. The results demonstrate that the proposed morphology guided deep learning improves classification performance and interpretability. It provides a lightweight and biologically informed solution for automated identification of J2 root-knot nematode species.

title: Artificial intelligence methods for morphological analysis and diagnosis of bacterial and fungal leaf diseases
abstract: Bacterial and fungal leaf diseases frequently produce overlapping visual symptoms, complicating automated diagnosis and limiting the transferability of models across crops and field conditions. This review systematically evaluates artificial intelligence methods for the morphology-based detection and differentiation of these diseases. Following a PRISMA-based selection process, 95 records published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, of which 59 eligible studies were included. The survey covers the morphological characteristics that distinguish bacterial and fungal diseases, traditional image processing and machine learning approaches, deep learning and generative AI techniques, and publicly available datasets. It also critically compares the performance, advantages, and limitations of existing diagnostic approaches. The findings indicate that deep learning dominates the literature, particularly in fungal disease detection, whereas research on bacterial diseases and generative AI applications remains comparatively limited. Although convolutional and transfer-learning models generally demonstrated strong classification performance, comparisons across studies were constrained by differences in datasets, evaluation protocols, and performance metrics. The principal barriers to practical adoption include morphological overlap between infections, class imbalance, and scarcity of expert-annotated images of bacterial and early-stage diseases, reliance on controlled-background datasets, limited external validation, model complexity, and insufficient interpretability. Future research should prioritize pathogen-balanced multicrop field datasets, standardized reporting and cross-dataset evaluation, multimodal fusion of RGB images with spectral and environmental data, domain adaptation, validated generative augmentation, explainable models, and lightweight edge deployment. By connecting lesion morphology with methodological and dataset evidence, this review provides a structured roadmap for developing robust, interpretable, and field-ready plant disease diagnosis systems.

title: A closed loop multimodal auditing framework for enhancing artificial intelligence reliability in medical emergency response
abstract: Ensuring the reliability of AI-powered information retrieval systems is critical in high-stakes domains such as first aid. Traditional audit methodologies are often static, manual, and unimodal, failing to address the dynamic, time-sensitive, and multimodal requirements of these applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce RADAR-FirstAid (Reliability-Aware Dynamic Auditing Framework), a closed-loop auditing pipeline — not a competing information system — for real-time, multimodal, and edge-aware auditing. Its key components include a Dynamic Query Simulator for generating criticality-weighted scenarios, a Multimodal Audit & Fusion Agent for verifying cross-modal consistency, a Differentiable Reliability Evaluator that employs LLM-based judges for automated assessment, and an Edge-Optimization Scheduler for efficient deployment. Applying the framework to a curated dataset of 1, 508 first-aid queries, we conduct a large-scale audit of Google’s AI Overviews (AIO) and Featured Snippets (FS), operated purely as black-box Systems under Audit. The audit reveals substantial reliability gaps: automated consistency scores of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\Phi _{cons}=0.68$$\end{document} (FS) and 0.72 (AIO), safety/relevance scores of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\Phi _{safe}=0.71$$\end{document} (FS) and 0.76 (AIO), and pronounced weaknesses on safety-critical “Binary” and “How-to” queries and on negative-sentiment queries where cautious tone matters most. Manual annotation on a 200-query subset validates the automated evaluation (Spearman \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\rho = 0.74$$\end{document}–0.87). RADAR-FirstAid offers a scalable, automated, and reproducible audit instrument for AI-powered search systems in safety-critical domains.

title: Enhanced cotton leaf disease classification Through ConvNeXt and Random Walk Grey Wolf Optimization
abstract: India has the highest number of cotton-cultivated land globally, thus placing it among the biggest producers of cotton in the world. Despite the huge cotton production, cotton leaf diseases still remain one of the most significant causes of yield losses in the crop. Accurate and early diagnosis is one of the first steps towards finding the solutions to mitigate the effects of the disease. In this research paper, we present the ConvNeXt deep learning framework used along with Random Walk Grey Wolf Optimizer (RWGWO) to diagnose and classify various diseases in cotton leaf. In its performance, ConvNeXt shows better accuracy when compared to the traditional CNN, Self-Organizing Map Artificial Neural Networks (SOMANN), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and other hybrid models with classification accuracy of 98.39%. Among others, our model successfully diagnoses and classifies the diseases of bacterial blight and aphid infestation, powdery mildew, armyworm, target spot, and healthy cotton leaves. All this is possible through a carefully chosen data set with proper data augmentation. The results of this research indicate that there is a high potential in using deep learning technology to improve agribusiness and textile fibers supply chain through early detection and management of the diseases outbreaks, which reduces the waste of pesticides associated with the late disease diagnosis. On the other hand, it should be noted that the use of ConvNeXt has limitations since larger models of this framework (ConvNeXt-Large and ConvNeXt-XL) have high computational complexity and energy consumption. The future work will include using field data sets and implementation of multi-modal learning, which will take into consideration various environmental factors.

title: AI driven oral cancer diagnosis from clinical imaging and computational pathology to precision therapeutics
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a computational approach for analysing the complex and heterogeneous data generated across oral cancer diagnosis and management. This narrative review provides an integrated overview of AI applications from early oral lesion detection, computational pathology, prognostic assessment, and precision therapeutics. It describes how machine learning and deep learning process clinical photographs, digitized histopathological images, whole-slide images, radiological examinations, and molecular or clinical data to generate task-specific outputs. The review covers AI-assisted identification of suspicious oral lesions, histopathological detection of oral epithelial dysplasia and oral squamous cell carcinoma, assessment of tumor differentiation, characterization of disease progression, and prediction of treatment response for therapeutic stratification. Particular attention is given to the relationship between the input data, computational task, and clinically relevant output rather than to model architecture alone. Although several studies report high diagnostic performance, much of the current evidence remains based on retrospective datasets and internal validation, while external, multicentre, and prospective evaluations are comparatively limited. Major challenges include dataset quality and representativeness, domain shift, annotation variability, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows. Future progress will require patient-level evaluation, multicentre validation, multimodal integration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and prospective assessment of clinical utility. This review outlines the evolving role of AI as a potential decision-support framework across the oral cancer care pathway.

title: Spatial distribution and severity of soil acidity across land uses in Gozamen District, Upper Blue Nile Basin, Ethiopia
abstract: Ethiopia is facing a soil pH problem that has not yet been accurately measured due to limited research on this issue. This study attempts to quantify the range of acid soils and develop land use-specific soil acidity characteristics in the selected kebeles of Gozamen District of northwestern Ethiopia through field soil survey, GIS, and digital soil mapping. Soil samples were taken using stratified random sampling over six kebeles of the Gozamen District. Soil pH was analyzed based on the standard procedure of FAO (2020) and GLOSOLAN (2019). Atmospheric images of Sentinel-2 Level-2 A were analyzed for vegetation cover via Random Forest (RF) Machine Learning Models, producing land-use/land-cover map with an overall accuracy of 92% and a Kappa Coefficient of 0.88. Spatial variability of soil pH was found to range from a minimum of 4.11 to a maximum of 6.58 throughout the selected kebeles of Gozamen District. Approximately 43% of the Gozamen District (selected kebeles) is very strongly acidic, and 39% is strongly acidic, with only 16% exhibiting moderate to slightly acidic pH, making them potentially useful for agricultural production. Agricultural and grazing lands were identified as having the greatest level of acidification, while forest ecosystems retained comparatively higher levels of soil pH, demonstrating the positive impact of natural vegetation in preserving healthy soils. This combination of field soil sampling, Sentinel-2 imaging, RF classification, and geostatistical interpolation offers an effective and economical method to develop accurate high-resolution mapping for soils that will ultimately lead to site-specific liming, precision soil fertility management, and planning for land restoration as part of Ethiopia’s agricultural transformation and sustainability initiatives.

title: Mapping and synthesis of evidence on soil fertility management, fertilizer use efficiency, and greenhouse gas outcomes
abstract: Soil fertility management influences fertilizer use efficiency (FUE), crop productivity, and greenhouse gas (GHG) outcomes, yet these dimensions are often reported separately. This study mapped and synthesized evidence linking soil fertility management with FUE and GHG outcomes using a structured analytical framework. Specifically, the study (i) assessed the distribution of soil fertility and nutrient management practices, (ii) explored reported FUE responses, (iii) evaluated GHG outcomes, and (iv) examined integration across soil, efficiency, and emission dimensions. A PRISMA-ScR-informed evidence mapping approach was applied to 40 open-access studies comprising field experiments, long-term trials, surveys, modelling studies, reviews, and meta-analyses. Evidence was extracted using a structured matrix and synthesized using a weighted Evidence Index (EI) and Integrated Evidence Score (IES). Integrated soil fertility management accounted for 12 studies, organic amendments for 10, enhanced-efficiency fertilizers and inhibitors for 9, and precision or optimized nutrient management for 9. Reported NUE values ranged from 25% to 70%, with increases of 10–40% for enhanced-efficiency fertilizers, 15–35% for organic amendments and biochar approaches, and 10–25% for precision or optimized nutrient management. Reported N₂O reductions ranged from 10% to 50% across management categories. NUE, N₂O, and soil organic carbon were reported in 70%, 65%, and 50% of studies, respectively. Category-level EI ranged from 1.79 to 2.17, whereas IES ranged from 1.89 to 2.42, reflecting differences between methodological weighting and dimensional coverage. The synthesis provides a structured basis for harmonizing soil fertility, nutrient efficiency, productivity, and GHG indicators in future evidence synthesis and agricultural management research.

title: When does competitive intensity improve service quality? The moderating role of differentiation strategy
abstract: Competitive intensity is widely assumed to push firms toward higher service quality, yet the strategic conditions under which this pressure actually translates into quality gains remain poorly understood. Drawing on contingency theory, this study examines whether a firm’s differentiation strategy moderates the relationship between competitive intensity and service quality, and specifically tests whether strong differentiation substitutes for, rather than amplifies, the quality-enhancing effect of competition. The study uses survey data from 204 non-manufacturing business units operating in the United Kingdom, drawn from a broader research project on costing systems (data collected September–December 2018). The present analysis addresses a distinct research question and an interaction-form contingency model that was not examined in the original study. Competitive intensity, differentiation strategy and service quality were measured with multi-item, previously validated survey scales. Hierarchical moderated ordinary least squares (OLS) regression was used, with continuous predictors mean-centered before the interaction term was formed; heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors were applied as a robustness check, and simple-slope and Johnson–Neyman analyses were used to probe the interaction. Competitive intensity and differentiation strategy were each positively associated with service quality. Contrary to a simple reinforcement account but consistent with a substitution logic, differentiation strategy significantly and negatively moderated the competitive intensity–service quality relationship (b = − 0.094, p = .013; HC3 p = .015). The positive effect of competitive intensity on service quality was strongest among low differentiators and weakened, without fully disappearing across the observed range, among firms with the strongest differentiation commitments. The study contributes to contingency-based strategy research by reframing competitive intensity and differentiation strategy as interacting rather than independent antecedents of service quality, and by providing empirical evidence, from a UK non-manufacturing sample, of a substitution pattern between external competitive pressure and internal strategic commitment as drivers of service quality. Because the design is cross-sectional and based on a single respondent per business unit, the findings should be interpreted as associational rather than causal. Practical implications for managers balancing strategic positioning and competitive response are discussed.

title: Phytohormonal networks and thermomemory in plant heat stress tolerance: From mechanistic integration to precision engineering.
abstract: Rising global temperatures pose a major threat to crop productivity, requiring mechanistically informed, scalable strategies to enhance heat stress (HS) tolerance. Phytohormones are central regulators of plant HS responses; however, tolerance instead emerges from dynamic, context-dependent network behavior. This review provides a mechanism-oriented synthesis of how major phytohormones coordinate HS adaptation. Specifically, we (i) reframe phytohormone action through core regulatory modules, including redox control, carbon-energy allocation, reproductive stability, and growth-defense trade-offs; (ii) resolve phytohormonal crosstalk into functional interaction networks that determine stress outcomes; (iii) define the molecular basis of heat priming and thermomemory; and (iv) evaluate translational strategies, including genetic engineering, precision breeding, and advanced delivery systems, together with their limitations under field conditions. We propose a unifying conceptual model in which HS tolerance is an emergent property of hierarchical phytohormonal networks operating across fast signaling, transcriptional memory, and metabolic buffering layers. This framework shifts the focus from single-pathway manipulation toward precision "hormonomics" and network-level engineering, providing a systems-level platform for developing climate-proof crops in a future, hotter climate.

title: Fault Diagnosis for Optical Transmission Systems Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Attention Mechanism Using DSP Power Monitoring
abstract: This paper proposes a fiber fault diagnosis method based on multi-scale feature fusion and an attention-enhanced neural network utilizing digital signal processing (DSP) power monitoring data, with potential applicability to online monitoring in optical transmission systems. The proposed approach employs a parallel convolutional architecture to extract multi-scale features, while an attention mechanism is introduced to emphasize critical features. Furthermore, a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) network is utilized to capture the temporal characteristics of the signal sequence, enabling accurate fault identification in optical transmission systems. Experimental validation was conducted using five typical types of optical fiber faults collected from a 400-Gb/s wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) operational network environment. The results show that the proposed method achieves an average window-level recognition accuracy of 99.15%, outperforming convolutional neural networks (CNN), CNN-BiGRU, and Transformer models by 5.38, 7.65, and 12.72 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method improves fault identification capabilities in optical communication networks, showing potential as a practical solution for intelligent fault diagnosis based on DSP monitoring data.

Biophysically constrained learning from healthy neural priors improves motor decoding in pathological cortical networks
abstract: High-performance brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) rely on stable neural representations, yet brain functional impairments inherently disrupt canonical encoding, creating a fundamental decoding paradox. Conventional data-driven approaches struggle to bridge this gap because of pathological data scarcity and heterogeneity. Here, we propose to leverage healthy neural priors and introduce Pathology-Aware Consensus Training (PACT), a paradigm embedding biophysical constraints into healthy neural recordings to guide neural decoding. In a gesture classification task using high-density electrocorticography from patients with gliomas infiltrating the motor cortex, PACT improved the accuracy by more than 10%, effectively restoring the distorted semantic geometry of motor commands and realigning them with healthy canonical representations (correlation increase: r = 0.66 to r = 0.94). Mechanistically, PACT induced an emergent “inverse weighting” strategy: The model autonomously suppresses high-power pathological noise while reanchoring spatial attention to functional compensatory regions. This study provides a proof of concept for improving decoding in compromised networks by harnessing healthy neural dynamics, laying the theoretical foundation for future BCI deployments in clinical populations.

title: An in situ forming immunomodulatory hydrogel reinvigorates exhausted CD8 + T cells via preserving their mitochondrial fitness
abstract: CD8 + T cell exhaustion driven by mitochondrial dysfunction remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy. Here, we report an in situ forming d -α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS)–based hydrogel [multifunctional thermosensitive composite gel (MTC Gel)] that reinvigorates exhausted CD8 + T cells by preserving mitochondrial fitness through a two-pronged strategy. After intratumoral injection, MTC Gel rapidly undergoes gelation at physiological temperature and dissociates to generate a high local concentration of TPGS, which targets cancer cell mitochondria to trigger prodeath mitophagy. This process induces robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) and blocks tunneling nanotube–mediated mitochondrial hijacking. Meanwhile, NLG919-loaded hybrid nanoparticles released from MTC Gel synergistically restore mitochondrial biogenesis in CD8 + T cells suppressed by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. Across multiple murine tumor models, MTC Gel reprograms T cell immunity by reducing CD8 + T cells exhaustion while enhancing effector and cytotoxic functions, thereby eliciting potent tumoricidal activity. These findings highlight this rationally designed hydrogel system as a clinically translatable platform for next-generation ICD-based cancer immunotherapies.
