title: Prism: Efficient Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning for On-Device LLMs
abstract: On-device fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs) is becoming increasingly important for personalized AI assistants and adaptive agents. However, standard backpropagation imposes substantial training-state memory overheads that often exceed the stringent resource budgets of mobile platforms. To address this, Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization leverages forward-only probing instead of backpropagation, drastically reducing memory footprints and offering a compelling alternative for on-device adaptation. Nonetheless, scaling ZO fine-tuning to billion-scale trainable parameter spaces remains challenging, as the cost of recovering reliable update directions scales poorly with dimensionality under mobile constraints. In this paper, we present Prism, a mobile-native infrastructure for practical billion-scale on-device ZO fine-tuning. Prism re-architects the ZO loop around a scalable probing substrate, bringing both per-step training latency and memory overhead closer to the inference footprint. We implement Prism end to end on commodity smartphones and evaluate it across diverse tasks and multiple model scales. Prism achieves accuracy comparable to that of state-of-the-art ZO fine-tuning baselines while reducing per-step latency by 53.4%-76.3% and peak memory by 10.6%-13.8% relative to the best baseline in each setting. These results demonstrate the practical feasibility of billion-scale on-device ZO fine-tuning for LLMs under real mobile constraints. We will release our code to support future research.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking

title: Mechanically Programmable Reflective Metasurfaces: A General Low-Cost Paradigm for High-Frequency Wavefront Control
abstract: Programmable reflective metasurfaces enable flexible wave manipulation, but conventional resonance-based designs suffer from high cost, narrow bandwidth, complex calibration, and limited deployability at high frequencies. We present MetaX, a low-cost mechanically programmable metasurface that controls wavefronts by continuously deforming a reflective membrane with only 64 micro-motors. Geometric path-length modulation enables broadband, calibration-free operation across different wave domains. We further develop a differentiable model that maps actuator commands to 3D surface deformation and wave responses, and use gradient-based inverse design to generate mechanical code-books for wide-angle single-beam steering and concurrent multi-beam generation. Experiments with a 64-actuator prototype demonstrate stable RF beam steering over 77-81 GHz with a maximum frequency-induced pointing deviation of only 2.5° and support for four concurrent beams with at most 1.07 dB average inter-user power imbalance. The experiments further demonstrate that adjusting the motor spacing enables the MetaX prototype to support beam steering across other frequency bands within 20-85 GHz. The complete prototype costs approximately $81, demonstrating low-cost, broadband, and multi-beam wavefront control for high frequencies.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking

title: From Soil, For Soil: Self-Powered Moisture Sensing via Natural Electrical Transients
abstract: Soil moisture is a critical variable for irrigation management, crop health monitoring, and hydrological modelling, and plays a central role in large-scale rural IoT deployments. However, existing soil moisture sensing techniques, including resistive probes, dielectric sensors, and RF-based methods, require continuous electrical excitation, exhibit strong dependence on soil properties, and often require frequent calibration or battery maintenance, limiting their long-term deployment. In this paper, we present SoilSense+, a self-powered soil moisture sensing system that infers moisture from naturally occurring electrical transients at the soil-electrode interface. When two passive electrodes are inserted into moist soil, intrinsic electrochemical dynamics generate a characteristic galvanic-RC relaxation response whose temporal behaviour correlates with volumetric water content. SoilSense+ captures these transient responses using a minimal sensing frontend and reconstructs high-fidelity signals through a lightweight learning-based pipeline trained under controlled indoor conditions and applied to outdoor environments. We further develop a physical relaxation model linking transient voltage dynamics to soil moisture and implement a low-cost wireless sensing prototype built from commodity components. Extensive experiments across multiple soil textures and deployment configurations show that SoilSense+ achieves indoor and outdoor moisture estimation errors of approximately 3.2% and 7.46%, respectively, comparable to commercial dielectric probes, while requiring no external power supply, no soil-specific calibration, and only $6.87 in hardware cost. These results demonstrate that intrinsic soil electrical transients can serve as a practical sensing mechanism, enabling environmentally friendly, low-cost monitoring for rural IoT.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking

title: Demo: Responsible Physical AI with Edge-based Guardrails
abstract: Physical Artificial Intelligence (PAI), the augmenting of physical systems with artificial intelligence, is becoming the next frontier for agentic systems. Robotic embodiments, powered by the advances in AI models, are quickly gaining traction for general-purpose deployments in enterprise offices, homes, and factory floors. With a vision anchored in automation, mobile robotic manipulation is one of the most important emerging workloads for mobile systems [13]. Even as PAI is at the cusp of widespread deployment, we believe there is an important challenge that must be overcome for widespread practical adoption: guardrails for safe operations.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking

title: Demo: Per-UE Baseband Routing in vRAN
abstract: Today's virtualized RANs (vRANs) bind every User Equipment (UE) in a cell to a single, monolithic PHY (L1) implementation, forcing an all-or-nothing model for L1 evolution: an L1 implementation cannot be tested or rolled out to a subset of users without exposing the entire cell to risk. This precludes the possibility of safe, incremental L1 updates, incell A/B testing of new L1s, and any form of per-UE service differentiation at the L1. We present Thor, the first system to introduce per-UE baseband routing as a practical, standards-compliant primitive for vRANs. Thor allows multiple L1 instances to run concurrently for the same cell and dynamically routes each UE to its designated instance, by interposing two lightweight middleboxes at the FAPI and O-RAN fronthaul interfaces, alongside a control-plane component that manages the UE-to-L1 assignment, requiring no modification to existing MAC implementations or commercial radio units (RUs). We demonstrate Thor on our O-RAN testbed with a commercial O-RU, showcasing concurrent multi-L1 operation within a single cell, seamless per-UE routing across L1s, and UE-level isolation among L1s.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking

title: RadioLens: Seeing and Interacting with the Invisible Radio Environment on AR Glasses
abstract: Wireless signals are invisible, making wireless network deployment and optimization difficult. Engineers cannot directly see how signals propagate through and interact with the physical environment. Existing AR tools can render simulated or measured radio signals in space, but they largely stop at simple visualization of existing data. They cannot accurately infer the radio field at unobserved locations or support effective diagnosis of radio propagation. We present RadioLens, an AR-glass system that constructs a continuous, room-specific 3D radio field from sparse measurements, enabling users to query the radio environment anywhere and interactively edit the environment to evaluate how the field changes. At its core, RadioLens embeds a lightweight differentiable ray-tracing engine on the device, which combines scanned room geometry with sparse radio measurements to adapt the propagation model to the physical site. Built on this field, RadioLens supports coverage diagnosis, propagation-path inspection, and what-if analysis of transmitter placement, environmental objects, and passive reflectors for network deployment and optimization.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking

title: Demo: ChannelAgent: Agent-Driven One-Click Digital Twin Channel Generation for AI-Native 6G
abstract: Digital twin is emerging as a key enabler for the intelligent design, analysis, and operation of artificial intelligence (AI)-native sixth-generation (6G) networks. Digital twin channel (DTC) extends this paradigm to wireless communication by providing high-fidelity, real-time representations of the physical wireless channels. However, DTC generation faces key challenges in channel task parsing, ubiquitous environment construction, and real-time channel twinning. This demo presents ChannelAgent, the first agent-driven platform for one-click DTC generation. By combining agent-driven task orchestration, an environment generation large language model (EnvGen LLM), and high-performance electromagnetic computation, ChannelAgent forms an end-to-end workflow of task parsing, intelligent scheduling, environment reconstruction, and channel twinning. The prototype completes each electromagnetic propagation computation within 50 ms with a mean absolute path loss error below 5 dB, enabling high-fidelity and real-time DTC generation across diverse 6G environments.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking

title: Demo: Can AI Agents Adapt to Your Daily Life? Horae, a Behavior-Aware Scheduler Grounded in Mobile Sensing
abstract: Modern scheduling tools manage fixed events but do not automatically adapt as a user's life changes—for example, when a user starts a scheduled activity later than planned, disrupting the rest of the day. Horae bridges this gap with a behavior-aware scheduler that adapts to evolving routines. Horae processes mobile sensor data directly on the user's device, learns what is normal for that person, and recommends simple schedule changes that better reflect changes in their life. In blinded evaluations, an AI reviewer preferred Horae's suggestions in 71.8% of cases. Human raters also preferred Horae, selecting its suggestions 57.3% of the time, compared with 36.5% for suggestions based only on existing calendar events and 6.3% for leaving the schedule unchanged. We demonstrate Horae's end-to-end workflow live; a recorded video is available at: Demo Link.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking

title: Deep learning-based differentiation of FLASH ultrasound windows
abstract: Equine colic emergencies present highly stressful, time-critical scenarios for both clinicians and patients, thus rapid and accurate diagnostic triage is paramount. To support veterinarians under these high-pressure conditions, deep learning tools can be leveraged for automated image recognition to assist in localizing abdominal organs and interpreting FLASH (Fast Localized Abdominal Sonography of Horses) ultrasound windows. A software tool was developed to identify FLASH-specific ultrasound windows on the equine abdomen and to recognize ultrasonographic organ patterns. Retrospective-prospective comparison of software and clinical examination, model development. A deep learning approach for image classification was used to train software to assign ultrasound images to FLASH windows. Strongest software performance was observed for the duodenal window, with all test images correctly classified, corresponding to a recall of 1.00. Nephrosplenic window demonstrated high classification accuracy, but 23% of images were misclassified as gastric window. While 84% of ventral images were correctly classified, 16% were predicted as duodenal window. Most pronounced confusion was observed between ventral and thoracic windows, with only 55% of thoracic images correctly identified. Left and right middle third FLASH windows 4 and 6 were substantially underrepresented and were therefore excluded from further analyses. In addition, these windows exhibited high anatomical similarity, which further complicated their differentiation. Sources of selection bias was interpretation of windows and the definition of normal physiological ultrasound images by the examiners. The specific FLASH windows were not homogeneously dispersed in the dataset (e.g., FLASH windows 4 and 6 were underrepresented). The developed deep learning tool demonstrates the feasibility of automated recognition of standardized equine FLASH windows and may support ultrasound training as an educational aid for first-day competencies. Future incorporation of organ-level annotations and probe position information may improve discrimination between anatomically similar windows and enhance model performance.

title: Luxury fashion brands’ AI-powered sustainability chatbot communication: how information qualities and brand luxury perception shape consumer trust and behavior
abstract: This study examines how sustainability communication in luxury retail shapes brand trust and behavioral intentions, focusing on consumers' post-exposure perceptions of information quality and provider type. Building on perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness, the study explores how consumers evaluate identical sustainability information attributed to either a human agent or an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot, and how these perceptions influence brand trust, information acceptance intention, and purchase intention. A scenario-based experiment with 346 participants was conducted, and the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness were positively associated with brand trust, which inturn mediated their relationships with information acceptance intention and purchase intention. The indirect effect of perceived objectivity was significant only under AI communication, suggesting that algorithmic provider cues may strengthen the trust-mediated role of objectivity, whereas perceived persuasiveness remained consistently associated with trust and behavioral intentions across provider types. Subgroup analyses further suggest a conditional pattern: among consumers with lower perceived brand luxury, the links between brand trust and behavioral intentions were stronger under AI communication, whereas no significant provider differences emerged among those with higher perceived brand luxury. As these results derivefrom split-sample multi-group comparisons rather than a formal interaction test, they should be regarded as subgroup-based evidence. These findings extend luxury branding research by showing how AI provider cues shape perceived information quality in sustainability communication and by highlighting the need to align provider strategy with consumers' perceptions of luxury brands.

title: Evaluating machine learning and econometric models for inflation forecasting: evidence from a Sub-Saharan African panel
abstract: Policymakers in Sub-Saharan Africa increasingly face decisions regarding the adoption of machine learning methods for inflation forecasting, yet these approaches are rarely benchmarked against simple persistence models. This study constructs a reproducible, annual panel of macroeconomic indicators for eight Sub-Saharan African economies (1972–2024, N = 424) to compare eight forecasting approaches: a naive random-walk benchmark, two linear econometric models (pooled OLS and country fixed effects), three machine learning models (Elastic Net, Random Forest, and XGBoost), and a recurrent neural network (LSTM) evaluated with and without early stopping. Using a chronological train/validation/test split and pairwise Diebold–Mariano tests, we evaluate out-of-sample predictive accuracy. The empirical results indicate that no estimated model statistically outperforms the naive persistence baseline. While Random Forest, XGBoost, Elastic Net, and the early-stopped LSTM show no statistically significant difference from the random walk, traditional linear models and the uncorrected LSTM are significantly dominated by it. Although implementing early stopping substantially improves LSTM performance, it does not yield a competitive advantage over simpler tree-based ensembles. These findings align with the well-documented random-walk puzzle in global inflation forecasting, suggesting that structural breaks, high volatility, and modest sample sizes pose substantial challenges for highly parameterized forecasting architectures. Consequently, these results suggest that regional central banks and finance ministries should maintain simple persistence models as active baselines when evaluating investments in complex forecasting infrastructure. These conclusions are robust to a battery of additional checks: HAC-Newey–West/Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold-corrected and Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted Diebold–Mariano tests, a strictly lagged-only predictor respecification, expanding-window recursive re-estimation, per-country and subperiod decomposition, LSTM input-sequence-length sensitivity analysis, a pooled AR(1) benchmark, a five-seed LSTM replication, and a country-clustered block-bootstrap Diebold–Mariano test.

title: The Khoton People of Mongolia
abstract: The Khoton ethnic group of western Mongolia represents one of the most distinctive ethnocultural communities in Inner Asia. Concentrated primarily in the Tarialan region of Uvs Province, the Khotons are notable for their Islamic religious heritage, historical association with sedentary agriculture, and traces of Turkic linguistic ancestry within a predominantly Mongolic environment (Potanin, G. 1881. Ocherki Severo-Zapadnoi Mongolii. Imperial Russian Geographical Society; Vladimirtsov, B. 1929. Comparative Grammar of Mongolic Languages and Ethnographic Notes on Western Mongolian Peoples. Academy of Sciences of the USSR). Their origin, ethnic identity, language, religion, and genetic composition have long attracted scholarly attention, yet many aspects remain unresolved. This article synthesizes historical, linguistic, ethnographic, anthropological, and genetic studies to present a comprehensive interpretation of Khoton ethnogenesis and cultural development. The study argues that the Khotons are not a homogeneous ethnic population derived from a single ancestral source; rather, they emerged through centuries of interaction among Central Asian Turkic peoples, Oirat Mongols, Islamic sedentary communities, and neighboring Inner Asian groups (Golden, P. B. 1992. An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples. Otto Harrassowitz; Soucek, S. 2000. A History of Inner Asia. Cambridge University Press). Historical evidence suggests that many of their ancestors were relocated into western Mongolia during the period of the Dzungar Khanate in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries (Allsen, T. T. 2001. Culture and Conquest in Mongol Eurasia. Cambridge University Press; Atwood, C. P. 2004. Encyclopedia of Mongolia and the Mongol Empire. Facts on File). Linguistic evidence indicates that the Khoton language belonged to the Turkic language family but gradually disappeared through long-term assimilation into Oirat Mongolian speech communities (Vladimirtsov, B. 1929. Comparative Grammar of Mongolic Languages and Ethnographic Notes on Western Mongolian Peoples. Academy of Sciences of the USSR; Poppe, N. N. 1955. Introduction to Mongolian Comparative Studies. Otto Harrassowitz). Contemporary genetic studies likewise demonstrate that the Khotons possess a mixed Central Asian genetic profile distinct from neighboring Mongolian populations (Katoh, T., B. Munkhbat, K. Tounai, S. Mano, H. Ando, G. Oyungerel, et al. 2005. “Genetic Features of Mongolian Ethnic Groups Revealed by Y-chromosomal Analysis.” Gene 346: 63–70). The article further explores the role of Islam in preserving ethnic identity after linguistic assimilation, examines the sociocultural functions of oral traditions and ritual texts, and discusses the contemporary revival of Khoton cultural consciousness in the context of globalization and digital heritage preservation (DeWeese, D. 1994. Islamization and Native Religion in the Golden Horde. Pennsylvania State University Press; Privratsky, B. G. 2001. Muslim Turkistan: Kazak Religion and Collective Memory. Curzon Press). The Khotons thus provide a valuable case study for understanding language death, ethnogenesis, religious adaptation, and cultural hybridity in Inner Asia.
journal: Mongolian Diaspora. Journal of Mongolian History and Culture

title: A Review of Deep-learning-based Seismic Data Denoising and Its Promising Paradigm Shift to Foundation Models
abstract: Denoising is a long-standing and widely-concerned topic in seismic data processing, for it can significantly increase the signal-to-noise ratio of seismic data. Numerous deep learning (DL) methods have shown promising denoising performance, but most of them are task-specific and focus on a certain type of seismic background noise. The real condition that seismic datasets are often contaminated by various types of noises motivates us to explore a well-generalized and versatile DL model for seismic data denoising. Recently, in the fields of computer vision and natural language processing, foundation models (FMs) pre-trained on vast datasets demonstrate outstanding adaptability and generality across diverse downstream tasks. This paradigm offers a promising path to address the challenges faced by task-specific DL denoising models, such as poor generalization, retraining from scratch for different noise, and the lack of labeled data. We first provide a brief review of traditional seismic denoising methods, followed by a comprehensive review of existing DL-based denoising methods categorized by noise type. Furthermore, we conduct a case study on a dedicated seismic denoising foundation model termed SeisDeFM. This is the first study in geophysical research to develop and validate a seismic denoising foundation model on pre-stack gathers with diverse noise conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with task-specific DL baselines, SeisDeFM achieves superior denoising performance and cross-noise generalization by the advantages of sufficient pre-training and appropriate downstream adaptation, and it effectively preserves weak reflection events while suppressing complex noise in pre-stack seismic data.

title: Vision Foundation Models for Multi-Modal Medical Image Classification
abstract: Clinicians combine several imaging modalities to reach a diagnosis. Yet assembling large annotated datasets for every modality combination is rarely feasible, and modalities are frequently missing in practice. Vision foundation models (FMs) could ease both problems by transferring from few labels, but this has mainly been shown for single images. We therefore compare FM initialisation (DINOv2 and MedSigLIP) against random initialisation, across fusion and training strategies, on three tasks: glioma subtyping from multi-sequence MRI, HER2 scoring from paired histopathology stains, and liver-lesion classification from multi-phase MRI. At full data, FM initialisation matched or outperformed random initialisation, raising liver-lesion sensitivity from 54 % to 76 %. The advantage held as labels grew scarce and was largest under missing modalities, where FM initialisation kept sensitivity near 73 % as random initialisation fell to 29 %. For multi-modal medical imaging, FM initialisation is a strong default, most valuable when labels are scarce or acquisition protocols incomplete.

title: Crop Yield Estimation With Help of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) & Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Determining Crop Yield Potential is increasingly becoming part of Intelligent Precision Agriculture Technology used to optimise management of farms, to enhance the use of resources & to achieve sustainable food production. Traditional Yield Assessment methods carried out through manual observation and statistical assessment (in most cases) require significant time, resources, and are often not effective because they do not account for the spatial variability present within agricultural fields. Therefore, this research proposes the development of an innovative intelligent crop yield prediction framework based on UAV technology, and advanced Remote Sensing & Artificial Intelligence Techniques, as an alternative to the traditional method of measurement. The current study reports on data collected from wheat fields using UAV collected high-resolution aerial photographs captured with RGB imaging cameras. The collected aerial imagery data were then processed using photogrammetric reconstruction techniques to create orthorectified maps of fields and 3D representations of wheat crops-from this data advanced image processing was performed for the purpose of Segmentation, Canopy Extraction and analysis of the Spatial Variability in Wheat Crops. UAV imagery was used to obtain various crop features (phenotypic and spectral), including: percentage of vegetation coverage, canopy texture, plant vigor, biomass characteristics, and growth variability. RGB-based vegetation indices (GLA, VARI, RGBVI, and ExG) were derived from UAV images for analysis of crop health and physiology. The extracted features were used to develop yield prediction models based on machine learning and deep learning algorithms. To predict yield, we used various predictive models (RF, SVM, DN, and LASSO). Performance of the models was compared using statistical measures such as root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R²). The results showed that the deep learning models outperformed the other prediction algorithms, due to their ability to learn complex spatial/non-linear relationships from UAV imagery. The suggested framework offers a quick, automated, and non-destructive method of estimating agricultural yield and for use within precision agriculture. The combination of aerial imagery from UAVs (drones), analysis through GIS, and data mining through Artificial Intelligence will permit a more efficient means for monitoring agriculture and making data-driven decisions at the farm level. The results of this research highlight the benefits that can be achieved from the development and application of UAV-enabled Smart Agriculture systems in terms of increasing productivity, decreasing resource wastage, and contributing to sustainable agricultural practices.

title: VirtualLab_CC: An LLM-augmented virtual laboratory for automated computational chemistry research
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have opened new avenues for automating scientific research workflows. Systems like the AI Scientist [1] demonstrate fully autonomous endto-end research pipelines for machine learning, but their applicability to domains requiring expensive high-performance computing (HPC) resources, specialized quantum chemistry software, and rigorous thermochemical accuracy remains unexplored. Here we present VirtualLab_CC, a hybrid LLM-augmented virtual laboratory for computational chemistry that integrates Claude (Anthropic) as an orchestration layer with a multi-agent architecture, gated lifecycle management, and bidirectional HPC cluster synchronization. Unlike fully autonomous systems, VirtualLab_CC enforces human-in-the-loop quality gates at every critical decision point while automating routine operations: conformer searches, input generation, job submission and monitoring, output parsing, failure diagnosis, and manuscript preparation. The system manages 21 specialized skills spanning literature review, cluster operations, result extraction, novelty verification, AI-assisted peer review, and citation validation. We demonstrate VirtualLab_CC on a prototype case study of 1,3-dipolar cycloadditions between stabilized Criegee intermediates and biogenic terpene dipolarophiles, involving 17 molecular species, 34 conformers, and over 100 SLURM jobs across multiple calculation stages. The system successfully identified and autocorrected cluster failures, detected a methodological anomaly (a suspiciously low dioxirane barrier requiring IRC verification), and coordinated multi-method validation across three DFT functionals. VirtualLab_CC bridges the gap between fully autonomous AI research and the rigorous quality control demands of computational chemistry, providing a practical framework for LLM-augmented scientific workflows in resource-constrained HPC environments.

title: A PRIVACY PRESERVING PERSONAL AI ASSISTANT AND THE COST OF CLOUD MODEL INFERENCE: ARCHITECTURE, CAPABILITY TRADEOFFS, AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL
abstract: Personal AI assistants need reliable research and controlled access to private data. This report specifies a local-first Windows architecture and examines the capability, privacy, and operating-cost tradeoff between local Llama 3.2 3B through Ollama and self-hosted Kimi K2.5 on rented NVIDIA GPUs. We analyzed a supplied project design summary, mapped trust boundaries and failure modes, and calculated illustrative costs from a documented eight-H200 deployment and published rental rates. The design separates public research from authenticated browser sessions, enforces permissions outside the model, and requires evidence-supported answers. At an illustrative $4.59 per GPU-hour, eight H200s cost $36.72 per running hour, $4,406.40 for four hours daily over 30 days, or $26,438.40 for continuous 30-day operation, before storage and operations. An assumed 100 W incremental local draw for four hours daily at $0.15/kWh costs $1.80 monthly on an existing PC. These are scenarios, not measured deployments. Kimi K2.5 offers multimodal and agentic capabilities that a text-only 3B baseline should not be assumed to match; no matched end-to-end test was performed. Stronger cloud inference can impose substantial dedicated GPU rental cost and transfers prompts to a cloud operator. Local inference preserves a narrower data boundary at far lower incremental cash cost but requires direct task-quality evaluation.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Securing the Ai-first Sdlc: Identity, Access, and Data Protection for Enterprise Ai Agents
abstract: AI agents can now participate in several steps of software delivery: reading requirements, changing code, requesting tests, and preparing releases. Giving them this freedom creates a difficult security question. How can an enterprise allow useful work without giving an agent more authority than the task requires? Existing practices such as least privilege, identity management, separation of duties, and audit logging provide much of the foundation. The challenge is applying them consistently when a human delegates work to agents that use several connected systems. This paper proposes Agentic Identity and Access Governance (AIAG), a security framework for the AI-First Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). Four connected mechanisms define the proposal: a Role Conflict Matrix that checks the combined permissions of people and their sponsored agents; an Agent Access Manifest that records permitted tools and operating limits; a governed boundary between live personal-information access and general AI-assisted work; and an MCP Gateway that enforces access policy before tool calls execute. A customer notification-preference change is used to explain how these mechanisms affect development, testing, release approval, and support. We also describe credential handling, data-egress controls, audit, and practical ways to evaluate the framework. The work is conceptual, informed by technical analysis and exploratory proof-of-concept activity. No end-to-end deployment or measured security results are claimed.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Machine Learning-Based Regional Assessment of Second-Crop Corn Yield Using Climatic and Water-Balance Variables
abstract: Second-crop corn is an important component of Brazilian grain production and is highly exposed to climatic variability because crop development occurs during the transition from the rainy to the drier season. This study assessed the performance of machine learning algorithms for estimating second-crop corn yield within the 2012–2023 historical data domain in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. Municipal yield data from 22 municipalities and daily climatic data covering the period from 2012 to 2023 were analyzed. Yield data were obtained from Aprosoja/MS, whereas climatic variables, including solar radiation, air temperature, evapotranspiration, relative humidity, wind speed, and precipitation, were obtained from NASA/POWER. Pearson correlation analysis was used as an initial screening procedure to identify climatic variables associated with yield variability. Multiple linear regression (MLR), a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a support vector machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and a gradient boosting regressor (GBR) were evaluated. Under the observation-level random partition adopted in this study, RF and XGBoost showed the highest performance in the randomly held-out testing subset, both reaching R2 values of approximately 0.80. However, XGBoost exhibited near-perfect calibration performance followed by a substantial decrease during testing (MAPE = 14.05%; R2 = 0.80), indicating overfitting. Random Forest achieved similar testing performance with a smaller calibration-to-testing gap. Therefore, under the specific random partition used in this study, RF was considered the preferred model. In contrast, GBR failed to provide reliable predictive performance under the present dataset and configuration, with a testing MAPE of 547.78%, and was therefore considered too unreliable for interpretation in this study. Importantly, because the partition did not preserve temporal or spatial independence, these results represent generalization within the 2012–2023 historical data domain and should not be interpreted as evidence of future-year or spatially independent predictive performance. Because the dataset was partitioned randomly at the observation level without preserving temporal independence, the reported performance represents generalization within the 2012–2023 historical data domain and should not be interpreted as future-year forecasting performance.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Cyber Defense: From Intelligent Threat Detection to Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: The article provides a comprehensive analysis of the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in cybersecurity, taking into account the latest technological trends of 2024–2026. The main possibilities of applying AI to protect information systems are studied: automatic detection of threats and anomalies, real-time incident response, prediction and prevention of cyberattacks, recognition of malicious code and phishing, and continuous learning and adaptation of defense systems. Particular attention is paid to the phenomenon of autonomous AI agents as a new stage in the evolution of intelligent cyber defense systems: practical cases of agentic incident triage and investigation systems (Microsoft Security Copilot), autonomous vulnerability discovery (Google Big Sleep), autonomous penetration testing (XBOW, PentestGPT), as well as the first documented case of an AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign are analyzed. The risks and challenges associated with the use of AI are considered: misuse of technologies by attackers, false positives and missed threats, vulnerabilities of machine learning models and agentic systems, and ethical and legal aspects. The necessity of a balanced approach combining automated AI systems with expert human control based on human-in-the-loop and human-on-the-loop models is substantiated.

title: Digital Literacy in Agriculture: Current State and Development Prospects
abstract: Digitalization of Kazakhstan’s agricultural sector is a strategic direction of state socio-economic policy. The introduction of digital technologies into the agro-industrial complex contributes to increasing the efficiency of production processes and rationalizing the use of material, financial, and natural resources. Objective – to substantiate the impact of digital literacy on the performance of digital management in the republic’s agricultural sphere, to determine vectors for the development of digital competencies of economic entities. Methods – a systems approach allowing digital management to be viewed as a complex multi-level series of interconnected elements to establish the scale of AIC computerization in the country. The quantitative principle was applied in assessing the effect of digital culture on the effective regulation of the agricultural industry. The information base of the study consisted of legal acts of the Republic of Kazakhstan, state programs in digital transformation of agro-industrial production, statistical data, materials of international organizations, and scientific works of domestic and foreign researchers. Results – it was shown that information readiness represents not only a set of individual skills and knowledge, but also a vital institutional potential necessary for the optimal functioning of the agricultural sector administration model. Conclusions – it was revealed that the presence of formal access to digital technologies and information systems does not ensure methodically structured coordination in the absence of digital erudition among specialists and managers of the agro-industrial complex. The widespread dissemination and promotion of digital literacy will reduce management costs, strengthen competitive advantages in the agri-food market, address pressing environmental problems, stimulate labor productivity growth, adapt to climate change, improve crop yield indicators, and enable timely planning of field work.

title: Developing an Institutional Readiness Framework for Agentic AI Adoption in Bangladesh Public Universities: Insights from Faculty and Policy Stakeholders
abstract: The evolution of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the landscape of higher education as AI can plan activities, make use of digital tools, and carry out progressively independent acts in teaching, administration, support services, and research processes. The development of such technology brings along new opportunities for the universities, but at the same time, it poses certain challenges to them, which include infrastructure issues, institutional capabilities, governance issues, ethical issues, and human supervision. Such challenges are quite relevant to public universities of Bangladesh. The study constructs a contextualized IRF for adopting agentic AI in Bangladesh public universities. Based on interpretivist approach and adapted TOE framework, this study adopted qualitative research methodology involving semi-structured interviews with 18 university faculty members and policymakers. Four main themes were emerged from thematic analysis: Infrastructure-Policy gap, Socio-cultural inertia, Ethics and Grassroot innovations. The findings indicate that institutional readiness is not solely a technological condition but is shaped by organizational culture, leadership capacity, regulatory preparedness, ethical considerations, trust, and human oversight. Based on these findings, a four-level Institutional Readiness Framework is proposed, comprising foundational readiness, cultural readiness, regulatory readiness, and implementation readiness. The framework emphasizes strengthening digital infrastructure and literacy, developing institutional awareness and role clarity, establishing context-sensitive and human-in-the-loop governance mechanisms, and implementing supervised AI pilots supported by training and review processes. The study contributes to the emerging literature on agentic AI by providing a context-sensitive readiness framework grounded in the realities of public universities in the Global South. It also provides practical implications for policymakers and university administrators seeking to develop responsible, equitable, and contextually appropriate pathways for agentic AI adoption in Bangladesh.

title: Comparative Study of a Biomass-Derived Activated Carbon Catalyst and a Synthetic Silica–Alumina Catalyst on the Heat Transfer Rate Characteristics of Coconut Oil Droplet Combustion
abstract: This study compares the effect of a biomass-derived catalyst (areca-husk activated carbon, hereafter termed the biocatalyst) and a synthetic catalyst (silica–alumina) on the combustion characteristics and heat transfer rate of crude coconut oil (CCO) droplets, a renewable fuel that is difficult to burn because of its high viscosity. Each catalyst was blended into CCO at 1, 2, and 3 ppm, and 0.001 mL droplets suspended at a K-type thermocouple junction were ignited by a Ni–Cr wire heated at 12 V. Flame evolution was recorded with a digital camera and temperature–time data with a data logger, with five repetitions per condition; the heat transfer rate was estimated from the measured temperature using Newton's law of cooling. The biocatalyst blends burned for 1.68–2.00 s and reached peak flame temperatures of about 700–720 °C and peak heat transfer rates of 0.94–0.96 W, whereas the synthetic-catalyst blends burned longer (1.92–2.16 s) but peaked lower, at about 650–665 °C and 0.87–0.88 W. The biocatalyst blends also had a lower kinematic viscosity (27.37–27.46 cSt) than the synthetic-catalyst blends (30.54–32.52 cSt). Within the range tested, the biocatalyst mainly accelerates and intensifies heat release, with 2 ppm giving its longest flame (2.00 s), while silica–alumina mainly prolongs and stabilises combustion, with 3 ppm giving the longest flame of all blends (2.16 s). These findings indicate that low-cost activated carbon from agricultural waste can be used to improve the ignitability of raw vegetable-oil fuels in burners and small-scale combustion systems, whereas silica–alumina is better suited where a steady, sustained flame is required.

title: Assessing diversified farming’s effects on Central American cacao and coffee smallholders’ food security and vulnerability
abstract: Diversified farming is one of several agroecological strategies for reducing smallholders’ risk and building resilience to climate change and other hazards. Accumulating evidence shows that farmers can use agroecology to improve household food security and influence food system transformations. However, additional research is needed to identify which agroecological strategies are used by whom and to what degree diversification, household characteristics, context, or other strategies contribute to farmer well-being and resilience. In 2022, we conducted a livelihood, agriculture, and food security survey with 429 randomly sampled smallholders, including 309 coffee farmers in northern Nicaragua’s Segovias region and 120 cacao farmers in north-central Nicaragua’s Waslala region. We examined the relationships linking diversified production—and other key agroecological principles—to food security, water security, and dietary diversity. We integrated statistical analysis into our participatory mixed methods approach using partner feedback to help design the survey and 13 farmer interviews to inform and interpret the statistical models. We found that cacao farmers in the wetter growing zone reported more crop diversity and organic production and less seasonal hunger than coffee growers. Food and input price inflation were more pressing concerns than the impact of hurricanes Eta and Iota for all producers. Our multivariate analysis found that significant correlates of food security included surplus subsistence (corn and bean) production, water security, farm size, and income. Product diversity and farmers’ formal education correlated significantly with household dietary diversity. This study finds evidence that agroecological diversified farming can enhance food security and dietary diversity among coffee and cacao smallholders. This is among the first studies comparing how cacao and coffee farmers’ diversified and agroecological production strategies relate to food security, water security, nutrition, and vulnerability, potentially holding implications for the 15 million plus smallholder coffee and cacao growers seeking more sustainable livelihoods and landscapes.

title: A psychological prediction automatic reasoning framework for explaining potential cognitive states
abstract: Psychological prediction, the ability to infer human behavior and intentions, is essential for artificial intelligence and human–machine interaction. Existing deep learning models often rely on surface-level fitting and lack structured abductive interpretability, while traditional neuro-symbolic systems suffer from non-differentiable discontinuities and limited adaptability to dynamic contextual constraints. This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic automated reasoning framework for modeling latent cognitive states under contextual constraints. The framework introduces a context-aware adaptive SMC resampling operator (CAR-SMC), which uses energy-based penalties to filter hypotheses violating contextual constraints. We further design an executable differentiable program synthesis (EDPS) module and a hybrid iterative program–cognition interaction (HIPCI) mechanism. Through stop-gradient-based directional optimization, HIPCI separates the update pathways of belief and program representations during alternating fixed-point optimization, reducing circular gradient entanglement. Experiments on OpenToM and FANToM show that the framework improves the abductive consistency rate (ACR), an empirical belief–action consistency metric, to 70.8% and 52.1%, respectively. Under the adopted classification-oriented evaluation setup, these results indicate additional ACR gains over pure fine-tuned encoder classifiers and higher ACR than the evaluated few-shot ToT reference baseline (~ 7B), while using fewer parameters and maintaining an average inference latency of 215 ms per instance. Overall, this work provides a differentiable framework for machine Theory of Mind with process-level structural interpretability under the evaluated text-based classification setting.

title: Novel index on the propensity for digital transformation in agriculture (PADiTIndex)
abstract: Digital agriculture is one of the levers that will enable food systems to adapt and remain resilient in the face of climate change. However, in addition to being generally slow to take off, its adoption is not geographically uniform. While studies at the producer level have investigated the rationale for this disparity, we argue that it could be that different countries and markets are prepared to absorb digital technologies into their value chains. This study assesses the propensity of different countries and markets to digitally transform their agriculture using a new proposed index named Propensity for Agricultural Digital Transformation Index (PADiTIndex) . It uses four indicators including the economic weight of agriculture in the country’s economy, the vulnerability/resilience of the country’s agricultural sector to climate change, the country’s agricultural productivity, and its openness to innovation. To this end, time series data for these four indicators were collected from FAOSTAT, ND- GAIN, USDA and WDCR for the period 2015–2022, making the assessment scalable. A few cases of missing data were completed by interpolation while normalization was used to transform the four indicators that were in different units into a single comparable format. The results indicate that the value of agricultural production per agricultural worker, the resilience of food systems to climate change, and national openness to innovation are the country-level dimensions most closely associated with the propensity of economies to digitally transform their agriculture. In this regard, the Netherlands, Israel, Belgium, Denmark, and Luxembourg stand out as the top five countries where the digital transformation of agriculture is most evident. Conversely, the five countries with the lowest rankings are in Africa (Niger, Madagascar, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, and Guinea), suggesting room for improvement, beginning with fostering a stronger commitment to modernizing their agricultural sectors to enhance their resilience. This work also corroborates findings from studies, highlighting the well-documented importance of socioeconomic factors in climate change adaptation planning.

title: Machine Learning Model Using Clinical and Contrast-Enhanced MRI Features Differentiates Cerebral Tuberculoma from Lung Cancer Brain Metastasis.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES Cerebral tuberculomas (CTB) and lung cancer brain metastases (BM) frequently show overlapping appearances on conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) but require entirely different treatment strategies. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model integrating clinical and contrast-enhanced MRI features to noninvasively differentiate these two entities. MATERIALS AND METHODS The internal dataset (n = 188, 122 CTB, 66 BM) was split into training/validation (n = 131) and internal test (n = 57) sets. Feature selection (univariate and stepwise logistic regression) was performed only on the training and validation set, yielding four predictors. Machine learning classifiers were trained using these predictors with repeated 5-fold cross-validation. An external test set (n = 51, 26 CTB, 25 BM) from another hospital was used for independent validation. RESULTS Multivariate logistic regression retained four independent predictors: age (OR = 1.046, 95%CI: 1.003-1.091, p = 0.036), carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) (odds ratios [OR] = 1.711, 95%confidence intervals [CI]: 1.235-2.370, p = 0.001), multiple lesions (OR = 0.080, 95%CI: 0.015-0.438, p = 0.004), and ring with mural nodule (OR = 11.289, 95%CI: 2.551-49.952, p = 0.001). The Gradient Boosting model built on these four features achieved the best performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.970 (95%CI: 0.925-0.998) on the internal test set and 0.957 (95%CI: 0.900-0.995) on the external test set. On the external test set, the model showed a sensitivity of 88.0% and a specificity of 92.3%. CONCLUSION A Gradient Boosting model integrating age, CEA, multiple lesions, and ring with mural nodule effectively distinguishes CTB from BM with robust external test performance, providing a noninvasive tool to assist clinical decision-making.

Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
abstract: Accurate estimation of diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) is critical for optimising photovoltaic system performance and energy forecasting yet remains challenging in regions lacking comprehensive ground-based instrumentation. Recent advancements using Vision Transformers (ViTs) trained on extensive sky image datasets have shown promise in replacing costly irradiance measurement equipment, but the scarcity of long-term, high-quality sky imagery significantly restricts practical implementation. Addressing this critical gap, this study proposes a novel dual-framework approach designed for data-scarce scenarios. First, calculated atmospheric parameters, including extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time encodings, are integrated to represent sky conditions without utilising any instrumentation. Next, a sequential pipeline initially predicts synthetic global horizontal irradiance (GHI) and uses it as a feature, to refine DHI estimation. Finally, a dual-parallel architecture simultaneously processes raw and overlay-enhanced fisheye sky images. Overlays are generated through unsupervised, physics-informed cloud segmentation to highlight dynamic sky features. Empirical validation is performed using data from the Chilbolton Observatory, chosen for its temperate climate and frequent cloud variability. To simulate data-scarce conditions, models are trained on a single month (e.g., January) and evaluated across a temporally disjoint, full-year test set. Under this setup, the sequential and dual-parallel frameworks achieve RMSE values within 2-3 W/m^2 and 1-6 W/m^2, respectively, of a state-of-the-art ViT trained on the complete dataset. By combining physics-informed modelling with unsupervised segmentation, the proposed method provides a scalable and cost-effective solution for DHI estimation, advancing solar resource assessment in data-constrained environments.

title: One-shot federated unsupervised domain adaptation with Smoothed Knowledge Distillation and teacher refinement
abstract: Federated unsupervised domain adaptation (FUDA) addresses the challenge of adapting models to an unlabeled target domain using decentralized source domains while preserving data privacy. However, existing FUDA methods typically require multiple communication rounds, rely on complex aggregation strategies, and often struggle with noisy pseudo labels and inconsistent source knowledge. To address these challenges, we propose SKD-ETR, a novel one-shot FUDA framework that combines Smoothed Knowledge Distillation (SKD) and Exponential moving average-based Teacher Refinement (ETR). SKD trains a student model on the target domain using smoothed soft pseudo labels generated by the ensemble of source models. This reduces overconfidence, mitigates noise, and improves robustness. ETR further refines each source model by interpolating its parameters toward the student via exponential moving average (EMA), thereby transferring target-domain knowledge back to the teachers. This bidirectional refinement enhances pseudo-label quality and student generalization without additional communication overhead. SKD-ETR eliminates complex aggregation by initializing the student model randomly and performing a single-round distillation process. Extensive experiments on OfficeHome, Office-Caltech, and DomainNet demonstrate that SKD-ETR achieves competitive performance while being communication- and computation-efficient, and robust under noisy supervision. The code for this paper is available at https://github.com/A-Abedi/SKD_ETR.

title: Humanity in the loop: Reframing artificial intelligence and the global medical imaging divide.
abstract: OBJECTIVES Access to radiology and nuclear medicine remains profoundly unequal across global health systems. Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face persistent shortages in imaging equipment, specialist workforce, digital infrastructure, maintenance, regulation and sustainable financing. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly positioned as a mechanism to improve imaging access, but it may also reinforce existing inequities. This narrative review examines the potential for discriminative, generative and agentic AI to reduce or widen inequities in LMIC medical imaging and proposes a sociotechnical governance framework based on the concept of Humanity-in-the-Loop. KEY FINDINGS Discriminative AI may improve image interpretation, triage, segmentation, quantification and image-quality assessment; generative AI may enhance reporting, education, translation, communication, synthetic data generation and research workflows; and agentic AI may coordinate referrals, scheduling, follow-up, supply logistics and imaging pathways. They may also exacerbate inequity through data colonialism, algorithmic under-performance, dataset shift, infrastructure dependence, commercial lock-in, second-tier automation, liability transfer and unequal participation in AI research and development. CONCLUSION Human-in-the-loop governance is insufficient for equitable AI implementation in LMIC medical imaging because the assumptions underpinning effective human oversight are often absent in resource-constrained settings. The proposed Humanity-in-the-Loop sociotechnical framework embeds equity, local agency, contextual validity and public benefit throughout the AI lifecycle. The framework comprises six interconnected domains: patient humanity, workforce humanity, community humanity, data humanity, system humanity and global humanity. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE Responsible implementation of AI in medical imaging requires governance frameworks that extend beyond algorithm performance to include workforce development, data sovereignty, infrastructure, community priorities, equitable partnerships and sustainable capacity building. Adoption of a Humanity-in-the-Loop approach may help ensure that AI narrows rather than widens the medical imaging divide between high-income countries and LMICs.

title: Synthetic activation of gibberellin signalling reveals spatial coordination of root growth.
Conflict with industrial fleets undermines the contributions of small-scale fisheries to sustainable development in vulnerable regions
abstract: Equitable and sustainable governance of small-scale fisheries (SSFs) is essential for achieving food security and conservation in coastal areas. Yet in increasingly industrialized oceans, competition and conflict with large-scale fisheries (LSFs) threaten the contributions of SSFs to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Here we have developed a small-scale and industrial fisheries interaction index and applied it to 126 countries using 2 recent global datasets. Vulnerability to conflict is highest in countries where SSFs are vital for nutrition, but governance is weak, especially in Africa, Oceania and Asia. We also identify low-exposure outlier countries with unexpectedly low risk of SSF–LSF interactions, providing insights for proactive policy. Preferential access areas granting spatial rights to SSFs are common in both low- and high-vulnerability countries, suggesting such policies are often reactive and may be insufficient alone without strong enforcement. As ocean industries expand, it will be necessary to strengthen SSF access rights and limit LSF overcapacity to reduce conflict and advance sustainable development. Small-scale fisheries are vulnerable to conflict with industrial fishing. The small-scale and industrial fisheries interaction index reveals regions with weak governance and emphasizes the need for enhanced access rights and management strategies.

title: The global potential of aquavoltaics for power generation and offsetting the carbon footprint of freshwater aquaculture
abstract: Global inland freshwater aquaculture has rapidly expanded, intensifying greenhouse gas emissions and sustainability challenges. Here we estimate whether aquavoltaics, integrating photovoltaics with aquaculture, could offer multifunctional benefits. We integrate satellite observation products with realistic climate-driven photovoltaic system simulations to map the global expansion patterns and installation potential of aquavoltaics. Global aquavoltaics area covered 423 km2 in 2023, with China accounting for the overwhelming majority (97%). We estimate that deploying photovoltaics with a 40% coverage rate across over 50,000 km2 of landside clustering of aquaculture ponds globally could yield an electricity generation potential of 4,143 ± 145 TWh yr-1. Aquavoltaics deployment could support energy self-sufficiency in 878 cities and offset the freshwater aquaculture carbon footprint in 61 countries through grid-level avoided emissions. These findings highlight aquavoltaics as a scalable pathway within the energy-food-climate nexus to support sustainable aquaculture and low-carbon energy futures alongside aquatic food production.

Long-term effects of crop rotation and nitrogen management on nitrous oxide emissions in agricultural systems: a narrative review
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas with a global warming potential 265 to 298 times that of carbon dioxide over a century, and the principal anthropogenic stratospheric ozone-depleting substance now emitted to the atmosphere. Agricultural soils account for roughly 60% of anthropogenic emissions, so cropping sequence and nitrogen inputs directly shape emission rates. Drawing on 18 long-term field studies spanning 5 to 45 years and twelve countries, this review examines how crop rotation, tillage, organic and synthetic nitrogen fertilisation, and their interactions with soil and climate govern N2O across multi-decadal timescales. Management effects are rarely consistent across sites: no-till reduces emissions in well-drained temperate soils but raises them in waterlogged fine-textured soils, and organic fertilisers lower emissions when mineralisation matches crop uptake but raise them when labile carbon and nitrogen accumulate together. Mean N2O rises with temperature across studies, implying that warming will amplify emissions most in under-monitored tropical regions. The review identifies geographic gaps, inconsistent flux protocols, and weak integration of microbial ecology and process modelling as the main barriers to transferable guidance. Its contribution is a mechanistically grounded, management-organised synthesis that moves beyond aggregate effect sizes and proposes a research agenda for climate-smart nitrogen governance. This review is timely: as reactive-nitrogen use and global warming intensify together, and with N2O now the principal anthropogenic ozone-depleting substance emitted, it offers researchers, greenhouse-gas-inventory compilers and policymakers a transferable, mechanistically grounded basis for emission-reduction guidance across the diverse soils and climates where food is produced.

title: Probabilistic Response of Prestressed Concrete Box Girder Bridges under Stochastic Temperature–Humidity Environmental Conditions
abstract: To investigate the evolution of mechanical behavior in concrete box girder bridges during cantilever construction under the coupled influence of stochastic environmental temperature and humidity, a novel simulation method is proposed. This method integrates a temperature–humidity coupling analysis method for the internal fields of concrete and a constitutive model that accounts for multifactor interactions, including temperature-induced stress, drying shrinkage, creep, and the sensitivity of elastic modulus. The proposed method was applied to simulate and analyze the construction process of the Yuanhe Bridge in Jiangxi Province, China. Based on the statistical analysis of nearly two decades of daily historical meteorological data from the region, it was verified through fitting tests and statistical assessments that the probability distributions of temperature, humidity, and wind speed conform to Gaussian (normal) distributions. The results systematically reveal the statistical influences of stochastic environmental factors on the bridge’s camber, shear-lag effect, and prestress loss. The results indicate that the maximum camber and the shear-lag coefficient at the bottom slab–web junction exhibit slightly asymmetric distributions and can be well described by Bigaussian fitting curves, whereas the shear-lag coefficient at the top slab–web junction follows a Gaussian distribution. Increases in the daily temperature range and decreases in relative humidity are found to amplify the camber and the prestress loss. No discernible influence of wind speed on the camber, shear-lag effect, or prestress loss is observed. This study provides a crucial theoretical foundation and technical support for the refined control and optimization of cantilever construction of bridges under stochastic environmental conditions.

title: Transient ATM inhibition enhances knock-in efficiency in hematopoietic stem cells by attenuating the DNA damage response.
abstract: Precise genome editing in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) holds great potential for treating inherited blood disorders; however, low knock-in (KI) efficiency and loss of functional HSCs after genome editing remain major obstacles. Here, we demonstrate that transient inhibition of Ataxia-Telangiectasia Mutated (ATM) kinase markedly enhanced KI efficiency in mouse HSCs genome-edited with Cas9/ribonucleoprotein (RNP) and AAV donor DNA. Phosphoproteomic and capillary western blot analyses revealed that ATM inhibition suppressed aberrant Cas9-AAV-induced ATM activation and the subsequent DNA damage response, reduced p53-dependent apoptosis, and enhanced survival of KI HSCs. In serial transplantation assays, ATM inhibition preserved long-term engrafting KI HSCs, increasing their frequency from ~0.3 to 40% in secondary recipients, an over 100-fold improvement. Furthermore, in an X-linked severe combined immunodeficient mouse model, ATM inhibition increased KI efficiency and restored T- and B cell differentiation. Comprehensive safety analyses, including long-read nanopore sequencing, amplicon deep sequencing, whole genome sequencing and clonal tracking, did not detect increased genomic alterations, chromosomal abnormalities, or clonal expansion following transient ATM inhibition. Taken together, these findings establish transient ATM inhibition as an effective strategy to enhance KI-mediated genome editing while maintaining the long-term repopulating capacity of HSCs.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: The impact of racist events on post-trauma mental health symptoms among immigrants and refugees in Canada: the role of racial trauma.
abstract: Background: Immigrants and refugees are at greater risk of mental health symptoms, including elevated symptoms of depression, anxiety, and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). For racialized immigrants and refugees, frequent exposure to racist events is one of several predictors of mental health outcomes. According to race-based traumatic stress theory, repeated exposure to racist events can undermine safety, belonging, and dignity, and may lead to racial trauma, referring to the psychological and physiological stress responses arising from such experiences. However, it remains unknown whether racial trauma plays a mediating role in the relationship between racist events and mental health symptoms. To address this gap, the present study aimed to examine racial trauma as a mediator of this relationship among racialized immigrants and refugees in Canada.Methods: A sample of 182 immigrants and refugees in Canada (Mage = 30.76; 52.2% men; 52.7% of African descent) completed self-report measures. The mediating role of racial trauma in the relationship between racist events and mental health symptoms (PTSD, depression, anxiety) was examined using PROCESS Model 4.Results: Results indicated that racial trauma significantly explained the relationship between racist events and mental health outcomes, including PTSD (B = 0.35, CI [0.20, 0.56]), depression (B = 0.11, CI [0.06, 0.18]), and anxiety (B = 0.12, CI [0.08, 0.17]). The model accounted for 34.02% to 46.21% of the variances in mental health outcomes.Conclusions: Among racialized immigrants and refugees, greater exposure to racist events was associated with elevated racial trauma, which contributed to higher PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms. Clinicians, community organizations, and policymakers should integrate anti-racism strategies and racial trauma frameworks to support the mental health of immigrants and refugees.

title: Simulation of annual productivity and water dynamics of winter wheat-summer maize production system
abstract: This study focuses on the winter wheat–summer maize double-cropping system and aims to develop an annual process model that can accurately simulate crop growth and development along with soil moisture dynamics. Based on the field split-plot experimental data that combined different varieties with sowing date treatments, a wheat-maize double-cropping production system model was built, incorporating modules for crop development stages, leaf area dynamics, biomass accumulation and partitioning, yield formation, and soil moisture balance. The model parameters were calibrated using 2008–2009 data, and validated with independent 2009–2010 data, and model performance in key physiological and ecological processes and in yield formation is systematically evaluated by using root mean square error (RMSE) and normalized root mean square error (NRMSE). Validation results show: 1) excellent simulation of crop phenology, with NRMSE for development stages at 1.87% for winter wheat and 5.36% for summer maize; 2) the model capture of leaf area index dynamics, with NRMSE of 27.52% for winter wheat and 11.96% for summer maize; 3) aboveground biomass accumulation was simulated with NRMSE of 16.02% for winter wheat and 15.50% for summer maize; 4) yield simulation achieved NRMSE of 5.78% for winter wheat and 17.80% for summer maize; 5) soil water storage in the 0–60 cm soil layer was simulated with good accuracy (NRMSE = 15.13%). Under the specific site conditions and the tested genotype-by-sowing-date combinations, the model demonstrated reasonable capability in simulating key processes of the winter wheat–summer maize production system.

title: Reproduction in Ferns: Gametophyte Development, Sex Determination, Gametogenesis, and Embryogenesis
abstract: Sexual reproduction in land plants has diversified over more than 500 million years of evolution. Ferns occupy a key phylogenetic position among land plants because they possess a dominant sporophyte, as in seed plants, while retaining a free-living gametophyte that produces gametes through mitotic divisions, as in bryophytes. This combination of life cycle features provides a useful framework for understanding how reproductive and developmental programs have evolved across land plants. In this review, we summarize current knowledge of fern reproduction, with particular emphasis on the model fern Ceratopteris richardii and the related species C. thalictroides. We focus on four interconnected processes: (1) gametophyte development and the meristem, which functions as a signaling center required for prothallus formation and gametangium positioning; (2) sex determination by antheridiogen, including classical genetic models, hormonal regulation, and recent studies linking meristem identity to sexual fate; (3) gametangium development and gametogenesis, covering antheridium and archegonium formation as well as the differentiation of motile sperm and egg cells; and (4) fertilization and embryogenesis, including gamete interaction, zygotic polarity, and embryonic axis formation. Recent advances in genome sequencing, transformation, genome editing, live imaging, and transcriptomic analyses are beginning to connect the rich morphological literature on ferns with molecular mechanisms. These advances make Ceratopteris a key comparative system for uncovering how reproductive structures, stem cell functions, and embryogenic programs have been conserved, modified, and redeployed during land plant evolution.

title: Post-Hoc Feature Selection Layer for Neural Networks Interpretability
abstract: The interpretability of complex neural networks remains a critical challenge, especially for models already deployed in high-stakes domains. To address this, we adapted the Feature Selection Layer (FSL) to optimize feature weights post-training, a variant we term post-hoc FSL. Our approach reframes the FSL as a lightweight, trainable module that integrates with already frozen pre-trained models on tabular datasets to highlight the features the original model considers most important. This post-hoc FSL learns feature relevance by fine-tuning its weights based on the original model's learned outputs. Crucially, this process is non-invasive, operating without altering the original model's architecture or its learned parameters. We conducted our experiments using both statistical and visual metrics, including accuracy, F1 score, recall, precision, weighted t-SNE and silhouette score, and also analyzed the stability of the post-hoc FSL on high-dimensional synthetic and real-world tabular datasets. We compared the post-hoc FSL feature weighting method using these metrics against the original embedded FSL and other post-hoc interpretability methods, such as Integrated Gradients, Noise Tunnel, DeepLIFT, Gradient SHAP, and Feature Ablation. Experimental results demonstrate that the post-hoc FSL feature weighting method successfully identified relevant features across the different datasets, maintaining the predictive power of the original neural network while enhancing its interpretability.

title: Data-Driven Vision-Language Models for Remote Sensing: A Survey
abstract: During the deep learning era, innovations in remote sensing (RS) vision models primarily focused on optimizing network architectures for specific tasks and conducting end-to-end training. However, with the advent of the Vision-Language Models (VLMs) era, constrained by substantial computational resource demands, the mainstream research paradigm has shifted towards adapting general-purpose VLMs using RS vertical domain data for fine-tuning, rather than modifying their core architectures. This transition marks a change in the innovation pathway from model-centric to data-centric. Despite the increasing importance of data, the academic community still lacks a systematic, data-centric survey to guide researchers in constructing high-quality RS vision-language datasets for various application scenarios and in conducting effective model fine-tuning and performance evaluation based on these datasets. To address this gap, this paper presents a systematic review of the development status of RS datasets tailored for VLMs. It further provides a comprehensive practical guide for RS researchers in the large model era, covering the entire pipeline from data construction to fine-tuning and evaluation. This paper aims to encourage the academic community to build more diverse and higher-quality vision-language datasets for specialized RS sub-fields. Ultimately, the goal is to converge these efforts into a comprehensive RS vision-language corpus that offers extensive task coverage and a wide geographical distribution, thereby laying a solid data foundation for advancing towards general artificial intelligence in RS.

title: Hydromorphological Restoration of Streams Does Not Ensure the Recovery of Ecosystem Functioning
abstract: Ecological restoration is widely expected to recover multiple ecosystem attributes, yet biological structure and ecosystem functioning may respond differently to hydromorphological restoration. Interpreting functional change is further complicated because higher or lower process rates do not inherently indicate recovery; their ecological meaning depends on how degraded and restored conditions compare with an appropriate reference state. We synthesised 582 effect sizes from 66 studies to quantify responses of nine ecosystem functions to hydromorphological restoration of streams and to assess whether changes in biological structure coincided with functional responses. Ecosystem‐function responses varied substantially among processes and baselines. Gross primary production was significantly higher in degraded than in reference streams, illustrating that elevated functional rates do not necessarily indicate reference‐like ecological conditions. Restoration did not consistently reverse degradation‐associated functional differences: denitrification was significantly lower in restored than in degraded streams, whereas nitrate uptake remained significantly lower in restored than in reference streams. Other restored–reference differences were generally weak or uncertain. Functional responses did not differ systematically among broad restoration‐measure categories. Restoration age was associated with changes in gross primary production and denitrification relative to degraded conditions, but none of the functions showed detectable convergence towards or divergence from reference conditions through time. In studies measuring both biological structure and ecosystem functioning, biological responses to restoration were generally positive relative to degraded conditions, whereas functional responses were more variable. However, the available evidence was too uncertain to conclude that biological and functional responses systematically differed. Our synthesis shows that functional recovery cannot be inferred either from restoration‐associated change alone or from concurrent biological recovery. Assessing restoration success therefore requires direct measurements of ecosystem processes and ecologically meaningful reference conditions that reveal whether functional change represents movement towards a process‐specific restoration target.

title: Non‐Linear Increases of Soil Carbon Stocks and Turnover Along Alpine Greening Gradients on Different Bedrocks
abstract: Alpine ecosystems are experiencing warming, leading to alpine greening—an upward migration and enhanced productivity of vegetation. Although soils represent the largest carbon (C) stocks in these ecosystems, impacts of greening on soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics remain unknown, especially in the high alpine zone. We measured SOC stocks, quality and radiocarbon ( 14 C) based turnover rates along elevation gradients from (sub)alpine forests to periglacial zones on three bedrock types, representing trajectories of changes in climate and vegetation and weathering regime. Data were linked to SOC stabilizing pedogenic oxides (PO) to assess the potential of soils to sequester C upon alpine greening. Results show pronounced decreases in SOC stocks (from 10 to 1 kg C m −2 ) and increases in 14 C‐based turnover times (from decades to millennia) with increasing elevation. This pattern followed a non‐linear sigmoidal function with a threshold at the vegetation line where grassland transitions to the nival zone. High alpine soils showed low SOC:PO ratios, indicating low C saturation and a high capacity to stabilize SOC on reactive minerals. However, negligible 14 C‐derived carbon inputs suggest that low vegetation productivity constrains SOC sequestration in these soils. In contrast, towards lower elevation with a warmer climate, grassland soils receive higher C inputs, but appear more C saturated, leading to greater SOC turnover but little SOC stock changes. Bedrock influenced SOC dynamics with approximately 50% smaller SOC stocks and faster turnover rates in dolomitic than in siliceous soils, due to slower weathering and lower SOC stabilization. Using elevation as a space‐for‐time substitution, we infer that SOC sequestration under alpine greening will be confined to areas around the vegetation line, with parent material influencing the magnitude of C uptake. Future projections of SOC dynamics should account for vegetation shifts and bedrock‐driven stabilization to constrain the role of alpine soils in land carbon‐climate feedbacks.
