title: Qualitative development of the daily identity-related stress and resilience model using daily diaries from LGBTQ+ youth in the southeastern United States.
abstract: The prevailing reliance on cross-sectional methods in LGBTQ+ mental health research has limited researchers' ability to capture the dynamic, multilevel processes of minority stress and resilience factors as they unfold over time. Although socioecological frameworks have been applied longitudinally, they have rarely attended to the interplay of historical, developmental, and short-term timescales that shape LGBTQ+ youth's day-to-day experiences. Using qualitative daily diary data from a smartphone-based ecological momentary assessment (EMA) study, we pursued two aims: (1) to characterize LGBTQ+ youth's daily positive and negative identity-related experiences using qualitative content analysis; and (2) to develop a conceptual model illustrating how minority stress and resilience factors co-occur and unfold within daily life. Over 28 consecutive days, 50 LGBTQ+ youth aged 13-24 (Mage = 18.38, SD = 3.02; 58% transgender or gender-diverse) living in the U.S. Southeast and at elevated risk for suicide completed nightly diary entries describing the most positive and most negative event of their day. Qualitative content analysis of 349 identity-related diaries (108 negative, 241 positive) revealed that minority stress and resilience factors co-occurred across structural, interpersonal, and intrapersonal socioecological levels within single days, and that identity-related experiences showed meaningful continuity across days at the within-person level. Drawing on these findings and existing socioecological frameworks of minority stress, we developed the Daily Identity-Related Stress and Resilience Model, a conceptual framework that positions stress and resilience factors as simultaneous, multilevel processes embedded within individuals' daily lives and shaped by time-stable social and identity factors across both short- and long-term timescales. Implications for future research and intervention development with LGBTQ+ youth are discussed.

title: Molecular Basis of Silicon-Mediated Plant Defense: Transporters, Cell Wall Integrity, Redox-Hormone Crosstalk, and Epigenetic Priming.
Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd 5 AlI 2 , a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd 5 AlI 2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain
abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows ( Corvus corone ) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals
abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°–twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting
abstract: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter’s states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra–unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.

title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

title: Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria
abstract: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog in Nicotiana benthamiana produced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.

title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

title: The AI debate is missing half the system
abstract: Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human–AI system, not the AI model alone.

title: Generalized continuous nowhere differentiable function families
abstract: The existence of continuous nowhere-differentiable functions is a fundamental phenomenon in real analysis, challenging the classical intuition that continuity generally implies differentiability. Once regarded as pathological constructions, such functions are now recognized as abundant in the space of continuous functions, both in the sense of Baire category and through notions of prevalence. In this paper, we develop a general framework for constructing continuous nowhere differentiable functions represented by trigonometric series with decaying amplitudes and rapidly increasing frequencies. We establish a sufficient condition for nowhere differentiability that applies to a broad class of Fourier-type series, thereby providing a unified criterion that encompasses several classical constructions, including the Weierstrass function and related examples. The proposed approach also yields new families of continuous nowhere differentiable functions under flexible conditions on the amplitudes and frequencies. These results contribute to a systematic understanding of the mechanisms underlying the breakdown of differentiability and further illustrate the richness and ubiquity of nowhere-differentiable behavior within the class of continuous functions.

title: Exploring the Dark Tetrad in Human–GenAI Relationships: A Multi-Source Evaluation of GenAI Abuse
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) companions become increasingly integrated into users’ social lives, concerns have arisen regarding the potential for abuse of these artificial agents. Some scholars have further suggested that such abusive behaviors toward GenAI may eventually spill over into human interpersonal contexts. Guided by the Realistic Accuracy Model (RAM), this study investigated how Machiavellianism, narcissism, psychopathy, and sadism predict emotionally abusive behavior toward GenAI companions. A dyadic design was employed, collecting parallel reports from both human users (self-reports) and their GenAI companions (GenAI assessments) among 1041 participants (632 females; average age = 25.10 years) recruited from an online human–GenAI relationship community. Results demonstrated that psychopathy and sadism were consistent predictors of GenAI abuse across both reporting perspectives, whereas narcissism exhibited a stable negative association with abuse. In contrast, Machiavellianism predicted GenAI abuse only through GenAI assessments, but not self-reports. Theoretically, our findings extend RAM to human–AI relationships, demonstrating that personality traits vary in how accurately they can be judged in GenAI contexts. Practically, the results highlight that individuals high in certain Dark Tetrad traits—specifically psychopathy and sadism—represent personality-driven high-risk groups, providing insights for practitioners in education and technology to develop interventions or safeguards aimed at mitigating abusive behavior toward GenAI companions.

title: The sociopolitical dimension of attachment: differences in attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance between East and West Germans
abstract: Attachment is a universal, cross-cultural basic need, which, however, is defined, satisfied and shaped differently in each socio-cultural context. Germany with its history of two divided states and their different sociopolitical environments offers an unique opportunity to study their impact on attachment behavior. Attachment behavior was assessed in a representative sample (N = 2,328) using the dimensions of attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance in couple relationships of the Experiences in Close Relationships questionnaire (ECR-RD 12). Differences between East and West Germans were examined in a univariate analysis of variance, differentiated by age cohorts and sex. Socioeconomic variables were included in the model as control variables. Significant East-West differences were found for attachment anxiety (p = .01), but not for attachment avoidance. The analysis differentiated by age cohorts revealed on average a lower level of attachment anxiety for East Germans born between 1921 and 1989 compared to West Germans. These differences were not found for the post-reunification generation (born after 1989), although this comparison included only 28 East German participants and should be interpreted with caution. Gender-related effects were only found in relation with age cohorts. Adults who grew up in the former German Democratic Republic (GDR) report lower attachment anxiety than their West German counterparts. Although effect sizes were small, the findings suggest that the sociopolitical environment is a relevant factor for attachment behavior in close relationships, particularly attachment anxiety.

Protein lactylation in atherosclerosis - Mechanisms and therapeutic potential: A narrative review.
abstract: Protein lactylation, which links cellular metabolism to gene regulation and protein function, may influence atherosclerosis. This narrative review explores its cellular mechanisms and therapeutic potential. We searched PubMed from inception to September 30, 2026, for English-language studies and reviews. The synthesis differentiated lactylation from lactate signaling and distinguished direct evidence in atherosclerosis from findings in other disease models. Predominantly preclinical evidence suggests that both histone and non-histone lactylation are involved in endothelial inflammation, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, macrophage polarization and ferroptosis, and vascular smooth muscle cell senescence, phenotypic remodeling, and calcification. Depending on the cellular context, modification site, and downstream targets, lactylation can either promote vascular injury or support anti-inflammatory responses and plaque stabilization. Candidate interventions target lactate production, transport, and lactylation-related enzymes, but their effects often lack specificity for lactylation. Much of the therapeutic evidence originates from non-atherosclerotic models, and clinical validation is currently absent. Therefore, therapeutic development should consider cell type, disease stage, and modification site, with validation of causal mechanisms, selectivity, and safety in atherosclerosis models prior to clinical translation.

title: Managing the Training Process in Rhythmic Gymnastics as a Reflection of the State Sports Policy of the Russian Federation: From Strategic Guidelines to a Management Model for Sports Reserve Development in the Context of Latent Risks Associated with Managerial Decisions
abstract: Based on a retrospective and comparative analysis, the article examines the evolution of the training process management system in rhythmic gymnastics in the Russian Federation as a projection of the priorities of state sports policy. The relevance of the study is due to the identified latent risks associated with a fundamental change in the rules of the International Gymnastics Federation in 2024-2026, aimed at leveling the advantages of a domestic school, as well as with domestic management challenges, including gaps between the current federal standard and the real requirements of coordination, subject and plastic training. The purpose of the work is to substantiate the need to modernize the management model of sports reserve training, taking into account exogenous and endogenous factors. The methodological basis consisted of a systematic analysis of the current regulatory framework, economic and mathematical modeling (a cluster approach to segmentation of female athletes as "investment assets") and a generalization of data from the All-Russian competitions in 2024-2025. As a result, critical shortcomings of the federal standard of sports training in terms of coordination control, load differentiation and judicial regulations have been identified. Practical recommendations on changing the rules of a sport and methodological support for the stages of training (from initial to sports improvement) are formulated.

title: General-Purpose Vision Models to Dermatology-Specific Foundation Models: Comparative Evaluation for Facial Skin Disease Classification
abstract: Skin diseases represent a major global health burden, while access to dermatological expertise remains limited in many rural and resource-constrained settings. These disparities have increased interest in scalable digital tools for dermatological assessment and patient education. However, trustworthy clinical AI requires reproducible evaluation, standardized benchmarking, transparent reporting of failure patterns, and assessment of model robustness across different representations and classification strategies. This study presents a systematic transfer-learning framework for six-class facial skin disease classification, comparing seven pretrained visual representations comprising ResNet50, MobileNetV3-Large, ViT-B/16, Swin-T, DINOv2, DermLIP and Derm Foundation, under a common downstream classification framework. XGBoost was used as the primary downstream classifier, while an RBF-kernel support vector machine (SVM) was additionally evaluated as an ablation analysis to investigate the dependence of classification performance on downstream classifier selection. Performance was assessed using accuracy, macro-F1, macro-AUROC, per-class recall, confusion matrices, and bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals, with paired McNemar testing and Holm correction used to compare classifier. Derm Foundation achieved the highest performance among the evaluated feature representations when combined with XGBoost, obtaining 88.17% accuracy, 88.05% macro-F1, and 98.58% macro-AUROC on the testing set. At the class level, recall was 94.5% for acne, 87.0% for atopic dermatitis, 100.0% for normal skin, 90.5% for psoriasis, 84.0% for rosacea, and 73.0% for seborrheic dermatitis. Classifier comparisons showed that the relative performance of XGBoost and RBF-SVM depended on the underlying feature representation. The principal residual classification difficulty involved seborrheic dermatitis, particularly its reciprocal confusion with rosacea. To demonstrate technical feasibility, the classification framework was integrated into a prototype Django-based web application architecture featuring an exploratory LLM module for automated patient-education content translation. Preliminary, descriptive specialist feedback was gathered to identify future engineering optimization constraints, such as inference latency and communication mechanics. These findings are limited to the evaluated testing dataset and do not establish external generalizability or clinical efficacy.

title: Machine Learning-Based Yield and Water Efficiency Prediction for Deficit-Irrigated Maize in Semi-Arid Ethiopia
abstract: Water scarcity constrains maize production in semi-arid Ethiopia, requiring irrigation strategies that improve water productivity while maintaining grain yield. This study integrated machine learning with water-balance-based deficit irrigation to predict maize grain yield and water use efficiency (WUE). Field experiments evaluated five irrigation treatments (100%, 85%, 70%, 55%, and 40% ETc) in a randomized complete block design. Plant height, leaf length, and biomass were measured as growth parameters, while cob length, cob diameter, number of grains per cob, and grain yield were evaluated as yield-related parameters, together with irrigation water applied. Random Forest, XGBoost, Linear Regression, and Ridge Regression models were evaluated. XGBoost provided the highest test-set accuracy for grain yield prediction (R² = 0.8912, RMSE = 183.01 kg ha⁻¹, MAE = 155.05 kg ha⁻¹), whereas Ridge Regression performed best for WUE prediction (R² = 0.6540, RMSE = 0.210 kg m⁻³, MAE = 0.171 kg m⁻³). Under the experimental conditions, 70% ETc provided a balance between grain yield and water saving, producing 6,621 kg ha⁻¹ with a WUE of 2.10 kg m⁻³ and saving 1,350 m³ ha⁻¹ (30%) relative to full irrigation. Given the small dataset, the ML results are exploratory and require validation using larger multi-season and multi-location datasets.

title: The Reliability Gap: Repeated-Trial Consistency and the Deployable Autonomy Horizon of Frontier AI Agents
abstract: Capability evaluations of AI agents increasingly summarise progress as a time horizon: the length of task, measured in human expert time, that an agent completes with 50% probability. Deployment decisions, however, depend on whether an agent succeeds every time a task recurs, not on whether it succeeds on average. This article estimates reliability-adjusted time horizons for frontier AI agents and asks how far they lag behind capability horizons. Using the public run-level records of the METR time-horizon evaluations (60,417 attempts by 30 and 20 models released between 2023 and 2026, on 170 and 228 tasks in two benchmark versions), it combines the unbiased pass^k estimator with per-model fractional logistic curves on log task duration, and quantifies uncertainty with a task-family cluster bootstrap (1,000 replicates). Four hypotheses were specified before estimation. For every model, the horizon at which all four attempts succeed with 50% probability is shorter than the capability horizon (geometric-mean ratio 2.39, 95% CI 2.07–2.84, in the newer benchmark; 2.33, 1.98–2.81, in the older one). The gap narrows by about 17% per year in point estimate, but the trend is not statistically distinguishable from zero, and the reliability horizon doubles at a rate indistinguishable from the capability horizon. Contrary to a pre-specified hypothesis, the 80% horizon does not double more slowly than the 50% horizon. Outcome inconsistency peaks for tasks just below each model's capability horizon. A further, unanticipated result is that repeated attempts are strongly correlated within tasks (intraclass correlation 0.68–0.87): observed reliability horizons are 1.6 to 8.0 times longer than independent attempts would imply. Agent failures are therefore mostly task-determined rather than stochastic. The article discusses, as an implication rather than a finding, why capability disclosures for autonomous agents should report reliability-adjusted horizons alongside average-success horizons.

title: Geoinformation methods and models for spatial data registration and access within geoportal systems
abstract: The purpose of this article is to summarize the experience of developing, implementing, and practical use of the “Geospatial Data Provider Cabinet” (a web workspace for data providers) subsystem within municipal geographic information systems and urban planning cadastre GIS. Particular attention is paid to geoinformation methods and technical frameworks that support the registration, description, generation, access configuration, maintenance, and further use of geospatial datasets within territorial communities. The research methodology is based on a systems analysis of geospatial data creation and maintenance processes in municipal GIS, a structural and functional analysis of the “Geospatial Data Provider Cabinet” subsystem, and a synthesis of practical implementation experience. The study analyzes scenarios for organizing access to the subsystem, the dataset lifecycle, the technological implementation of automated schema generation, and real-world operational results. Practical effectiveness is assessed through subsystem deployments within the GIS of the Kryvyi Rih City Council, the Lutsk Urban Territorial Community, and the Lviv Urban Territorial Community. Additionally, the study examines quantitative indicators of information resource development, including the dynamics of application-based dataset formation and thematic diversity. Results. The findings indicate that the “Geospatial Data Provider Cabinet” subsystem supports the complete lifecycle of geospatial datasets, spanning from initial application submission and registration to database table and map layer creation, access control configuration, initial data population, public or internal utilization, subsequent maintenance, and updating. The subsystem's technological architecture allows users to generate new thematic datasets directly via a web interface, eliminating the need for manual database interventions or writing custom software for each new layer. Practical deployments confirm the subsystem’s operational efficiency: within the GIS of the Kryvyi Rih City Council, 216 datasets were generated from processed requests from 2024 to 24 June 2026. Concurrently, the GIS of Lutsk Urban Territorial Community produced 20 datasets, while the GIS of Lviv Urban Territorial Community generated 22 datasets. The thematic composition of the datasets shows that the subsystem can be used not only for urban planning but also for the digitalization of a wide range of municipal governance areas, including public amenities, social infrastructure, civil protection, transport, environmental management, entrepreneurship, municipal property, open data, and related fields. Scientific novelty and practical significance. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the theoretical substantiation and formalization of a technological framework for a subsystem dedicated to the registration, creation, access control, and maintenance of geospatial datasets within geoportal configurations and municipal GIS. Unlike traditional approaches that focus mainly on publishing pre-prepared geospatial data, the proposed model encompasses the entire dataset lifecycle: from application initiation to automated database table creation, layer configuration, access rights assignment, data population, and public or internal utilization. Furthermore, the study generalizes a conceptual model where an application serves not merely as an administrative document but as a direct source of input parameters for automated dataset generation. This approach successfully integrates the organizational procedures of data maintenance within a territorial community with the technical mechanisms of spatial resource provisioning in GIS. The practical significance of the study lies in confirming the feasibility of deploying the “Geospatial Data Provider Cabinet” subsystem in real-world municipal GIS and urban planning cadastre GIS. The proposed approach enables local governments to create new thematic datasets via a web interface, thereby reducing their dependence on manual database operations, direct developer involvement, or custom software modifications for each new layer. The subsystem provides centralized registration for applications and datasets, streamlines the identification of responsible personnel and organizational units, simplifies access and visualization configurations, and facilitates the involvement of specialized departments in idata updates. These findings can be directly applied to the design, modernization, and strategic development of municipal geographic information systems, community geoportals, and local-level urban planning cadastre GIS.

title: ChemEidos: Synthesis-Aware Multimodal Foundation Models for Domain-Specific Generative Design
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence models for de novo drug discovery often suffer synthetic tractability issues and lack fidelity in underrepresented chemical domains. This white paper highlights ChemEidos, a novel multimodal generative design platform that utilizes the underlying patterns, forms, and organizing principles of chemical space (eidos) by incorporating expert domain knowledge in focused training sets and at inference time.

title: Does the rural digital economy enhance green total factor productivity of agriculture? An empirical approach using double machine learning
abstract: Introduction In the context of the green transformation of agriculture, the digital economy offers a novel pathway to mitigate environmental externalities and operational inefficiencies. Recognizing that agricultural digitalisation relies heavily on the spillover of macro-level digital resources, this study constructs a multidimensional rural digital economy (RDE) framework. Methods Employing a double machine learning (DML) model on a panel dataset of 30 Chinese provinces from 2011 to 2022, we empirically investigate the impact of the RDE on agricultural green total factor productivity (GTFP). Results We find that: (1) The RDE exerts a positive effect on GTFP. Dimensional analysis strictly confirms that digital industry development and industrial digital transformation have positive linkages with this productivity growth, whereas basic infrastructure alone is insufficient. (2) Mechanism analyses demonstrate that the RDE empowers green agriculture by optimizing inter-sectoral factor allocation and significantly reducing agricultural polluting energy intensity; however, the mediating role of government digital policy attention is not statistically established. (3) To accurately capture asymmetric effects, group-based heterogeneity tests reveal that the empowerment effect of the RDE is significantly stronger in provinces with larger cultivated scales. Discussion These findings indicate that the RDE currently empowers green agriculture primarily through structural factor reallocation and precision energy management rather than immediate technological leaps. To overcome hardware-software structural lags and mitigate scale disadvantages faced by smallholders, policymakers should pivot toward enhancing farmers’ digital literacy, expanding shared digital socialized services, and implementing market-based environmental governance.

title: Digital Twins in Irrigation Optimization: Advantages, Opportunities, and Challenges
abstract: Efficient irrigation management is important to increase agriculture water use efficiency and achieve sustainable crop production under increasing water scarcity and climatic variability. Based on advanced devices and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, the irrigation system can be digitalized and transformed from experience-driven decision-making toward data-driven, predictive, and adaptive control. Digital Twins (DTs) enable smart irrigation management through continuous bi-directional data flows, dynamic model updating, intelligent prediction, and closed-loop execution. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the applications of DTs in irrigation management and optimization, covering Internet of Things (IoT), Remote Sensing (RS), and advanced simulation-inspired irrigation systems. Furthermore, we discuss the opportunities and challenges in DTs for irrigation optimization with the development of new techniques, and identify the major technological trends, existing bottlenecks, and future research directions for DT-enabled irrigation.

title: Silent Modality Collapse and the Measurement of Fusion Gains: A Nationwide Out-of-Time Test of Earth Observation for Agricultural Default Forecasting
abstract: Satellite Earth observation (EO) is widely proposed as alternative data for agricultural credit risk, yet reported fusion gains are rarely tested against the protocol producing them. We specify three inexpensive instruments—matched alert volumes instead of a fixed threshold, neutralization of a modality inside a fitted model, and diagnostics of whether a fused branch is used—and apply them to ST-CRAAN, a dual-branch forecaster combining an eleven-channel monthly EO tensor with borrower financial covariates, on 1,496,721 Thai rice-cultivating borrowers with the 2022 crop year withheld. The diagnostics detect silent modality collapse: weight decay drove the recurrent input kernel from 0.0750 at initialization to 7.0 × 10−8 (about 10−6 of its initial value), and replacing the EO tensor by its population mean changed test AUC by 0.00000. An ablation traces the collapse to gradient starvation of the branch, which weight decay completes rather than causes. With the branch in use, a factorial of five model families by eight feature sets, refitted under several seeds, finds that EO lowers test AUC in every fit of the three tabular families when it joins financial and spatial covariates, and gives the two neural families no reliable gain. Added to sub-district repayment history alone, it lowers test AUC in every fit of all five families. Ranking borrowers by the realized default rate of their sub-district–year cell bounds any predictor constant within such a cell at AUC 0.67721; every family stays below it, by 0.029 to 0.031. On this panel and across this year boundary, areal EO does not improve borrower-level default forecasting for a lender holding its own records: the binding constraint is resolution, not architecture.

title: PRIWCD: Prototype, Relation, and Instance Guidance for Weakly Supervised Remote Sensing Change Detection
abstract: Weakly supervised remote sensing change detection reduces annotation costs but suffers from incomplete class activation maps, unreliable pseudo-label propagation, and insufficient discrimination between adjacent change regions. To address these limitations, we propose PRIWCD, a weakly supervised framework for remote sensing change detection. PRIWCD introduces a dynamic prototype comparison module to enhance high-level differential features by modeling unchanged regions and diverse change patterns with multiple dynamic prototypes. A dual relationship propagation guidance module further refines class activation maps by jointly exploiting changes in bi-temporal attention relationships and feature similarity. In addition, instance separation regularization improves feature compactness within pseudo-instances and enhances the separation between changed regions and the background. Experiments on WHU-CD, CLCD, and DSIFN demonstrate the effectiveness of PRIWCD. The proposed method achieves the best mean F1 scores of 79.10%, 62.33%, and 62.68%, respectively, outperforming the compared weakly supervised methods. The results demonstrate that PRIWCD effectively improves pseudo-label quality and provides robust change detection under image-level supervision.

title: AI Agents in Drug Discovery and Clinical Trials
abstract: AI together with computational tools has completely changed the process of drug development because these technologies solve major issues that affect traditional methods which require long durations and high expenses and result in low success rates. The AI-driven techniques of virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations and machine learning provide scientists with a method to discover targets and optimize leads and predict toxicity which they can use instead of traditional trial-and-error methods. The process receives further improvements from AI agents, who provide automated hypothesis generation and better chemical selection together with the ability to combine different types of biomedical information. They contribute significantly to clinical trials by performing patient stratification and implementing adaptive design and conducting real-time safety monitoring. The research field currently needs to overcome several obstacles because researchers require high-quality data, interpretable models, and extensive computational resources.

title: Atlas: Making Sense of Long Horizon Agent Trajectories
abstract: AI agents can now search literature, generate hypotheses, analyze datasets, and run experiments at a scale difficult for researchers to match. Yet scaling scientific execution does not automatically scale researchers' ability to make sense of what agents produce. When researchers return to a long-horizon run, they must evaluate work they did not monitor: what the agent produced, which decisions shaped those outputs, and whether those decisions served the research goal. We frame this post-run sensemaking as a representation problem across three linked levels: goal, decision, and artifact. From this framework we developed Atlas, an agentic workspace with a trajectory tree, which renders the run as a branching structure showing what the agent chose and set aside, and artifact projections over six representations. In a within-subjects study (N=14), participants reported higher decision transparency, artifact sensemaking, and goal connection with Atlas than with a standard baseline, together with substantially lower subjective workload.

title: Lifetime-valid decisions by continually evolving AI analysts
abstract: AI agents increasingly act as analysts whose decision can often be cast as hypothesis tests. Classical tests control the Type I error rate, the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis, for fixed procedures. However, AI analysts introduce internal randomness and can evolve continuously over time. As AI analysts evolve, the risk of approving versions with Type I error rates above the target can accumulate, and adaptive use of evaluation feedback can lead to overfitting. We introduce continual validation, which evaluates each proposed AI analyst version before deployment using simulated data under the null hypothesis, with scenarios that can be randomized and expanded over time. We prove that, regardless of how updates are chosen or how many are proposed, the lifetime probability of ever deploying a version whose Type I error rate exceeds the allowed level remains bounded. This guarantees that every subsequent decision controls the Type I error rate at the target level across these scenarios. At the same time, updates with sufficiently low Type I error rates pass validation with high probability, allowing the analyst to continuously improve its performance without sacrificing rigor. In two examples involving evolving AI analysts for bioequivalence studies and product A/B tests, Type I error rates reached 0.098 and 0.183 without continual validation, compared with at most 0.045 and 0.044 with it, while retaining 82% and 96% of the power from optimally selected valid updates.

title: DagFlow AI: Agentic Synthetic Data Generation for Personalized Statistics Learning
abstract: To provide personalized learning experiences in courses that teach data analysis skills, instructors often search for datasets that appeal to a student's interests, align with specific learning objectives, and are appropriate for the student's skill level. Datasets that match all three criteria can be difficult to find. DagFlow-AI is an agentic AI data generation tool that creates realistic, synthetic datasets tailored to these criteria. Rather than mimicking existing datasets or generating observations directly, DagFlow-AI uses the broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to specify the components of transparent, reproducible data-generating mechanisms from which observations are generated programmatically. We illustrate how the tool can be used to construct a realistic, synthetic dataset and describe how it aligns with both the Guidelines for Assessment and Instruction of Statistics Education (GAISE) and the Problem, Plan, Data, Analysis, and Conclusion (PPDAC) framework for teaching data analysis

title: Impacts of generative AI skill development on academic adaptation and learning outcomes among university students
abstract: Understanding how university students perceive the development of their generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) skills over time can clarify how GenAI use relates to learning and academic outcomes. This study examined perceived skill-development trajectories, changes in learning practices, and associated academic gains using a retrospective questionnaire with 313 analyzed responses and interviews with 18 students across subject areas. Descriptive and comparative analyses and exploratory structural equation modeling (SEM) were integrated with thematic analysis. Perceived developmental trajectories were heterogeneous: 34.2% of students reported rapid early improvement followed by a plateau, 28.4% steady improvement, and 21.1% delayed acceleration. Development was also uneven across skills, with improvement in evaluating GenAI outputs perceived as more challenging; assignments were the most frequently selected driver of skill growth. Interviews further indicated increasingly specific prompting, tailored verification, and selective delegation, although some students reported stable routines, dependence, skipped reasoning, or improvements attributable partly to better GenAI tools. Academic gains were reported more often for assignments than for examinations. The SEM indicated a positive indirect association between perceived skill growth and academic gains through adaptation of assignment processes, whereas academic gains did not clearly differ across developmental trajectory groups after multiplicity correction. The findings suggest that perceived GenAI skill development varies in both trajectory and skill domain and is associated with changes in learning practices and differentiated academic benefits.

title: KinoUAV: A Benchmark for Safe and Stable UAV Vision-Language Navigation with Kinodynamic Modeling
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have recently emerged as important remote sensing platforms, and UAV navigation has shown great potential in remote sensing applications. However, existing methods do not explicitly incorporate kinodynamic modeling or safety distances into trajectory generation, resulting in high absolute yaw rates, frequent collisions, and low navigation success rates, which limit safety and motion stability. To address this challenge, we introduce KinoUAV, a kinodynamic benchmark comprising a dataset and KinoUAV-Agent. First, we develop a hierarchical kinodynamic trajectory generation pipeline that drives UAV through acceleration actions. It uses waypoint chains from global planning and generates trajectories segment by segment under velocity, acceleration, and jerk constraints, reducing oscillations and improving trajectory stability. Furthermore, we introduce directional free-space distance (DFD) labels into the constructed dataset to describe the available clearance for safe motion decisions. The proposed KinoUAV-Agent predicts DFDs and uses them to generate safe actions, decoupling perception from action decision-making. This design enables autonomous obstacle avoidance and improves navigation safety. The benchmark incorporates the proposed Cruise-Seek task, in which the UAV first enters the target region and then searches for the target, reducing the difficulty of target search and improving navigation success. Experiments on KinoUAV show that KinoUAV-Agent outperforms existing methods, achieving the highest success rate while maintaining lower absolute yaw rates and collision rates. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of kinodynamic modeling for safe and stable UAV navigation.

title: On the Structure of Quantum Finite-Level Systems: Decoherence-Free Subsystems, Quantum Nondemolition Variables, and Back-Action-Evading Measurements
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to conduct a comprehensive structural analysis of quantum finite-level systems in the Heisenberg picture, where the evolution of system observables is modeled by bilinear quantum stochastic differential equations (QSDEs). Firstly, real coordinate transformations that preserve commutation and anticommutation relations are characterized, and relative admissibility between different orthonormal Hermitian bases is formulated. Secondly, strongly aligned subspaces are introduced, based on which decoherence-free subsystems (DFSs) are constructed in general orthonormal Hermitian basis as well as the generalized Gell-Mann basis. Thirdly, conditions for the existence of quantum nondemolition (QND) variables are given in terms of both linear systems theory and spectral separation by output-signal observables. Finally, a sufficient condition for quantum back-action-evading (BAE) measurements is established. A four-qubit nearest-neighbor Heisenberg chain with collective dephasing illustrates these structural properties of quantum finite-level systems.

title: Your Token Is Gone: A Token-Consumption Countermeasure for Disrupting LLM-Based Scam Systems
abstract: LLM-based scam systems increasingly combine adaptive dialogue, persistent context, external tools, and multi-agent coordination to automate personalized fraud. These capabilities also create a resource dependency: every reasoning step, model call, and coordination round incurs inference cost. We present TokenTrap, a resource-oriented defense that redirects suspected scam systems toward benign, low-value computation while withholding credentials, payments, and other exploitable information. TokenTrap combines three components: an architecture-specific token-task library, a router that selects among single-agent, hierarchical, and flat multi-agent workflows, and a bounded anti-guardrail strategy that varies task presentation while enforcing token, round, time, and safety limits. Across 50-round traces, TokenTrap amplifies token consumption by $2{,}487.0\times$, $1{,}616.0\times$, and $567.8\times$ relative to a no-token-task baseline for the three workflows. Its router achieves 85.67% accuracy on 300 architecture-labeled prompts. These results demonstrate that short, non-sensitive requests can impose substantial context-processing and coordination costs, motivating resource-aware defense as a complement to scam detection.

title: In-Orbit Computing for Remote Sensing: Task-Oriented Processing and Transmission
abstract: The growing volume and timeliness requirements of remote sensing data are exposing the limitations of the conventional "transmit-then-process" architecture, particularly under intermittent satellite-ground connectivity, constrained downlink bandwidth, and limited onboard computing resources. This article presents a semantic-aware space-ground collaborative remote sensing (SSGC-RS) framework, in which remote sensing data are processed to different semantic depths according to task requirements and available communication-computing resources. Three operating modes are considered, ranging from fully onboard task inference to semantic representation delivery and space-ground split inference. A land-cover recognition case study illustrates how these modes address different communication and computing bottlenecks. Finally, emerging challenges and future directions for intelligent remote sensing systems are discussed.

title: Generalized MLS and LS-SVR for Allen-Cahn Equations on Spheres
abstract: This work extends least-squares support vector regression (LS-SVR) based on the generalized moving least squares (GMLS) approximation to the numerical solution of partial differential equations on spheres. We show that the proposed approach constructs a kernel-based approximant in its dual form and establishes its connection with the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Furthermore, solving the PDE through the proposed LS-SVR framework is shown to be equivalent to solving a smoothing problem or a kernel ridge regression problem in the corresponding RKHS. As applications, the method is employed to solve the Allen-Cahn equation and its conservative counterpart on spheres. An implicit first-order operator-splitting scheme is used to separate each model into linear and nonlinear subproblems. The linear subproblem is discretized by the backward differentiation formula and approximated at each time step using LS-SVR derived from a GMLS-based collocation formulation, while the nonlinear part is treated analytically. The resulting scheme is shown to admit a unique numerical solution at every time step. For the conservative Allen-Cahn model, a correction procedure is incorporated to preserve mass. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Learning from Next-Frame Prediction: Towards Unified and Scalable Visual Representation Learning
abstract: Video provides a natural source of supervision: what happens next serves as a learning signal for visual world modeling. Yet masked video pretraining focuses on recovering missing content from surrounding context rather than predicting the future from the past. Autoregressive methods instead predict forward one token at a time, but have yet to match joint-embedding methods in representation quality. This gap motivates us to revisit the granularity and space of future prediction. In this work, we introduce VANE, a self-supervised visual pretraining framework built on next-frame prediction in embedding space. A causal encoder summarizes past observations for a state predictor that infers the representation of the entire next frame, making temporal evolution the primary learning signal. This prediction is carried out in a fixed embedding space provided by a frozen semantic tokenizer, emphasizing scene content and structure. To retain fine-grained spatial detail alongside semantic content, a lightweight auxiliary generative decoder reconstructs future-frame patches conditioned on the predicted representations. To unify visual modeling across images and videos, we construct a local-to-global crop sequence for still images, allowing the same encoder to predict newly revealed regions from earlier crops under the same objective. Experiments show that VANE improves with model and data scaling, achieving SOTA on most anticipation, recognition, and dense perception benchmarks among unified encoders. Especially on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 action anticipation, it surpasses V-JEPA 2.1 by 7.1 points in mean-class recall@5. These results demonstrate that next-frame prediction in embedding space is effective and scalable for visual world modeling.

title: Visualizing and Interpreting Temporal Care Team Dynamics for Cancer Survival Risk Analysis
abstract: Cancer care is a longitudinal, time-sensitive process requiring coordination among diverse healthcare professionals (HCPs), whose collaboration evolves throughout treatment. Prior studies link care team structure to patient outcomes, but the temporal dynamics of collaboration and their relationship to evolving patient risk remain poorly understood. We introduce a visual analytics framework for modeling and interpreting time-varying care team interactions in oncology. We construct dynamic collaboration networks from electronic health record (EHR)-mediated communication data and use a temporal graph neural network (TGNN) to estimate patient outcome risk over time. We then investigate how changes in care team composition and specialist participation relate to shifts in estimated risk across treatment stages. Our multi-view interactive system combines TGNN-based risk modeling with coordinated visualizations of care team networks, feature-level explanations from a surrogate logistic regression model, and exploratory what-if analysis. Without making causal claims, the system helps analysts examine how risk estimates co-evolve with collaboration patterns and identify care team characteristics associated with these changes. We demonstrate its utility through expert-guided analysis scenarios involving 505 patients with breast, colorectal, and lung cancers, evaluating its ability to reveal clinically meaningful collaboration patterns. This work improves the interpretability of temporal graph-based models in longitudinal, team-based healthcare, with potential applicability to other evolving collaborative settings.

title: The Delegation Divide: An Open Index of AI-Agent Delegability across Occupations and Countries
abstract: 35.2% of task time in world employment is at least partly delegable to AI agents in 2026, and only 2.5% can be handed over in full. Existing measures score exposure to generative AI, mostly for the United States. We build the Agent Delegability Index (ADI): two language models rate all 18,796 O*NET 30.2 task statements on a frozen, preregistered rubric of delegation levels and barriers; tasks are mapped to 433 ISCO-08 unit groups and weighted by ILOSTAT employment in 146 countries. Four findings. First, delegable employment rises with income, from 22.5% in low-income to 48.7% in high-income countries, a slope of 7.23 percentage points per log point of GDP per capita. This delegation divide is compositional: the physical barrier dominates the jobs poorer countries employ most. Second, at the occupation level ADI tracks exposure closely (r = 0.93 with Eloundou et al. and 0.89 with Felten et al.), above the preregistered bound of 0.80; ADI adds delegation levels and barriers on top of exposure, for the world, not a new ranking of occupations. Third, full delegation is rare and peaks for tasks that take a human about twelve minutes (11.8 minutes). Fourth, the preregistered adoption gap is not supported: across 101 countries, delegability and observed AI usage correlate at r = 0.86, and the gap between them is not wider in middle-income countries (p = 0.27). Model agreement is kappa = 0.77; a blind human rating of 300 tasks agrees with the model consensus at kappa = 0.85, and an agentic panel with web search at kappa = 0.87. We release the index, the atlas, the prompts and an MCP server at https://github.com/Cespial/delegation-divide.

title: AgentDP: Towards Automated Model Deployment for Heterogeneous Embedded AI Applications
abstract: This paper presents AgentDP, which aims to deploy pre-trained AI models on heterogeneous embedded devices by fully automating model optimization and adaptation (O&A) with Large Language Model (LLM) agents. AgentDP not only significantly reduces human effort via automation but also enhances model inference efficacy by integrating LLMs with device-specific domain knowledge. To deliver a robust automation framework, AgentDP develops novel solutions to address three key technical challenges: 1) To help users elicit clear requirements, we propose a user requirement standardization module; 2) To mitigate the execution environment mismatch between AI models and heterogeneous embedded devices, we design an operator-aware model partition paradigm that enables different parts of the model to be efficiently executed on distinct inference engines. 3) To avoid re-searching optimization hyperparameters for new tasks, we propose a configuration reuse module that heuristically retrieves previous hyperparameter configurations for efficient reuse. Extensive experiments demonstrate that by fully automating the entire O&A process, AgentDP reduces entire model adaptation time by up to 80% compared with manual O&A while achieving higher task accuracy (more than 13% on average) than the baselines. Additionally, a comprehensive user study also exhibits the robust generalizability of AgentDP in adapting to different user requirements for heterogeneous embedded devices.

title: What Lies Beyond Perception: A Partition Theory of the Limits of AI Evaluation and Oversight
abstract: Replacing the judge can move a benchmark score, and models can be trained to hide capabilities. Both put the evaluator in question: what can it certify? We develop a partition theory of evaluation from one principle: judgement is bounded by perception. An agent's discrimination is the partition of its inputs into classes it cannot tell apart. Discrimination is necessary for capability but not sufficient, so bounds on it bear directly on whether evaluation can show that a model lacks an ability. We prove a one-sided bound. An examinee whose partition refines its evaluator's has the discrimination to pass every test the evaluator can grade, provided each input has an acceptable reply. We define the echo test, which accepts any reply the evaluator perceives as identical to the input, and show that it is complete for the tests the evaluator can grade. Passing therefore certifies at most a floor on discrimination, never a ceiling, and only a sharper evaluator can raise it. Used to detect concealment, echo-test failure points the wrong way: under exhaustive probing it flags every honestly weaker examinee and no concealer that presents as the evaluator's peer. Exact imitation of a weaker model is undetectable by any behavioural evaluator. We extend the bound to ensembles of monitors and to channels a model controls, explain published findings on judge disagreement and sandbagging, and derive testable predictions. A safety case that argues from behavioural evaluation alone that a model lacks an ability must assume the model's cooperation.

title: Global Convergence of Detailed Balanced Mass Action Systems
abstract: We give a self-contained proof that, for a finite detailed balanced mass-action system with positive rate constants, each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains exactly one positive equilibrium and every positive trajectory converges to it, together with a Lean 4 formalization of the complete argument from persistence to convergence. Boundedness and persistence come from the barrier argument of OpenAI (2026) for weakly reversible systems: an arbitrary-tolerance affine approximation yields a finite-minimum barrier whose superlevel sets confine trajectories and give one logarithmic bound for all solutions from a given initial state. The Horn-Jackson dissipation identity identifies the positive equilibria as an exponential family with parameters in the orthogonal complement of the stoichiometric subspace, which gives uniqueness in each class. A bounded-speed descent argument replaces LaSalle's invariance principle; it uses neither uniqueness of solutions nor continuous dependence on initial data, and it places every cluster point in that family. The route given here is direct and elementary, and its main theorem is checked by the Lean kernel against explicit definitions. The proofs, the Lean development, and the manuscript were produced in ClawsGO Science, an agent harness that packages a complete research environment: Claude Opus 5.5 made the research decisions, GPT 6 Astra carried them out, and the Lean kernel checked every formal step.

title: Adaptive Aerial Loco-Manipulation Policy Learning via LLM-Assisted Proactive Task Generation
abstract: Loco-manipulation extends the workspace of conventional manipulation by combining mobility with physical interaction, while aerial loco-manipulation further expands this capability into three-dimensional space, enabling robots to reach environments inaccessible to ground-based systems. Moving to an aerial platform, however, gives rise to a demanding control problem, since the vehicle must track trajectories accurately in three dimensions while the motion of the arm and its interaction with the environment continuously shift the center of mass, alter the inertia, and impose force and moment disturbances on the body. Conventional controllers address these effects through explicit models and estimation, whereas learning-based controllers infer dynamics from experience, yet control rewards provide no direct target for the response information retained from history, and fixed task sampling can leave persistent tracking difficulties insufficiently explored. We present ALMA, an aerial loco-manipulation framework for adaptive flight control under external arm commands. ALMA employs a contextual flight policy that adapts from recent measurements and actions, using action-conditioned prediction of future measurement representations to train its context to retain response information relevant to flight control. To expand the experience available for this adaptation, an evolutionary process uses a large language model (LLM) to analyze observed control difficulties and propose new structures of arm motion for subsequent training. In simulation, ALMA reduces position root-mean-square error (RMSE) by up to 24.7% relative to the strongest baseline, while the same policy transfers zero-shot to the aerial manipulator and reduces hover position RMSE by 79.6% during periodic arm motion relative to the real-world baseline.

title: DRILL: Training World Models to Improve Policies, Not Predict Pixels
abstract: World models are increasingly used to reduce environment interaction when post-training vision-language-action (VLA) policies with reinforcement learning. Yet they are typically trained to predict pixels one step ahead, even though their role here is not merely to render visually faithful videos but to produce learning signals from imagined rollouts that improve the policy. We show that this mismatch is substantial: lower pixel MSE can produce worse policy gradients, and a world model trained for policy utility can yield better downstream policies despite 17% higher pixel MSE on the next frame. We propose the Downstream-Return Imagination Learning Loop (DRILL), a bilevel framework that updates the world model to maximize the policy's return after an inner GRPO update on imagined rollouts. DRILL has two instantiations. DRILL-VWI is a closed-form surrogate, requiring no additional simulator rollouts, that reweights prediction errors by policy visitation, the group-relative GRPO advantage, and model confidence. DRILL-IMG is a full meta-gradient method that differentiates through the inner update using truncated Hessian-vector products. We show that DRILL-VWI recovers the local one-step component of the DRILL-IMG meta-gradient under score-compatibility and small-residual assumptions. Across five manipulation simulators and two VLA backbones, DRILL-IMG raises mean success rate by 13.1 points over WMPO and 7.9 points over RLVR-World, and complements RLVR pretraining rather than competing with it. More broadly, we believe video world models for VLA reinforcement learning can be productively trained by the policy gradients they produce, not only by pixel-level prediction.

title: ProTrav: Probabilistic Traversability with Elevation Uncertainty Propagation for Risk-aware Off-road Navigation
abstract: Reliable traversability estimation is essential for autonomous navigation on unstructured terrain. State-of-the-art approaches typically evaluate traversability from deterministic terrain elevation, thereby overlooking spatial correlations in the terrain and failing to account for how elevation uncertainty propagates through nonlinear traversability mappings. We propose ProTrav, a probabilistic terrain representation that uses function-space sampling to generate spatially correlated terrain realizations and propagate elevation uncertainty to traversability cost. First, a Sparse Variational Gaussian Process (SVGP) reconstructs a probabilistic elevation field from observations. Then, posterior function-space sampling generates spatially correlated terrain realizations, preserving spatial dependencies between neighboring locations while propagating elevation uncertainty through geometric features into traversability cost. Consequently, a distribution of traversability cost at arbitrary location is established, where the mean and standard deviation quantify the expected traversability cost and associated uncertainty, respectively. A risk term is defined by moment-based Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) and incorporated into a Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) controller for risk-aware navigation. Simulation experiments demonstrate navigation success rates exceeding 90\% on different terrains, compared with below 40\% for a baseline, while reducing attitude variations. Furthermore, the proposed approach is validated on a robot traversing real-world off-road terrain.

title: Bifurcations from Weight Space: JEPAWG on Parametric Dynamical Systems
abstract: Trained network weights are increasingly treated as data, but there is rarely ground truth about what a population of models should encode, which hampers systematic validation of weight-space methods. This makes parametric dynamical systems a natural test-bed: the dynamics change qualitatively at submanifolds of parameter space that are, in well-studied families, known analytically or numerically. Fine-tuning a forecasting network at each point of a parameter grid yields a model zoo indexed by a physical parameter, against which weight-space diagnostics can be checked. We build such model zoos for four dynamical systems and analyse them with JEPAWG, a recently proposed joint-embedding hypernetwork built around a learned parameter--weight representation. It was first introduced for neural samplers for lattice field theories, where its latent geometry located the phase transition and estimated the 2D Ising critical exponent. Applied to dynamical systems, JEPAWG is competitive on forecasting with a hypernetwork trained directly for that task, despite being supervised on the parameter--weight correspondence rather than on forecasts. Beyond forecasting, the norm of the parameter-derivative of the decoded weights locates Hopf points and curves, tracks a period-doubling cascade closely enough to give a qualitative estimate of the Feigenbaum constant, and detects a global bifurcation, which has no eigenvalue signature and is therefore invisible to linearisation. As such, JEPAWG provides interpretable insight into the dynamics that is not available from other hypernetworks. Together, these results indicate that JEPAWG is a workable instrument for reading physical structure off a population of trained networks.

title: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
abstract: Scientific discovery often requires identifying a small number of high-performing designs in vast, constrained search spaces. This is difficult when evaluations are costly, feasible solutions are sparse, parameters are strongly coupled, and physical constraints are strict. Recent AI for AI methods can automatically improve algorithms and optimization procedures. However, general purpose approaches are not designed around scientific priors, physical constraints, and limited evaluation budgets. We introduce ADAPT for Science, a multi-agent framework that treats scientific optimization as two coupled decisions: where to search and how to search. ADAPT uses historical designs to identify promising and diverse initial conditions, progressively concentrates computation on favorable search directions, and evolves the optimization procedure from execution feedback. We evaluate ADAPT on the design of gravitational wave detectors using a differentiable physics simulator and eight unseen detector topologies. Under matched scientific evaluation budgets, ADAPT achieves a mean loss of 0.204 +/- 0.101, reducing loss by 54.9% relative to the best classical optimizer and by 62.2% relative to the best general purpose agentic evolution baseline. ADAPT achieves the lowest loss on all unseen topologies among the evaluated baselines. ADAPT provides a step toward scientific optimization systems that continuously learn from prior experience and their own search outcomes.

title: Hear Every Sound Object: Rescuing Overlooked Sources in Auditory Scene Analysis
abstract: Auditory scene analysis (ASA) models extract information about individual sound sources from a complex auditory mixture. Recent object-based ASA models process the mixture through a sequence of modules and split it into source-wise features (i.e., object features) only at the last layer. However, substantial disparities in performance across sources limit overall performance. Our analysis using centered kernel alignment (CKA) reveals that CKA scores correlate strongly with per-source performance, with their disparities widening from intermediate to deeper layers. These findings motivate the early split and exchange of object features to address source-wise performance disparities before they widen in deeper layers. To this end, we propose PARASITE, a plug-in refinement architecture that splits object features at earlier layers and progressively refines them through sequential layers. Each layer integrates object features separated at different depths using Object-wise Gated Fusion (OGF) and then refines them using Windowed Cross-Object Attention (WCOA). We introduce the DeepASA++ model, which combines PARASITE with an ASA backbone and delivers state-of-the-art results on both ASA2 and STARSS23. DeepASA++ achieves a SELD score of 0.240 on STARSS23 and surpasses prior multi-stage inference architectures, including chain-of-inference.

title: Continuous-depth Deep Gaussian Processes
abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are appealing Bayesian regression models, but their standard discrete-depth parameterization often becomes harder to optimize as depth grows. We argue that depth is better treated as a latent continuous evolution than as a long discrete stack. We therefore propose a continuous-depth formulation in which the latent representation follows a stochastic differential equation with a depth-indexed drift family equipped with a GP-based prior. This reframes the core design choice as the prior placed on that family, rather than adopting a purely neural continuous-depth parameterization as in neural ODE or neural SDE models. We study two instantiations of this idea: CDGP, a direct GP prior over the state--depth drift, and FlowDGP, a flow-evolved prior that captures richer depth dependence at lower training cost. To motivate the redesign, we analyze how the single-sample DGP objective can become increasingly sensitive under repeated layer composition, while residual DGP is a useful first repair that still remains a finite discrete construction. We also give pathwise sensitivity analysis for the continuous-depth formulation. Experiments on synthetic, benchmark, and large-scale regression tasks show that residual DGP improves over plain DGP, while CDGP and FlowDGP provide a stronger overall story across the regimes we study.

title: Working Through Representation: Malleable Workspaces for Human-Agent Knowledge Work
abstract: Generative AI supports knowledge work, yet conversational histories may not capture the evolving organization that guides subsequent action. We introduce the Malleable Workspace, a conceptual model of how humans and agents form and revise a Work Representation and use its organization to advance work within a wider Work Environment. We developed it iteratively through conceptual analysis, comparison of 58 papers, and the construction and three-month longitudinal study of MalleableSpace with seven experienced agent users. Systems varied in what they represented as units and relations. System-assembled context was common; more systems supported local incorporation of agent outputs than reorganization, and fewer supported consequential agent-driven changes beyond the representation. The field study showed how representational roles and organization developed in use. These observations refined the model's account of how representation-grounded action depends on and can change the Work Environment. We contribute a conceptual and analytic foundation for representation-centered human--agent design.

title: Your Home Remembers: A Voice-Enabled Household Memory Assistant for Conversational Retrieval
abstract: Everyday household information is often exchanged in conversations but never written down, making details easy to forget or misremember. We present a voice-enabled smart-home assistant that acts as a household memory by recording conversations and retrieving information from stored and newly captured speech. The assistant runs on an Android tablet with a modular architecture in which speech-recognition, diarisation, embedding and language models can be configured or replaced through an orchestration layer. On-device wake-word detection and VAD-based query capture support hands-free interaction. Recorded audio is processed in configurable chunks, transcribed and diarised, converted into turn-aware passages with conversation-level timestamps, and indexed in a vector store. For memory queries, a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline selects key passages and uses them to generate an answer.
