title: Abstract B013: OncoProfilingTools: An agentic AI–enabled R framework for end-to-end cancer pharmacogenomics and biomarker discovery
abstract: Large-scale pharmacogenomics resources such as PRISM/DepMap provide great opportunities for biomarker discovery and precision oncology. However, their adoption remains challenging because drug response data, molecular profiles, and biological interpretation are typically fragmented across multiple tools and require extensive custom scripting. We developed OncoProfilingTools (OPT), an open-source R framework that unifies pharmacogenomics data management, statistical analysis, predictive modeling, and AI-assisted interpretation within a modular workflow. OPT provides pre-integrated PRISM/DepMap drug sensitivity and multi-omics datasets using standardized Bioconductor data structures, facilitating seamless integration with genomic analysis workflows. The framework currently implements a Sensitivity module for differential drug response analysis between user-defined biological or clinical groups, with forthcoming Prediction and Biomarker modules supporting machine learning–based response prediction and biomarker prioritization. OPT incorporates an integrated agentic AI framework that coordinates downstream analyses, including pathway enrichment, transcription factor analysis, immune deconvolution, and functional annotation. Outputs from specialized agents are synthesized by an AI Hypothesis Generator into candidate biological mechanisms and therapeutic hypotheses, which are summarized in structured reports by an AI Report Writer. A Shiny interface further enables interactive exploration, interpretation, and reporting without requiring scripting. OPT supports integrated pharmacogenomics data loading, standardized preprocessing, and differential drug sensitivity analysis through reproducible workflows that generate statistical summaries, publication-quality visualizations, and prioritized therapeutic candidates. In a colorectal peritoneal metastasis case study, OPT identified multiple candidate therapeutics, including the FDA-approved drug fruquintinib, while its agentic AI framework generated mechanistic interpretations that were independently reviewed and found to be consistent with current biological knowledge. The same workflow supports comparative analyses across user-defined cohorts to identify cohort-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities. OPT integrates standardized pharmacogenomics analyses with agentic AI–driven interpretation to accelerate biomarker discovery and hypothesis generation in precision oncology. Its modular architecture is designed to accommodate external pharmacogenomic datasets, enabling future comparative analyses across public and institution-specific cohorts, including applications in cancer health disparities research. title: Abstract B014: An Artificial intelligence multi-agent ecosystem for multi-omics, microbiome, and social determinants-driven population-informed precision oncology and cancer health disparities research across gastrointestinal cancers
abstract: Persistent disparities in gastrointestinal (GI) cancer incidence, treatment response, and survival among underrepresented populations highlight the need for computational platforms capable of integrating molecular, clinical, microbiome, and social determinants of health (SDoH) data. Although large-scale biomedical datasets have become increasingly available, existing analytical frameworks remain fragmented, disease-specific, and poorly equipped to investigate the complex biological and social drivers of cancer health disparities. To address this challenge, we developed AI-HOPE (Artificial Intelligence Agent for High-Optimization and Precision Medicine), a collaborative ecosystem of specialized conversational AI agents designed to perform real-time, multimodal analyses that support precision oncology and population-informed cancer disparities research. AI-HOPE integrates biomedical large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, automated code generation, and statistical inference within a modular architecture supporting interoperable analyses across multiple biological domains. The platform harmonizes genomic, clinical, microbiome, and SDoH data from TCGA, AACR Project GENIE, cBioPortal, and the institutional PE-CGS/COPECC colorectal cancer microbiome cohort. Specialized AI agents interrogate colorectal cancer signaling pathways (AI-HOPE-PI3K, AI-HOPE-TP53, AI-HOPE-TGF-β, AI-HOPE-WNT, AI-HOPE-MAPK, AI-HOPE-RTK/RAS, AI-HOPE-JAK/STAT), precision medicine & SDoH (AI-HOPE-PM), tumor-associated microbiome profiles (AI-HOPE-Microbiome), and disease-specific molecular landscapes in pancreatic, gastric, hepatic, and appendiceal cancers (AI-HOPE-Pancreatic, AI-HOPE-Gastric, AI-HOPE-Hepatic, & AI-HOPE-Appendiceal). The AI-HOPE ecosystem enabled rapid, reproducible integration of multi-modal datasets across diverse gastrointestinal malignancies, supporting comprehensive characterization of molecular and clinical heterogeneity among diverse populations. The platform successfully reproduced established biological associations while facilitating discovery of population-specific genomic, microbiome, and pathway-level signatures associated with gastrointestinal cancer disparities. Interoperability among specialized agents enabled coordinated analyses spanning multiple cancer types and biological domains, substantially reducing analytical complexity and execution time while generating publication-ready statistical, graphical, and narrative outputs through conversational queries. AI-HOPE establishes a scalable computational infrastructure that extends precision oncology beyond molecular characterization by incorporating biological, clinical, microbiome, and social determinants of health into a unified, population-informed artificial intelligence ecosystem. The platform provides the technological foundation for autonomous Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-enabled orchestration, facilitating distributed reasoning across domains and accelerating cancer health disparities research. title: Abstract B034: Can artificial intelligence amplify community voice? Evidence from a multisite formative evaluation of the AI-Powered ALEX Portal to enhance equity in clinical trial access
abstract: Patients with cancer and their caregivers face challenges accessing clinical trials because trial information, eligibility criteria, search, and referral pathways are complex and fragmented. These barriers can contribute to unequal access across racial, ethnic, and language groups. ALEX (Agents Leveraging Empathy for eXams) is a web-based portal that uses AI-enabled virtual health educators with synthesized voices and lip-synced facial animation to deliver trial education and a large language model to simplify trial information for search and referral. AI-generated content and virtual humans require human and community evaluation for accuracy, authenticity, and trust. This study examined how community feedback informed the iterative design and refinement of ALEX. The dataset included 34 English- and Spanish-language transcripts (about 44 hours) from focus groups and usability interviews using think-aloud procedures to evaluate the portal. The sessions were conducted from 2023 to 2025 at Mayo Clinic, UF-Gainesville, UF-Jacksonville, and the University of Miami. They examined 136 participants’ responses to the virtual health educators and their use of the portal for trial education, search, and referral. Participants reported their race as White (48.5%), Black or African American (47.1%), Native American or Alaska Native (0.7%), or other (3.7%). Separately, 50.7% identified as Hispanic or Latino, and nearly 25% reported Spanish as their primary language. Throughout data collection, feedback was reviewed and translated into design requirements for successive portal updates. We used deductive and inductive qualitative analysis to identify feedback patterns and user needs and reviewed version history to document portal changes. Three of the six themes derived from 1,653 coded excerpts were Trust Before Trial Search (“Who is Alex?”), Layered and Controllable Education (“If it was more in short bullets, maybe better”), and Motivation, Burden, and Research Trust (“There has to be some trust, some transparency or at least some acknowledgement”). Feedback informed portal refinements, including clearer language and institutional branding and content that was easier to scan. The virtual health educators were evaluated on representation, voice authenticity, lip-sync, warmth, and human likeness. Words like “sponsored study,” “diagnosis,” and “symptoms” guided language refinement. Suggested improvements included sample search terms, easy-to-read study cards, the ability to save results, a question guide, and direct coordinator contact. Research trust, privacy, security, and participation burden remained key priorities. To create an AI-enabled clinical trial portal that meets user needs, we used community feedback to identify modifiable barriers to communication, search, and referral. The goal of this formative process is to transparently incorporate that feedback into trial tools that are more credible, usable, acceptable, and equitable. Future work should evaluate whether these revisions improve referral outcomes. Fan Wang, Rashi Ghosh, Christopher You, Trevor Kauer, Andrew H. title: Abstract C141: Race-dependent epigenetic restoration of acinar identity in normal human pancreatic 3D organoids
abstract: Pancreatic cancer is preceded by acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM), an early precursor event. ADM is tightly controlled epigenetically by DNA methylation and histone acetylation; active Hippo signaling also regulates ADM. We explored the ability of three classes of compounds to promote acinar re-expression in a 3D organoid model of ADM. Following the establishment of 3D organoids from normal human acinar tissue, cultures were treated with 1 µM and 500 nM of the HDAC inhibitors romidepsin and trichostatin A (TSA) for 2 days. In parallel, acinar cultures were treated from Day 0 with a combination of the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor decitabine (10 nM, spiked in daily) and a potent, covalent inhibitor of TEAD-mediated transcription, CV-4-26 (10 µM), for 2 days. Additionally, we evaluated proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs); bifunctional molecules that recruit an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a target protein to drive its selective proteasomal degradation, using a 3-day treatment with an HDAC8-targeting PROTAC (YL352) and a dual HDAC3/8-targeting PROTAC (YX968). Viability was assessed by LIVE/DEAD staining. Acinar reexpression was assessed by increased AMY2A and reduced KRT19 mRNA expression, with decitabine/CV-4-26 producing a 25-fold increase in AMY2A and a 10-fold decrease in KRT19. Romidepsin and TSA combination caused a ∼10-fold induction of AMY2A and ∼10-fold suppression of KRT19. As our prior studies indicated that acinar re-expression following HDAC inhibition differed by donor race, we examined the ability of the PROTACs to promote acinar re-expression in organoids from Black, White, and Hispanic donors. The PROTAC to HDAC8 produced a race-dependent increase in the AMY2A/KRT19 ratio in the order of Black < White < Hispanic donors. Since maintenance of acinar identity suppresses cellular plasticity and limits ADM, restoration of acinar gene expression represents a promising differentiation-based therapeutic strategy for early pancreatic cancer. title: Abstract C144: Explainable artificial intelligence predicts disparity-associated miRNA regulatory axes in non-small cell lung cancer
abstract: MicroRNAs are important post-transcriptional regulators of gene expression that influence lung cancer cell-state plasticity. One key process is dedifferentiation, in which differentiated epithelial cells lose their mature epithelial identity and acquire more stem-like, adaptable characteristics. Dedifferentiation is biologically relevant because it contributes to epithelial remodeling, tumor plasticity, invasive behavior, and resistance-associated cell states. In disparity-focused lung cancer models, population-associated miRNA expression patterns may help identify regulatory miRNA-target axes that influence epithelial cell identity and dedifferentiation. Integrated miRNA and target-gene expression datasets were analyzed from African American (AA) and European American (EA) lung cancer cell-line models. The AA models included H23 and H810 cell lines, and the EA - H1437 and H1573 cell lines. Control and 30 min/100 ng/ml samples were analyzed for both model groups. Candidate miRNAs were predicted by integrating population-associated miRNA expression, predicted miRNA-target interactions, dedifferentiation and stem-like marker-associated marker genes, and bulk RNA-seq expression of the target genes. scRNA-seq data (PRJNA1404196) were used to evaluate target-gene expression across differentiation-related cell populations, including AT1, AT2, basal, club, stem-like, EMT, transitional epithelial, proliferating, tumor-associated macrophages, and CD8+ T cells. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed for 500ns using an AGO2-miRNA-target RNA complex containing the predicted miRNA-binding site. Explainable AI using SHAP and LIME was applied to prioritize candidate miRNA-target regulatory axes. RNA-seq analysis showed that the dedifferentiation marker HMGA2 was more highly expressed in AA samples than EA samples. HMGA2 expression was 5841.00 in AA control samples and 6960.75 in AA 30 min/100 ng/ml samples, compared with 1966.00 and 1465.50 in EA samples, respectively. miRNA expression analysis identified hsa-miR-6893-3p as an AA-enriched candidate, exhibiting approximately 2.8-fold higher expression in AA than EA samples. scRNA finds HMGA2 expression across differentiation-related cell populations, including stem-like, EMT, transitional epithelial, AT1, AT2, basal, club, and proliferating cell states. MD simulations of the AGO2-miRNA-target RNA complex were stable and supported structural evaluation of the predicted interaction between hsa-miR-6893-3p and the HMGA2miRNA-binding site. XAI integrated RNA-seq, miRNA expression, dedifferentiation-associated gene features, sc RNA-seq cell-state validation, and molecular simulation data to prioritize the hsa-miR-6893-3p–HMGA2 regulatory axis as the strongest candidate associated with lung cancer dedifferentiation. XAI predicted hsa-miR-6893-3p–HMGA2 regulatory axis as a candidate associated with lung cancer dedifferentiation. This axis may provide a molecular basis for disparity-associated epithelial dedifferentiation and lung cancer cell-state plasticity. title: Abstract IA006: Autonomous artificial intelligence agents, microbiome and multi-omics to advance cancer health disparities
abstract: Cancer outcomes vary across racial and ethnic populations because of differences in tumor biology, treatment exposure, environmental factors, and access to precision oncology. To address the limitations of conventional analyses, the Velazquez-Villarreal Lab developed AI-HOPE, an infrastructure of autonomous conversational artificial intelligence (AI) agents that integrates genomic, transcriptomic, microbiome, spatial, clinical, and treatment data. We evaluated AI-HOPE for molecular characterization and disparity-aware biomarker discovery across gastrointestinal cancers. AI-HOPE uses natural-language queries to construct clinical cohorts, execute reproducible analyses, interpret results, and coordinate specialized agents. Pathway-specific agents, including AI-HOPE-WNT, TGFβ, PI3K, RTK-RAS, JAK/STAT, and MAPK, analyzed colorectal cancer by ancestry, age at diagnosis, molecular alterations, survival, and treatment exposure. Disease- and data-specific agents, including AI-HOPE-Microbiome, Gastric, Hepatic, and Pancreas, supported cancer-specific clinical and molecular analyses. AI-generated findings were evaluated using conventional statistical methods. AI-HOPE analyzed approximately 2,600 colorectal cancer cases stratified by ancestry, age of onset, and FOLFOX exposure. WNT alterations were highly prevalent, predominantly driven by APC, but their associations with genomic burden and survival varied among African American, Hispanic/Latino (H/L), and non-Hispanic White populations and across age and treatment groups. In H/L colorectal cancer, AI-HOPE-WNT identified age- and bevacizumab-specific differences involving RNF43, AXIN1, AXIN2, TCF7L2, and AMER1. WNT alterations demonstrated context-dependent survival associations, supporting their potential as disparity-aware biomarkers. Complementary agents characterized additional oncogenic pathways relevant to chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy selection. AI-HOPE-Microbiome identified microbial–host relationships involving Agathobacter faecis, Parvimonas micra, Fusobacterium hwasookii/nucleatum, and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, together with TP53, SOX9, and LRP1B alterations and relevant clinical characteristics in colorectal and pancreatic cancers. Disease-specific agents (AI-HOPE-Hepatic, AI-HOPE-Gastric and AI-HOPE-Pancreas) also evaluated survival, molecular co-occurrence, and integrated clinical-genomic patterns in hepatocellular, gastric, and pancreatic cancers. AI-HOPE provides a scalable infrastructure for integrating clinical, treatment, genomic, pathway, and microbiome data in cancer health-disparities research. Expansion to spatial, proteomic, metabolomic, and longitudinal data may accelerate equitable biomarker discovery and treatment selection for populations historically underrepresented in precision oncology. title: Trajectory Divergence of Low Fertility and its Determinants: Evidence from International Comparison and China
abstract: Low fertility has spread from a small group of industrialised countries to most of the world, yet countries that fall below replacement level follow strikingly different paths thereafter. This thesis examines divergence within the low-fertility stage and its determinants, combining an international comparison with an analysis of China’s regional variation. Group-based trajectory modelling of total fertility rates for 218 countries and territories (2000–2023), multinomial and fixed-effects panel Logit models, spatial Durbin models for 319 Chinese prefectural cities, and long-difference regressions for 31 provinces trace fertility change from global pattern recognition to sub-national explanation. Three trajectories emerge: sustained low-level decline, moderate medium-level decline and slow high-level decline, differentiated by development, welfare, education and urbanisation. Among low-fertility countries, higher development raises the odds of stabilisation or rebound, while welfare acts mainly as a buffer. In China, fertility shows a stable west-high, east-low gradient reinforced by ethnic difference and spatial spillover. Coordinated packages of time, cash and service support relate more consistently to stabilisation than any single instrument.
journal: Gender and Sustainability in the Global South

title: Algorithms of agricultural navigation
abstract: Rationale. Automation of self-propelled agricultural machines and machine-tractor units (MTU), which ensures round-the-clock performance of field work without tractor driver's participation, can improve the efficiency of crop production and increase food production. The obstacle is the lack of formed agricultural navigation as an independent scientific direction on instrumental methods and technical means of controlling the movement of unmanned MTU. Research objective. Formation of the theory of agricultural navigation of tilled MTU. Research methods. The research is exploratory, aimed at using theoretical knowledge to solve the applied problem of determining the trajectory control error of unmanned MTU. The methods used are analogies, full-scale and thought experiments, mathematical modeling, intuition, comparisons, etc. Information from navigation, electrodynamics, mechanization, automation, instrumentation, etc. were used as initial information. The methods of analogies, natural and mental experiments, mathematical modeling, intuition, comparisons and were used. Information from navigation, electrodynamics, electro-exploration geophysics, agronomy, mechanization of mobile crop production processes, automatics, instrumentation, agricultural engineering, etc. was used as initial information. Results. Programming of MTU trajectories is carried out in coordinate systems rigidly “tied” to the terrain by physical landmarks. There are only three ways of specifying coordinate systems: two points, one point and a direction, a line along the entire trajectory. The location of the MTU is defined either in the same coordinate system or in a mobile coordinate system defined by the location of the “leading” point of the tractor and the directions of its axes. In both cases, the location of the MTU is determined by the distance between the MTU and the landmarks of the stationary coordinate system. Point landmarks are hundreds of meters and more distant, linear landmarks - on units of meters. Therefore, it is easier to determine the MTU location by the distance to linear landmarks than to point landmarks. It is advisable to use stationary underground current-carrying wires as linear reference points. The currents of the wires create navigational magnetic fields that allow to determine the location of MTU with high accuracy. Programming of trajectories in the magnetic fields of current-carrying wires is carried out by “guiding surfaces”, which represent the geometric location of points, when the leading point of the tractor is aligned with them, there is no trajectory control error signal formed by the navigation device of location determination. The trajectories are programmed by setting the planned values of the “electric” and “mechanical” navigation parameters of the positioning device. The first parameter determines the lateral displacement of the leading point relative to the current carrying wire, the second parameter determines the lateral displacement of the leading point relative to the longitudinal axis of the tractor. The planned value of one or both of these parameters can be zero. The maximum accuracy is possessed by positioning devices with zero planned electrical parameter. The article considers algorithms of formation of trajectory control error signals by less accurate but structurally simpler devices with zero value of mechanical parameter. Conclusion. For programming the required and determining the actual trajectories of unmanned MTAs, including tilled ones, it is advisable to use the systems of coordinates set by stationary landmarks in the form of underground current-carrying wires. Key words: agricultural navigation; navigation inductor; location algorithm; unmanned agricultural technologies.

title: Trends in the development of machines for strip tillage technology
abstract: BACKGROUND: Modern agriculture is characterized by the transition to resource-saving technologies that reduce energy consumption and preserve soil fertility. Strip tillage, being a nature-like technology, meets the strategic goals of technological leadership and digital transformation of the Russian agro-industrial complex. Its effectiveness is largely determined by the perfection of the machine, which makes it relevant to analyze the trends in the development of this technology. OBJECTIVE: Identification of the main trends in the development of machines for strip tillage technology at the present stage. METHODS: The research is based on the analysis of domestic and foreign scientific publications, patents, catalogs of machine-building companies and technical documentation for serial and experimental machines for strip tillage technology. Methods of systematic and comparative analysis, as well as generalization, were used. The designs were compared according to a set of classification features, including the method of aggregation, type of working bodies, depth of processing and fertilizer application system. RESULTS: It is established that the development of machines for strip tillage is characterized by increasing complexity of structures and the transition from simple linear machines to modular systems with independent kinematics of sections. The key trends are the combination of operations (deep loosening, local application of fertilizers of different aggregate states and sowing in one technological passage), as well as the adaptation of row spacing to the specific agrotechnical requirements of cultivated crops. The evolution of the working sections is shown, where the main focus is the modular layout principle using damping systems to protect against obstacles. The design features of the frames are analyzed depending on the width of the aisles. Russian developments are presented, including a high-speed cultivator and combined sections, including a seeding machine. CONCLUSION. The review shows that the further development of machines for strip tillage technology is aimed at creating highly adaptive, energy-efficient and multifunctional units. Their improvement, based on modularity, combining operations and applying precision farming solutions, is critically important for the practical realization of the potential of resource-saving technologies, ensuring technological sovereignty and increasing the competitiveness of agriculture.

title: A HIERARCHICAL DISTRIBUTED EDGE AI FRAMEWORK FOR REAL-TIME APPLE LEAF DISEASE CLASSIFICATION
abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) in agriculture has transformed crop management, particularly in the detection of plant diseases. Apple trees, a key agricultural commodity, are vulnerable to various diseases, which can severely impact crop yields. Traditional disease detection methods, often reliant on manual inspections, are time-consuming and prone to error. In response, this study proposes a novel two-stage edge AI framework for apple leaf disease classification that integrates RGB imagery with distributed edge computing. The first stage performs binary classification to distinguish between healthy and diseased leaves, achieving an F1 score of 95.50%. This optimization is achieved by utilizing lightweight models on edge devices, thereby enhancing computational efficiency. The second stage employs a consensus-based multiclass classification approach, achieving a 96.44% F1 score in identifying specific diseases. This dual-stage system, supported by an edge AI architecture, ensures real-time disease detection while minimizing resource consumption and enhancing scalability in large-scale agricultural environments. The full system achieved a 95.50% accuracy and F1 score on the special dataset. The results demonstrate the system’s efficacy in controlled laboratory conditions, offering a promising solution for precise, real-time agricultural monitoring. This study underscores the potential of distributed edge AI systems for scalable and efficient disease detection in precision agriculture.
journal: Facta Universitatis, Series: Automatic Control and Robotics

title: Attractiveness of the Agrotechnology Study Program and the Role of Social Media in Student Enrollment Decisions
abstract: Increasing competition among higher education institutions has prompted study programs to develop effective strategies to attract prospective students. Social media has become an important channel for disseminating academic information and presenting institutional identity, particularly among Generation Z. This study aimed to analyze the attractiveness of the Agrotechnology Study Program at Universitas Pembangunan Nasional “Veteran” Yogyakarta and to examine the role of social media in students’ enrollment decisions. A quantitative descriptive survey was conducted among 140 newly enrolled Agrotechnology students in 2026 using a structured questionnaire with five-point Likert scales. The questionnaire assessed factors influencing study program selection, perceptions of social media content, and social media utilization. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and correlation analysis. Modern agricultural technology was the highest-rated factor influencing enrollment decisions (mean = 4.11), followed by accreditation (4.06) and practical activities (4.04). Information obtained from social media received the lowest mean score among the enrollment factors (3.35). Modern agricultural technology and innovation was also the most attractive type of social media content (mean = 4.09). A positive correlation was observed between modern agricultural technology content and the decision to choose the Agrotechnology Study Program (r = 0.45). These findings indicate that social media may function primarily as an information and awareness channel, while students’ enrollment decisions are also shaped by academic, practical, and career-related considerations. The study contributes empirical evidence for developing evidence-based digital communication strategies for agricultural higher education.
journal: RSF Conference Series: Engineering and Technology

title: EDUPATH AI A Rag-Based Multi-Agentic AI Framework for Personalised Education and Career Advisory
abstract: Choosing a career is a tough decision to make in itself. Things get trickier when it comes to information a student actually needs: which scholarships they're eligible for, where courses lead, where students can get in based on their marks, etc., and all that information is spread out across dozens of government portals, college websites, and PDFs that don't always agree on what they're offering. The majority of the career-guidance tools that are available today are not really a solution to this. They either give a general response from a brief questionnaire, or release a chatbot which will freely associate a response that seems confident but is not true. Neither verifies whether a student is qualified or not for what it suggests. This paper is an attempt to bridge that gap by employing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline to achieve this using a set of cooperating agents, instead of a single large model performing all the tasks. The first step is to process a student's academic record, interests, financial status, location, class and career category, and goals to create a structured profile, which is then fed into agents that search for verified information, validate eligibility for scholarships based on hard rules, not assumptions, and compile a plan that is concrete and easily explained. We evaluated the retrieval layer on ten representative queries, including career paths, welfare schemes, higher education and scholarships, and it achieved a top five correct source hit rate of 90% and a Mean Reciprocal Rank of 0.7167. To sum up, if you base the model's output on retrieved evidence and ensure that eligibility decisions are deterministic then you end up giving guidance that a student can actually trust and follow — something that a pure language model and a static rule engine can't do alone.
journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology

title: GIS and remote sensing based multicriteria analysis for identifying potential agricultural land: A case study on Savar Upazila, Bangladesh
abstract: Despite of gradually decreasing its contribution to gross domestic product (GDP), agriculture, however, is the backbone of the Bangladeshi economy. Farming is the primary mean of rural livelihoods in Bangladesh but agricultural land is slowly declining day by day. Although, at present, Bangladesh is self-sufficient in terms of producing food, especially rice and some other major agricultural products, it is predicted that, in near future, the country is going to face immense challenges due to climate related threats. The research aims to identify the potential lands for suitable farming in Savar Upazila (sub-district) under Dhaka district applying a geographic information system (GIS) and remote sensing (RS) based multicriteria analysis. Relevant biophysical characteristics of soil, terrain, and landuse and land cover (LULC) were considered. Soil and evelvation data was collected from Soil Resource Development Institute (SRDI)and Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM), respectively, whereas satellite images were collected from Landsat-8. The maximum likelihood supervised classification technique was used for LULC classification, and the multicriteria evaluation (MCE) and analytical hierarchy process (AHP) approach was employed to identify suitable areas for farming. The research finds the LULC classes are agricultural land, built-up area, fallow land, vegetation cover, waterbodies, and wetland are 12.42%, 31.01%, 25.69%, 25.98%, 4.81%, and 0.09%, respectively. This research also finds that agricultural land suitability was classified as highly suitable, moderately suitable, marginally suitable, and not suitable are 24.28%, 29.53%, 24.66%, and 21.53%, respectively. In contrast, the current agricultural land usage accounts for just 12.42% of the total land area in this research area. The Kappa accuracy has been measured at a value of 0.88 and an overall accuracy value of 0.90 which indicates that the LULC classification is done almost perfectly. This study offered information at the local level that farmers may utilize to decide on cropping patterns and appropriateness. Bangladesh Rural Development Studies, 26(1), 2023 (13-26)

title: Genomic Prediction with Genotype-by-Environment Interaction Using a Residual Network and Transformer Framework
abstract: Genotype, environment, and their interactions collectively determine crop phenotypes. While integrating genotypic and environmental data has the potential to improve genomic prediction performance, most existing methods do not adequately incorporate environmental factors or the actual growth conditions of crops, and their prediction accuracy remains suboptimal. In this study, we propose Resformer, a genotype-by-environment interaction genomic prediction model that combines residual networks with Transformer architecture. The model employs gated convolution and Transformer to capture genetic features, residual network and fully connected layers to extract environmental features, and a cross-attention mechanism to model genotype-by-environment interactions. We evaluated Resformer on the G2F dataset against three traditional machine learning methods and two state-of-the-art genotype-by-environment interaction approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that Resformer consistently achieves better predictive performance, confirming its effectiveness and generalizability for genomic selection in crop breeding.

title: Ethylene Response Factors in Plant Stress Adaptation: Regulatory Mechanisms and Opportunities for Crop Improvement
abstract: Ethylene response factor (ERF) proteins constitute a major branch of the AP2/ERF transcription factor superfamily and are conventionally divided into six groups (B1–B6) on the basis of conserved sequences and phylogenetic relationships. ERFs recognize cis-elements such as the GCC-box and dehydration-responsive element/C-repeat and assemble regulatory complexes with coactivators or corepressors. They thereby coordinate responses to drought, salinity, low and high temperatures, hypoxia, flooding, and pathogen attack. Their outputs are determined not by a single motif but by DNA-binding preference, interacting partners, tissue context, and post-translational control through mitogen-activated protein kinase phosphorylation, ubiquitination, and the N-degron pathway. Crop studies increasingly show that ERF alleles and regulatory modules can improve stress tolerance and disease resistance, although constitutive manipulation frequently compromises growth, yield, or quality. This review focuses on the narrowly defined ERF subfamily, evaluates the evidence linking classification, transcriptional regulation, protein stability, and stress phenotypes, and examines breeding strategies based on molecular markers, tissue-specific expression, cis-regulatory editing, and favorable alleles. We argue that progress now depends on causal analysis under combined stresses and multi-environment yield validation, enabling stress protection to be decoupled from agronomic penalties.

title: An Enhanced Genomic Transformer for Multi-Dataset Forward-Validation Benchmarking in Pig Genomic Prediction
abstract: Genomic prediction models in pig breeding should forecast the performance of future selection candidates, yet random cross-validation does not accurately reflect this sequential setting. Here, we introduce an enhanced genomic transformer (EGT) that compresses genome-wide SNP profiles into compact tokens and incorporates a differentiable scoring term alongside mean squared error (MSE) during training. We constructed 70%/10%/20% forward-validation datasets for three pig datasets and evaluated single-trait and multi-task EGT variants against GBLUP, support-vector regression, random forest, XGBoost, CNN, and RNN across 12 prediction tasks. The better-performing EGT variant achieved a higher test-set Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) than the baseline for 10 of the 12 prediction tasks, with the largest improvement on LDL-C (+0.057). In BloodLipid ablations, autoencoder-only representation yielded the highest mean PCC (0.285), while Pearson–MSE objective reached 0.293 versus 0.291 for MSE-only training. Integrated-gradient analysis revealed a recurrent candidate region on Sus scrofa chromosome 13 across three lipid traits, and masking the top-attributed features reduced predictive performance more than a marker-count-matched random control for HDL-C, LDL-C and TG, whereas masking increased test-set PCC for TCHOL. This work establishes forward-validation benchmarks across three pig datasets and reports results to inform model selection and region prioritization in pig breeding.

title: Rice Yield Prediction Using Multi-Modal Regression Learning with Optimized Ensemble Models
abstract: Accurate rice yield estimation is important for agricultural planning, resource allocation, and food security assessment, but yield depends on interacting climatic, vegetation, remote sensing, seasonal, and crop growth factors. This study presents a Multi-Modal Regression Learning (MMRL) framework for continuous rice yield prediction. The framework integrates rainfall, temperature, humidity, normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), VH synthetic aperture radar (SAR) backscatter, season, rice cultivation area, and leaf wetness information. Predictor relevance is assessed before model development, and multiple regression learners are trained using a common feature set. Their validation predictions are combined through non-negative ensemble weights constrained to sum to one, thereby producing a single optimized prediction. Experiments were performed on a modeled spatio-temporal agricultural dataset representing Karnataka conditions, with 10,000 observations used for the regression comparison. The proposed MMRL ensemble achieved an R2 of 0.9515, an RMSE of 0.6334 tons/ha, an MAE of 0.5075 tons/ha, and an MAPE of 9.81%, outperforming the evaluated individual regression models. Diagnostic plots further indicated close agreement between predicted and reference yields across most of the evaluated range. The MMRL workflow was also evaluated on a separately reconstructed synthetic dataset generated with fully specified distributions, sampling rules, noise terms, a yield generation equation, and fixed random seeds.

title: A Three-Level Framework for Spatial Demand Estimation and Latent-Demand Reconstruction in Paid Parking Systems
abstract: Estimating paid parking demand is difficult when transaction data are censored by full occupancy and when tariff changes create structural breaks. This study proposes an interpretable three-level framework combining (i) dynamic modelling of the cumulative client base and aggregate parking demand, (ii) recovery of model-implied latent potential demand in capacity-constrained zones using a transferred beta arrival profile and cohort-based survival curves, and (iii) spatial allocation of capacity-adjusted demand using road-network accessibility, land use, tariffs, capacity, and competitive-supply factors. Demand is estimated separately for four parking-duration groups using transaction data from Vladivostok, Russian Federation. Three validation questions are kept distinct. A one-origin, 15-month aggregate revenue scenario forecast after the June 2025 tariff change achieved MAPE 6.5% versus 18.8% for a seasonal-naive benchmark. Leave-one-zone-out spatial cross-validation produced OLS R2 values of 0.49–0.63 across duration groups (0.61 for total sessions), whereas chronological cross-regime transfer of the zone model yielded R2 values near zero or below. The evidence therefore supports spatial demand estimation, latent-demand reconstruction, and transparent scenario analysis; it does not support a claim of robust short-term temporal forecasting for zone-level demand.

title: Organ-Specific Distribution and Functions of Major Secondary Metabolites in Tomato
abstract: Tomato is an economically important crop, and its secondary metabolites produced in leaves, fruits, and roots are crucial for environmental stress responses and fruit quality formation. Leaf glandular trichomes mainly synthesize defensive compounds, fruit development involves metabolic transitions, and root exudates act as key signals regulating rhizosphere microbial interactions. However, a comprehensive organ-specific understanding of this metabolic network remains fragmented. This review synthesizes the general theoretical framework of plant secondary metabolism. Using tomato as a model plant, it systematically explores the compositional features, functional differentiation, and regulatory mechanisms of secondary metabolites across leaves, fruits, and roots. We emphasize how metabolic partitioning orchestrates the trade-offs among defense, quality, and symbiosis, and highlight existing knowledge gaps, including the insufficient functional characterization of root metabolites and unclear cross-organ transport mechanisms. Future studies should focus on: (1) functions of root-specific metabolites (e.g., acylsugars); (2) molecular mechanisms of long-distance transport; (3) genetic associations of metabolic reprogramming during domestication; (4) transcriptional regulation of carotenoid cleavage; and (5) domestication selection modules coordinating defense and fruit quality. Integrating spatial metabolomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and gene editing to construct a spatiotemporal regulatory network will provide a theoretical foundation for the coordinated improvement of stress resistance and fruit quality.

title: Adaptive Deep Sequential Learning for Treasury Yield-Curve Forecasting: Integrating Affine Term-Structure Factors and Experience Replay
abstract: Accurate out-of-sample yield-curve forecasting requires models that capture complex non-linear temporal dynamics while respecting the cross-sectional economic structure of the term structure. This paper introduces an economically structured deep sequential learning framework for multi-horizon Treasury yield forecasting that unifies multi-head self-attention, temporal convolutions, bidirectional recurrent states, and latent affine term-structure factors. To address the severe optimization degradation caused by strong temporal autocorrelation during gradient descent, we introduce adaptive experience replay dynamics—specifically comparing uniform, prediction-error-based prioritized, and structural yield-entropy sampling regimes—under strict chronological out-of-sample evaluation protocols. Empirical results demonstrate that experience replay mechanisms significantly outperform traditional chronological training regimes. Structurally, entropy-based sampling achieves optimal performance in aggregate yield forecast accuracy and latent factor estimation, while prioritized experience replay excels in absolute point error minimization and conditional volatility tracking. Crucially, incorporating cross-sectional no-arbitrage constraints prevents structural yield-curve inversions and monotonicity violations without compromising predictive precision. Statistically superior point forecasts translate directly into enhanced economic tracking fidelity for duration-based bond portfolio pricing. Overall, the findings demonstrate that unifying structural term-structure constraints with non-uniform historical memory sampling provides a powerful, economically coherent methodology for fixed-income modeling and financial risk management.

title: Transforming Image-Structured Financial Time Series for the Joint Model of Return and Covariance
abstract: Accurate forecasting of financial returns and their associated risks is fundamental to effective risk measurement, portfolio construction, and financial decision-making. However, expected returns and covariance structures are often modelled separately, potentially overlooking their interdependence and evolving cross-asset relationships. Motivated by the analogy between multi-asset financial time series and video data, this paper proposes an image-structured representation for jointly forecasting next-day mean returns and covariance matrices using the Time-Space Transformer (TimeSformer). Financial features are organised as temporal sequences of matrix-structured frames, enabling the model to learn temporal and cross-asset dependencies simultaneously. We evaluate shared two-head and separate two-tower architectures with multiple probabilistic and non-parametric loss functions for return and covariance prediction, while ensuring positive-definite covariance forecasts through Cholesky parameterisation. Empirical results demonstrate the proposed covariance-informed TimeSformer models substantially outperform the Vanilla Transformer and LSTM baselines across the principal mean-return and covariance forecasting measures, although the zero-return forecast and covariance persistence remain strong benchmarks for mean and covariance prediction, respectively. Incorporating historical covariance structure directly into the input further improves both forecasting tasks and yields the strongest covariance performance among the learned models. Diebold–Mariano tests confirm that several of these improvements are statistically significant, particularly for covariance forecasting and the covariance-informed representations. Economic evaluation of portfolio optimisation using global minimum variance portfolios further shows that covariance-informed TimeSformer models achieve strong risk-adjusted performance, with the best configuration attaining the highest Sharpe ratio among the evaluated models. Overall, the results demonstrate that spatiotemporal attention, task-specific objectives, and covariance-informed representations provide an effective framework for jointly modelling multi-asset return and risk dynamics.

title: Radial Spectral Barcode Watermarking for Remote Sensing Images: Extending the Detectable Scale Limits
abstract: To extend the scale limits within which a template watermark remains detectable, this paper proposes a template watermarking algorithm for remote sensing images based on a radial spectral barcode (RSB). The RSB is a new geometry of template watermark whose inner and outer boundaries are separated along the radial direction of the discrete Fourier transform magnitude spectrum. In the embedding stage, the spectrum is divided into angular slots, a synchronization sequence generated from the secret key and the watermark are assigned to alternate slots, and the magnitude within the radial interval of each slot is modulated according to its sign. In the detection stage, the angular profile of the received spectrum is computed under a set of geometric hypotheses, the synchronization sequence is located by circular correlation, and the watermark is read from the synchronized profile without correcting the image. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method extends the detectable scale interval well beyond that of the ring-template methods while retaining robustness against rotation, translation, cropping, affine transformation, map reprojection, and signal-processing attacks. It outperforms the comparative algorithms in robustness at an equal or higher PSNR, with a low false detection rate.

title: FLNet: A Deep Learning Detector for Floating-Debris Detection in Close-Range Aquatic Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Floating debris threatens aquatic ecosystems, yet detecting it in close-range aquatic remote sensing imagery remains difficult because small, irregular, or partially submerged objects resemble specular highlights and ripples. This study proposes FLNet, a YOLO11-L-based detector for water-surface monitoring from unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). FLNet redesigns the backbone, neck, and head with three components: a Dynamic Polarity-Aware Robustness Block that calibrates deep activations and models similar and opposing feature relations; an Adaptive Multi-Receptive Pyramid that repeatedly fuses three adjacent scales through multi-branch depthwise convolutions; and a Detail-Preserving Shared Head that applies one boundary-sensitive prediction trunk to all scales. On a custom five-category dataset of 12,237 images, FLNet achieved 85.93% macro-Precision, 85.08% macro-F1, and 88.77% mean average Precision at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.5 (mAP@0.5), the highest single-run values among the evaluated detectors, with 24M parameters and 83 GFLOPs. Across three random seeds, its macro-Precision and macro-F1 advantages over the strongest competitor, Hyper-YOLO, exceeded seed-to-seed variability, whereas its mAP@0.5 was statistically comparable to that of Hyper-YOLO and Hyper-YOLO retained a higher mAP@0.5:0.95. In separately trained benchmarks, FLNet achieved the highest F1-score on FloW-Img (80.26%) and the highest macro-F1 on MarineDebris-yolo (79.82%). With TensorRT half-precision (FP16) acceleration, detector-side inference reached 29.8, 111.2, and 56.4 frames per second on Jetson Xavier NX, AGX Orin, and Orin Nano Super, respectively. FLNet therefore offers a favorable accuracy–efficiency balance for close-range floating-debris detection.

title: Spectral Proxy Parameter Linking Remote Sensing Reflectance and Inherent Optical Properties in Case-2 Waters
abstract: A spectral proxy parameter linking remote sensing reflectance (Rrs) and inherent optical properties (IOPs) was evaluated for six selected areas of the Baltic Sea. Measured IOPs from the individual optical datasets were used to calculate Morel’s unscaled proxy reflectance, whereas area and wavelength specific median IOPs were used as representative inputs to Monte Carlo radiative transfer simulations. Comparison of the individual proxy estimates with the corresponding area-specific Monte Carlo reference reflectance enabled determination of the spectral proxy parameter k. The results demonstrate a clear wavelength dependence and substantial area to area variability of this parameter. The purpose of the study is not to introduce a new fundamental IOPs–Rrs relationship, but to quantify how the effective scaling coefficient of a widely used proxy relationship varies spectrally and regionally in optically complex Case-2 waters. For each investigated Baltic Sea area, the spectral variability of k was approximated using a three-coefficient second-order polynomial. Area-specific parameterizations provide compact descriptions of the regional median k spectra, while a generalized formulation describes only the pooled central tendency. A radiometric evaluation was performed using 24 in situ OCP-100 spectra from the Gulf of Gdańsk (N = 96 wavelength-level pairs). Predicted and measured Rrs yielded r = 0.680, R2 = 0.462, a regression slope of 0.258, a mean bias of −0.00475 sr−1, an RMSE of 0.00590 sr−1, and a MAPE of 62.1%. Within-wavelength correlations were weak at 555 and 620 nm (r = 0.140 and 0.067, respectively). Thus, the regional parameterization preserves broad spectral ordering but underestimates absolute Rrs and does not establish strong station-level predictive skill. The results should be interpreted as a regional, configuration-dependent spectral scaling framework.

title: ONOA-YOLO: Orthogonal-Nesting Orientation-Aware Small Object Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Object detection in remote sensing imagery is a fundamental and crucial task within the remote sensing domain. However, small object detection in remote sensing images remains a challenge for SOTA methods. This is because small objects often have large aspect ratios, exhibit characteristic variations across different orientations, and are distributed within complex backgrounds. Current methods, which employ square convolutions, often retain excessive background information during feature extraction, leading to suboptimal detection performance. In this paper, an orthogonal-nesting orientation-aware small object detection network based on YOLOv10 is proposed to achieve small object detection in complex backgrounds. ONOA-YOLO employs an orthogonal-nesting module to enhance the features of small objects from multiple orientations, improving the sensitivity of the network to their intrinsic features. Additionally, it incorporates a background-suppression module based on large convolutional kernels. This module integrates the contextual information of small objects as guiding cues with other features, enabling the suppression of background interference while preserving the extracted small object features.

title: Remote-Sensing-Supported Transboundary Ecosystem Service Mapping: A Robust Integrated Index for the Heilongjiang–Amur River Basin
abstract: Comparable ecosystem service mapping across international borders requires inputs and choices that remain consistent across the study area. We harmonized satellite-derived and geospatial datasets for the Heilongjiang–Amur River Basin to a common 1 km grid for 2000, 2010, and 2020. Landsat-derived land cover, MODIS burned area, harmonized nighttime lights, terrain, climate, and modeled soil products supported four InVEST indicators: Habitat Quality, Carbon Storage, Annual Water Yield, and Soil Retention. Pooled p01–p99 normalization and equal weighting produced a dimensionless, relative, modeled integrated ES index. Robustness was assessed using alternative normalization, leave-one-service-out tests, bounded weight perturbation, land-cover-excluded XGBoost–SHAP models, and spatially blocked cross-validation. The basin-wide mean index values were 0.444, 0.461, and 0.451. The Chinese-side means were 0.357, 0.365, and 0.361, compared to 0.528, 0.555, and 0.538 on the Russian side; the Russia–China contrast remained positive across tested construction alternatives. The random-split R2 values were 0.819, 0.806, and 0.793, whereas the spatially blocked R2 values were 0.651, 0.582, and 0.606. SHAP analysis characterized associations in fitted predictions rather than causal effects. The three benchmark-year differences are indicative and remain sensitive to Annual Water Yield, interannual climate, and index construction.

title: MambaDPSMVS: Remote Sensing Multi-View Height Estimation Based on Mamba-Enhanced Feature Pyramid and Deformable RPC Sampler
abstract: Aiming at the problems of complex RPC geometric modeling in multi-view stereo matching (MVS) of satellite remote-sensing images, significant feature noise caused by cross-view occlusion and inconsistent lighting, and blurred edge details of height maps, this paper proposes a satellite MVS height estimation network based on a Mamba-enhanced feature pyramid and deformable RPC sampling, MambaDPSMVS. In the feature extraction stage, the cross-view Mamba module and the single-view self-Mamba enhancement module are designed to realize explicit feature interaction between and within views through direction prediction, direction routing, geometric gating fusion and state-space sequence modeling, and suppress view noise from the source. A deformable sampler for an RPC geometry, RPC-DPSampler, is proposed to achieve accurate alignment of source-view features with the reference view through 3D deformable coarse alignment, block sampling, 2D sub-pixel fine-tuning and view-level attention-weighted aggregation. Then, the cascaded cost is constructed, and the loop encoder–decoder regularization is used to complete the height estimation from coarse to fine. Experiments on the WHU-TLC and US3D datasets show that the MAE/RMSE of the proposed method reaches 1.688 m/2.867 m and 1.744 m/3.847 m, respectively, and the PAG<1 m reaches 61.81% and 62.18%, respectively, which values are better than those of baseline methods such as Sat (Red-Net) and Sat (CasMVS-Net). The ablation experiment further validated the complementarity of Mamba enhancement features and the RPC-DPSampler module in feature expression and geometric alignment.

title: Crop Water Demand, Drought Management, and Groundwater Conservation: A Review of Crop-Switching Strategies in US Irrigated Agriculture
abstract: Groundwater depletion increasingly threatens irrigated agriculture across many parts of the US, where intensive row-crop production has substantially reduced aquifer storage. While the groundwater conservation literature emphasizes irrigation efficiency improvement, pumping restrictions, and groundwater governance, crop choice itself remains an underexamined aspect of agricultural water demand. This review synthesizes evidence on the water-saving potential of transitioning from conventional irrigated row crops to specialty and alternative crops (SACs) in the US High Plains and other drought-stressed regions. These SACs consistently show biophysical advantages, including lower evapotranspiration (ET) requirements, greater drought tolerance than traditional irrigated row crops, and even superior profitability in certain growing conditions (e.g., marginal lands). However, SAC adoption remains constrained by policy environments favoring conventional row crops, thin markets for SACs, limited extension and other technical support. Regional case studies show that mechanisms like collective groundwater governance and integrated crop-energy land use transition can accelerate crop switching to SACs across semiarid regions, but rebound effects, workforce availability, community acceptance, and lack of policy support and coordination are still practical challenges. The review concludes that crop switching can meaningfully support agricultural groundwater conservation, but only as part of an integrated adaptation strategy combining agronomic suitability, economic incentives, and policy support.

title: Entrepreneurial Orientation and Strategic Agility in VUCA Africa: Developing an Ambidextrous Strategic Emergence Model for FinTech organisations
abstract: This conceptual theory-building study examines how African FinTech organisations navigate volatility, uncertainty, complexity and ambiguity (VUCA), using Mukuru as a paradigmatic single case. It develops the Mukuru Ambidextrous Strategic Emergence Model (MASEM) by integrating Entrepreneurial Orientation, Strategic Agility, Organisational Ambidexterity, Chaos Theory and Strategic Decision-Making Theory. Using secondary evidence, longitudinal organisational analysis and abductive cross-theoretical synthesis, the study explains how Mukuru combines exploitation of established remittance and agent-network capabilities with exploration of digital innovation. The analysis identifies multidexterity, the orchestration of multiple, potentially contradictory business models across heterogeneous regulatory settings, as a key capability linking strategic agility to sustained emergence. MASEM conceptualises VUCA pressures as external conditions, entrepreneurial and adaptive capabilities as the strategic core, responsible AI and green digital finance as enabling capabilities, and resilience, inclusion and antifragility as intended organisational outcomes. The model is conceptual rather than empirically validated; accordingly, future research should test its constructs and causal relationships across multiple African FinTech organisations. The study contributes an Africa-centred framework and practical guidance for managers seeking to align innovation, governance, sustainability and regulatory adaptability under persistent environmental turbulence.
journal: International Journal of Business Ecosystem & Strategy (2687-2293)

title: Strategic Emergence in a VUCA Developing Economy: Building a Purpose-Driven Global Business Process Outsourcing Platform for Emerging organisations
abstract: This paper examines how a purpose-driven organisation emerging from a highly volatile developing economy can build a globally competitive business process outsourcing (BPO) platform while contributing to brain-drain reversal. Using ZimWorX, a Zimbabwean-headquartered BPO enterprise, as a longitudinal case study, the study aims to develop a theoretically grounded framework explaining strategic emergence under conditions of volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity (VUCA) for an emerging organisation. Situated within the broader transformation of global outsourcing markets and the democratisation of digital talent, the paper positions Zimbabwe not as a peripheral participant but as a credible contender in high-value global services delivery. The research adopts a qualitative single-case study design grounded in conceptual theory-building. Drawing on secondary data, organisational records, industry reports, and contextual economic analysis, the study employs abductive reasoning to synthesise four theoretical lenses: Entrepreneurial Orientation Theory, Market Entry Strategy frameworks, Chaos Theory, and Strategic Decision-Making Theory. Through cross-theoretical integration, the analysis traces how ZimWorX navigated Zimbabwe’s macroeconomic instability, currency volatility, high unemployment, and institutional constraints to construct a resilient and differentiated service platform serving clients primarily in the United States and the United Kingdom. The findings reveal that ZimWorX’s success is not attributable to cost arbitrage alone, but to a distinctive combination of entrepreneurial vision, purpose-driven culture, agile niche-focused market entry, and a disruptive “insourcing” philosophy that reframes outsourcing as premium human capital partnership. The firm’s strategic posture reflects adaptive decision-making under disequilibrium conditions, where uncertainty becomes a catalyst for innovation rather than paralysis. Importantly, the organisation embeds social purpose, specifically the reversal of skilled migration and the creation of dignified employment, into its competitive strategy, thereby aligning commercial performance with developmental impact. The study culminates in the development of the ZimWorX Strategic Emergence Framework (ZSEF), a conceptual model that illustrates how emerging-economy firms can integrate entrepreneurial orientation, strategic agility, purposeful positioning, and adaptive market entry to achieve sustained global competitiveness in VUCA environments. The framework advances emerging organisation theory by demonstrating how firms operating in structurally disadvantaged contexts can convert institutional adversity into strategic differentiation. The paper concludes that purposeful strategic emergence offers a viable pathway for developing economies seeking participation in knowledge-intensive global value chains. Rather than replicating traditional offshore outsourcing models, African BPO platforms can leverage mission-driven identity, digital infrastructure, and agile governance structures to compete on quality and relational capital. The study recommends that policymakers support digital talent ecosystems, regulatory clarity, and export-oriented service platforms, while organisational leaders institutionalise adaptive strategic processes and purpose-centred cultures. Future research may test the ZSEF across multiple African BPO firms, examine performance implications quantitatively, or explore comparative applications in other emerging-market knowledge industries.
journal: International Journal of Business Ecosystem & Strategy (2687-2293)

title: Quantum-Enhanced DenseNet Architecture for Automated Plant Disease Recognition from Leaf Images
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of plant diseases is super important for boosting crop productivity and cutting down on economic losses. Deep learning models have really nailed image-based disease detection lately, but they face some hurdles like complex feature distributions and class imbalance in ag data sets. This study takes a neat approach to solve those issues – a hybrid quantum-classical deep learning framework. It combines a pretrained DenseNet121 with a Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC). The DenseNet121 grabs key visual features from leaf images, while the quantum part does fancy nonlinear feature transformations in a high-dimensional quantum space. To make the model tougher and more adaptable, the researchers used Mixup augmentation, label smoothing, and balanced sampling when training it. Their tests on the Plant Pathology dataset scored an 89% accuracy overall, with precision, recall, and F1-score coming in at 88%, 87%, and 88%, respectively. So it seems hybrid quantum-classical learning could seriously beef up plant disease classification and maybe even pave the way for smarter ag diagnostic tools in the future

title: Theory of Developer Momentum: The Developer's Experience of Progress and the Craft of Maintaining Motion
abstract: This paper introduces a Theory of Developer Momentum that helps us see the activity of developing software in motion and the skilled craft through which progress unfolds. We define Developer Momentum as the developer's experience of progress and forward motion toward the goal of a task. Our theory disentangles the related constructs of flow state, momentum, and motivation, so we can more clearly see the relationships between them and how they interweave to support progress. In order to make progress, developers build up working context in memory, become immersed in a cognitive puzzle, and gain clarity through motion in uncertain terrain. The theory provides researchers with a rich experiential lens to investigate how developers' cognitive experiences are shifting in emerging AI workflows. Building on prior grounded theory work, we conducted in-depth interviews with a theoretically sampled subset of 12 professional developers, and eight feedback interviews to evaluate resonance and investigate how the theory translates to agentic AI workflows. We followed a Constructivist Grounded Theory approach to construct a theory grounded in empirical data. Our theory contributes a novel paradigm for seeing the motion of developing software at multiple scales and resolutions, seeing the living capacities that support this motion, and expanding what becomes available for improvement, skilled judgment, and craft.

title: T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training
abstract: Muon has recently emerged as a strong optimizer for large language model pretraining by exploiting matrix structure through polar orthogonalization. However, it processes each parameter matrix independently, whereas recent tensor-aware extensions of Muon jointly update groups of eligible matrix parameters through matrix unfoldings. In contrast, we propose T-MUON, a t-SVD-based generalization that groups structurally related Transformer gradients into third-order tensors and defines the corresponding Muon-style update directly through the $M$-transform. We show that the exact T-MUON update is a steepest-descent direction under the $\star_M$-spectral norm and establish a convergence guarantee. Across GPT-2-style and LLaMA-style models from 51M to 1.3B parameters trained on FineWeb and FineWeb-Edu, head-wise T-MUON with the identity transform consistently achieves lower validation perplexity than AdamW, Muon, and variants using DFT, DCT, or DST transforms. These gains persist in additional experiments with longer context lengths and larger token budgets, although the preferred tensorization mode varies across settings.

title: Active rheology shapes collective flows in uniaxially compressed 3D spheroids
abstract: How compression changes both the magnitude and organization of cell motion remains unclear. Using a three-dimensional active vertex model, we examine how tissue state and active dynamics shape the response of confined spheroids to uniaxial compression. With polarity alignment switched off, compression enhances transverse motion in solid-like spheroids throughout the tested activity range, whereas the fluid-like response reverses from acceleration at low activity to slowing at high activity. Changes in contact persistence organize these responses along a common empirical trend. Passive five-cell calculations reveal how compression reshapes local rearrangement barriers: the response depends on geometry and loading direction, and a high-strain increase in the fluid-like mean coexists with many low-barrier paths. In a separate high-alignment regime, strong compression induces coherent rotation in solid-like spheroids, while fluid-like spheroids show no comparable collective rotation. The rotating solids have a higher contact-persistence index than the fluids and exhibit tangential peripheral cell organization. Controlled perturbations reveal compression-induced softening of a differential-twist mode and slower relaxation with activity. Together, these results identify an activity-dependent reversal of the motility response and compression-induced coherent rotation as two distinct outcomes of loading, linking them to contact persistence, local rearrangement costs, and active coordination.

title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents
abstract: AI coworkers must coordinate tools, communicate across turns, and act on changing workspace state while respecting workflow constraints. Constructing training experience for these capabilities requires coherent requests, service records, tool interfaces, and grading checks. We present CoworkEnv, a capability-guided framework for synthesizing executable training environments for AI coworkers. Workflow requirements guide task construction, and programmatic validation with feedback repair checks generated specifications and grading behavior. Teacher executions yield curated demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while student interactions provide rollouts and rewards for reinforcement learning (RL). Using these resources, we train compact PocketWorker models. For Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, SFT raises the mean score from 46.6 to 64.1 on Claw-Eval, including a 31.9-point gain on Multi-turn tasks. An SFT-only extension to ClawMark demonstrates applicability across coworker benchmarks. We further compare RL training dynamics across configurations that vary reward processing and credit assignment. Improving training rewards provide preliminary evidence that the constructed environments support policy optimization.

title: Meta Inverse Prompting for Video Generative Models
abstract: Recent advances in video generative models have enabled flexible conditional generation and editing pipelines, such as text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-guided synthesis. However, these workflows are inherently one-directional, mapping conditions to videos without providing a mechanism to invert this process. In complex media production settings, the ability to recover controllable textual conditions from a given video is highly desirable, yet remains underexplored. While inverse prompting has been studied for image generation, directly extending these approaches to video is challenging due to the need to capture temporal dynamics beyond static appearance, as well as the substantial computational cost of per-video optimization. In this work, we propose the first practical framework for efficient video inverse prompting. Specifically, we formulate inverse prompting as a meta-learning problem and introduce Meta Video Inverse Prompting (MVIP), which learns a meta-prompt optimized over temporal dimensions to enable fast and effective prompt inference. Our approach amortizes the inversion process, eliminating the need for costly iterative optimization at test time. Experimental results demonstrate that MVIP recovers higher-quality inverse prompts with significantly improved reconstruction fidelity compared to image-based inversion and iterative captioning baselines, while achieving substantial gains in efficiency. Code and video results are available at https://ueriniuno.github.io/mvip-page/.

title: MultiAltitudeSR: Multi-Altitude Agricultural UAV Image Super-Resolution via Physical Ground Sampling Distance Conditioning
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) enable high-throughput platforms for crop monitoring but face a fundamental trade-off between flight altitude and image spatial resolution. Many existing super-resolution (SR) methods for UAV imagery rely on oversimplified synthetic degradation models and are restricted to fixed integer upsampling scales, limiting their ability to handle real-world degradations and varying flight altitudes. This study proposes MultiAltitudeSR, a framework that conditions feature modulation and reconstruction on source and target ground sampling distances (GSDs). MultiAltitudeSR trained jointly on real UAV images at altitudes of 10 to 70 m above ground level supports all 21 source-to-target altitude pairs without pair-specific fine-tuning, covering scale factors ranging from 1.18$\times$ to 6.03$\times$. The framework can be extended to additional source-target GSD combinations by incorporating corresponding image pairs into training. On the 20-to-10 m pair, the model achieved competitive perceptual performance compared with pair-specific baselines, with LPIPS of 0.2236, DISTS of 0.2431, and NIQE of 8.9020. Experiments using the same architecture demonstrated the value of acquiring real-world multi-altitude UAV image pairs for SR training, with real-pair training achieving better average reconstruction performance across the 21 altitude pairs than training with the tested synthetic degradation pipeline. Downstream zero-shot segmentation case studies illustrated task-dependent benefits of super-resolved imagery for crop monitoring, suggesting potential UAV flight-time savings through image acquisition at higher altitudes.

title: Block Recursive Transformers for Structured Parameter Sharing
abstract: Recursive Transformers depend not only on how many parameters are shared, but also on how shared parameters are organized across depth. Existing static schemes adopt two extreme reuse topologies: layer-wise repetition, where each layer is reused independently, and global cyclic reuse, where the entire stack is repeatedly applied as a single shared function. We argue that sharing granularity is an important factor in recursive parameter sharing. This study proposes Block Recursive Transformers (BRT), which partition layers into contiguous blocks and recursively reuse each block before moving to the next. This intermediate topology enables local refinement within blocks while preserving depth-wise transitions, without adding routing modules, auxiliary states, or extra training objectives. Across decoder-only models up to 1.7B parameters, with additional encoder-decoder and encoder-only studies, BRT improves validation negative log-likelihood and downstream accuracy over static recursive sharing baselines. Ablations and representation analyses further show that intermediate block granularity better balances local refinement and depth-wise differentiation. Project website: https://aim-skku.github.io/BRT/

title: Pseudodifferential structure, rigidity, and sharpness for the Steklov problem on differential forms
abstract: We resolve four questions concerning Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential forms. First, for $0\leq p\leq n-2$, we prove that the operator is classical pseudodifferential of order one and compute its principal symbol, which is elliptic on the coclosed symbol space. This answers Open Question 7.19 in the survey of Colbois, Girouard, Gordon, and Sher [7]. Second, the symbol calculation yields a Weyl law with remainder $O(τ^{n-2})$, resolving the smooth case of their Open Question 7.23 in [7]. Third, in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$, we show that conformal deformations of the Euclidean ball fixing the boundary metric preserve the full operator. Nonisometric metrics therefore retain all equalities in Karpukhin's initial equality range, disproving the isometry-rigidity assertion of Conjecture 2.12 in [19](the rigidity assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]). Fourth, we establish the all-index sharpness asserted in Conjecture 2.13 in [19](the sharpness assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]) in the class of smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian manifolds with boundary. For $p\geq1$, a shrinking-core construction inspired by the collapsing models of Anné and Takahashi produces manifolds with fixed spherical boundary and explicit two-sided bounds for an initial eigenvalue cluster.

title: Don't Judge an Agent by Its Messages: Private-State Leakage under Passive Monitoring of Agent Communication
abstract: An AI agent can reproduce the distribution of its messages and of the receiver's task outcomes while disclosing private information that the task never required. We ask what a passive audit can certify when the auditor knows the authorised sender and the exact observable law but has no trusted pairing of messages with the private states behind them. For a single round, compatible mutual-information leakage forms a sharp interval, and fixing the entire task-relevant message law, with every declared task utility, can still leave a full private bit undetermined; total leakage is determined if and only if, in every task state, the remaining private state or the authorised message is a deterministic function of that state. For a sender, such as an LLM, that selects among its own responses, we prove that in a balanced case its change to the message law within each task state equals $(1-2^{-k})$ times the honest messages' dependence on the attribute, which also sets, up to a constant, how many messages a monitor needs. With Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on a synthetic routing task, selection among 16 responses lets a public decoder recover a private bit in all 8,192 held-out rounds at 98.60\% routing accuracy (honest sender 98.90\%). A monitor that knows the selection rule reaches AUC 0.645 on single messages, close to the ceiling of 0.671 that honest messages predict, and 0.972 over 16, while generic monitors stay near chance. A law-preserving sender built from the same samples recovers the bit in 97.7\% of rounds, and every monitor without the true bit stays near chance against it. A canonical task interface preserves every receiver decision and bounds the remaining information about a balanced attribute by twice the routing-error rate, even for a receiver that shares a key with the sender. These results distinguish what passive auditing can certify from what restricting communication can enforce.

title: Dynamic Skill-Based Routing for Call Centers with Transfers: A Value-Based Framework
