The Planner teacher supervises which evidence-seeking questions to ask, when to stop gathering evidence, and how to compose the final answer. The Perception teacher supervises the video-grounded answers to those questions. At inference, the student executes this adaptive workflow end-to-end, without external spatial tools. Across three spatial reasoning benchmarks, EgoP$^{2}$C students built from Qwen3-VL-8B and SenseNova-SI-1.3-8B outperform their base models by an average of 9.2 and 7.5 percentage points, respectively. Across both backbones, EgoP$^{2}$C reduces inference FLOPs by 65.8-66.3% and achieves $1.29$-$1.49\times$ speedups over their shared Dual-LoRA teacher.

title: Managing complexity for integrated fusion reactor design using a differentiable graph-based MDAO framework: PROCESS as a case study
abstract: Integrated design of nuclear fusion reactors requires combining an increasingly large number of models from different disciplines self-consistently, with model selection and parametrisation changing between design studies. Manual definition of execution order and solvers for cyclic dependencies is error-prone, inefficient, and inflexible. We propose to use a generic graph-based coordination and execution core that enables automated execution order, cycle detection, and solver architecture specification for any set of models or parametrisation. To this end, a computational dependency graph of purely functional models is extended by a conditional node and nesting edges, treating solvers and optimisers in the same way. A minimal set of graph operations then allows for fine-tuned control on feedback resolution, making both optimiser and solver architectures easily reconfigurable. Existing monolithic multidisciplinary design analysis and optimisation (MDAO) architectures can be recovered by sequentially applying these operations. The cottax package implements this extended dependency graph, graph operations, executability checks, and a JAX-based execution layer. This execution layer eliminates runtime overhead and provides native gradient computation through the whole graph. As a proof of principle, cottax is then applied to the PROCESS systems code. Graph sequencing shows that for PROCESS only three small coupled components need to be solved every optimiser iteration. Monolithic MDAO architectures are then assigned to seven different PROCESS configurations, demonstrating the ease of (re)configuring its architecture. Compared to PROCESS, the sequencing and execution back-end together yield a two to three orders of magnitude reduction in model runtime during optimisation. cottax is currently being considered as the basis for developing an integrated stellarator MDAO framework.

title: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
abstract: AI agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, yet they consume webpages as screenshots or text, exposing their LLMs to unvetted third-party content. Browsers enforce semantics under which what an element can do depends on what it is and where it comes from, not on what it says. Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none. As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does. We propose Intact, which runs on an unmodified browser. Intact builds GenTree, a bespoke representation that captures provenance and web semantics. Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text. Its harness executes each step only within the capabilities of the step's element and asks the user before acting on third-party content. On 1,270 real webpages, GenTree attributes 2.3x as many elements to third parties as the browser, which misattributes 58.7% of them to the first party. On 1,091 of these webpages with injected attacks, only 12.8% of attacks get through Intact's planner, each at most as a consent request, against 73.1% for a conventional planner. Isolation disrupts functionality on only 3.7% of tasks, and a parallel schedule could remove most of its added latency.

title: ACE: An AI-Orchestrated Intrusion Detection and Compliance Mapping Engine
abstract: This study proposes the Automated Compliance Engine (ACE), an AI-orchestrated framework that links intrusion detection, regulatory control mapping, and automated countermeasure deployment for security operations environments. ACE integrates Suricata IDS, a LangGraph five-stage workflow, retrieval-augmented generation, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control retrieval, large language model-based control ranking, and SSH-based Suricata rule deployment. The framework was evaluated in a two-virtual-machine laboratory using eight simulated attack scenarios and three legitimate traffic tests. ACE processed all eight attack alerts, achieved 100% alert detection, 0% false positives across legitimate traffic tests, generated deployable AUTO rules for 37.5% of alerts, verified 100% deployment of generated rules, and achieved an average NIST control-mapping confidence score of 0.87. The DeepEval assessment produced 1.0 scores for answer relevancy and faithfulness, while the hallucination score reflected known LLM-as-judge calibration limitations. The evaluation was conducted in a controlled environment with a limited attack set. Further validation is required using enterprise-scale telemetry, multiple IDS sensors, and an analyst-in-the-loop review. The results demonstrate how AI-assisted security automation can reduce analyst effort in translating IDS alerts into compliance-relevant evidence and defensive actions. ACE contributes an integrated detection-to-compliance-to-response workflow combining IDS telemetry, RAG-based control mapping, and automated rule deployment.

title: GlobeBench: Evaluating Text-Based World Model Capabilities for Scalable Environment Simulations
abstract: Text-based world models have recently shown potential to simulate complex RL environment state transitions for a diverse set of use cases. However, no standardized benchmark exists to compare, study and improve these models. Through this paper, we attempt to solve this problem by building GlobeBench, a novel benchmark with 1,632 tasks across five separate domains and nineteen simulation skills. The tasks check whether models can predict the environment's response to a specific action given the full agent trajectory by understanding earlier state changes, following environment rules, and predicting the effects of actions on both related and unrelated objects. We compare the predicted environment response with an execution-derived reference, using a hybrid architecture with both deterministic gates and a semantic judge. Among 20 general-purpose LLMs and specialized text world models, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest task success rate at 49.57%. We find that model accuracy decreases as actions affect a larger portion of the environment. Specifically, when the agent's changes must propagate to dependent objects, task success drops to an average of 5.1% across all 20 models. Although model strengths differ across tasks, 631 tasks remain unsolved by any model, suggesting a significant gap in general LLM capabilities as a world model.

title: Normalizing Flow Maps
abstract: Scalable approaches to learning neural dynamical systems have placed diffusion, flow matching, and few-step generators in flow maps at the forefront of generative modeling. Such state-of-the-art models have limited access to explicit model densities despite evolving from classical generative modeling approaches that leveraged tractable likelihoods, e.g., Normalizing Flows and Autoregressive models. In this paper, we combine these threads of few-step generation and tractable sample likelihoods and introduce Normalizing Flow Maps (NFM), a class of exactly invertible pushforward maps that generalizes normalizing flows and flow maps. More precisely, NFMs learn the integrator of an underlying dynamical system, but crucially, they provide efficient exact likelihood evaluation by construction. To enable scalable training of NFMs, we derive two complementary axes of consistency inherent to NFMs that yield (self) distillation objectives: (1) pointwise matching, which unlocks $\ell_2$-based flow-map style regression losses, and (2) distributional matching, which matches pushforward distributions to the marginals of a prescribed forward process. On conditional image generation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64, NFMs achieve state-of-the-art sample quality among parameter-matched normalizing flows, while supporting likelihood-based RLHF. For equilibrium sampling in Boltzmann Generators, NFMs outperform prior state-of-the-art normalizing flows on both single-system and transferable peptide benchmarks.

title: LEMON: Equivariant Learning over Attention Maps for Zero-Shot Misbehavior Monitoring on New LLMs
abstract: Large language models exhibit misbehaviors that hinder deployment in high-stakes settings. One approach to monitor such failures is to use an external LLM as a monitor, but this is prohibitively expensive. A well-known and efficient class of monitors can detect such failures from internal representations (such as activation probes), but are tied to the model they were trained on, requiring costly re-annotation as new LLMs appear. A natural way to avoid this repeated annotation cost is to develop internal-representation based monitors that transfer zero-shot across LLMs. However, such transfer is challenging because internal representations are not naturally aligned across models; in particular, attention maps, known to contain signals of misbehavior, may differ in head function, ordering, and model depth. In this work, we characterize those cross-model attention mismatches as algebraic symmetries and use geometric deep learning principles to build LEMON (Language-model Equivariant MOnitoring Network) an online graph neural network-based monitor, whose predictions are invariant under these symmetries. LEMON processes attention maps token-by-token, as they are produced and outputs a score after every token (or every window of $W$ tokens) at negligible cost. Across 16 LLMs and six datasets, in the zero-shot cross-model setting, LEMON outperforms all baselines on both hallucination and jailbreak monitoring tasks, improving over the strongest by up to 14 ROC-AUC points.

title: TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
abstract: Advances in frontier coding agents have sharply increased the token costs of AI-assisted software engineering. Their token efficiency is typically evaluated on isolated tasks, whereas real-world developers use them to continuously build, update, and maintain large-scale projects. This mismatch motivates us to evaluate agents over sequences of realistic coding tasks, where we find that agents exhibit recurring environment-dependent token costs that existing methods struggle to reduce. To minimize these costs, we introduce TokenEconomizer, an external controller that cuts environment-specific token costs over a sequence of tasks. These cuts come from determining (i) which operational micro-skills to inject, (ii) which persistently irrelevant tools to prune, and (iii) when to intervene in unproductive failure loops. Across Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot CLI paired with frontier models, TokenEconomizer reduces the average token cost by 18.4-30.9% with comparable task success. Savings hold in every repository under every tested agent-model setting and generalize to diverse domains such as sequential web development and security auditing, where costs fall by 6.4-21.2% depending on task structure. Our work establishes adaptive black-box cost control as a promising direction for reducing token costs of coding agents in realistic settings.

title: Negative-binomial ensemble filtering for discrete-time Hawkes network reconstruction
abstract: We develop a sequential ensemble filter for reconstructing directed excitation networks from overdispersed multivariate counts observed on a regular time grid. The data-generating model is a discrete-time negative-binomial Hawkes process, for which we prove exact first- and second-moment stability conditions and derive a row-wise sufficient condition. The filter learns the network and the dispersion online, and a row-composition parameter forecast keeps enough ensemble variation to respond to structural change. In synthetic experiments, we demonstrate that a Poisson-based filter provides comparable point-estimate accuracy of the network, while the proposed filter provides substantially better calibrated predictive and parameter uncertainty. Under an abrupt redistribution of influence, the filter recovers connections that are absent before the change. An application to daily property-crime counts in sixteen Chicago community areas gives broadly calibrated one-step predictions and a recovered network consistent with independent temporal and geographic information.

title: An Anatomy-Aware Staged Pipeline for Vessel-Specific Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation in CT and MR Angiography
abstract: The TopAneu 2026 challenge requires intracranial aneurysms to be segmented at the voxel level and assigned to one of more than fifty vessel-specific classes, on CT and MR angiography alike. We address it with a six-stage anatomy-aware pipeline rather than a single segmentation network. A logistic-regression classifier routes each scan to a modality-specific branch; networks segment the vasculature, first as a binary mask and then over the full 36-class arterial taxonomy; a candidate localiser turns raw angiography and vessel priors into suspicious regions; a candidate-centred network segments the lesion in each crop; connected components become instances; and a per-instance classifier assigns each its anatomical location. Two principles organise the design. Whenever an upstream model output becomes a downstream training input it is generated out-of-fold, so no stage trains on unrealistically clean predictions of itself. And the anatomical decision is made once per lesion rather than once per voxel, which fits the data: of 406 connected aneurysm components in the full release, 405 carry exactly one location label. Task 1 is read off the Task 2 mask, making the two consistent by construction. We report stage-wise performance and a five-part ablation isolating what vessel priors and class-aware sampling contribute at each stage.

title: QR CODES: A PATHWAY TO TECH-LED DISSEMINATION OF AGRICULTURAL INFORMATION
abstract: Quick Response (QR) codes have emerged as a powerful tool to bridge the gap betweendigital information and users by providing instant and easy access to online resources. The presentstudy evaluated the effectiveness of QR code-based dissemination of potato extension publicationsand identified demographic factors influencing farmers’ successful access to these digital resources.The study involved 100 farmers from western Uttar Pradesh participating in training programmesorganized at ICAR–Central Potato Research Institute, Regional Station, Modipuram, Uttar Pradesh.QR codes linked to online extension publications were provided to participants and their abilityto access the documents was recorded. Information on age, gender and education was collectedand analysed using binary logistic regression. Overall, 65% of respondents successfully accessedthe QR code publications. The regression model was significant (LR χ2 = 34.04, P < 0.001) with75% prediction accuracy. Age negatively influenced QR code access (P = 0.007), while educationallevel had a significant positive effect (P = 0.015); gender was non-significant. Follow-up assessmentindicated that most respondents found the publications useful, whereas preference for printedmaterials, limited smartphone access and lack of awareness remained important constraints. Thefindings demonstrated the potential of QR codes as a low-cost and scalable tool for agriculturalinformation dissemination.

title: POTATO LATE BLIGHT CAUSED BY PHYTOPHTHORA INFESTANS: BIOLOGY,EPIDEMIOLOGY, CLIMATE CHANGE, AND SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES
abstract: Potato late blight, caused by Phytophthora infestans, remains one of the mostdestructive diseases affecting global potato production, resulting in substantial yield and economiclosses. This review summarizes the pathogen’s biology, disease cycle, epidemiology, host–pathogeninteractions, and current diagnostic approaches, along with major management strategies, includingcultural practices, host resistance, biological control, botanical extracts, chemical control, diseaseforecasting, and integrated disease management. It also highlights the impacts of climate changeon disease distribution and severity, as well as recent advances in molecular breeding, genomeediting, and precision agriculture. Overall, sustainable management of potato late blight requiresintegrating resistant cultivars, environmentally friendly control measures, disease forecasting, andjudicious fungicide use. Continued research on durable resistance, climate-smart management, andemerging biotechnological tools will be essential to enhance potato resilience and ensure futurefood security.

title: DRIVERS OF ICT UTILIZATION AMONG POTATO GROWERS IN GUJARAT: EVIDENCE FROM ABINARY LOGISTIC REGRESSION MODEL
abstract: The adoption of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in agriculture playsa critical role in enhancing farm productivity and improving decision-making. This study examinesthe extent of ICT utilization and its determinants among potato growers in Banaskantha districtof Gujarat using a Binary Logit (BL) model. Primary data were collected from 150 farmers acrossthree talukas, namely Dantiwada, Deesa, and Lakhani. The results indicate that mobile phones,television, and internet services are widely used by farmers, whereas Agricultural InformationServices such as web portals and Kisan Call Centres remain underutilized. The Binary Logit analysisidentifies income (p = 0.000, OR = 96.10), source of information (p = 0.066, OR = 1.461), attitudetowards ICT (p = 0.039, OR = 1.203), and knowledge level (p = 0.001, OR = 2.306) as significantdeterminants influencing ICT adoption. The large odds ratio associated with income reflects theeffect of categorical income measurement rather than a marginal increase in income, highlightingthe importance of financial capacity in facilitating ICT adoption. Model diagnostics indicate a goodfit, as confirmed by the Omnibus Test (χ² = 106.565, p < 0.001) and the Hosmer–Lemeshow test (χ² =5.023, p = 0.755). The model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 84.0%, correctly predicting88.4% of non-adopters and 78.1% of adopters. The findings suggest that strengthening rural ICTinfrastructure, improving digital literacy, and enhancing affordability, along with reinforcing digitalagricultural extension services, are essential for promoting ICT adoption and reducing the digitaldivide among farmers.

title: Climate Misinformation and Media Literacy: A Case Study of Rwanda: A Research Paper
abstract: This paper examines climate misinformation through the case of Rwanda, a country combining high climate vulnerability with a tightly regulated media environment. Drawing on climate science, disaster response, and media-freedom literature, alongside Rwanda-specific data on digital access, literacy, and misinformation literacy from adjacent COVID-19 research, the paper argues that Rwanda's information-control approach appears to reduce measured public exposure to misinformation without a clear basis for concluding that it reduces underlying vulnerability. The analysis further shows that Rwanda's low overall internet and social media penetration, combined with a pronounced urban-rural digital divide, means that radio, community networks, and closed messaging channels such as WhatsApp are likely more consequential vectors for climate misinformation among the agricultural populations most exposed to climate risk than the open social media platforms that dominate existing misinformation research. The paper concludes by identifying the need to measure climate misinformation exposure directly in Rwanda, an evidence gaps the existing literature has not yet filled.
journal: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
pdfUrl: https://iiardjournals.org/get/RJMCIT/VOL. 12 NO. 8 2026/Climate Misinformation and Media Literacy 1-11.pdf

title: Calidad de Vida en Trabajadores de la Salud en México
abstract: Introduction. Quality of life (QoL) among healthcare workers is highly important, as they are the ones responsible for the health of the general population, often under working conditions that are less than optimal in countries such as Mexico. Objective. To analyze and predict the relationship between sociodemographic variables and working conditions with the four domains of the WHOQOL-BREF Questionnaire in healthcare workers in Mexico. Method. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional study with a predictive-correlational scope. The sample consisted of 152 healthcare workers from six Mexican states, selected through non-probability convenience sampling; the instrument was distributed through social media, email, and digital platforms. Results. Of the sociodemographic variables analyzed (marital status, sex, body mass index, work area, and type of contract), none were predictive on their own nor showed significant correlations, with the exception of seniority, which emerged as a robust predictor with a significant positive relationship in the psychological, social relationships, and environmental domains. Likewise, after controlling for the remaining variables in the multiple regression model, single marital status emerged as a significant predictor of lower psychological and social relationships quality of life, and working in the medical area was associated with lower quality of life compared to other healthcare areas. Conclusions. It is recommended that healthcare institutions design differentiated psychosocial support strategies, primarily targeting medical staff and single employees, two groups identified as more vulnerable, as well as strengthen support programs during the first years of service, a period in which perceived quality of life appears to be lower.
journal: Ibero Ciencias - Revista Científica y Académica - ISSN 3072-7197

title: inClinico Agent for clinical trial endpoint prediction and prospective evaluation
Intersectional Trajectories in Physical and Mental Health: A UK Longitudinal Study (2009-2024)
abstract: Health inequalities are often examined through single axes such as class or ethnicity, obscuring how these dimensions interlock. This study applies a longitudinal intersectional approach to examine physical and mental health trajectories across five generations in the UK. We analysed 14 waves of the UK Household Longitudinal Study (2009-2024) using longitudinal Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA). We modelled SF-12 physical and mental health trajectories for 398 intersectional strata defined by gender, ethnicity, occupational class, and generation. Physical health inequalities widened with age, consistent with cumulative disadvantage, while mental health inequalities were more evident among later-born cohorts. The 'Boomer' generation exhibited a relatively flat mental health trajectory across its observed age range. In contrast, 'Generation Z' had lower predicted mental health, particularly among White British women with no work history - a group with poorer predicted trajectories than their South Asian peers. Our study shows how health inequalities are structurally differentiated by cohort and intersectional position. Policy responses should support proportionate universalism, combining broad population-level support with intensified action for groups showing poorer health.

title: ANN-Based sensitivity analysis for the prediction of energy consumption and head rice yield in a pneumatic paddy dryer
abstract: In this study, the performance of a pneumatic paddy dryer was investigated through a sensitivity analysis with an artificial neural network, in order to identify the relative importance of the process variables affecting the energy consumption and head rice yield (HRY). Experiments were conducted using Thai Jasmine 105 paddy rice, which was dried from 24% to 14% wet basis at drying air temperatures of 60°C, 80°C, and 100°C. Increasing the drying air temperature increased the drying rate from 0.46 to 1.11 kgwater/h. Drying at 60°C resulted in the lowest specific energy consumption (SEC) of 3.17 MJ/kgwater and the highest HRY (51.91%), but approximately 6 h was needed to reach the target moisture content for a batch of 20 kg. Higher drying temperatures substantially shortened the drying time but increased the SEC and reduced the HRY to 39.01–41.15%, suggesting a trade-off between drying rate, energy use, and milling quality. The model accurately predicted the moisture content, electrical energy consumption, and HRY, with coefficients of determination (R²) ≥ 0.997 for both the training and testing datasets. Through a sensitivity analysis, the paddy grain temperature (Tpaddy) was identified as the most informative predictor, accounting for approximately 38% of the total relative importance, followed by drying time (32%) and drying air temperature (21%). These findings indicate that Tpaddy provides valuable information on the transient thermal state of the grain, and can serve as a key process variable for forecasting drying behavior. Rather than representing a standalone commercial drying solution, the framework presented here provides a basis for developing multi-stage drying strategies in which rapid pneumatic pre-drying can be followed by tempering or drying at lower temperatures to strike a balance between drying efficiency and HRY.

title: SPECIFIC FEATURES OF MANAGING ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY IMPLEMENTATION IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION
abstract: The article examines the management of environmental policy implementation in agricultural production in the Republic of Tajikistan. The study aims to systematize the institutional conditions and mechanisms for improving the environmental sustainability of agricultural production. It employs systems-based structural and institutional approaches, analysis of government programmes, classification, and logical synthesis of scholarly materials. The principal areas for improving management include preserving soil fertility, using land and water resources rationally, introducing resource-saving technologies and digital monitoring, and developing agroecological practices. The study highlights the need to align environmental requirements with agricultural producers’ economic capacities and to expand investment and advisory support. It concludes that an integrated approach to managing environmental improvements in agricultural production is appropriate, followed by an assessment of the effectiveness of the proposed measures at farm and regional levels.

title: From Copilots to Coworkers: How Autonomous AI Agents Reshape Organizational Roles and Decision Authority: A Structured Integrative Review and Research Agenda
abstract: Autonomous artificial intelligence agents extend generative AI from producing content on demand to pursuing goals through planning, memory, tool use, environmental feedback, and iterative action. This shift matters organizationally because agency is no longer confined to recommendation: systems can increasingly initiate and coordinate consequential work. This article integrates research on AI-enabled work, algorithmic management, organizational design, human–AI collaboration, automation, and responsible AI to explain the transition from copilots to digital coworkers. The review distinguishes five configurations—tool, copilot, teammate, delegate, and coworker—and argues that the central organizational variable is not technical capability alone but the allocation of decision authority. We synthesize evidence showing that AI assistance can improve speed and quality in bounded tasks, often benefiting less experienced workers, while also producing uneven performance at the frontier of model capability. Extending this evidence to agentic systems, we develop an authority allocation matrix based on task risk, reversibility, verifiability, and auditability. We identify three mechanisms through which agents reshape organizations: role reconfiguration, authority redistribution, and coordination redesign. Benefits arise when agents compress search and execution costs, diffuse expertise, and enable new forms of modular organizing. Risks arise when action outpaces verification, responsibility becomes diffused, tacit knowledge erodes, or agents acquire excessive access to organizational resources. We propose a layered governance architecture combining explicit mandates, least-privilege access, execution limits, provenance, continuous monitoring, and human escalation rights. The article concludes with propositions and a research agenda for studying agentic organizing through field experiments, longitudinal process research, digital trace analysis, and comparative institutional designs.

title: Sustainable Destination Management as a Marketing Strategy: The Roles of Destination Image and Perceived Value in Destination Loyalty
abstract: As tourism destinations face increasing competition, destination managers must not only pursue sustainable development but also translate sustainability-oriented practices into effective marketing strategies and favorable market outcomes. Drawing on strategic marketing, destination management, destination image, perceived value, and customer loyalty perspectives, this study examines how tourists’ perceptions of sustainable destination management relate to destination loyalty. Specifically, the study develops and tests a sequential model in which perceived sustainability-oriented destination practices are positively associated with destination image, which in turn is associated with tourists’ perceived value and ultimately with destination loyalty. Using survey responses from 462 tourists in China, the proposed relationships were examined through structural equation modeling. The results indicate significant positive relationships between sustainable destination marketing and destination image, destination image and perceived value, and perceived value and destination loyalty. The sequential indirect association through destination image and perceived value was also statistically significant. The study contributes to management and marketing research by conceptualizing sustainability-oriented destination management as a strategic resource and by identifying a customer-perception pathway through which responsible practices may be connected to marketing outcomes. The findings suggest that sustainability may create strategic value when managers integrate environmental protection, cultural conservation, community interests, and responsible tourism practices with positioning, image management, customer value creation, and relationship marketing. From a managerial perspective, destination management organizations should move beyond treating sustainability solely as an operational or policy objective and consider how credible, visitor-facing sustainability practices can support differentiation, perceived value, customer loyalty, and long-term competitiveness. Because the data were collected through a cross-sectional tourist survey, these relationships should be interpreted as associations rather than as proof of causal effects.

title: Application of Revenue Management Methods in the Tourism Industry
abstract: Revenue management has become an important approach to improving the commercial performance, capacity utilization, and competitiveness of tourism enterprises. This article develops a conceptual model of the interrelated components of revenue management in tourism and explains how these components contribute to decisions concerning demand, distribution, pricing, customer relationships, and the sale of tourism services. The study considers marketing research, the effectiveness of advertising campaigns, tourist loyalty management, the creation and positioning of attractive tourism products, service upgrades and upselling, commission and corporate discount policies, overbooking, ancillary service sales, competitor benchmarking, segmentation of revenue sources, and dynamic pricing. Drawing on a theoretical and methodological analysis of specialist literature and practitioner-oriented materials, these activities are examined as parts of an integrated management system rather than as isolated operational techniques. The analysis distinguishes revenue growth from profitability and emphasizes that price optimization should be considered alongside service quality, distribution costs, customer expectations, and operating constraints. Marketing research supplies information about demand and consumer behavior; segmentation differentiates market opportunities; loyalty initiatives and ancillary services can support customer value; and pricing and availability decisions help align limited capacity with changing demand. The proposed component model identifies functional connections among these activities and offers a structure for tourism enterprises seeking to coordinate commercial decisions more systematically. The article also discusses possible operational risks, particularly the consequences of poorly managed overbooking and inappropriate pricing or discount decisions. It argues that revenue management is not merely the adjustment of prices, but a coordinated managerial process that combines market intelligence, forecasting, product development, customer relationships, channel management, and performance monitoring. The findings are conceptual and should not be interpreted as evidence of a measured causal improvement in profit at particular enterprises. Further empirical research is needed to test how the proposed components interact across different types of tourism businesses and market conditions.

title: Beyond Conventional Fertilization: Integrating Soil Stoichiometry, Microbiomes and Crop Demand for Sustainable Nutrient Management
abstract: Synthetic fertilisers have supported modern crop production, but nutrient use efficiency remains constrained by losses, nutrient imbalances and the biological processes that regulate nutrient availability. This review examines sustainable nutrient management by integrating three complementary perspectives: soil ecological stoichiometry, soil and rhizosphere microbiomes, and dynamic crop nutrient demand. It synthesises evidence showing that carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus ratios influence microbial growth, nutrient immobilisation and mineralisation, while microbial communities regulate nitrogen transformations, phosphorus mobilisation and root access to nutrients. Crop nutrient requirements are shown to vary with genotype, phenological stage and root acquisition traits, making temporal and spatial synchrony between nutrient supply and crop demand essential. The review also evaluates microbial inoculants, organic amendments and precision nutrient-management approaches, emphasising that their effectiveness depends strongly on soil conditions, resource balance and biological context. An integrated diagnose–amplify–deliver framework is presented in which soil and microbial diagnostics guide the strengthening of biological nutrient supply and the targeted delivery of mineral nutrients according to crop demand. The synthesis indicates that this approach could improve nutrient use efficiency while reducing unnecessary nutrient surpluses, although its practical application requires locally calibrated indicators, field validation, reliable microbiome interventions and accessible decision-support tools. The framework also recognises contrasting regional priorities, from reducing excessive nutrient inputs to rebuilding fertility in nutrient-depleted systems.

title: Assessing the Economic Impact of Climate Change on Cocoa Production in Osun State, Nigeria
abstract: Nigeria ranked among the world's four leading cocoa producers in 2021, with estimated output of between 250,000 and 300,000 metric tonnes, which contributed significantly to the country's non-oil export earnings. The southern states of Ondo, Cross River, Osun, Ekiti, Edo and Oyo are the main production areas. However, the sector has faced challenges such as low productivity, ageing trees and declining yields relative to those of regional peers. Among the effects of climate change experienced by Nigerian cocoa farmers are irregular rainfall, prolonged dry periods and greater pest and disease pressure on cocoa trees. These pressures have contributed to lower yields and deterioration in bean quality. Multiple linear regression was employed to identify climatic variables showing significant associations with cocoa yield. To investigate climate-related changes in cocoa production in the study area, downscaled outputs from six global circulation models (GCMs) were used. Climate and crop-yield simulations covered three periods: 1976–2005 (historical), 2021–2050 (mid-term) and 2071–2100 (long-term), under the RCP 4.5 emissions scenario. Fig. 5 illustrates the projected future changes in cocoa yield under RCP 4.5. For the study area, the GCM ensemble indicated annual yield reductions of 13,696 tonnes/year by 2050 and 20,004 tonnes/year by 2100. If these ensemble projections materialise, the resulting losses are estimated at approximately US$60,947,200 in 2050 and US$89,017,800 in 2100, respectively, on the assumption of a cocoa price of US$4,450 per tonne. Farmers should implement effective adaptation measures to limit the effects of future climate change on cocoa yield, with necessary inputs, including fungicides and pesticides, supplied to control cocoa black pod disease.

title: Single-Cell Resolution Mapping of Osteoarthritis-Associated Chondrocyte Dynamics Using a High-Density CMOS MEA Platform.
abstract: Fibrosis is a major cause of chronic tissue dysfunction and contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality worldwide. Osteoarthritis (OA), affecting over 590 million people, is a prevalent fibrotic joint disease for which disease-modifying therapies remain lacking, partly because disease progression remains incompletely understood. As human-relevant in vitro models, including organ-on-chip and microphysiological systems, become increasingly important, non-invasive technologies capable of continuous cellular monitoring are urgently needed. Here, we implement high-density complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) multielectrode array (MEA)-based impedance profiling as a label-free platform for longitudinal assessment of OA-relevant chondrocyte remodeling. Human primary chondrocytes cultured on CMOS-MEA chips exhibited impedance increases that correlated with electrode occupancy and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. Spatial impedance mapping enabled visualization of injury-response dynamics, while oxidative stress induced progressive impedance decline accompanied by apoptosis, morphological remodeling, and chondrocyte dedifferentiation, evidenced by reduced collagen II and SOX9 expression and increased collagen I expression. In contrast, osteogenic de-differentiation produced increased impedance associated with ECM remodeling and matrix mineralization. Together, these findings support high-density CMOS-MEA impedance profiling as a non-invasive approach for monitoring cellular remodeling and provide a foundation for future integration of spatially resolved impedance sensing into advanced microphysiological systems for OA and other fibrotic diseases.

title: Distribution of doublecortin in the developing retina of birds: A comparative analysis.
abstract: The avian retina presents an elegant and highly accessible model for investigating the spatial and temporal dynamics of neurogenesis within the central nervous system. In recent years, the microtubule cytoskeleton has emerged not merely as a structural scaffold, but as a dynamic regulator of the transition of a morphologically homogeneous pool of multipotent progenitor cells to postmitotic neurons. Doublecortin (DCX) is a microtubule-associated protein broadly recognized for its fundamental roles in neuronal migration, differentiation, and structural plasticity within the developing nervous system. While its roles in the brain are well-documented, the precise spatiotemporal distribution of DCX in the developing retina of birds remains poorly understood. In this study we investigated the expression pattern of DCX during embryonic development of the retina of one altricial (zebra finch, Taeniopygia guttata) and two precocial (chicken, Gallus gallus; Japanese quail, Coturnix coturnix) bird species using immunohistochemical techniques. Our results demonstrated that the onset of DCX expression coincided chronotopographically with the onset of neurogenesis in the developing retina. In these early stages, DCX expression is tightly colocalized with the neuronal marker class III β-tubulin. As retinal histogenesis progressed to more advanced stages, DCX expression persisted and segregated into specific subsets of ganglion, amacrine, and horizontal cells. Furthermore, prominent immunoreactivity was maintained within the ciliary marginal zone (CMZ), highlighting its association with late-stage retinal progenitors and ongoing neurogenesis. These findings reveal a conserved spatiotemporal expression pattern of DCX across diverse avian species. Furthermore, it suggests that some elements of the cytoskeleton and its associated regulatory proteins form a functional continuous biological continuum: first acting as drivers of neurogenesis and migration and, subsequently, transitioning into structural stabilizers that lock in and maintain the complex morphology of fully differentiated, mature retinal neurons.

title: Bayesian Multivariate Two‐Stage Volatility‐Return Models (MTS‐VR)
abstract: This paper develops a class of models to capture the joint dynamics of asset returns and multivariate volatility. Owing to its two‐stage construction, this class is referred to as the multivariate two‐stage volatility‐return (MTS‐VR) model. The first stage of the MTS‐VR model focuses on modelling the dynamic trend of the multivariate stochastic volatility process. This stage is constructed by calibrating the model using time‐varying covariance matrices, which are estimated from multiple financial asset return series. Within this component of the MTS‐VR framework, we propose two new classes of dynamic volatility models formulated under a Bayesian paradigm. The first class directly models the stochastic dynamics of the covariance matrix, whereas the second separately models each asset's stochastic volatility and the dynamics of the correlation structure. The second stage of the MTS‐VR model involves the modelling of the multivariate asset returns profiles, conditional on the trend model of the multivariate volatility dynamic obtained from Stage 1. This involves a class of multivariate Student‐ t stochastic models, conditionally driven by the volatility dynamic of Stage 1 and a return trend process. We evaluate the performance of the proposed models using both simulated and financial data. The models are implemented in Rtan within a Bayesian framework. The simulation study examines the effect of the degrees of freedom parameter of the Wishart distribution in the data‐generating process. In the empirical application, the second model specification is preferred based on its superior performance.

title: Mixed Cropping of Narrow‐Leaved Lupin With Oat Improves Grain‐Yield Stability Across Five European Locations
abstract: Pulse x cereal mixtures are promoted to stabilise yield and reduce fertiliser dependence, yet robust multienvironment evidence for narrow‐leaved lupin (NLL, Lupinus angustifolius ) × oat ( Avena sativa ) mixed cropping remains scarce. We tested whether NLL × oat mixtures maintain productivity while enhancing grain‐yield stability. A randomised complete block design (four blocks) evaluated three NLL and three oat varieties grown in pure stands and as all nine pairwise mixtures with a replacement design (NLL 90%, oat 10% of pure‐stand density). The experiments ran for 13 environment‐years across five European locations. Productivity was summarised with land equivalent ratio (LER) and crop performance ratio (CPR). Yield stability was assessed using (i) the coefficient of variation (CV), (ii) Finlay–Wilkinson regression slope b 1 and Eberhart–Russell deviation variance (S 2 di ), and (iii) additive main effects and multiplicative interaction‐derived weighted average of absolute scores (AMMI‐WAAS). Mixed‐effects models were used to assess mixed cropping effects. Across environments, LER did not differ from unity (LER = 1) whether fertilised or unfertilised oat monocultures were the reference. By contrast, total CPR and oat‐specific CPR consistently exceeded 1 (mean CPR = 5.3; CPR_N = 4.6), indicating system‐level gains driven by the oat component without penalising NLL. While CVs did not separate treatments, many mixtures and pure stands were environmentally responsive, but the most stable mixtures combined near‐average responsiveness with very low variation and sensitivity to the environmental conditions (Bison × Probor and Troll × Jowisz). Lastly, fertilised oat monocultures were more stable than unfertilised counterparts. Stability gains arose from reduced environmental sensitivity of the mixture rather than the individual variety, underscoring the need to evaluate mixtures directly rather than inferring stability from monocultures. Our results support deploying pulse‐centric cereal × legume mixtures as a pragmatic option to buffer climate variability while sustaining protein‐rich production.

title: Accuracy of Machine Learning in Differential Diagnosis of Multiple System Atrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is frequently misdiagnosed as Parkinson's disease (PD) or progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), posing significant diagnostic challenges. OBJECTIVE The aim of the study was to systematically evaluate the efficacy of machine learning (ML) in differentiating MSA from other neurodegenerative disorders. METHODS We conducted a systematic search in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (up to July 5, 2025), including ML-based MSA diagnostic studies. QUADAS-2 assessed bias risk, and a bivariate mixed-effects model synthesized diagnostic metrics. RESULTS A total of 51 studies (comprising 3595 MSA patients and 18,189 total cases) were included in the systematic review. Of these, 38 studies contributed to the quantitative synthesis, whereas the remaining 13 studies were summarized qualitatively. In the primary analysis comparing MSA with PD, the pooled sensitivity was 0.86 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.81-0.90), specificity 0.87 (95% CI: 0.83-0.90), and the area under the summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve (AUC) 0.93 (95% CI: 0.90-0.95). Overall, pooled sensitivity was 0.85 (95% CI: 0.82-0.88), specificity 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89-0.94), and AUC 0.94 (95% CI: 0.92-0.96). Positron emission tomography (PET)-based models achieved optimal performance (sensitivity: 0.90, specificity: 0.96, AUC: 0.97), whereas deep learning models outperformed others (sensitivity: 0.93, specificity: 0.98, AUC: 0.99). CONCLUSION ML models integrating PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy for MSA. Future work should prioritize prospective multicenter validation and standardized external testing to facilitate clinical implementation.

title: 3D Microfluidic Networks Formed by Mechanically Guided Compressive Buckling for Large-Scale Perfused Tissue Culture.
abstract: Engineered tissues and organoids offer transformative potential for drug screening and regenerative medicine, yet their application is constrained by limited size and slow maturation. Despite the development of various channel networks for large-scale engineered tissue perfusion culture, achieving sufficiently dense, architecturally complex networks with microscale channels in large-scale matrix has remained challenging. In this work, we introduce a design and fabrication strategy for creating intricate three-dimensional microfluidic networks (3D MFNs) within centimeter-scale cell-laden hydrogels using sacrificial 3D-assembled templates. A theoretical model was established to inversely design 3D MFNs with target architectures by optimizing the two-dimensional (2D) geometries of precursor structures and applying compressive strains for mechanically-guided 3D assembly. Multiple types of 3D MFNs were presented, including interconnected ribbons, ribbon-film hybrids, and multilayer networks. In particular, a dendritic MFN template was embedded within a 1-centimeter cell-laden 12 wt.% GelMA hydrogel, where template dissolution yielded robust microchannels that enabled efficient nutrient transport and supported cell survival and differentiation in vitro. Moreover, when implanted in vivo, the dendritic MFN functioned as a passageway for nutrient delivery and endogenous cell migration into the hydrogel, significantly enhancing cell survival. This strategy provides a versatile platform for large-scale 3D tissue culture and targeted tissue differentiation.

title: Understanding environmental adaptation in intermediate wheatgrass.
abstract: Intermediate wheatgrass (IWG; Thinopyrum intermedium) is a perennial grain crop that offers many environmental benefits through extensive root systems in addition to food production. IWG's distribution across broad environmental gradients in Eurasia provides a model system for studying climate adaptation genetics essential for developing climate‐resilient varieties, and exploring this can help provide opportunities for allele mining and population improvement for breeding programs. Genome–environment association methods were used to explore 296 georeferenced accessions genotyped with 17,797 single‐nucleotide polymorphisms across 19 bioclimatic variables. An environmental genome‐wide association identified 10 associations (p < 2.8 × 10− 6, genome‐wide Bonferroni correction) with large individual effects (R 2 = 6.1%–10.4%, mean = 8.2%), indicating oligogenic genetic architecture was characteristic of climate adaptation traits. Two‐way analysis of variance testing genotype × cluster interactions revealed predominantly parallel adaptation, with 75.8% of associations showing consistent allelic effects across genetic backgrounds. The combination of large‐effect loci and consistent allelic effects across clusters enables many different breeding strategies that can focus on distinct markers associated with temperature adaptation, precipitation adaptation, or improving specific clusters that show resilience.

Virtual reality (bio-)markers differentiate ADHD from depression and controls.
abstract: The heterogeneity of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and its symptom overlap with other mental disorders limit the clinical utility of isolated diagnostic markers. Virtual reality (VR)-based paradigms offer potential to aid individual diagnostic decisions. This study investigated the diagnostic value of classification models based on multimodal data derived from a virtual email sorting task (VEST). Data were pooled from two studies and used to distinguish unmedicated participants with ADHD (n = 43) from medicated participants with ADHD (n = 23), participants with major depressive disorder (MDD, n = 16), and control participants (n = 21). During the VEST, objective measures of task performance, head actigraphy, and eye tracking were recorded. Subjective data were obtained by assessing task-related ADHD symptoms. Using nested cross-validation, support vector machines were trained and tested, comparing model performance between objective, subjective and combined parameters. The highest balanced accuracy for the classification of participants with ADHD versus control participants (0.85) was achieved by a single-feature model using self-reported inattentiveness. Participants with ADHD and MDD were differentiated with 0.75 balanced accuracy using a 13-feature model combining subjective and objective measures. A 13-feature model derived exclusively from objective measures yielded 0.64 balanced accuracy for the differentiation of medicated versus unmedicated participants with ADHD yet did not perform significantly above chance level. These findings underscore the potential of VR-based multimodal assessments and machine learning to advance precision diagnostics and highlight the utility of self-report measures to detect ADHD while demonstrating the diagnostic potential of objective measures to distinguish disorders and capture medication effects.

Hybrid deep ensemble learning for crop disease prediction and climate-resilient disaster management in smart agriculture
abstract: Accurate crop disease prediction and climate-resilient disaster management are essential for improving agricultural productivity and ensuring food security under increasingly dynamic environmental conditions. Existing deep learning approaches typically perform crop disease detection and climate forecasting independently and often rely on deterministic CNN–LSTM architectures without effective multimodal feature fusion, predictive uncertainty estimation, or comprehensive statistical validation. Consequently, their ability to provide reliable decision support under changing climatic conditions remains limited. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel hybrid deep ensemble learning framework for integrated crop disease prediction and climate-resilient disaster management in smart agriculture. The proposed framework combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial crop image feature extraction with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for temporal climate forecasting. An attention-based multimodal feature fusion mechanism is employed to integrate heterogeneous crop and climate information, while Bayesian uncertainty estimation and deep ensemble learning are incorporated to improve prediction reliability, robustness, and confidence-aware decision support. Experimental evaluation is performed using multimodal datasets comprising crop images and climate observations collected from the PlantVillage, NOAA, and NASA EOS datasets. The dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using a 70:15:15 ratio. The proposed framework is evaluated using classification and regression metrics, including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and AUC-ROC. To ensure reproducibility, all experiments are repeated five times using different random seeds, and the results are reported with mean \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\pm$$\end{document} standard deviation, 95% confidence intervals, and paired Student’s \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$t$$\end{document}-tests. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms conventional CNN, LSTM, and CNN–LSTM hybrid models by achieving higher classification accuracy, lower climate forecasting error, improved robustness under varying climate conditions, and statistically significant performance improvements. The proposed framework provides a reliable, scalable, and uncertainty-aware solution for intelligent climate-resilient smart agriculture and early agricultural disaster management.

title: Supporting the implementation of a conservation action plan for three sympatric hoverflies
abstract: Hoverflies (Diptera: Syrphidae) are important pollinators, benefiting up to 30% of crops produced globally. However, the populations of specialist hoverfly species are particularly vulnerable. For example, some species in the genus Neoascia likely depend on Butterbur (Petasites hybridus) plants for reproduction, making them vulnerable to habitat loss. We aim to: (1) study the distribution of the three Butterbur-dependent fen flies, Neoascia annexa (Müller 1776), Neoascia obliqua (Coe 1940); and the globally endangered Neoascia unifasciata (Strobl 1898) in Luxembourg, and (2) identify variables that affect their encounter rates (individuals caught/hour). From April to June 2025, we sampled 54 Butterbur stands in Luxembourg and the Greater Region (cross-border regions of Belgium, France, and Germany). We collected data on five local and six landscape variables at six spatial scales, analyzing them with generalized linear mixed-effects models. We found that all three species are more widely distributed than previously thought, and that Butterbur stand area was the strongest positive predictor of combined fen fly encounter rates. For N. unifasciata, encounter rate was also positively associated with that of the other two species (but not the other way around) and canopy openness. Protecting and restoring Butterbur stands, while ensuring a sufficient light regime in alluvial forests, will likely bring conservation benefits for these specialized species. Our data will inform the implementation of the conservation action plan of N. unifasciata, bridging the gap between conservation knowledge and action while benefiting other species relying on Butterbur, such as N. annexa and N. obliqua.

Seasonal lags and legacy effects on vegetation cover and carbon uptake in Kuwait from 2014 to 2024: A MODIS GPP–ET–NDVI analysis
abstract: Remote sensing provides a consistent framework for quantifying vegetation dynamics in hyper-arid environments where field observations are sparse. This study integrated MODIS-derived gross primary productivity (GPP), evapotranspiration (ET), and normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) with GPM IMERG precipitation to evaluate seasonal variability, carbon–water coupling, rainfall-response lags, and cumulative hydroclimatic controls across Kuwait during 2014–2024. Vegetation activity peaked in spring, when mean GPP reached 2.25 ± 0.41 g C m⁻² d⁻¹ and NDVI 0.26 ± 0.05, compared with 0.92 ± 0.21 g C m⁻² d⁻¹ and 0.12 ± 0.03 in summer. ET was strongly associated with GPP (R² = 0.680, p < 0.001) and NDVI (R² = 0.533, p < 0.001), whereas same-month precipitation explained substantially less variation in GPP (R² = 0.189, p = 0.003) and NDVI (R² = 0.081, p = 0.061). Cross-correlation analysis showed that both vegetation indicators responded strongly when rainfall preceded vegetation activity by one month (GPP: r = 0.711; NDVI: r = 0.678; both p < 0.001), with the NDVI response persisting longer than GPP. At the cumulative interannual scale, ET remained significantly associated with GPP (R² = 0.524, p = 0.012) and NDVI (R² = 0.630, p = 0.004), whereas cumulative precipitation was not significant. These findings demonstrate that vegetation dynamics in Kuwait are better characterized by ecosystem water use and antecedent rainfall than by contemporaneous or cumulative precipitation alone, highlighting the importance of rainfall timing and short-term hydroclimatic legacy effects in hyper-arid ecosystems.

title: Active Control of Random Vibration in Composite Laminated Thin Plates with MFC Patches
Automated Inventory Management and Quality Assessment of Ornamental Nursery Crops Using End-to-End Deep Learning
abstract: Ornamental crop production is a rapidly developing sector of US agriculture. Accurate inventory management and quality assessment are critical tasks for monitoring sales, yield, space requirements, production timing, and quality improvements of ornamental nurseries. Current inventory practices rely on manual counting, which is labor-intensive and often inaccurate. This study develops an automated system for plant counting and quality assessment of container nursery stock. An unmanned teleoperated ground vehicle, “NurseryBot,” was developed for plant counting and quality assessment of container nursery stock. The NurseryBot utilized RGB cameras to collect video data from a downward-facing perspective. A deep learning framework based on YOLOv11 model variants was trained and tested on a panoramic dataset to detect and segment plants efficiently. Cross-species knowledge adaptation approaches were explored to improve segmentation generalization. Morphological parameters, including area, perimeter, eccentricity, and circularity, were extracted to systematically evaluate plant quality using image-based parameters. The YOLOv11-m instance segmentation model showed the highest precision, recall, and counting accuracy among the evaluated variants for plant detection and segmentation. For bounding boxes, the model attained precision, recall, and mAP50 values of 0.971, 0.970, and 0.941 for azalea and 0.968, 0.966, and 0.915 for sunshine, respectively. For mask segmentation, the model achieved precision, recall, and mAP50 values of 0.969, 0.968, and 0.901 for azalea and 0.967, 0.966, and 0.907 for sunshine, respectively. The proposed system achieved counting accuracies of 95.59% for azalea plants and 95.37% for sunshine plants. This study demonstrates an end-to-end robotic and deep learning-based system for automated inventory counting and plant quality assessment in container nurseries. The proposed approach provides an accurate alternative to manual inventory practices under the nursery conditions evaluated in this study. This technology provides growers and researchers with an efficient way to accurately maintain inventory counts and assess plant quality.

title: Bayesian assessment of return levels for observed temperature extremes across Odisha in India
abstract: Temperature-extreme risk is often assessed through trend-based indices, but regional climate-risk planning also requires uncertainty-aware estimates of rare thermal events and their spatial variability. This study presents a grid-wise Bayesian extreme-value assessment of observed temperature extremes over Odisha, India, using IMD daily maximum and minimum temperature data for 1951–2024. Annual and seasonal hot-day, warm-night, and cold-night block-extreme series were constructed for retained 1° × 1° grid cells. Stationary and nonstationary generalized extreme value models were fitted independently to each grid-series combination, with standardized time, ENSO, and IOD covariates evaluated as predictors of the location parameter. Model selection prioritized diagnostically clean candidates, retaining explicit cautions where needed; posterior 10-, 20-, and 50-year return levels were estimated for early and recent climate states. Of 30 Odisha-overlap grids, 28 were model-ready (93.3% spatial model-ready support); all 140 selected grid-series fits yielded numerically valid return levels. Annual and March–June daytime maxima were nearly identical, confirming concentration of annual hot-day extremes within the extended pre-monsoon heat season. The recent spatial median 50-year TXx MAMJ return level was 43.81 °C; selected stationary M0 models impose zero early-to-recent change. Warm-night extremes showed stronger time-varying model support, and recent TNx JJAS return levels were lower than early-period values. Common-M1 sensitivity indicated small positive but generally uncertain TXx changes, coherent negative TNx changes among eligible fits, and near-zero/mixed TNn changes. Within diagnostically eligible matched support, negative TNx coefficients persisted in the 1951–2007 sensitivity (12/12 Annual; 19/19 JJAS grids). Teleconnection-supported models were sparse and showed mixed coefficient evidence. Return levels provide conditional fitted-tail summaries of observed extremes, not deterministic forecasts.

title: Comparative genomics of seed dormancy using Brachypodium distachyon as a model for temperate cereals
abstract: Seed dormancy is a natural mechanism that delays germination until conditions are most suitable. Previous studies have shown that phylogenies and environmental conditions shape the evolutionary trajectories of seed dormancy, making it an interesting subject for comparative genomics analysis between the dicot model plant Arabidopsis thaliana (Arabidopsis), the tropical cereal crop rice (Oryza sativa), and Brachypodium distachyon (Brachypodium), the monocot model plant for temperate grasses, which include important cereal crops like wheat, barley, and oat. We curated genes with known functions in seed dormancy and compared their evolutionary relationships between Arabidopsis, rice, and Brachypodium (accession Bd21), highlighting conserved central hormonal pathways while also revealing gene loss and duplication events. The Brachypodium genome encodes conserved components of major pathways regulating seed dormancy induction, maintenance and release, most notably seed covering-mediated dormancy imposition, plant hormones (ABA, GA, Auxin, Ethylene, Jasmonate, Brassinosteroids) metabolism and signalling, environmental signals (temperature, light and nutrient) perception and integration. Major seed dormancy genes, including MFT, MKK3, Sdr4, AlaAT and DOG1, show high homology between cereal species while lacking similar roles in Arabidopsis in some cases. Overall, our results indicate a conserved mechanism governing seed dormancy via the central hormonal pathways integrating diverse environmental cues through coordinated molecular components.

A dataset of differentiable biologically derived single-neuron models
abstract: Biological neural networks contain diverse cell types with heterogeneous electrophysiological properties. Artificial neural networks (ANNs) model computational aspects of biology but use homogeneous neurons, limiting realism. A key obstacle to building bio-inspired ANNs is the absence of a database of neuron models that both fit biological data and remain differentiable for gradient-based learning. We present such a database: over 1,000 differentiable single-neuron firing-rate models with accompanying PyTorch code. The models belong to the linear-nonlinear (LN) class, which, for ease of reference, we term generalized firing rate (GFR) neurons. Each GFR neuron uses input and firing-rate history filters across multiple timescales, followed by a nonlinearity to generate firing rates. Models are fit to patch-clamp recordings from mouse and human central nervous system slices. Parameter clustering reflects electrophysiological diversity and partially aligns with transgenic lines. This resource will enable development of bio-inspired ANNs built from biologically grounded, differentiable single-neuron models.

title: Straw-to-biochar shift in alternate wetting and drying paddies: Unlocking carbon sequestration and net GWP reduction synergies
Global modelling of atmospheric lead (Pb) concentrations and health risks during 2000-2019.
abstract: Atmospheric lead (Pb) is a persistent toxic heavy metal that endangers global ecological and public health. Despite extensive regional Pb pollution investigations, the long-term global spatiotemporal evolution and health impacts of particle-bound Pb during 2000-2019 remain insufficiently clarified. Here, we constructed a refined global Pb emission inventory and adopted the GEOS-Chem model to comprehensively simulate global Pb spatiotemporal variations across eight typical regions for the first time, followed by a quantitative assessment of Pb-related carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic health risks for adults and children. The correlation of simulations and observations reaches 0.82, indicating the robust modelling results. The results exhibited profoundly uneven global Pb distributions, with China dominating the highest pollution levels (15.3 ± 11.7 ng/m3), while developed and low-industrialized regions maintained relatively low concentrations. Distinct hemispheric seasonal discrepancies were identified: Northern Hemisphere regions peaked in boreal winter due to heating emissions and stable boundary layer trapping, whereas Southern Hemisphere Pb maxima occurred in austral autumn derived from biomass burning. A universal global Pb turning point emerged in 2013, with concentrations rising during 2000-2013 and declining afterward. Strict emission controls reversed China's growing Pb pollution, while continuous increases prevailed in India, Sub-Sahara Africa (SSA) and South America (SA), revealing a clear pollution shift from developed to emerging industrial regions. Children and adults did not show significant non-carcinogenic risks though East and South Asia as primary health hotspots. This study clarifies the differentiated mechanisms and health implications of global Pb pollution, providing reliable support for targeted global heavy metal risk prevention and control.

title: Integrated evidence-based assessment of in vitro and in vivo data supports that the effects of phenmedipham in Xenopus laevis are consistent with generalised toxicity rather than thyroid disruption.
abstract: Phenmedipham (PMP), an herbicide registered for various crops across different geographies, is under re-approval in Europe and should be evaluated for potential endocrine-disrupting properties according to the current legislation on pesticide active substances. This paper describes an evidence-based assessment of potential thyroid-mediated effects of PMP in Xenopus laevis as model species for thyroid modality. As an indication of thyroid activity, rat thyroperoxidase inhibition was reported in a single in vitro assay in the US-EPA ToxCast database. The results of a 27-day Extended Amphibian Metamorphosis Assay with X. laevis showed very little evidence of the consequences of potential thyroperoxidase inhibition in vivo. A minor non-statistically significant delay of 0.76 days in the mean time to reach metamorphic climax was estimated for tadpoles from the highest treatment group (0.5 mg/L) which reached the metamorphic climax at a significantly lower rate over time compared to control. As it is within the historical control data variability (± 2.72 days), the estimated developmental delay of 0.76 days is not adverse for individuals, and no population-level impact is therefore expected in field. Other statistically significant low-magnitude effects (e.g. ≤ 4.2 % for reduced survival and growth) were observed at the highest PMP concentration at study termination. Minor statistically significant histopathological changes in the thyroid of tadpoles from the highest treatment group could be explained by the effects on developmental timing. Overall, the response pattern observed in X. laevis was consistent with generalised toxicity and thus, PMP does not meet the endocrine disruption identification criteria for thyroid modality.
