title: Active Acoustic Probes for AI Voice Call Detection
abstract: AI voice calls are making it increasingly practical to impersonate people during live audio conversations, whether through voice cloning, real-time conversion, or autonomous voice agents. Current defenses remain mostly passive: they inspect received audio for artifacts created by current generators, which locks defenders into an arms race structurally favoring the attacker. Active defenses invert this dynamic by injecting fresh evidence during the call, but they typically require the remote speaker to cooperate by performing a challenge task. We propose an active acoustic probe that requires no such cooperation: it verifies whether the returned audio traversed a genuine physical speaker-to-microphone path. During a call, the verifier sends a brief high-frequency acoustic challenge and checks whether it survives in the returned audio. Normal physical paths preserve the challenge, whereas the tested voice-conversion paths suppress it. This yields a simple, explainable signal-processing rule calibrated only on normal physical-path recordings. The probe is correctly detected in 99% of trials across diverse consumer audio form factors, from open laptop/phone playback to ear-worn headphones and earbuds, while all 200 outputs from four tested speech-to-speech and voice-conversion configurations fail the detector.
journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Workshop on Deepfake, Deception, and Disinformation Security

title: PAX3::FOXO1 and the INO80 complex sustain replication fork progression in fusion positive rhabdomyosarcoma.
abstract: Transcription factor fusions are recurrent drivers of sarcomas and other cancers, but their oncogenic reorganization of chromatin is difficult to target. One such fusion, PAX3::FOXO1, drives an aggressive subset of pediatric rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) through chromatin remodeling, blocking terminal differentiation and sustaining proliferation. We hypothesized that identifying PAX3::FOXO1 genetic dependencies would reveal new facets of transcription factor fusion biology. We report an unexpected role for PAX3::FOXO1 in driving DNA replication fork progression, uncovered by its dependence on the INO80 chromatin remodeling complex (INO80c). Loss of the INO80c member UCHL5 reduces the competitive fitness of fusion positive (FP), but not fusion negative (FN) RMS cell lines, and is accompanied by reduced DNA replication fork speed. UCHL5 is required to maintain the N-terminal subdomain of INO80c, but a catalytically dead UCHL5 is sufficient to rescue complex formation, fork progression, and FP-RMS fitness. Similarly, loss of PAX3::FOXO1 rapidly leads to RPA32 foci and slows DNA fork progression. These findings demonstrate that PAX3::FOXO1 and INO80c are each critical to maintain replication fork progression in FP-RMS, a novel function for this transcription factor fusion. Implications: PAX3::FOXO1 and the N-terminal INO80 complex are both required to drive replication fork progression in FP-RMS, offering a counterpoint to models in which fusion oncogenes drive replication stress, and identifying INO80 complex members as a genetic dependency in FP-RMS cells.

title: Analysis of Cytogenetic Biodiversity in Little Millet
abstract: This work presents an extensive somatic karyotype analysis of ten accessions of Panicum sumatrense (Little Millet), a minor yet genetically valuable tetraploid crop (2n = 4x = 36) known for its high resilience to abiotic stress. Accessions were obtained from the National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR), New Delhi, and analysed using standardised cytogenetic methodologies. Using the method described by Levan et al. (1964), chromosomes were grouped by length and arm ratio. Karyotype symmetry was assessed according to the classification system proposed by Stebbins (1958). Three-dimensional idiograms were created to show how the volume of different accessions changes. All accessions exhibited 1A symmetrical karyotypes, characterised by predominantly metacentric chromosomes. Even though the number of chromosomes was the same in all accessions, there was considerable variation among them in total chromatin length, centromeric index, gradient index, symmetry index, and volumetric metrics, including chromatid radius and chromosomal volume. These differences indicate structural chromosomal polymorphism among accessions, suggesting genomic diversity. This basic cytogenetic investigation reveals chromosomal variability within the species P. sumatrense, which can be further utilised in breeding programs and conservation strategies. The present dataset can be further used in advanced cytogenetic exploration, such as FISH and banding, to establish genomic relationships with other cultivars and facilitate genetic improvement in this underutilised millet species.

title: Integration of a Photovoltaic Power System and a Solar Water Heater at an Industrial Facility: Data Reconciliation, Hybrid Energy Balance, and Measurement and Verification Methodology
abstract: Industrial facilities increasingly combine photovoltaic electricity and solar thermal heat, but audit reports may compare incompatible energy records or aggregate electrical and thermal savings into a single figure. This creates a risk of overstating system performance and double counting displaced energy. This study develops a data-quality-aware measurement and verification methodology for an existing 40 kW rooftop photovoltaic system and a proposed 400 L/day solar water-heating system at an industrial confectionery facility. Audit records were classified by temporal coverage, measurement source, and alternating-current/direct-current boundary; partial-period specific yields were calculated; photovoltaic performance indicators were structured in accordance with IEC 61724-1; useful thermal demand was estimated from the water mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature rise; and a 50-85% solar-fraction sensitivity analysis was integrated with separate electricity and heat ledgers. The audit reports 52.5 MWh for July-December 2025 and 36.2 MWh for January-April 2026, corresponding to partial-period specific yields of 1,312.5 and 905 kWh/kWp. These values cannot be compared directly with a separate 26.928 MWh annual forecast until meter identity, capacity boundary, period completeness, and self-consumption/export allocation are reconciled. For the 400 L load, 18.6 kWh of useful heat is required per cycle, and annual useful solar heat varies from 3.39 to 5.77 MWh over the investigated solar-fraction range. The proposed architecture prevents double counting by maintaining separate physical ledgers and integrating them only at the cost, emissions, or primary-energy layer. Data reconciliation and uncertainty disclosure are therefore prerequisites for credible technical and economic decisions.
journal: American Journal of Mechanics and Applications

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Dentistry: Promise, Pitfalls, and Evidence Gaps.
abstract: GLP-1RAs (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists) have become one of the fastest-growing drug classes worldwide, with prescriptions for obesity treatment increasing by 587% from 2019 to 2024. While their metabolic and cardiovascular benefits are well established, the implications for oral health remain largely unexamined. Preclinical evidence consistently demonstrates anti-inflammatory and osteoprotective effects on periodontal and peri-implant tissues: GLP-1RAs promote osteogenic differentiation of periodontal ligament stem cells, reduce alveolar bone resorption in animal models of periodontitis, and enhance implant osseointegration in diabetic rats. However, these findings are based exclusively on in vitro and animal studies, with only a single retrospective cohort study providing limited clinical data. Conversely, several oral adverse effects have been reported based on pharmacovigilance analyses, including xerostomia, dysgeusia, and anosmia, particularly for semaglutide. Gastrointestinal side effects, particularly nausea (15% to 50%), vomiting (5% to 24%), and gastroesophageal reflux, pose a plausible but unquantified risk for tooth erosion and secondary caries. A bidirectional link between GLP-1 signaling and the oral microbiota, mediated by bacterial dipeptidyl peptidase (DPP)-4-like enzymes that degrade endogenous GLP-1, adds further complexity. Despite this breadth of potential interactions, no prospective study has used any dental outcome as an endpoint in patients receiving GLP-1RAs. This critical appraisal synthesizes the evidence across multiple dental disciplines, grades it in each domain, and identifies the gaps that demand urgent investigation.

title: Photobiomodulation-Mediated Modulation of TGF-β/Smad Signaling in Stem Cell-Driven Osteogenesis.
abstract: Bone regeneration remains a significant clinical challenge as a result of limitations presented by autografts, allografts, and synthetic implants. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) serve as key drivers of osteogenesis as they can differentiate into osteoblasts and osteocytes. This process is, however, regulated by the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling pathway, which can upregulate the Runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) to promote early proliferation and commitment through canonical Smad signaling, and also inhibit late-stage differentiation to prevent excessive matrix deposition. These responses are refined further by noncanonical pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM), a noninvasive light-based therapy, has emerged as a promising modulator of stem cell-driven osteogenesis, as it can interact with the TGF-β/Smad pathway. PBM exerts effects on the mitochondria, activating cytochrome c oxidase, increasing ATP production, and generating reactive oxygen species in a controlled manner. This leads to a stimulation of MSC proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation. Emerging evidence from various studies shows that PBM can also modulate TGF-β/Smad signaling by activating latent TGF-β, enhancing Smad phosphorylation, and modulating the noncanonical pathways. However, evidence examining this interaction specifically during MSC osteogenesis are few, and the mechanisms underlying their interaction are incompletely understood. This review, therefore, critically examines existing evidence to elucidate some of these mechanisms for MSC osteogenesis. Although it is promising, challenges still exist in standardizing PBM parameters and conducting targeted studies in clinically relevant three-dimensional models. A clearer understanding of these interactions could provide a basis for future research aimed at advancing noninvasive regenerative strategies for bone defects and osteoporosis.

title: A Potato Leaf Disease and Pests Identification Algorithm Based on Deep Learning
abstract: China boasts a diverse range of crops. The yield and the quality of crops exert an influence on economic development and farmers’ income. The healthy and stable development of agriculture has consistently been a goal pursued by the country. Therefore, it is of great significance to rapidly and precisely identify the types of crop diseases and pests and offer timely and accurate prevention and control measures. The recognition of traditional crop pest and disease images mainly relies on agricultural experts to recognize the color and shape of disease images. This approach is not only labor-intensive and inefficient but also subjective, and it can easily lead to misjudgment and cause the optimal treatment time to be missed. Potatoes are crucial for food processing and daily consumption. They are a representative crop that is also prone to significant economic losses due to pests and diseases. In order to solve the problem of identifying crop pest and disease images, this article combines image processing and VGG deep-learning techniques to implement an improved computer vision model and conducts experiments on seven types of pest and disease images of potato leaves. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional VGG16 model, the new model has a higher identification rate of pests and diseases on potato leaves, and it also has significant reference value for the pest and disease identification methods of other leaf crops.

title: Benchmarking time series foundation models for multi-country infectious disease forecasting: a retrospective evaluation across over 70 diseases
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Global governance, regulations, and policy responses to environmental antimicrobial resistance
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has become a critical global threat, often described as a “silent pandemic.” Although the broad application of antibiotics across various sectors has yielded significant benefits, inadequate regulation has led to inappropriate antimicrobial use, reducing treatment effectiveness. Thus, the development of resistance genes has accelerated, leading to rising global mortality. The rapid spread of these genes through soil, water, and air highlights the environment’s role as a critical reservoir and transmission pathway. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of the environmental dimensions of AMR alongside the associated governance, regulatory, and policy challenges through a One Health perspective. Literature was drawn from recent peer-reviewed studies and key international reports to evaluate global governance structures, including the WHO Global Action Plan, National Action Plans (NAPs), and the One Health approach. Major policy gaps include weak enforcement of environmental regulations and insufficient integration of the environmental sector into One Health initiatives. Furthermore, regulatory oversight is limited by a lack of specific antibiotic discharge standards and inadequate monitoring of pharmaceutical effluents and agricultural runoff. The review also examines the potential of digital technologies and artificial intelligence to enhance AMR surveillance and early detection. Eventually, stronger global governance, enforceable environmental standards, improved intersectoral coordination, and the integration of environmental indicators into NAPs and Sustainable Development Goals are essential to mitigate AMR and maintain intergenerational equity. By aligning policy frameworks with scientific evidence and technological innovations, more resilient systems can be established to protect global health.

title: A model for the spatial population dynamics of the European invasion of the Japanese beetle (Popillia japonica)
abstract: Popillia japonica is an invasive beetle first detected in Northern Italy in 2014 and considered as one of the most dangerous pests for crops due to the economic, environmental, and social costs by European phytosanitary authorities. Here we develop a process-based model for quantifying the invasion dynamics of P. japonica with the goal to elaborate risk maps for the design of surveillance and control strategies. The proposed spatially heterogeneous model captures the different behaviors of both adults, which drive the invasion through flight and short-distance human-mediated transport, and ovo-larval stages, which affect demography due to their susceptibility to environmental conditions. Both processes are biologically informed through variables that are known to influence population dynamics, namely the number of summer days, affecting the flight ability of the adults, and the environmental suitability for larval survival. The simulated presence of adult beetles is then contrasted to pest observation data at the municipality scale from Northern Italy and Switzerland from the initial invasion to December 2023. Results reveal that the ongoing outbreak is occurring in one of the most favorable areas for the beetle, the Po Valley, which favors rapid spread and can sustain high population densities. Mountain regions emerge as obstacles to the progression of the invasion, with the Alps, excluding the valleys, being an almost insurmountable defense, whereas the Apennines only slow down the southward advancement without stopping it altogether. The projected speed of invasion, within and outside the outbreak area, ranges between 0 and almost 20 km/year and it is modulated by environmental conditions. The predicted speed of invasion at continental level constitutes an actionable tool for invasion management, since it provides phytosanitary services with a critical evidence base for optimizing the geometry and extent of delimitation and containment areas.

title: Nonlinear threshold responses of agroecosystem water use efficiency to increasing vapor pressure deficit
abstract: Increasing vapor pressure deficit (VPD) alters ecosystem carbon and water exchange, but agroecosystem water use efficiency (WUE) may respond nonlinearly to rising atmospheric evaporative demand. The VPD levels at which these nonlinear transitions occur, their spatial consistency, and the factors associated with spatial variation in breakpoint magnitude remain poorly understood. We therefore examined nonlinear WUE responses to increasing VPD and assessed how breakpoint magnitude varied across croplands in relation to environmental and agricultural characteristics. Using multisource observations from 111 sub-basins of the Songhua River Basin during 2002–2024 and independent eddy covariance observations from cropland sites, we identified a nonlinear WUE–VPD relationship. The first derivative of the generalized additive model fit indicated a point of maximum WUE sensitivity to VPD at approximately 0.27 kPa, whereas piecewise linear fitting identified the primary basin-scale breakpoint at approximately 0.41 kPa. Repeated subsampling indicated that the basin-scale breakpoint was robust to sampling variation, while local breakpoint estimates varied across sub-basins. Statistically supported breakpoints were detected in 59 of the 111 sub-basins, and site-level screening retained breakpoint estimates for 20 of the 28 evaluated cropland flux sites. The mean breakpoint estimate across the 20 retained flux sites was approximately 0.43 kPa. Sub-basin breakpoint magnitude was negatively associated with leaf area index, soil bulk density, and mean growing-season precipitation total, and positively associated with C4 crop proportion. Above the basin-scale breakpoint, the sensitivity of gross primary productivity to VPD increased significantly, whereas the sensitivity of evapotranspiration showed no significant change, indicating an asymmetric carbon–water response. At the retained flux sites, higher Bowen ratios and lower evaporative fractions above the site-specific breakpoints were consistent with a relative shift in energy partitioning toward sensible heat. The approximately 0.41-kPa breakpoint characterizes the basin-scale WUE response to increasing VPD but does not represent a universal local threshold. Spatial variation in breakpoint magnitude was associated with climate, vegetation structure, soil properties, and crop composition, although the observational design precludes direct causal attribution to individual management factors. These findings clarify spatial variation in nonlinear agroecosystem WUE responses to increasing VPD and underscore the importance of local environmental context when interpreting carbon–water responses to atmospheric drying.

title: ChatGPT’s feedback credibility and students’ perceived learning: the role of agent-related social perceptions
abstract: This paper examines whether students’ agent-related social perceptions of ChatGPT are associated with the perceived credibility of its feedback in academic tasks and whether such credibility, in turn, is related to students’ perceived learning. It also investigates whether the relationship between feedback credibility and perceived learning varies according to students’ sensitivity to the quality of their academic work and their sensitivity to grade-based rewards. To address this, we develop a theoretical model grounded in social perception theory and prior research on students’ experiences with AI-based tools. The model is tested using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) on data collected from 230 students who completed an academic writing task. The findings reveal that students’ agent-related social perceptions—particularly perceived competence and human-like empathy—are positively connected to the credibility students attribute to its feedback. In turn, perceived feedback credibility is interestingly related to students’ perceived learning in the context of academic writing. Furthermore, the positive link between credibility and perceived learning is weaker among students with higher grade-based reward sensitivity. This research contributes to the educational technology literature by advancing understanding of how students evaluate the credibility of ChatGPT-generated feedback and how such evaluations are associated with learning perceptions. It also shows that agent-related social perceptions play a significant role in students’ credibility judgements. Finally, the findings offer practical implications for educators and students seeking to integrate ChatGPT effectively into academic activities.
journal: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

title: Automation and Digital Agriculture Tools
One dataset, four meta-analyses: synthesising mean effects and heterogeneity within and among populations.
abstract: Ecological syntheses (meta-analyses) usually ask 'what is the average effect?' But many questions also depend on whether outcomes become more or less variable and whether effects are predictable across contexts. We show how one dataset can support a workflow that synthesises both mean effects and within-group variability while also separating heterogeneity among study-level effects from residual heterogeneity among effect sizes within studies. Using an organic versus conventional crop-yield dataset, we analyse mean effects with the log response ratio (lnRR; Model 1) and within-group variability with the log variability ratio (lnVR) and log coefficient of variation ratio (lnCVR; Model 2), all calculated from the same summary statistics (means, s.d.s. and sample sizes). We then use multilevel location-scale meta-regression to test whether fertiliser type shifts expected lnRR and lnVR/lnCVR effects (Models 3 and 4) and whether residual and study-level heterogeneity differ between contexts. These heterogeneity components respectively inform consistency among represented comparisons and transferability to a new study. Analysing mean effects, within-group variability and context-dependent heterogeneity together can provide a more informative description of ecological responses than focusing on average effects alone.

title: Deficiency of placental GDF15 causes fetal growth restriction by inhibiting fetal hepatic STAT3-IGF2 axis.
abstract: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a major cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality, yet its underlying mechanism remains elusive. Here, we show that growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) levels are significantly reduced in the placenta and fetal circulation in mouse and pig FGR models and correlate positively with fetal weight. Placenta-specific GDF15 deficiency causes FGR, while placenta-specific Gdf15 mRNA delivery through targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) effectively alleviates FGR. Mechanistically, placental GDF15 is a major contributor to the fetal circulating GDF15 pool and enters the fetal compartment, where it activates the hepatic STAT3 signaling pathway to stimulate IGF2 production during pregnancy. Placental GDF15 deficiency decreases hepatic STAT3 phosphorylation and IGF2 levels in fetuses. Inhibition of STAT3 in primary mouse fetal hepatocytes blocks GDF15-induced IGF2 upregulation. Placenta-specific Gdf15 mRNA-LNP administration rescues the decreased hepatic p-STAT3 and IGF2 levels in FGR fetuses. Collectively, our findings identify a placenta-fetal liver metabolic axis where placental GDF15 promotes fetal growth by activating the fetal hepatic STAT3-IGF2 pathway, revealing a potential therapeutic target for FGR.

title: AI-Based Intent Normalization and Service Routing in Distributed Agentic Microservices
abstract: LLMs are increasingly being embedded into a variety of distributed agentic systems, in the form of agents with APIs, microservices, workflows, and external tools for task completion. Systems need to be able to handle requests that are worded differently but mean the same thing, to make sure routing is consistent, caching can be reused, latency is reduced, reliability is ensured, and governance is supported. Conventional intent representations, beyond simply conveying what users want with their intent and respective slots, do not encode information about user authorization, policies with implications for execution, side effects of actions, locality of execution, and operational implications of intents. Prior work has provided frameworks for normalization, capability discovery and routing in distributed agentic systems, but all this work is done independently and thus does not provide a unified pipeline for handling requests in distributed systems. The main contribution of this paper is to propose a unified framework describing the normalization, discovery, routing, execution control and runtime feedback in distributed agentic systems. The core of this work is the introduction of a canonical representation of intent, called an intent record, which can convey all kinds of semantic information, as well as context, policy, and operational information about the system as a whole, including its uncertainty, to be used by the system’s routing layer. We also introduce a new constraint-first multi-criteria routing process. A reference architecture is also given for such sorts of systems. The architecture’s main functional components are semantic control and its decoupled, cross-governance-deterministic execution. An evaluation framework for the proposed approach in the future is also presented. This framework is not validated through implementation or benchmarking experiments. Such an empirical evaluation is left for future work.
journal: International Journal of Computer Trends and Technology

title: A Nightshade-SWIN Transformer-Based Framework for Enhanced Multi-Crop Plant Disease Classification
diffct: Differentiable CT Operators from Circular Orbits to Arbitrary Trajectories
abstract: diffct implements computed-tomography projection and reconstruction in PyTorch using Numba CUDA kernels. Its native forward model integrates a cell-constant attenuation field along rays defined by per-view acquisition geometry; the backprojector is the matched discrete adjoint. The same model supports parallel, fan and cone beams, non-circular trajectories, and parameterized detector surfaces. This report describes the implementation through release 2.2.1: the geometry and sampling conventions, Siddon traversal, data and first-order geometry derivatives, differentiable analytical FBP/FDK, and execution on one or several GPUs. We derive the ownership and reduction rules for distributed view and spatial partitions and explain how spatial, view and detector blocks extend native operations to CPU-backed and disk-backed data. Experiments include measured walnut cone-beam data, synthetic reconstruction and calibration, and a recorded 512³ scaling benchmark. On A100-SXM-64GB GPUs, eight GPUs on two nodes reduce forward projection from 493.05 to 73.18 ms and the amortized cost of a ten-step CGLS solve from 2054.36 to 373.38 ms per iteration. Analytical gathers have their own discrete transposes; differentiability does not make FDK an exact inverse. We distinguish numerical correctness, reconstruction quality and execution cost, and state the limits of each experiment.

title: Assessing the Role of AI Agents in DNA Methylation Analysis and Biomarker Discovery
abstract: DNA methylation biomarker development spans data discovery, assay-specific processing, marker selection, model development, and independent validation. Agentic systems could help coordinate these stages, but current studies use the term agent for systems with markedly different levels of autonomy and domain-specific evidence. We conducted a structured evidence synthesis, screening 2,801 unique records and organizing relevant systems along three dimensions: workflow autonomy (M0–M4), direct methylation-task evidence, and evidence maturity (E0–E5).Current systems cover complementary parts of the workflow. MethylCurate supports public methylation-data curation; AutoBA and BioMaster execute methylation-analysis pipelines; CpG Atlas provides a self-correcting query interface; and EpiBench, BixBench, and BixBench3 provide direct benchmark evidence for bounded methylation tasks. Across these studies, evidence is strongest for data access, workflow execution, and task-level evaluation. Among systems with task-level evidence reviewed here, we did not identify one that spans dataset discovery, marker selection, classifier development, independent validation, and sample-level uncertainty reporting within a single validated workflow.We therefore propose a matched evaluation framework comparing fixed workflows, rule-based routers, and general or domain-specific agents under shared data, tools, compute, and retry budgets. The framework separates execution reliability, scientific validity, replication, uncertainty, and resource use. Current evidence supports agentic components for methylation analysis, while end-to-end autonomous biomarker discovery remains an open evaluation problem.

title: A Survey of Security in Real-World Agents: From Digital Agents to Embodied AI
abstract: Real-world agents extend language-model reasoning to digital operations and physical action, raising a central security question: how do digital-side attacks cross trust boundaries in robotic systems, and what physical safety conclusions can existing evidence support? This survey examines semantic hijacking, sensory manipulation, and middleware injection across software agents, modular robotic agents, and vision-language-action (VLA) systems. We compare how untrusted content acquires task authority, corrupted observations affect action generation, and middleware access reaches execution interfaces under different permission and control assumptions. An experiment-level analysis examines environment, trajectory, privilege and exposure, consequence, and assurance, distinguishing generated plans, software-state changes, simulated execution, and physical robot actions. The comparison reveals important evidence boundaries: RoboPAIR evaluates driving plans in Dolphins but API-mediated robot actions in Jackal, while Apollo point-cloud replay demonstrates altered braking decisions without measuring physical deceleration. These differences prevent planning or command-level success from being treated as direct evidence of physical safety violations. Across defenses, protection depends on the integrity of the state used for checking, coverage of executable command paths, and the timing of intervention. Reported attack suppression also need not imply useful protection: Safe Prompting reduces targeted attack success to zero while clean-task success also falls to zero in its LIBERO evaluation. Together, these findings identify the conditions under which digital compromise reaches physical execution, delimit the safety claims supported by current experiments, and motivate stronger assurance of action enforcement and recovery under compromised state.

title: Discretization-Induced Constitutive Bias in Differentiable Memory-Kernel Identification
abstract: Optimization through a discrete forward solver can introduce constitutive bias into recovered memory kernels, even when fitted trajectories appear accurate. We characterize this discretization-induced bias and assess how independent validation exposes it and nested-solver correction reduces it. A local perturbation analysis separates noise, discretization, and smooth regularization contributions to estimation error. An inverse-crime-free protocol combines independently generated observations, independent forward evaluation, and nested-grid Richardson correction. Four synthetic benchmark families comprise 5480 completed runs, with 20 paired seeds per stochastic condition. Matched-discretization controls yielded nearly exact kernel recovery despite substantial forward state errors relative to the continuous reference. Independent observations exposed systematic resolution-dependent kernel errors. In the exponential benchmark, corrected kernel error decreased at approximately order 1.89, compared with 1.14 for coarse inversion; the manufactured KWW benchmark gave a corrected endpoint rate of approximately 1.54. Correction also improved multiscale and constrained nonparametric recovery, but benefits diminished under noise, sparsity, and misspecification. Accurate Prony kernel recovery coexisted with substantial fast-mode parameter error. Raw forward defects did not reliably estimate kernel error, and fractional and numerical correction orders differed in the tested scheme. These findings support independent forward validation and numerical-convergence assessment as essential components of credible memory-kernel discovery.

title: Soil Health Assessment for Crop-Specific Production: Linking Soil Microbiomes, Pathogen Risk, and Crop Nutritional and Phytochemical Quality
abstract: Soil degradation is one of the greatest threats to sustainable agriculture, yet current soil health assessment frameworks largely rely on physicochemical indicators and may insufficiently account for crop-specific biological requirements and microbiome functions. Increasing evidence indicates that different crops require distinct combinations of physical, chemical, and biological soil properties and recruit differentially enriched rhizosphere microbial assemblages that regulate nutrient cycling, disease suppression, plant performance, and nutritional quality. This review critically examines current concepts of soil quality and soil health and highlights the need to shift from generalized toward crop-specific soil health assessment. We synthesize the principal physical, chemical, and biological indicators of soil health, with emphasis on soil microbiomes, beneficial microorganisms, soil-borne pathogens, molecular diagnostic approaches, and representative sampling strategies. Using publicly available FAOSTAT and EPPO datasets as an exploratory European case study, we describe continental crop production patterns and the geographical occurrence of major plant pathogens to illustrate how regional crop production and pathogen records can provide context for crop-specific soil health assessment. We further assess evidence linking soil properties and plant-associated microbiomes with crop nutrient composition and bioactive phytochemical accumulation. Collectively, this review proposes a crop-specific conceptual framework that integrates ecological, biological, and agronomic processes to support the interpretation of soil health measurements and provides a basis for future empirical validation.

title: Gas Lift Evaluation and Production Forecasting Through a Transfer Learning Dual-Track Machine Learning Framework
abstract: As reservoirs deplete and natural flow declines, artificial lift becomes necessary to sustain production, and gas lift is one of the most applied methods in unconventional horizontal wells. Injecting high-pressure gas lowers the density of the flowing column and increases drawdown, but the production response is not proportional to the gas injected. It is governed by nonlinear interactions among injection rate, wellbore pressures, geometry, and fluid properties. Beyond an optimum, additional gas reduces production. Machine learning captures such relationships well and predicts oil rate with high accuracy, yet that accuracy is almost always measured within the same wells a model was trained on. A companion study of 11 Eagle Ford wells (Al Raisi et al., 2026) reported R2 as high as 0.960 under a random split but strongly negative values under leave-one-well-out (LOWO) evaluation, because field measurements cluster in a narrow band of conditions and much of the gas lift domain is never observed. This study's framework combines two tracks. Track A applies data-driven models to daily field data from the 11 wells. Track B uses a steady-state multiphase flow simulator to build a physics-consistent synthetic dataset in two complementary designs: a broad dataset of 6,000 nodal-analysis cases sampled by Latin Hypercube Sampling, establishing which operating conditions exist and where gas lift helps, and a controlled sweep of 700 scenarios evaluated at 11 injection rates each, resolving how production responds to injection. Together these required 13,700 simulation cases. A deep learning neural network is then trained through a staged transfer learning procedure that pre-trains on the broad dataset, refines on the sweep dataset, and fine-tunes on field data. The simulations reproduce established gas lift behavior, which is what makes them usable as a training signal. Feasibility rises from 90% to 99% with gas lift, 285 of 295 otherwise non-productive cases are enabled, and the resulting performance curves fall into monotonic, plateau, and post-peak decline classes separated by tubing size, wellhead pressure, and fluid properties. Under LOWO evaluation, staged transfer learning raises the average R2 from 0.149 to 0.414, reduces MAE from 70 to 56 STB/D, and lowers MAPE from 56% to 38%. Neither dataset suffices alone: broad-only pre-training yields 0.146 and sweep-only 0.322, so breadth and structure are both required and the order matters. The gains concentrate on wells the baseline fails, most notably Well 4, which moves from a strongly negative to a positive R2. Applied to a well-level injection scenario, the model ranks lift responsiveness across operating states in the physically expected order, supporting open-loop screening and gas allocation. The study also reports a useful negative result: despite 135 post-peak-decline scenarios in training, predicted curves rise monotonically and do not reproduce over-injection. Expanded coverage and explicit physical constraints are therefore complementary rather than interchangeable.
journal: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

title: A Physics-Informed Machine Learning Framework for Real-Time Predictive Diagnostics and Conformance Control in Produced Water Management
abstract: The global hydrocarbon exploration and production (E&P) industry is severely impacted by increasing produced water management challenges, evidenced by average water-oil ratios (WOR) frequently approaching 9:1. This excessive aqueous phase volume significantly escalates operational expenditure (OPEX) through costly handling, separation, and treatment processes, simultaneously diminishing the net efficiency of hydrocarbon recovery. Current conventional water conformance control strategies exhibit an estimated success rate of approximately 40%, primarily due to the latency in intervention deployment and the diagnostic ambiguity in precisely characterizing the spatial origin and mechanism of water influx within the reservoir-wellbore system. This study introduces a novel methodology predicated on integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms for advanced, real-time diagnostic analytics of produced fluid dynamics. The core ML models are trained on a globalized, multivariate production dataset comprising production profiles and sensor telemetry from over 25 distinct operational wells. The algorithms are specifically engineered to perform spatiotemporal pattern recognition within the WOR signature. This enables the system to differentiate diagnostically between near-wellbore conformance issues (e.g., inadequate cement bond, channeling) and deeper reservoir-scale heterogeneity effects (e.g., thief zones). The trained ML models yield high-fidelity predictive analytics, capable of forecasting future water production trends and accurately predicting the imminent onset of significant water breakthrough events. These proactive capability transitions produced water management from a reactive framework to a data-driven decision support system (DSS). The real-time integration of high-frequency sensor data enhances the system's responsiveness and adaptive capability. The resulting output guides operators toward the timely deployment of optimized, targeted chemical or mechanical water shutoff treatments, moving beyond reliance on conventional, time-averaged flow measurements. The proposed AI-enabled workflow represents a significant innovation in reservoir management. By achieving early and precise identification of conformance breaches, the system empowers operators to implement remediation strategies that are both mechanistically specific and spatially optimized. This approach is crucial for: (1) maximizing hydrocarbon recovery efficiency, (2) substantially reducing OPEX by minimizing the volume of treated water, and (3) sustaining optimal reservoir sweep performance. Selected case studies will be presented to quantitatively demonstrate the potential efficacy of this methodology in delivering superior water conformance control and optimizing overall field economics.
journal: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

title: Scaling the Expert Eye: Automating Subsurface Model Evaluation and Tuning via Reservoir Engineering Inspired AI Agents
abstract: Predicting the behavior of oil fields is a notoriously complex endeavor, often relying on high-fidelity predictive models (e.g. simulation models) that are sensitive to a myriad of geological and operational parameters. Traditionally, the "gold standard" for refining these models has been the manual intervention by reservoir engineers. These experts possess the nuanced domain knowledge required to interpret data anomalies and perform "history matching"—adjusting model inputs to align with historical performance. However, this human-centric approach is often a bottleneck; it is slow, difficult to scale, and limited by the speed at which a human can iterate through high-dimensional data sets. To address this, we introduce an autonomous AI agent designed to bridge the gap between expert intuition and computational efficiency. In order to perform this task autonomously, the AI Agent needs the ability to do the following: (1) Validate a model's quality using the same qualitative and quantitative metrics as used by the experts (2) Determine what needs to be changed and how to change them to improve the model (3) Modify these parameters and evaluate the model in order to improve the model (4) Repeat the process until all metrics are satisfied. This is achieved by using state-of-the-art LLMs (large language models) with system prompts fed with documentation of all the steps above, along with LangChain-based agent architecture developed specifically for this purpose. By codifying the analytical workflows and heuristic strategies used by veteran reservoir engineers, the agent performs automated parameter tuning across predictive models. The system leverages an assisted data assimilation approach already in place, using rigorous back-testing to evaluate the impact of each adjustment in real-time. Instead of a brute-force search, the agent applies specialized logic to identify which "knobs" to turn—such as permeability or porosity ranges —to generate results that best mirror reality, effectively mimicking the "expert eye" at scale. The integration of this agent transforms the modeling pipeline from a labor-intensive manual task into a high-speed, expert-driven optimization process. Initial results tested on multiple real field models demonstrate that the agent can achieve model fidelity comparable to manual tuning while significantly reducing the time-to-insight from weeks to hours, and also minimizing critical errors that might be introduced by human engineers due to the complex model validation process. By automating the iterative back-testing/history-matching cycle, organizations can democratize the specialized knowledge of their top engineers across entire portfolios of assets. This ensures that predictive models remain robust, reliable, and grounded in the practical realities of field operations, allowing human engineers to focus on high-level strategic decision-making rather than repetitive parameter tweaking.

title: Field Calibrated Dual Porosity THM Modeling and Physics-Guided Machine Learning for Probabilistic Enhanced Geothermal System Forecasting at Utah FORGE
abstract: Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) depend on connected fractures for fluid circulation and heat extraction, but those same pathways control pressure buildup, thermal contraction, transmissivity evolution, stress redistribution, and the potential for induced slip. This study develops a field anchored, two-dimensional reduced order thermo-hydro-mechanical response model of the Utah Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy (Utah FORGE) injector-producer corridor and couples it with audited machine-learning surrogates for probabilistic geothermal-performance and fracture-stability screening. Public Well 58-32 geophysical logs, X-ray-diffraction mineralogy, thermal-conductivity measurements, and processed 2024 Wells 16A/16B circulation records are integrated through an explicit evidence hierarchy, while published fracture, thermal, and stress information constrains the model domain and parameter ranges. The parent model represents thermal decline, quasi-steady pressure support, thermo-poroelastic stress redistribution, fracture-aperture evolution, cubic-law permeability feedback, and orientation-dependent frictional criticality. Two 20-year operating cases are evaluated: a prospective 60 kg/s injection case and a 26.5 kg/s field-rate reference case. A 2,500-realization physics-generated ensemble is used to train surrogate models for five independent outputs, followed by 50,000 Monte Carlo evaluations. The apparent wellhead pressure-difference/rate index decreases from 0.688 to 0.650 MPa/(L/s), equivalent to a 1.89% cubic-law aperture increase if the full trend is attributed to fracture transmissivity. At Year 20, the 60 kg/s case predicts a production temperature of 180.3°C and thermal power of 32.7 MW, compared with 183.8°C and 14.8 MW for the lower-rate case. The higher-rate case produces a maximum aperture change of 8.10%, a maximum permeability ratio of 1.263, and a friction ratio of approximately 1.07 for the south-striking, moderately west-dipping fracture set, whereas the lower-rate case remains below the simplified frictional threshold. Independent 750-case validation yields (R^2) values of 0.997 for production temperature, 0.9996 for proxy injection pressure, 0.9992 for aperture change, and 0.9958 for thermal-breakthrough time. Maximum friction ratio is less transferable ((R^2=0.605)); therefore, geomechanical Monte Carlo outputs are interpreted as conditional screening results rather than seismic-hazard probabilities. The study establishes a traceable workflow in which real observations constrain a reduced-order THM replica, physics-based simulations generate the training manifold, ML enables rapid uncertainty propagation, and probabilistic analysis defines a heat-recovery-versus-mechanical-criticality operating envelope for risk-aware EGS design.

title: From Manual to Autonomous: Field Experience and Lessons Learned from Implementing the First AI-APC Autonomous Gas-Lift Optimization Solution
abstract: Gas-lift optimization in large oil fields is often constrained by manual well reviews, intermittent well-test data, limited visibility of bottomhole conditions, and difficulty of implementing new setpoints across a large well stock. This document summarizes the field experience from implementing an AI-APC Autonomous solution for gas-lifted oil producers. The solution combines artificial-intelligence assisted inferential models, digital well-performance calculations and Advanced Process Control (APC) to autonomously adjust gas-lift and production-control settings while respecting reservoir-management, well-integrity and surface-facility constraints. This integration allows seamless and precise well adjustments, optimizing an entire portfolio of wells simultaneously with minimal operational footprint and human intervention. The system utilizes up-to-date well models to calculate in real time the optimal gas lift and downhole flowing pressure based on actual flowing conditions, thereby continuously achieving production targets. The solution promotes more efficient energy usage by automatically managing all producing wells while enforcing reservoir management strategy, respecting surface facility constraints and safeguarding well integrity. Ultimately, this results in maximized performance, enhanced efficiency, and reduced exposure to adverse environmental and process conditions, supporting more sustainable operations by reducing greenhouse gas emissions compared with previous practices. The system was deployed across hundreds of strings in a major smart field, leveraging existing instrumentation and requiring only a single additional APC server in the control room. Multiple autonomous scenarios were tested for maximum efficiency, optimal energy utilization, and maximum production. Results included in this work demonstrate the solution's benefits, with potential gains of 2–5% in additional production. This centralized approach enables rapid and large-scale deployments with a minimal footprint and no production loss during the deployment stage. In practice, a significant reduction in effort was observed when updating and executing gas-lift optimization across numerous wells. The world-first AI-APC solution for gas-lifted wells enabled effective and reliable autonomous operations. This represents an important operating-philosophy shift, moving from manual well adjustments toward autonomous and precise control by virtual agents, unlocking the Digital Barrel and stepping into a new era of smarter operations.

title: Data Analytic Coupled Machine Learning Applications for Active Reservoir Management: CO2-EOR Use Case
abstract: Carbon dioxide-enhanced oil recovery (CO2-EOR) is a vital tertiary recovery technique used to extend the lifetime of mature oilfields and mobilize trapped residual oil. While it is a proven practice with potential for growth, effective implementation faces considerable technical challenges. Managing reservoir heterogeneity, maintaining optimal pressure, and monitoring CO2 migration present major challenges. Traditional simulation methods address these issues, but they can be slow and limited in scope. This necessitates advanced tools that can provide rapid, accurate, and comprehensive insights. Integrating dynamic, real-time analytical and digital capabilities that can provide rapid and comprehensive reservoir insights may directly enhance the decision-making framework of field-level CO2-EOR operations in ways necessary to optimize complex injection strategies and maximize overall asset value. This study addresses this need by deploying a physics-based semi-analytical capacitance resistance model (CRM) to perform rapid, field-scale history matching and multi-scenario production forecasting for CO2-EOR. Using 30 years of simulated operational data from the Scurry Area Canyon Reef Operator's Committee (SACROC) field in Texas, the CRM characterized inter-well connectivity and simulated recovery responses across 22 injection and 23 production wells. The CRM was calibrated using 25 years of injection and production data at SACROC. It was then used to evaluate six late-stage reservoir management scenarios over a 5-year forecast window. Simulation results demonstrate a strong agreement with synthetic production volumes in the history-matched calibration timeframe and reflect a stark divergence in performance across flooding strategies in the forecasted period. Simulation Case 6 (Post-water-alternating-gas [WAG] CO2 Flood) emerged as the most effective recovery strategy, utilizing a continuous gas flood to surge forecast-period oil production by 56.7% compared to the Base Case (Case 1). However, Case 6 resulted in the largest volumes of produced liquid along with oil. Conversely, Case 5 (Post-WAG Water Chase) underperformed significantly, leading to a 48.2% decline in oil production relative to Case 1. High-throughput water and gas injection (Case 2) offered a competitive alternate pathway, yielding an 11.0% boost in oil production. Meanwhile, altering WAG cycle lengths (Cases 3 and 4) yielded marginal differences in cumulative oil, though longer cycles introduced severe liquid rate oscillations. The significant recovery gains demonstrated in Case 6 require handling an extensive 64.1% surge in total produced liquids and associated costs for sourcing, transporting, and recycling makeup CO2. In contrast, while the water chase in Case 5 minimized surface handling by reducing liquid volumes by 48.2%, it failed to effectively mobilize residual hydrocarbons compared to other operational cases. Disparities noted in forecasted production profiles highlight the operational and cost trade-offs for operators.

title: Building an Evaluation Harness for Oil & Gas AI Agents
abstract: While operators and service companies are aggressively deploying AI agents for various oil and gas use cases, methods to evaluate their outputs and behaviors remain rarely discussed. Existing publications focus mostly on the accuracy of the final outputs, neglecting important metrics like consistency and efficiency. The objective of this project is to build an evaluation harness and use it to measure the performance of agents against drilling data analysis tasks. DrillingGPT (DGPT), a drilling data AI agent, is one of 100+ agents deployed in Occidental's internal agent platform. We developed an evaluation suite consisting of 19 tasks of varying difficulties, curated and verified by subject matter experts. Each task was run 5 times (i.e k=5) to compute pass@k and pass^k metrics to measure success rates and consistency. Additionally, tool call precision, recall, and redundancy rate were measured to assess the agent's behaviors. Traces were then examined to provide additional details about potential failure modes. In one pilot execution, DGPT achieved pass@k of 63%, pass@1 of 48%, and pass^k of 37%, which indicated that the agent can often reach correct answers but did not do so consistently. Performance was somewhat satisfactory on easy and medium tasks, while hard tasks showed a pronounced decline in all metrics. Trace analysis identified key failure modes that include partial errors in multi-well responses, compounding mistakes in multi-table aggregations, and failure to refuse out-of-scope requests. From tool-calling perspective, DGPT appeared to act more conservatively with high precision and lower recall. We also observed cases where DGPT skipped necessary tools to achieve its goals. The harness offers significant improvement over a simple accuracy metric for evaluating agent performance. These insights offer valuable guidance for developers and engineers in identifying areas and methodologies for further iteration. This project introduces a quantitative and systematic approach to evaluate AI agents built specifically for oil and gas use cases, providing a more holistic framework that goes beyond simple output accuracy by also considering factors like consistency, efficiency, and tool usage in real-world scenarios.

title: Aggregation-Based Upscaling for Geologically Consistent High-Fidelity Reservoir Simulation with Process-Based Models
abstract: Process-based stratigraphy models, simply referred to as process-based models (PBMs) for turbidite reservoirs capture the complex interplay between topography, gravity-driven flow, and associated sediment deposition and erosion events in a more consistent fashion with natural observations compared to alternatives. Recent developments in computer hardware and algorithms have started enabling the construction of full-field PBMs conditioned to static data. In this paper, we describe key enabler algorithms for the effective field-scale dynamic simulation of PBMs under subsurface uncertainty for more robust hydrocarbon recovery performance predictions. We have developed a protocol for physics-based representation of thin but laterally extensive shale layers (shale drapes), and their incorporation into surface-based grids in terms of transmissibility multiplier surfaces for more memory efficient simulations. We have developed stratigraphy-driven aggregation-based upscaling method that significantly reduces the active gridblock count and simulation run time while retaining flow-relevant features of PBMs. Our upscaling method operates both in vertical and areal directions adaptively and preserves high-resolution solutions near wells. The method adapts automatically to the presence of shale drapes and preserves their dynamic effects with minimal modification to model connectivity attributes. We show that high-resolution field-scale shale-draped PBMs can be constructed rapidly and simulated within acceptable simulation times using a connectivity-list based new generation reservoir simulator. We show that the proposed upscaling method reduces the gridblock count by at least 50% and yields order-of-magnitude simulation run time speedup while retaining an excellent level of accuracy. Screening a large ensemble of PBM realizations at full resolution for dynamic forecast uncertainty quantification can still be time consuming. Here, we demonstrate the use of upscaled PBMs within an accelerated dynamic screening workflow. In this context, we introduce a clustering-based representative-model selection method driven by dynamic performance criteria such as the recovery factor and cumulative oil/water production. We show that upscaled models capture the reference uncertainty range obtained using solely fine-scale models with reasonable accuracy on a realistic model for a deepwater development setting. This takes conditioned PBMs one step closer to ensemble-based history matching.

title: The Influence of Impermeable Boundaries in Fractal Reservoirs
abstract: The purpose of this work is to present analytic relations that assist in diagnosing the reservoir-boundary configurations of shale reservoirs, which are conceptualized as fractal objects due to their highly heterogeneous nature. The resulting expressions can help address the non-uniqueness problem in determining the reservoir's fractal parameters in certain cases. Once the reservoir-boundary model and fractal parameters are defined, this information can be used to establish a direct connection between the identified reservoir characteristics and the observed production decline curves, particularly those exhibiting multiple power-law regimes and extended transition periods, thereby enhancing interpretation and forecasting capabilities in unconventional reservoir analysis. We apply the method of images to the fractal source solution to model pressure transient behavior in the presence of impermeable boundaries, considering both single- and dual-porosity reservoirs with a transient interporosity flow model, which is intended to represent a multi-fractured horizontal well scenario. The use of the method of images enables an accurate representation of flow restrictions in complex reservoir systems, including the influence of production from adjacent wells. In our analysis, we consider three boundary configurations: (1) a single boundary, (2) parallel boundaries (channel geometry), and (3) rectangular boundaries (closed and open). Our results show that the transient performance behavior of a fractal reservoir can yield multiple power-law flow periods in the presence of impermeable boundaries. For the single boundary case, we have derived a mathematical expression to estimate the distance from the well to the boundary. Similarly, for the parallel boundaries/channel case, an expression to estimate the channel width is provided. These expressions can be utilized to provide an approximation of the Stimulated Reservoir Volume Boundary (SRVB). This work introduces an analytical framework for modeling fractal reservoirs with impermeable boundaries using the method of images, capturing complex rate/pressure transient behaviors. It reveals that such reservoirs can exhibit multiple power-law flow periods, reflecting the heterogeneity of the system. By linking fractal reservoir parameters directly to observed production decline curves, the approach provides a powerful tool for interpreting and forecasting performance in unconventional reservoirs.

title: A Multi-Agent AI Optimization System for Improving Rig Utilization and Production Gains in the Burgan Field
abstract: Scheduling a fleet of workover rigs across a mature giant field requires balancing production objectives against a dense web of operational constraints: artificial lift readiness, material availability, location doability, site and pad access, and rig–well compatibility. In the Greater Burgan complex, this forward planning has historically been built and maintained manually in the well delivery management (WDM) system, an in-house rig-scheduling application in which of the order of ten stakeholder teams continuously record and revise workover activities and their constraints. Across a typical year, the programme spans on the order of 500 workover wells and roughly 40 active rigs; distributing that fleet across the candidate wells and their ordered sequences yields a combinatorial space of astronomical size, on the order of hundreds of septillions of feasible arrangements and beyond, that cannot be searched by hand. This paper describes the design, deployment, and field evaluation of a multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) scheduling system introduced by the Operator's Integration Excellence team to optimize the 90-day forward plan across the full workover operation of approximately 40 rigs and 200 workover wells. The system decomposes scheduling across cooperating agents: data preprocessing, rig–well resource matching, constraint validation, schedule optimization by a genetic algorithm adapted to the Operator's scheduling rules and operating over short- and long-term memory, execution monitoring, and feedback, with a human-in-the-loop review and approval workflow retained throughout. Planners select one of two objective modes (maximize production gain or meet a specified production target) while the optimizer enforces stability rules that protect active and next-scheduled jobs, group multi-well sites, and honor rig–well compatibility. Performance was evaluated by comparing manually prepared schedules against system-optimized schedules over identical planning inputs and, separately, through historical validation (backtesting) over rolling 90-day look-back windows. To respect data-confidentiality requirements, production results are reported in normalized form and absolute volumes are withheld. In a field-wide evaluation, the optimized schedule increased the projected 90-day production gain by 16% over the manual baseline, an advantage that compounded across the horizon, while fleet-average rig idle time fell by 46% and schedule preparation collapsed from about ten days of manual coordination to minutes of computation. The paper presents the constraint taxonomy and scheduling logic in transferable form and outlines an ongoing extension to new-drill planning, where injector–producer relationships, injection timing, and rig-contract capability introduce additional considerations.

title: Evaluating the Dynamic Response of Depleted Sandstone Gas Reservoirs to Microbial Stimulation: A 3D Reactive-Transport Simulation of Biogenic Methane Generation
abstract: Depleted gas reservoirs occur in every mature petroleum province and are considered spent once pressure falls below the economic limit. However, their pore spaces retain residual hydrocarbon and dormant anaerobic microbial communities capable of converting that carbon to methane. While microbial kinetics establish the conceptual feasibility of accelerating this conversion through microbial stimulation, field application requires predicting the spatio-temporal evolution of methane, biomass, and pressure across the formation. This study evaluates the spatial-temporal response of a depleted sandstone asset to microbial stimulation using a three-dimensional, finite-volume reactive-transport model. A late-life Agbada Formation gas sand with 87% screening suitability served as the case study. A nutrient system was adopted and scaled via pore-volume analysis to an injection slug of 8,000 m3 per cycle. The simulator integrates two-phase flow, advective-dispersive transport, microbial growth, and stoichiometric methane generation across 1,600 grid blocks. To ensure physical rigor, the biological module enforces thermodynamic potential limits on syntrophic steps while tracking chemical oxygen demand (COD) to distinguish amendment-derived carbon from residual hydrocarbon degradation. The model was verified analytically (R-squared = 0.99917), converged within 0.1%, and matched historical depletion from 4,056 to 800 psia. Forecasting a five-year, five-cycle stimulation program across a 1.44 km2 pattern, the base case yielded 680 MMscf of incremental biogenic methane compared to zero production in the unstimulated baseline. Treatment converted 4.7% of residual hydrocarbon in place to methane, increasing average reservoir pressure by 53 psi, while advection-dominated transport and cell detachment drove 94% pattern colonization within 12 months. A global sensitivity analysis of 104 realizations attributed 90 percent of the forecast variance to the oil-water interfacial area and the degradation flux across it (P10: 134 MMscf, P50: 521 MMscf, P90: 1,073 MMscf) indicating these as the controls governing the outcome. Evaluated from the thermodynamics alone, the syntrophic chain is feasible only between hydrogen partial pressures of 5.6 and 2,979 Pa, providing a transferable screening criterion that generalizes beyond a single field. This work provides a reproducible and physically constrained basis for screening and designing microbial stimulation in depleted sandstone reservoirs.

title: Which wheat–legume yield comparisons survive sole-crop control reconstruction
abstract: Missing sole-crop controls do not remove every comparison from a plant-mixture experiment. We audited six French wheat–legume experiments at one station, withholding same-density references from 56 nonunit-density control pairs linked to 190 component means. Configuration differences sharing a control and complete factorial differences of differences retained their native and log contrasts. For 89 focal-cultivar comparisons relative to separate sole crops, all eight cultivar-agnostic estimators gave the same no-fit log ranking, with 28 reversals. An exact decomposition located their shared error in unrepresented differences between cultivar-specific density responses. Nine reversals remained among 50 comparisons whose observed and predicted log magnitudes both exceeded 0.10. Cultivar-history transfer reduced reversals to 25 but increased year-equal log error from 0.187 to 0.261. Retrospective maximum-error plateau deferral recovered 37 of 56 controls and automatically reported 37 of 190 comparisons without observed sign errors; all were negative. Q80 recovered 16 controls and reported 101 comparisons, with four errors sharing one control. A simple yield score reproduced the selected plateau recovery sets at the same annual budgets; shared-record coupling explained exceptions to the component-level threshold condition. German and UK means checked distinct transfer layers without fully matched multi-site component validation. The contribution is an empirical account of which comparisons survive missing references and which additional information is required. Data reuse should preserve comparison targets and shared-control identities before pooling ecological responses.

title: Biotecnología en comunidades indígenas: oportunidades, desafíos éticos y sostenibilidad
abstract: Biotechnology is considered a pillar of current scientific and technological development, and its implementation in indigenous communities poses ethical, social, and environmental challenges that require critical and contextualized analysis. This article aims to analyze the relationship between biotechnology and indigenous peoples, with emphasis on Latin America and Mexico, through a qualitative methodology based on a documentary review supported by critical-interpretive analysis of the scientific literature published between 2015 and 2026, aside from a few exceptions involving foundational works. It examines specific applications such as the conservation of native species, ecosystem restoration, sustainable agriculture, and genomics applied to health and territory. It also presents cases from indigenous communities, such as the Tzeltal and Tzotzil peoples in Chiapas and the Nahua peoples in Puebla, as well as experiences in Latin America (the Ecuadorian Amazon and Chimborazo), which reveal both potential benefits and existing tensions. Among the challenges identified are biopiracy, violations of free, prior, and informed consent, asymmetries in benefit-sharing mechanisms, and the persistence of colonial approaches in scientific research. The article incorporates new governance frameworks such as the Cali Fund for Digital Sequence Information (COP16) and the C.A.R.E. Principles of Indigenous Data Sovereignty. It concludes that biotechnology can effectively contribute to sustainable development when it is based on the principles of justice, effective community participation, and respect for cultural autonomy, and that co-design approaches integrating scientific and traditional knowledge are required.
