title: Financial Markets Report Boxes – Second Quarter 2026
abstract: During the second quarter of 2026, international financial markets continued to be largely influenced by developments associated with the conflict in the Middle East. In this context, global financial risk perceptions eased following the high levels reached at the onset of the conflict. This environment contributed to an improvement of financial conditions, declines in measures of expected inflation, and downward revisions to economic growth forecasts. Global inflation and interest rates remained high amidst a highly cautious stance by central banks - Inflation resumed its upward trend in major developed economies and remained above the central banks' targets. - Markets revised their interest rate expectations upward. - During the quarter, capital flows to emerging economies declined amid narrower interest rate differentials relative to developed economies. In Colombia, the macroeconomic and financial environment remains challenging amidst inflationary and fiscal pressures - Inflation increased vis-a-vis the previous quarter and remained above Banco de la República's target. - Banco de la República (the Central Bank of Colombia, Banrep) increased its monetary policy rate to 12.00% at its June meeting. - During the second quarter of the year, inflation expectations declined relative to the first quarter, although they remained well above Banrep's target. - Colombia's sovereign risk premium declined following the presidential election results; however, it remained elevated vis-a-vis its regional peers. - Risks associated with inflation and the external environment persist. - Looking ahead, the key drivers of local markets’ performance will be the trajectory of fiscal metrics, the external environment, and the monetary policy stance. Debt markets reflected an environment of higher inflation and interest rate expectations, alongside episodes of increased risk aversion, in line with developments surrounding the conflict in the Middle East and concerns over public finances. - Globally, sovereign bond yields showed mixed performance. - In Latin America, most sovereign bonds posted gains amid higher risk appetite and portfolio inflows into bonds. - In Colombia, TES (Colombian government bonds) posted significant gains vis-a-vis their regional peers, driven primarily by the decline in sovereign risk aversion after May. - This performance reflected the market’s expectations of fiscal consolidation. - Market liquidity improved slightly but remained below 2025 levels. - In this context, foreign investors increased their TES holdings in both the spot and derivatives market (non-deliverable forward - NDF). - The Ministry of Finance and Public Credit completed the settlement of the total return swap (TRS) transaction in May, which had been entered into with international banks in September 2025. The Colombian peso (COP) was volatile and appreciated significantly vis-a-vis the U.S. dollar, outperforming its regional peers. - The U.S. dollar (USD) strengthened vis-a-vis the basket of currencies comprising the developed market currency index (DXY; 1.22%) and followed an upward trend throughout most of the period. - The appreciation of the Colombian peso (COP) was supported by both external and idiosyncratic factors, including lower domestic risk aversion, higher oil prices (particularly in March), and still-attractive interest-rate differentials. - Foreign exchange market liquidity indicators improved vis-a-vis the previous quarter. - The FX derivatives market corrected the distortions observed at the end of 2025 and during 1Q26. Stock markets recorded gains amid an environment with a stronger risk appetite. - In the United States, performance was driven by strong corporate earnings, particularly in the technology and artificial intelligence sectors. - Toward the end of the quarter, expectations of a more restrictive monetary policy stance in the United States were revised downward. - In Latin America, equity markets posted declines during 2Q26, reversing the upward trend observed in previous quarters. - In Colombia, the MSCI COLCAP1 equity index posted a quarterly negative return, broadly in line with the regional trend.

title: State regulation of key economic sectors in wartime conditions
abstract: The article examines the peculiarities of state regulation of key sectors of the economy under martial law conditions. The necessity of transforming economic policy instruments in order to ensure macroeconomic stability, support critical infrastructure, maintain food security, and sustain the state’s financial system is substantiated. The study analyzes the specific functioning of the energy, agricultural, industrial, transport and logistics, and financial sectors under wartime risks. Directions for improving the mechanisms of state influence on strategic sectors of the economy are proposed, taking into account the principles of adaptability, flexibility, digitalization, and integration with international partners. Particular attention is paid to the study of institutional changes in the system of public administration that occur under the influence of military challenges, as well as to the assessment of the effectiveness of fiscal, monetary, and administrative regulatory instruments. The role of coordination between state authorities, local self-government bodies, and business entities in ensuring the resilience of the economic system is determined. The importance of international financial and technical assistance for stabilizing the budgetary system, restoring infrastructure, and supporting entrepreneurial activity under conditions of limited domestic resources is revealed. The paper emphasizes the need to develop a long-term strategy for the structural modernization of the economy aimed at increasing its competitiveness and resilience to external and internal shocks. The expediency of introducing innovative approaches to the management of state programs, expanding digital tools for control and monitoring, and deepening integration processes with international economic organizations is substantiated. The practical significance of the obtained results lies in the possibility of their application in the development of state economic policy measures during the period of martial law and in the post-war recovery of the country. In addition, the study highlights the importance of strengthening the institutional capacity of public authorities to respond effectively to economic challenges caused by wartime conditions
journal: Bulletin of Kamianets-Podilskyi Ivan Ohiienko National University. Economic sciences

title: Designing a Predictive Expense Tracking Mobile Application: A Comparison of Random Forest, Linear Regression, and Prophet-Based Models
abstract: In today’s fast-paced world, people engage in various forms of daily consumption, yet many lack the habit of tracking their expenses due to low financial awareness. Without proper expense recording and budgeting, individuals often struggle to understand their consumption habits and are at a disadvantage when it comes to financial planning, especially during emergencies. To address these issues, this project proposes the development of a user-friendly expense tracking mobile application designed to help adults build healthy financial habits and utilize predictive algorithms to forecast future expenses. The application enables users to record daily transactions, analyse their spending patterns, plan budgets, and receive personalized saving recommendations. An experiment was conducted to compare four forecasting models: Random Forest, Linear Regression, Facebook Prophet, and Neural Prophet. The models were evaluated using the same synthetically generated transaction dataset, which yielded a limited number of monthly observations for testing. Random Forest showed the most stable overall performance under this experimental setting and was selected as the forecasting model for the prototype, though these results should be interpreted with caution given the small evaluation sample.
journal: Journal of Informatics and Web Engineering

title: When Does Randomized Oversight Align AI Agents That Can Conceal?
abstract: Oversight changes the evidence it relies on. We ask when randomized audits and scoring align AI agents that can conceal misconduct and alter records. Stronger auditing makes undeterred violations better hidden. Because the provider writes the agent's objective, sanctions need not stop at forfeiture, and rare audits deter every type of agent if evidence survives concealment and audit draws cannot be learned in advance. When evidence can be erased, deterrence must come from lower gains from violation, such as credit for stopping, or from costlier or fewer ways to conceal. These conditions identify what failed when agents in OpenAI's cybersecurity evaluations compromised parts of Hugging Face's infrastructure in July 2026.

title: Impact of climate change on malaria incidence in Senegal and Nigeria: a machine learning approach
abstract: Malaria remains a leading climate-sensitive disease in West Africa, where temperature and rainfall variations strongly influence mosquito dynamics and transmission intensity. Senegal and Nigeria, representing the Sahel-Sudanian and rainforest-savanna ecological gradients, are among the most vulnerable zones. However, few climate–malaria forecasting studies combine systematic benchmarking, uncertainty quantification and model explainability within a single framework, or contrast two epidemiologically distinct settings. This study addresses that gap with three objectives: to benchmark a deep recurrent architecture against alternative machine-learning models in two contrasting settings; to quantify predictive uncertainty and validate the framework against independent surveillance data; and to identify the climatic predictors and lags driving the predictions. The BiLSTM implemented here captures the long-term temporal dependencies inherent in climate-driven transmission dynamics. Historical climate data (1985–2014) from the CMIP6 historical experiment were combined with CMIP6 multi-model future projections (2015–2080) under the SSP585 scenario to assess the climatic determinants of malaria incidence. The BiLSTM was calibrated using rainfall and temperature anomalies and benchmarked against six machine-learning models (standard LSTM, GRU, ANN, SVR, Random Forest and Decision Tree), which it matched or exceeded, and externally validated using independent national malaria surveillance data from Senegal and Nigeria. Results show that eastern Senegal experienced a +1.5 °C warming and 20% rainfall decline, while northern Nigeria warmed by +1.2 °C with a 15% rainfall increase. Under SSP585, additional warming of +2–3 °C is projected. The proposed BiLSTM model achieved high predictive accuracy in reproducing the VECTRI-simulated malaria incidence (R 2 between 0.93 and 0.98 across the training, validation and test partitions of both countries). Spatial projections indicate persistent hotspots in southeastern Senegal (Kedougou) and a northward expansion of risk zones in Nigeria by mid-century under SSP585. When the same framework is instead trained and evaluated on observed malaria surveillance data with observed NASA POWER climate in an autoregressive, one-step-ahead setting, it yields a more realistic estimate of operational forecasting skill (test R 2 = 0.72 for Senegal and 0.77 for Nigeria); the near-perfect accuracy obtained against the climate-generated target should therefore be interpreted as an upper bound rather than real-world performance.

title: Beyond the black swan: climate change and the evolving risk of multi-mycotoxin contamination
abstract: Major mycotoxin contamination events have traditionally been treated as “black swans,” rare, high-impact episodes that are unpredictable in advance and explained only after they occur. This framing assumes long intervals between events and a single dominant toxin per episode, an assumption that reflects, in part, historical single-analyte monitoring rather than proof that other toxins were biologically absent. Climate change is a plausible driver of change in both assumptions. As interacting climate factors, temperature, water availability and atmospheric CO 2 , become more frequent and more extreme, episodes that used to be spaced by decades could increasingly occur several times within the same cropping season. This would not only be a change in frequency. The same interacting factors have been shown, in experimental systems, to modify, and in many cases widen, the range of conditions under which mycotoxigenic fungi grow and, at the same time, the range of conditions under which they produce toxin, so that windows that used to be separate can overlap for several species at once. The consequence, consistent with survey data across several crops, food products and continents, though improved multi-analyte detection likely also contributes to it, may not be simply more of one toxin but the regular co-occurrence of multiple mycotoxins in the same raw material. Current risk models, surveillance programs and legislation remain largely built around single-toxin, single-species assumptions calibrated on historical, regional data. This Perspective proposes an ecological framework linking climate change to an increased risk of multi-mycotoxin contamination, offered as a plausible hypothesis rather than an established transition, and outlines what this implies for monitoring, modeling and regulation.

title: Deep learning for biodegradable metallic biomaterials: from degradation modeling to performance prediction with a practical case study
abstract: Biodegradable metallic implants are transitioning from laboratory concept to clinical deployment, yet predicting their corrosion rate and residual strength in the physiological environment remains a substantial scientific challenge. The interplay of electrochemical, mechanical, and biological factors creates a high-dimensional problem that conventional modelling cannot easily capture, while experimental datasets are often too sparse and fragmented for traditional statistical approaches. Deep learning architectures, including graph, recurrent, and transformer networks, combined with physics-informed loss functions, now offer accurate forecasts of degradation rates, yield strength, and biological responses. Interpretation tools such as SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and attention mapping further reveal which alloying elements and processing parameters dominate performance, tightening the prediction-experiment loop. This work also demonstrates MAGIC (Multi-task Alloy Gated-network with Integrated Constraints), a multi-task learner that fuses composition and processing modalities through learned uncertainty weighting. On a magnesium alloy dataset of 600 records it delivers cross-validated R 2 values of 0.864 for ultimate tensile strength and 0.907 for yield strength, with root-mean-square errors of 28.0 and 26.8 MPa for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and yield strength (YS), outperforming seven standard baselines and providing a reproducible template. The boundary of this contribution is explicitly emphasised: MAGIC predicts the pristine (as-processed) ultimate tensilestrength and yield strength of undegraded material; it does not predict corrosion rates or post-implantation residual strength, and the coupling between corrosion damage and mechanical degradation is identified as a key open direction rather than a solved capability. Substantial barriers persist, notably the gap between in vitro and in vivo environments, scarce openly shared data, and the rigorous demands of clinical validation. Nevertheless, deep learning is progressively integrating into biodegradable metal research, and the central question is evolving from feasibility to whether the community can establish the required data infrastructure and interdisciplinary trust.

title: Rotation system reshapes soil profile environmental gradients to reorganize bacterial communities and decouple potential nitrogen cycling functions
abstract: Cropping systems reshape soil profile environmental gradients, thereby driving the vertical reorganization of bacterial communities and regulating the coupling between microbial communities and predicted nitrogen-cycling (N-cycling) potential. This study integrated soil chemical analyses, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, co-occurrence network analysis, PICRUSt2-based functional prediction, and structural equation modeling (SEM) across three long-term cropping systems: unclaimed land (U), tobacco–maize rotation (R), and continuous tobacco cropping (C), sampled at three soil depths (0–20, 20–40, and 40–60 cm; n = 3). Environmental drivers exhibited distinct vertical shifts, with readily available nutrients (AN, AK, and AP) dominating surface soils (0–20 cm), microbial biomass (MBC and MBN) governing subsurface soils (20–40 cm), and total nutrient pools (OM, TN, and TP) becoming increasingly important in deeper soils (40–60 cm). Rotation buffered vertical environmental changes, increased bacterial richness in the 0–40 cm profile, enriched nitrifying and nitrogen-fixing taxa (e.g., Nitrospira, Sphingomonas, and MND1), and maintained higher predicted N-cycling potential throughout the soil profile, accompanied by enhanced network modularity and robustness. In contrast, continuous cropping reduced surface soil pH, OM, MBC, and MBN (with MBN declining by>60%), promoted stress-associated taxa (e.g., Bacillus and Lactobacillus), and weakened network connectivity and robustness, particularly at 20–40 cm where network fragmentation was most evident. SEM revealed a stronger statistical coupling among soil environment, bacterial communities, microbial networks, and predicted N-cycling potential under rotation (GOF > 0.7), whereas continuous cropping showed weakened associations among these components. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that crop rotation promotes the stability of soil microbial ecological functions by preserving environmental gradient continuity and enhancing network resilience, whereas continuous cropping disrupts microbial network organization and weakens the linkage between resource availability and predicted functional potential. This study highlights the importance of maintaining multiscale environmental and microbial connectivity for improving the sustainability of agricultural soil ecosystems.

title: Efficient-tomato: a high-precision and lightweight method for cherry tomato ripeness and disease detection
abstract: Accurate detection of cherry tomatoes at different ripeness and disease stages is important for automated harvesting and crop-quality monitoring, but illumination variation, fruit overlap, leaf occlusion, complex backgrounds, and small target sizes remain challenging. This study proposes Efficient-Tomato, a lightweight detector developed from YOLOv8s through the coordinated use of EfficientViT, BiFormer, CARAFE, and WIoUv1. EfficientViT serves as the backbone for lightweight multiscale feature extraction. BiFormer is inserted into the neck to enhance informative spatial regions, while CARAFE and lightweight neck-channel adaptation improve content-aware feature reconstruction. WIoUv1 replaces the CIoU component of the bounding-box regression loss, with DFL retained. The model was evaluated on a consolidated dataset of 1,583 original images containing six categories: disease, half-ripe, overripe, ripe, rotten, and unripe. The original images were divided into training, validation, and test subsets before augmentation, and only the training subset was augmented. Each model configuration was trained independently three times, and arithmetic means were reported. Compared with YOLOv8s, Efficient-Tomato increased precision from 89.5% to 97.5%, recall from 87.3% to 96.9%, mAP@0.5 from 88.5% to 96.7%, and mAP@0.5:0.95 from 81.6% to 87.9%. The F1 score calculated from the tabulated mean precision and recall increased from 88.4% to 97.2%. FPS increased from 150.2 to 172.5, while the parameter count decreased from 22.5 M to 14.9 M. These results indicate that the coordinated design improves detection performance while reducing model complexity. Because inference speed was measured on an NVIDIA V100 GPU, further validation on embedded devices and harvesting robots is required before field deployment.

title: Attention-enhanced YOLOv8n-CLS for lightweight and efficient tomato leaf disease classification
abstract: Tomato leaf diseases substantially reduce crop yield and fruit quality, creating a need for accurate, computationally efficient, and potentially deployable image-based disease-screening systems for precision agriculture. This study presents an Attention-Enhanced YOLOv8n-CLS framework for tomato leaf disease classification by integrating a lightweight spatial attention mechanism to enhance the representation of spatially informative image features while maintaining a compact computational structure. Unlike conventional object detection approaches that require bounding-box annotations, the proposed framework formulates disease recognition as an image-level classification task, requiring only class labels and thereby simplifying dataset preparation and model training. Experiments were conducted on two publicly available benchmark datasets, namely the PlantVillage Tomato Dataset and the Kaggle Tomato Leaf Disease Dataset. A systematic evaluation comprising binary and multiclass classification, five-fold cross-validation, ablation analysis, cross-dataset evaluation, comparative benchmarking, computational assessment, and Grad-CAM-based visualization was performed to assess classification performance, stability, transferability, and computational efficiency. The Attention-Enhanced YOLOv8n-CLS achieved a maximum classification Accuracy of 98.90%, an AUC of 0.991, a computational complexity of 7.5 GFLOPs, and an average inference speed of approximately 45 FPS on the evaluated computing platform. In five-fold cross-validation, the proposed model achieved a mean Accuracy of 98.50% ± 0.14% on the PlantVillage Tomato Dataset and 97.82% ± 0.29% on the Kaggle Tomato Leaf Disease Dataset. The model also demonstrated competitive performance relative to representative deep learning architectures, including ResNet50, DenseNet201, ResNet152V2, MobileNetV2, and YOLOv5. The cross-dataset experiments further demonstrated transferability between the evaluated PlantVillage and Kaggle image distributions using the 10 classes shared by the two datasets. The results indicate a favourable balance between classification performance and computational requirements under the evaluated experimental conditions, with potential for further investigation in resource-constrained applications. Grad-CAM visualization provided qualitative information about image regions associated with the model's classification decisions but did not independently establish biological causality or pathogen-specific recognition. Importantly, the proposed framework performs image-based symptom classification and preliminary disease screening using dataset-provided labels; it does not independently confirm causal pathogens. Therefore, the reported classification performance should not be interpreted as definitive pathogen diagnosis or field-level validation. Further evaluation using independently collected field images, laboratory-confirmed disease or pathogen status, diverse symptom presentations, and representative agricultural edge devices is required before practical agricultural deployment can be established.

title: Hierarchical cross-modal spatiotemporal attention network for crop yield prediction in complex Himalayan agroecosystems
abstract: Introduction Accurate crop yield prediction is essential for precision agriculture, climate-resilient farm management, and timely decision-making. However, yield prediction remains challenging because of complex, nonlinear, and multi-scale interactions among crop physiology, soil conditions, weather variability, and management practices. Conventional statistical, machine learning, and deep learning approaches, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, often have limitations in capturing long-range temporal dependencies, hierarchical spatial relationships, heterogeneous data modalities, and predictive uncertainty. Methods This study proposes a Hierarchical Cross-Modal Spatio-Temporal Attention Network (HCM-STAN) for crop yield prediction using a unified attention-based framework for integrating heterogeneous agro-environmental data. The architecture incorporates four principal components: (i) hierarchical spatio-temporal attention operating across tree, block, orchard, and regional scales; (ii) a cross-modal attention module for adaptive fusion of IoT-based soil sensor observations, weather data, plant physiological measurements, and drone-based multispectral imagery; (iii) a soil-aware attention head that explicitly models soil memory, hysteresis effects, and root-zone dynamics; and (iv) an uncertainty-aware prediction module combining Monte Carlo dropout and quantile regression to generate calibrated prediction intervals. The framework was evaluated using a multi-source dataset collected from Himalayan apple orchards during 2023–2026, comprising 1,247 monitored trees across three commercial orchards. Results The proposed HCM-STAN achieved an R 2 of 0.89 for four-week-ahead crop yield prediction, representing a 15.6% improvement over the CNN-LSTM baseline. Furthermore, zero-shot transfer to mango orchards achieved an R 2 of 0.67, corresponding to approximately 75% of the performance obtained under full training. Discussion The results demonstrate that integrating hierarchical spatio-temporal representation learning, cross-modal attention, soil-aware modelling, and uncertainty estimation can effectively address the heterogeneous and dynamic nature of crop yield prediction in complex mountain agroecosystems. The observed zero-shot transfer performance further indicates the potential of HCM-STAN to generalize across crop systems without crop-specific retraining. Overall, the proposed framework provides a promising foundation for reliable, uncertainty-aware yield forecasting and can support precision agriculture, climate-smart farm management, and data-driven decision-making in heterogeneous agroecosystems.

title: Case Report: Severe acute hypermagnesemia following inadvertent bath agent ingestion rapidly resolved by emergent hemodialysis
abstract: Severe acute hypermagnesemia from excessive magnesium (Mg 2+ ) exposure is rare but life-threatening and requires prompt recognition. We report a 54-year-old previously healthy man who presented to the emergency department with acute altered consciousness and generalized weakness. Physical examination showed stupor, hypothermia, hypotension, and generalized areflexia. Initial laboratory testing demonstrated mixed respiratory and metabolic acidosis, a normal serum creatinine concentration, and severe hypermagnesemia (serum Mg 2+ concentration, 15.8 mg/dL). The initial 12-lead ECG demonstrated diffuse ST-segment depression, and an artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) model identified an estimated mortality risk above the 99th percentile. Nasogastric decompression retrieved minimal gastric contents, and initial treatment with intravenous calcium, saline, and a loop diuretic did not produce meaningful neurological improvement. Emergent hemodialysis resulted in rapid recovery of consciousness and a decrease in serum Mg 2+ to 4.9 mg/dL during treatment, together with neurological improvement and a marked decline in AI-ECG-predicted mortality risk. Subsequent history-taking indicated inadvertent ingestion of approximately 100 mL of a private-label artificial hot-spring mineral preparation, for which spa personnel reported a nominal formulation of 30% magnesium chloride, 33% magnesium sulfate, and 10% potassium sulfate. He recovered without residual complications. This case emphasizes that a normal serum creatinine concentration at presentation does not preclude life-threatening magnesium toxicity after a large acute Mg 2+ exposure. Timely hemodialysis should be considered when severe symptoms persist despite initial therapy.

title: When Does Representation Learning Help Attack-Path Forecasting? A Controlled Multi-Cloud Study with CAPTURE-MC
abstract: Cloud defenders increasingly want to anticipate an attacker’s next move, not merely detect the last one. We study attack-path forecasting in multi-cloud environments: given the partial trace of an in-progress campaign, predict the next ATT&CK technique. We present CAPTURE-MC, a heterogeneous temporal-graph model that encodes cross-provider telemetry and forecasts the next technique under a transition prior, and we release MC-PathBench, a synthetic but structurally faithful benchmark with four leakage-controlled generalization splits (temporal, cross-cloud, unseen-composition, and campaign hold-out). Our central contribution is an honest, carefully controlled account of when learned temporal-graph representations help and when they do not. We find that the technique-transition structure is a very strong predictor: when the attacker’s current technique is known, a first-order Markov model and a uniform-over-allowed-transitions rule match or exceed CAPTURE-MC and a temporal-graph network, so the deep models add little in that idealized regime. The picture reverses in the realistic regime where the current technique must be inferred: as current-technique certainty degrades, the structural baselines, indexed entirely by it, collapse toward chance, whereas CAPTURE-MC degrades gracefully and nearly doubles their accuracy when the current technique is unknown. CAPTURE-MC is likewise robust to a substantially corrupted transition prior (missing, spurious, or misdirected edges). We also report, transparently, where CAPTURE-MC does not help: gradient-boosted trees remain the best per-event and campaign-level detectors; next-entity and time-to-transition prediction are at chance for every model; and the conformal layer, while achieving coverage, yields prediction sets larger than the list of allowed successors and so is not an efficiency gain. The prior is estimated only from training data, never the generator’s graph, which removes a leakage path present in an earlier version of this work and changes several conclusions. The practical lesson for predictive cloud defense is that structural baselines are strong and must be reported, and that the value of representation learning appears precisely where structural assumptions break down.

title: Pesticide Spraying Strategy Optimization for a Tracked Air-Assisted Spraying Robot Based on a Novel Virginia Creeper Optimization Algorithm
abstract: To address the limitations of conventional constant-rate pesticide application in adapting to spatial variations in crop canopy structure, this study proposes a pesticide spraying strategy optimization method for a tracked air-assisted spraying robot based on a novel Virginia Creeper Optimization Algorithm (VCOA). First, a multivariable nonlinear constrained optimization model is established by considering the coupled effects of robot chassis travelling speed, ducted-fan rotational speed, pump pressure, equivalent nozzle atomization diameter parameter and spray-boom pitch angle. A comprehensive spraying effectiveness objective function is constructed and maximized objective function is constructed to coordinate droplet deposition performance, canopy coverage uniformity, pesticide utilization efficiency, off-target loss, and operational energy consumption. Then, inspired by the random spreading, adhesive climbing, and phototropic growth mechanisms of Virginia creeper, VCOA is developed to enhance the balance between global exploration and local exploitation in complex non-convex optimization problems. The convergence behavior and optimization capability of the proposed algorithm are evaluated using benchmark functions and comparative algorithms. Furthermore, the algorithm is introduced into the variable-rate spraying control process of a tracked air-assisted spraying robot, and its practical effectiveness is verified through simulation and field spraying experiments. The results show that VCOA exhibits superior convergence robustness and global search capability compared with the selected benchmark algorithms. In field experiments, the VCOA-based spraying strategy significantly improves droplet deposition coverage, deposition density, and spatial uniformity, demonstrating its effectiveness and application potential for precision pesticide application in intelligent plant protection equipment.

title: MSTDP: Multimodal Spatio-Temporal Forecasting with Self-Correcting Attention and Hierarchical Feature Interaction
abstract: Real-world spatiotemporal data are frequently imbalanced across spatial regions and collected from heterogeneous sources with different structures, sampling frequencies, and semantics. Sparse regions provide limited supervision, whereas modality redundancy and structural heterogeneity make it difficult to exploit complementary information during fusion. To address these challenges, we propose MSTDP, a Multimodal Spatio-Temporal Data Prediction framework. A causal target-clock alignment procedure first maps high-frequency, low-frequency, and irregular observations to the forecasting timeline without using future information. MSTDP then employs modality-specific encoders to obtain source-dependent representations and constructs first-, second-, and third-order interaction features through a Multilayer Feature Interaction module. A Hierarchical Feature Fusion module aggregates the interaction features. To improve intermediate and high-level representations, we further introduce two plug-and-play components: a Unified Feature Interaction Module, which performs soft alignment and bidirectional feature exchange between heterogeneous token sequences, and a Self-Correcting Transformer Module, which recalibrates modality-specific and fused representations through cross-modal attention. A spatial-unit-balanced training objective first normalizes the prediction error within each region and then averages equally across regions, preventing data-rich regions from dominating the gradients. We evaluate MSTDP on four real-world benchmarks covering urban housing-price forecasting, county-level crop-yield prediction, and traffic-speed forecasting. Relative to the strongest baseline in each setting, MSTDP reduces RMSE by up to 8.6% and MAPE by up to 11.5%. Ablation studies confirm that hierarchical fusion, unified feature interaction, and self-correction provide complementary improvements. Observation-density stress tests further show that the model remains robust when entire spatial units are unavailable. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of MSTDP on the four evaluated datasets and provide empirical evidence that its interaction and correction modules can be reused across the studied housing, agriculture, and traffic forecasting tasks. Broader transferability to other multisource spatiotemporal problems remains to be established.

title: Hybrid Vulnerability Discovery in the Wild: Automated Screening, Fine-Tuned LLMs, and Four Published CVEs
abstract: Automated security scanners produce many alerts, but disclosure requires evidence of attacker control, reachability, impact, and reproducibility. We present an evidence-gated workflow that screens recently updated Python AI/ML and data-science packages then uses two separately fine-tuned open-weight agents to distinguish vulnerability plausibility from CVE worthiness: the first tests attacker control and reachability, and the second assesses novelty and impact before human proof-of-concept validation and coordinated disclosure. In a targeted campaign covering 400 packages, screening yielded 1292 clustered signals; the agents retained 96 vulnerability hypotheses, including 65 provisional CVE candidates. All 13 Critical or High candidates were reproduced with benign proofs of concept and acknowledged by a CVE Numbering Authority as valid security findings. As of 30 September 2026, four had published CVEs affecting OpenMed, Python StateMachine, uproot, and SpeechBrain; five had maintainer-acknowledged patches in progress; and four awaited maintainer response. Field detection accuracy was not measured.

title: Improving Estimates of Spatially Distributed Agricultural Land Use Using Pesticide Data
abstract: Accurate, spatially resolved agricultural land-use data are essential for estimating water demand, evaluating agricultural production, and understanding long-term changes in managed landscapes. However, existing land-use datasets are often temporally discontinuous, particularly for historical periods, and remotely sensed classifications face persistent challenges distinguishing spectrally similar crop types, capturing sub-annual rotations, and separating active from abandoned plantings. We developed the California Pesticide Use Reporting Land-Use Estimator (CalPUR-LUE), which converts grower-reported pesticide-application records into annual estimates of land use by crop class and cropped acreage at approximately 1-square-mile resolution across California. CalPUR-LUE performance was evaluated for 2018 using complementary spatial, categorical, and quantitative comparisons with California Department of Water Resources (CADWR) remotely sensed land-use data and county-level agricultural economic reports. At the county-meridian-township-range-section (COMTRS) scale, CalPUR-LUE and CADWR acreage estimates showed substantial proportional agreement (log-transformed Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient = 0.77) with a mean proportional bias of −15%. Crop-class agreement was high when CalPUR-LUE identified agricultural activity, with user’s accuracy exceeding 83% for all evaluated crop classes. Overall categorical agreement was 67% (Cohen’s kappa = 0.56). Grain crop underestimation contributed substantially to disagreement; however, there is evidence of CADWR systematic overestimation of grain during 2016–2019. County-level agricultural reports further corroborated CalPUR-LUE estimates and, in several cases, aligned more closely with CalPUR-LUE than with CADWR. These results demonstrate that pesticide-use reporting provides an independent and complementary source of agricultural land-use information that can corroborate contemporary estimates and reconstruct annual spatially distributed land use where historical data are limited.

title: Study on Spatiotemporal Evolution, Decoupling Characteristics and Driving Mechanism of Agricultural Carbon Emissions from Technological Progress—Panel Evidence from 21 Prefectures (States) in Sichuan Province, China
abstract: Against the dual goals of agricultural and rural carbon emission reduction, carbon sequestration and food security guarantee, this paper uses municipal panel data of 21 prefectures in Sichuan Province from 2015 to 2024 to calculate agricultural carbon emissions from multiple dimensions including farmland utilization, paddy field methane, crop cultivation, straw burning and livestock breeding. The standard deviational ellipse model (SDE) is adopted to reveal the spatiotemporal pattern of agricultural carbon emissions, and the Tapio decoupling model is applied to identify the decoupling relationship between agricultural carbon emissions and the agricultural economy. A panel model is constructed. The Breusch–Pagan Lagrange Multipkier (LM) test and Hausman test are performed to select the random-effects model to examine the impact of agricultural technological progress on agricultural carbon emissions. Robustness tests and grouped heterogeneity analysis are carried out. Furthermore, mediation and moderation models are introduced to identify the internal transmission paths and boundary conditions. The results show that: (1) From 2015 to 2024, the total agricultural carbon emissions in Sichuan Province generally declined. Animal husbandry was the primary emission source while carbon emissions from crop cultivation showed an upward trend, and carbon emission intensity kept decreasing. The spatial pattern of agricultural carbon emissions presented strong path dependence; the emission centroid remained stable in the central basin with a northeast–southwest spatial distribution. (2) The relationship between agricultural carbon emissions and the agricultural economy in Sichuan Province fluctuated alternately between strong decoupling and weak decoupling. Sustained and stable strong decoupling has not yet been achieved, and the incremental emissions from crop cultivation constitute a key factor disturbing the decoupling state. (3) Benchmark regression results indicated that agricultural technological progress significantly curbed regional agricultural carbon emissions, and urbanization also exerted emission-reduction effects. The proportion of primary industry, land scale operation and grain planting ratio significantly increased agricultural carbon emissions, whereas rural residents’ income and agricultural industrial structure showed no significant impacts. The carbon emission reduction effect of agricultural technological progress, constrained by regional endowments, presented notable regional heterogeneity. The emission reduction effect of technological progress was significant in plain and non-ethnic farming areas, while it was difficult to achieve emission reduction merely by relying on mechanization in ethnic regions and non-plain mountainous areas. (4) Mechanism tests demonstrated that fertilizer application intensity played a partial mediating role between agricultural technological progress and agricultural carbon emissions. Agricultural technological progress can indirectly reduce carbon emissions by lowering fertilizer application intensity. The multiple cropping index exerted a positive moderating effect. The higher the multiple cropping index, the stronger the inhibitory effect of agricultural technological progress on agricultural carbon emissions. This paper identified key regions, core emission reduction targets and directions for technological optimization for differentiated low-carbon agricultural governance in Sichuan Province, and provided empirical evidence for developing agriculture-specific carbon emission reduction plans tailored to local conditions. It also clarified the limits of the emission reduction effectiveness of agricultural technological advancements across different regions. The research findings can provide precise guidance for the green and low-carbon transformation of regional agriculture, assist local governments in addressing weaknesses in agricultural emission reduction efforts and mitigate risks such as rising emissions from crop cultivation and rebound effects from decoupling.

title: Do Agricultural Machinery Services Promote Grain-Oriented Land Use? The Countervailing Role of Farmland Rent in Rural China
abstract: Rural labor out-migration and low comparative returns to grain challenge food security in China. This study examines the association between agricultural machinery services (AMS) and the allocation of sown land between grain and economic crops, and whether farmland rent is linked to a countervailing pattern. Using data from the 2021 China Household Finance Survey (CHFS) for 421 villages and 5496 farming households, supplemented by the 2019 wave for the instrumental-variable analysis and additional diagnostics, we estimate province fixed-effects and instrumental-variable models. Greater AMS coverage is associated with a lower economic-crop share. Grain-specific service intensity is positively associated with relative gross sales revenue from grain and with farmland rent. Higher rent is positively associated with the economic-crop share in villages with active rental markets, but the estimated rent-related indirect association is imprecise: its bootstrap confidence interval includes zero. The data do not provide robust evidence that the rent association diminishes at higher rent levels. The association between AMS coverage and the economic-crop share is more negative in villages with better irrigation. These findings suggest that machinery services are linked to grain-oriented cropping, while the possible land-market feedback requires further investigation.

title: PREF-VG: Topology-Conditioned Residual Adaptation for Probabilistic Multi-Horizon Student Engagement Forecasting
abstract: Forecasting student engagement can inform timely support in online education. However, the incremental predictive value of evolving behavioural topology beyond numerical temporal representations remains unclear. Here, behavioural engagement is operationalised through recorded activity in the virtual learning environment (VLE). We propose Prefix-based Residual Engagement Forecasting with Visibility Graphs (PREF-VG) for probabilistic multi-horizon forecasting. Within each observed window, natural visibility graphs yield ordered insertion-time descriptors of connection spans and local connectivity. A recurrent encoder summarises this sequence, and a gated residual adapter refines selected logit and log-mean parameters of a pretrained causal temporal convolutional network forecaster (Raw-TCN). The model estimates a hurdle negative-binomial click-count distribution and a binomial active-day marginal across four consecutive weeks from 56-day histories. Experiments on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset used chronologically held-out course presentations and student-disjoint partitions. In the primary evaluation, under shared validation-based post-processing, results averaged across four horizons and five seeds showed that PREF-VG reduced click-count and active-day mean absolute errors by 3.24% and 4.19% relative to Raw-TCN, while increasing the area under the precision–recall curve for future inactivity from 0.7518 to 0.7686. On the primary test set, PREF-VG improved all five metrics over a parameter-matched raw-sequence adapter. In the alternative evaluation, gains over this control were supported for activity probabilities, inactivity ranking and active-day forecasts, with less certain click-count improvements. These comparisons support the incremental predictive value of insertion-time topology within the evaluated residual adaptation framework.

title: Integrated Soil–Crop System Management Promotes Microbial Necromass and Soil Organic Carbon Sequestration in Black Soil Through Microbial Transformation and Aggregate Protection
abstract: Long-term intensive cultivation has degraded soil structure and reduced soil organic carbon (SOC) retention in the black soils of Northeast China. However, the processes underlying SOC accumulation under integrated soil–crop system management (ISSM) remain poorly understood. An 11-year field experiment compared farmers’ practice (FP), high-yield and high-efficiency practice (IP), super-high-yield practice (HY), and ISSM. We assessed SOC stocks, aggregate stability, organic carbon chemistry, extracellular enzyme activities, microbial carbon-use traits, microbial community composition, and microbial necromass carbon (MNC), and used partial least squares path modeling as an exploratory analysis of potential linkages. Compared with FP, ISSM increased SOC content and stock by 87.0 and 77.0%, respectively, and achieved an SOC sequestration rate of 2.8 Mg C ha−1 yr−1. ISSM also increased mean weight diameter and geometric mean diameter by 45.0 and 61.0%, increased microbial biomass carbon and carbon use efficiency by 205.2 and 100.0%, and decreased qCO2 by 71.1%. Bacterial and fungal necromass carbon increased by 100.0 and 70.0%, respectively. The relative abundance of taxa operationally classified as growth-oriented also increased under ISSM. However, MNC/SOC did not differ significantly among treatments, while SOC aromaticity and hydrophobicity declined. Path analysis suggested that microbial carbon transformation was positively associated with necromass formation, whereas aggregate stability was associated with MNC and SOC retention. These results indicate that ISSM synchronously enlarged SOC and microbial necromass pools through sustained carbon inputs, efficient microbial transformation, and aggregate-mediated physical protection rather than through increased chemical recalcitrance.

title: Examining Ferrihydrite Nanomaterials: From Structure and Biosynthesis to Biomedical and Agricultural Applications
abstract: This multidisciplinary work is an attempt to synthesize advances in ferrihydrite (Fh, Fe10O14(OH)2·nH2O) research and applications ranging from physics to nanoagriculture. Fh nanoforms obtained via chemical or “green” synthesis methods using various bacterial cultures display unique catalytic and enzyme-like properties, surface reactivity, and magnetic properties. SAXS and SANS, supported by model-dependent fitting (FITTER) and model-independent ATSAS tools (Guinier approximation, p(r) function, and ab initio reconstruction), together with Porod-law and fractal analysis, provide a coherent multi-scale picture. Biogenic nanoparticles produced by Klebsiella oxytoca are built from 1–2 nm crystallites embedded in an organic matrix and exhibit a cultivation-dependent, hierarchical architecture: e.g., Fe12 yields a two-level hierarchical structure, whereas Fe34 produces a sponge-like surface. SANS further reveals that ferrihydrite nanoparticles in complex with lactate dehydrogenase form a core–shell bionanocomposite. The practical applications lie primarily in the biomedical field and plant cultivation, with significant implications for medicine and food production. A more thorough understanding of the underlying mechanisms, as well as studies to determine precise dosages and application methods, is critical. Investigating the biological activity of Fh NPs under both physiological and pathological conditions will facilitate the development of biologically informed engineering strategies for new Fh-based agents aimed at treating serious human diseases, improving plant mineral nutrition, protecting plants from phytopathogens, and remediating soil. Future directions include engineering nano-agrochemicals by functionalizing nanoforms tailored to specific crop types and soils with distinct physicochemical properties.

title: Integrated Flame Weeding and Biochar Reutilization Enhance Soybean Yield by Promoting Soil Microbial Abundance
abstract: Weed interference and crop residue are major constraints on sustainable soybean production, particularly in intensive tropical agriculture. Flame weeding provides a non-chemical approach for weed management, but the agronomic value of carbonized residues generated during this process remains largely unexplored. In this study, flame-weeding temperatures ranging from 300 to 800 °C were first screened based on weed carbonization efficiency and air-quality condition, after which 500 and 600 °C were selected for field evaluation. A two-season field experiment was conducted using a 3 × 2 treatment structure combining three pre-sowing flame-weeding temperatures (0, 500, and 600 °C) with or without biochar from flame-weeding (BFW) foliar spraying. Each treatment included four replicates. Flame weeding was applied before soybean sowing, whereas BFW foliar spraying was performed at the V4, R2, R4, and R6 growth stages. Flame weeding altered the soil environment, increasing electrical conductivity and reducing soil nematode abundance. Combined treatments produced the highest yields in soybean. In particular, T600-BFW increased the yield per plant by 73.32% and 32.43% relative to the CK in the two seasons, respectively. Flame weeding exerted a significant lethal effect on soil nematodes. Soil nematode density declined from 149.75 to 2.92 ind·20 g−1 of soil at week 10 following T600 treatment. Compared to CK, T600-BFW increased the root nodule number by 31.71%. The quantities of bacteria, fungi, and actinomycetes in T500 and T600 increased significantly after flame weeding. Redundancy analysis identified soil temperature, electrical conductivity, and pH as major variables associated with microbial community variation. The PLS-PM model showed that soil microorganisms exerted a significant positive effect on soybean yield. These findings indicate that flame weeding and BFW reutilization enhance soybean yield through complementary soil–microbe–root and leaf physiological improvement. This integrated strategy provides a potential pathway for simultaneously managing weeds, reutilizing field-derived carbonized biomass, and improving soybean production.

title: Combining Ability and Hybrid Performance of Cowpea Landraces Under Semiarid Conditions
abstract: Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp.) plays a key role in food security and income generation in semiarid regions, particularly for smallholder farming systems in the Brazilian semiarid. However, productivity remains low because of environmental limitations, genetic constraints, and traditional crop management practices. We evaluated diallel crosses among cowpea landraces to identify superior parents and cross combinations in terms of earliness and grain yield under semiarid conditions. Six landrace accessions, previously selected through participatory prospecting for adaptability and yield stability, were crossed in a complete diallel design to produce 15 F1 hybrids and their reciprocal crosses. The hybrids were evaluated under field conditions in the semiarid region during the 2023 growing season using a randomized complete block design with ten replications. The evaluations were conducted according to each genotype’s developmental stage and immature pod formation. Early-maturing varieties were harvested at 60 days, intermediate and late varieties between 65 and 75 days. At physiological maturity, early and intermediate genotypes were harvested at 80 days, while late genotypes were harvested between 85 and 90 days. General combining ability (GCA) and specific combining ability (SCA) were estimated using Griffing’s Method I (fixed-effects model), and treatment means were compared using the Scott–Knott test at the 5% significance level. Significant GCA and SCA effects (p < 0.05) were detected for 12 of the 14 evaluated traits, whereas reciprocal effects were significant for seven traits. The hybrid combinations L1 × L4, L1 × L5, and L4 × L5, and their reciprocal crosses, exhibited superior agronomic performance, highlighting their potential as valuable genetic resources for cowpea breeding under semiarid environments.

title: In-Depth Characterisation and Microwave-Assisted Conversion of Opuntia ficus-indica into High-Value-Added Platform Compounds
abstract: Nowadays, humanity is facing a paradigm change in the productive model, switching from fossil-based carbon sources and a linear economy, to more sustainable and circular alternatives. In this regard, lignocellulosic biomass is considered as a perfect substitute for fossil-based carbon sources. Opuntia ficus-indica (OFI) is a crassulacean acid metabolism species, capable of growing in arid places that are not suitable for food production. In this work, a systematic fractionation process combined with analytical techniques (nuclear magnetic resonance, thermogravimetric analysis, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy) unveiled the extraordinarily high carbohydrate content of OFI fruit. Therefore, OFI fruit is a perfect feedstock for the obtention of high-value-added chemicals, namely levulinic acid (LA) and 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF). By microwave-assisted thermochemical treatment of the most suitable fraction, LA was obtained in a 22.1 wt. % yield in an aqueous monophasic system, and 5-HMF in an 11.5 wt. % yield in a biphasic system. Reuse of the catalyst and co-catalyst in a monophasic system led to 5-HMF in a 14.3 wt. % yield after five cycles, avoiding the need for an organic co-solvent. This work demonstrates the potential of this feedstock to obtain high-value-added chemicals, employing marginal land in environments where other crops are unable to grow.

title: SDU-G2A: Self-Derived Uncertainty Guidance for Ground-to-Aerial Remote-Sensing Image Synthesis with Probabilistic BEV Footprints
abstract: Urban planning and land-use monitoring require not only semantic land-cover maps, but also image-like overhead observations that preserve the spatial organization of urban scenes. Conventional remote-sensing segmentation and image-generation methods usually operate by obtaining available overhead imagery or in reliable overhead conditions. Street-level panoramas are easier to collect and update, but they observe the target scene from a limited terrestrial viewpoint. Recovering overhead information from a single panorama, therefore, requires inferring from an unobserved land-cover footprint before synthesizing a nadir-view remote-sensing image. We propose SDU-G2A, a two-stage framework for aerial image synthesis from a single ground panorama. Stage I predicts a probabilistic BEV land-cover footprint from the input panorama. The proposed Azimuthal-Radial Mapper propagates azimuthal evidence and applies distance-aware supervision to improve semantic recovery in occluded and far-field regions. Stage II converts the inferred footprint into a remote-sensing-like aerial image through diffusion-based synthesis, making the reconstructed urban structure available in an overhead-image form for visual interpretation and geospatial-correspondence evaluation. The main difficulty is that the inferred BEV footprint exhibits spatially varying reliability. Treating it as a deterministic condition can force cross-view segmentation errors into the generated image. SDU-G2A, therefore, derives a pixel-wise uncertainty map from Stage I predictions and uses it as a spatial reliability layer. This design preserves structures with high prediction confidence while allowing uncertain regions to be completed under text-guided and prior-driven generation. Experiments on VIGORv2 show that SDU-G2A improves BEV land-cover estimation, reduces radial prediction errors, and achieves stronger geospatial correspondence and aerial-feature distributional realism than representative G2A baselines. These results indicate that self-derived land-cover uncertainty can bridge cross-view semantic footprint inference and reliable remote-sensing image synthesis from accessible street-level observations.

title: Multi-Source Remote Sensing for Mangrove Mapping in South China: Sensor-Configuration Responses and Cross-Regional Model Applicability
abstract: Mangrove mapping increasingly integrates multisource remote sensing, yet the geographically transferable value of additional sensors remains uncertain. This study evaluated Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, Sentinel-1 and GF-3 SAR, GF-5 AHSI hyperspectral observations, terrain variables, and sensor-independent coastal-context information across five coastal regions of southern China. Five nested feature configurations (D1–D5) were tested with Random Forest, XGBoost, DeepLabV3, and SegFormer under true leave-one-study-area-out validation on 349,898 common 10 m coordinates; deep models were replicated across three random seeds. Model-averaged F1-scores were 0.9025, 0.9031, 0.9123, 0.9134, and 0.9220 for D1–D5, respectively, but differences were not statistically supported across held-out regions (Friedman χ2 = 0.48, p = 0.9754). Sentinel-1, GF-3, and their interaction showed small, geographically inconsistent contrasts. GF-5 effects were model- and preprocessing-dependent, and cross-scene normalization altered performance in contrasting directions. Gain and grouped-permutation analyses indicated model-specific predictor use and sensitivity rather than independent sensor contribution. Overall, multisource benefits depended on sensor configuration, model representation, geographic domain, and preprocessing conditions, supporting context-specific sensor selection and geographically independent validation.

title: Dual Category-Guided Spatial Mamba Network for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
abstract: With the rapid development of aerospace technology, remote sensing images contain increasingly rich feature information, while large variations in object scales and imbalanced category distributions pose great challenges to remote sensing semantic segmentation. Current mainstream methods often rely on attention mechanisms for global modeling, yet they tend to over-average features, making it difficult to capture minority categories and preserve fine-grained details. To address these limitations, we propose a Dual Category-Guided Spatial Mamba Network (DGSMNet) that combines dual category guidance with a spatial Mamba mechanism. Specifically, a Dual-Stage Category Guidance (DSCG) module is designed to extract class information via wavelet transforms and guide feature learning, ensuring proportional representation of all categories across channels and enabling the model to learn underrepresented classes. In addition, a Spatial Mamba (SPM) module is introduced to enhance long-range modeling while retaining sensitivity to local details. By integrating DSCG and SPM, the proposed DGSMNet improves category-aware representation and spatial modeling on the evaluated benchmarks. Extensive experiments on the ISPRS Vaihingen and Potsdam datasets demonstrate that DGSMNet achieves competitive performance among the compared methods.
