Rapid CAR-T manufacturing with low-intensity priming enhances CAR-T cell fitness and limits inflammatory programming in a phase 1 study.
abstract: Conventional chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T manufacturing requires prolonged ex vivo activation and expansion, which may compromise T cell fitness and promote inflammatory differentiation. Here, we developed PrimeCAR, a 2-day manufacturing strategy combining low-intensity anti-CD3 priming with IL-7 and IL-21. Compared with conventionally manufactured CAR-T cells, PrimeCAR products exhibited a distinct transcriptional state characterized by preserved stemness-associated programs and a PrimeCAR-enriched primed naive T cell (Tn)-like state. Following antigen stimulation, PrimeCAR cells preferentially engaged proliferative programs while limiting exhaustion-associated regulators and inflammatory mediators. Functionally, PrimeCAR cells demonstrated enhanced expansion, persistence, and durable antitumor activity in xenograft models. In investigator-initiated phase I studies of relapsed or refractory B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and B cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, PrimeCAR showed encouraging clinical activity with a favorable safety profile. Together, these findings demonstrate that rapid manufacturing with controlled early T cell priming selectively restrains inflammatory programming while preserving CAR-T cell fitness, providing a practical strategy for improving CAR-T manufacturing and therapeutic performance.

title: Pulmonary nodules: classification, biomarkers, signaling pathways, diseases, early diagnosis and management
abstract: Pulmonary nodules are increasingly detected by thoracic imaging and low-dose computed tomography-based lung cancer screening, but most are benign, transient, or indolent. Clinically, the key task is to distinguish nodules that require timely cancer-directed evaluation from those that can be safely observed. This review summarizes the classification, disease spectrum, risk assessment, early diagnosis, biomarkers, signaling mechanisms, translational models, and management of pulmonary nodules. We first distinguish imaging phenotypes and disease entities, then differentiate the individual-level models used to select candidates for lung cancer screening from the nodule-level models and structured reporting systems used after nodule detection. Low-dose computed tomography remains the foundation of screening and surveillance approaches, whereas magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography, nonsurgical biopsy, surgical diagnosis, and local therapies play more selective roles depending on the probability of malignancy and patient fitness. Noninvasive biomarkers, including circulating cellular, nucleic acid, methylation, protein, autoantibody, extracellular vesicle, and metabolic analytes, are most likely to serve as adjuncts to imaging and clinical risk assessment rather than as stand-alone diagnostic tests. Artificial intelligence may support detection, workflow efficiency, malignancy risk reclassification, invasiveness assessment, and multimodal integration, but its value depends on external validation, calibration, implementation, and prospective evidence of management benefit. Mechanistic studies of adenocarcinoma spectrum subsolid nodules have implicated the involvement of early oncogenic signaling, genomic instability, immune escape, stromal and vascular remodeling, and adaptive survival pathways. Translational models can support mechanistic and procedural research, but do not replicate real-world nodule management in patients. Overall, care for pulmonary nodules should be risk-adapted, longitudinal, multidisciplinary, and patient-centered.

title: FTO promotes human NK cell proliferation yet restricts effector functions.
CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
abstract: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1highHmgb2+ precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200+ fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1+ G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function. Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are a subset of myeloid cells with immunoregulatory function. Here, the authors demonstrate that CD200-expressing fibroblasts drive the differentiation of neutrophil precursors into suppressive PD-L1+ G-MDSCs in the local joint microenvironment in inflammatory arthritis.

title: Hybrid stacked bidirectional deep learning with attention based air pollution prediction for environmental sustainability
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: Environmental sustainability for air pollution monitoring necessitates utilization of advanced technologies like internet of things (IoT) devices and Artificial Intelligence (AI) AI to track air quality in real-time, controlling policy and measures to reduce to mitigate pollution for ensuring long-term environmental health. This mechanism aids sustainable development by safeguarding general public, combating climate change and establishing more flexible communities. Hence pollutant level monitoring is of paramount significance to maintain the pollutant concentrations under control. Nevertheless, pollutant concentration monitoring is not easy as it necessitates installing monitoring stations to obtain pertinent pollutant data that comes with high installation and maintenance costs. In this research, an attempt has been made to simulate the concentrations at three districts in Dhaka, Bangladesh using Deep Learning (DL) methods by applying Hybrid Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention Mechanism (HSBi-LSTMA) method for environmental sustainability. An efficient model specifically tailored for encoding and generating multi-class imbalance results using Label Encoded Synthetic Edited Nearest Neighbor-based pre-processing for different air pollution concentration features provided as input is introduced. Next, Hybrid Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention Mechanism first used attention mechanism to select the most influential features of the original air pollution concentration features and then used Hybrid Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory to generate the classified results for air pollution prediction. Extensive experiments were conducted on Air Pollution Monitoring Generated Using IoT dataset, comparing the HSBi-LSTMA method with two existing methods. The results demonstrate that the HSBi-LSTMA method significantly improves the air pollution prediction accuracy by 25% and reduces the mean absolute error by 46% as compared to the existing methods. With this the HSBi-LSTMA method represents a notable evolution in advancing environmental sustainability.

title: Phonological Posterior Probabilities as Interpretable Markers of Articulatory Impairment in Motor Speech Disorders.
abstract: PURPOSE This study examined whether phoneme-level posterior probabilities generated by an articulatory-informed deep learning model (Phonet) can serve as interpretable and sensitive markers of articulatory impairment in motor speech disorders (MSDs). The goal was to determine whether these features distinguish individuals with and without MSDs and reflect varying severity levels of articulatory impairment. METHOD A total of 676 participants (199 with MSDs, 477 without MSDs) completed a remotely captured word repetition task. Speech recordings were phonetically aligned, and posterior probabilities were extracted using a retrained version of the Phonet model, which estimates frame-level probabilities for 23 phonological classes. Segment-level posterior values were computed and compared across groups and severity levels using linear mixed-effects regression models. RESULTS Posterior probabilities were significantly reduced in the MSD group across all phoneme types. Within the MSD group, posterior probabilities decreased progressively with greater clinical severity, as measured by both perceptual sound distortion ratings and a cumulative articulation error score. Segment-specific analyses revealed systematic differences across phoneme classes, indicating that posterior probabilities capture distinct patterns of articulatory degradation associated with motor speech impairment. CONCLUSIONS Phoneme-level posterior probabilities serve as interpretable, segment-specific indicators of articulatory impairment in MSDs. These features differentiate clinical status and reflect gradations of severity, making them promising tools for augmenting traditional perceptual speech assessments. Their linguistic transparency and scalability support future clinical applications in diagnosis, monitoring, and targeted intervention.
journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR

title: Nonlinear vegetation dynamics driven by socio-ecological coupling in the alpine canyon region of northwestern Yunnan, China
abstract: Northwestern Yunnan, located in the core of the Hengduan Mountains, is both part of a global biodiversity hotspot and a vulnerable socio-ecological system. In this region, complex topography and human activities jointly shape vegetation change, which exhibits pronounced nonlinear dynamics. Using long-term remote-sensing data from 2000 to 2023, this study integrates the BFAST01 model with the optimal parameters-based geographical detector (OPGD) to characterise the coupled gradual-abrupt dynamics of fractional vegetation cover (FVC) and identify their associated driving mechanisms. The results show that: (1) regional vegetation conditions have generally improved but remain strongly constrained by vertical zonation; the 1500–3500 m belt functions as the core ecologically active zone, whereas areas above 4500 m exhibit an abrupt decline in FVC under extreme environmental stress. (2) Nonlinear analysis reveals an apparent vegetation recovery accompanied by substantial instability: ~80% of areas identified as significantly increasing display highly unstable growth trajectories, corresponding to a potential degradation-risk estimate of 73.3%. (3) Temperature and net primary productivity (NPP) form the fundamental natural baseline regulating vegetation dynamics, while the explanatory power of human activities—proxied by night-time light intensity—increased by 87.9% over the past two decades. Through nonlinear interactions with this baseline, human activities appear to exert a disproportionately strong restructuring influence on local ecological patterns. These findings reveal a mismatch between vegetation evolution and environmental pressures in alpine valley systems and provide cross-disciplinary evidence supporting differentiated governance strategies that reconcile energy development with long-term ecosystem resilience.

title: Using AI-powered modelling for drought forecasting in the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea
abstract: Context The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is vulnerable to drought due to monsoon-driven variable precipitation that affects agricultural production and water security. Reliable multi-timescale drought forecasting aids risk mitigation; however, nonlinear non-stationary drought signals are hard to capture indata-scarce regions. Aims This study developed and validated a Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise-Long Short-Term Memory (CEEMDAN-LSTM) hybrid Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) drought forecasting model. Its performance is systematically compared against a standalone LSTM for multiple SPEI timescales under DPRK climatic conditions. Methods Monthly meteorological records from 10 stations collected over a period of 60 years were used to derive SPEI time series. CEEMDAN decomposed SPEI into intrinsic mode functions for noise reduction and trend extraction as LSTM inputs; hyperparameters were optimised by Bayesian optimisation. Model performance was assessed with Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE), Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Key results CEEMDAN-LSTM generally outperformed standalone LSTM with timescale-dependent skill. Short-term SPEI predictions had inherent accuracy limits (NSE < 0.5) yet reduced relative errors. Medium- to long-term SPEI yielded large accuracy gains (max NSE = 0.95 for SPEI-12), with residual-distribution analysis showing effective suppression of extreme prediction errors. Spatial heterogeneity existed; complex terrain at stations such as Chongjin limited decomposition-driven improvements. Conclusions CEEMDAN-LSTM improves forecast skill by processing non-stationary drought signals. Without complex external predictors, this hybrid method enables reliable medium-long-term drought monitoring and extreme-event detection. Implications This single-variable time-series method enables data-efficient drought early warning for data-scarce regions, supporting drought response and adaptive water management without large-scale remote-sensing or global datasets.

title: The impact of digital investment on AGVC resilience-with a discussion on the moderating role of domestic market size
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to examine the impact of digital investment on Agricultural Global Value Chain (AGVC) resilience and investigate whether this effect varies with domestic market size. Using country-industry-year fixed effects with nine-year panel data from the University of International Business and Economics Global Value Chain Database and Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development Inter-Country Input-Output Tables, this study investigates the relationship between digital investment and AGVC resilience, analyzing heterogeneity by digital investment type, processing segment, and digital investment source. A triple interaction term-combining domestic market size, digital investment, and value chain downstreamness-is introduced to capture the interdependence of these determinants. This study finds that digital investment strengthens AGVC resilience through improved institutional environments and optimized resource allocation, with labor substitution serving as a key mechanism-particularly in high-income economies. Market scale amplifies this via reverse-pull and agglomeration effects. Gains are strongest in deep-processing sectors and domestic-digital-driven chains but absent in primary processing. Foreign digital reliance offers no benefit and may weaken resilience. The positive interaction between digital input and domestic market size is significant under lenient international regulations or high institutional quality, but insignificant under strict regulations or low institutional quality. This study addresses the critical yet often overlooked topic of AGVC resilience-a key pillar of contemporary food security. It examines how digital investment strengthens AGVC resilience, offering new insights into the stabilizing role of technology adoption amid rising global disruptions. The research further highlights how domestic market scale critically amplifies the effects of digital investment.

title: The dynamic relationship between inclusive leadership, job crafting towards strengths and employees’ career calling: the moderating role of core self-evaluation
abstract: Drawing on the Work as Calling Theory (WCT), we developed and tested a longitudinal model of how employees’ career calling develops over time. Specifically, we examined the dynamic relationships among job crafting towards strengths (JCS), inclusive leadership, and career calling, as well as the moderating role of core self-evaluation (CSE). This study employed a three-wave longitudinal survey design with data collected from 309 Chinese employees at three-month intervals and analyzed the data using cross-lagged panel modeling (CLPM), supplemented by random-intercept cross-lagged panel modeling (RI-CLPM). CLPM results showed that JCS and career calling positively predicted each other from T1 to T2, whereas only career calling predicted subsequent JCS from T2 to T3. Perceived inclusive leadership and career calling showed reciprocal positive associations across both time intervals. Supplementary RI-CLPM analyses further suggested that these interrelationships partly reflected stable between-person differences, although T2 career calling positively predicted T3 JCS and perceived inclusive leadership at the within-person level. Furthermore, moderation analyses showed that the association between JCS and subsequent career calling became more positive at higher levels of CSE across both time intervals, whereas CSE weakened the positive association between perceived inclusive leadership and subsequent career calling from T2 to T3. This study extends Work as Calling Theory by advancing a more dynamic understanding of career calling and offers practical insights into how organizations can foster employees’ career calling through proactive job crafting, supportive leadership, and differentiated developmental support.

title: Lean tools and Industry 4.0 technologies: a multidimensional analysis of firm performance
abstract: This study aims to examine how Lean/Lean Six Sigma (LSS) tools and Industry 4.0 (I4.0) technologies relate to firm performance across multiple dimensions and time horizons. Prior research has focused predominantly on productivity; the authors extend this view to profitability, capital structure, financing conditions and internationalization, distinguishing between short- (2020–2022) and long-term (2012–2022) performance effects. Using survey data from 140 industrial firms in inland Portugal, Lean/LSS and I4.0 constructs were modeled through a parcel-based measurement approach and estimated using Structural Equation Modeling with robust maximum likelihood. Performance indicators were derived from secondary accounting data, expressed as short- and long-term deltas. The structural model incorporates a theoretically grounded performance cascade linking productivity, return on assets, indebtedness, interest rate and internationalization. Lean/LSS and I4.0 technologies exhibit strong complementarity, yet neither shows direct effects on short- or long-term financial performance indicators. Instead, performance evolves through a powerful internal propagation mechanism: productivity improvements drive increases in return on assets, which in turn reduce indebtedness. This cascade is significant in the short term and substantially stronger over the long term, explaining up to 91.5% of long-term return on assets variance and 62% of long-term indebtedness variance. Downstream effects on interest rate and internationalization remain non-significant. By combining a multidimensional performance framework with explicit temporal differentiation and a performance to-performance cascade, this study clarifies how operational improvements translate, or fail to translate, into financial outcomes. Results show that the impact of Lean and I4.0 is indirect and unfolds primarily through internal financial propagation rather than direct effects on top-level accounting metrics. This contributes new empirical evidence on the temporal and structural mechanisms linking operational and digital transformation to firm performance and suggests that firms should adopt a long-term perspective, combining Lean and digital transformation initiatives while monitoring performance across multiple dimensions.
journal: International Journal of Lean Six Sigma

title: Life cycle environmental and cost analysis of a building insulated with different insulation materials: a British case study
abstract: To evaluate the whole-life environmental and economic performance of four insulation materials used in the UK, hemp fibre, wood fibre, glass wool and extruded polystyrene (XPS), by comparing their embodied and operational impacts within a consistent regulatory and modelling framework. A like-for-like assessment was conducted for a representative British single-family dwelling by integrating dynamic energy simulation with life cycle assessment (LCA) and life cycle costing (LCC) within a cradle-to-grave framework aligned with EN 15978 and EN 15804. Operational energy demand (Module B6) was simulated using DesignBuilder/EnergyPlus. Embodied impacts across Modules A1–A5 and end-of-life Modules C1–C4 were calculated in One Click LCA using Environmental Product Declarations and aligned generic datasets. Whole-life costs were evaluated over a 70-year study period using discounted cash-flow analysis. Operational energy dominates whole-life impacts for all insulation options, with annual energy use ranging from 11,598 to 11,833 kWh and minimal variation due to equivalent regulatory U-value targets. Whole-life global warming potential is similarly close (≈2,342–2,418 kgCO2e/m2, excluding Module D), with hemp fibre and glass wool showing slightly lower values. Embodied impacts (A1–A5) differ more clearly, favouring hemp fibre and glass wool over wood fibre and XPS. LCC results are tightly clustered (NPV ≈ £49.2k–£49.4k; ≈ £1.89k/year), suggesting cost is not a key differentiator. The study offers a UK-specific integrated comparison combining dynamic simulation, LCA and LCC, highlighting that while insulation choice affects embodied carbon, major carbon reductions depend primarily on reducing and decarbonising operational energy.

title: Dynamic Interpolation for Training-Time Prediction Reshaping in Low-Light Image Enhancement
abstract: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) is an important image/video processing problem for reliable visual systems under poor illumination, yet it remains challenging due to the strong coupling among insufficient illumination, noise amplification, and structural degradation. Existing methods typically rely on sophisticated network architectures or engineered objective functions. While effective, the former increases model complexity and deployment burden, whereas the latter relies on empirically tuned loss weights. We revisit supervised LLIE from a training-dynamics perspective and observe that brightness-related errors tend to converge early, while residual noise and structural artifacts often remain insufficiently optimized in later stages. To address this issue, we propose a Dynamic Interpolation Training-only Module (DITM), which introduces no additional learnable parameters and adaptively reshapes the model prediction for supervised feed-forward LLIE training. Specifically, DITM employs brightness-aware interpolation, in which the model prediction is combined with a mean brightness-aligned image constructed by rescaling the model prediction according to the mean brightness of the ground-truth image. By reducing the relative dominance of global brightness discrepancy, DITM makes residual local errors more influential during backpropagation after global luminance has largely stabilized, thereby facilitating artifact suppression and fine-detail restoration in later training stages. DITM is used only during training and is fully removed at inference, introducing no additional inference cost. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets and CNN-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based LLIE backbones show that DITM consistently improves fidelity and perceptual quality while preserving the inference-time architecture and introducing no additional inference-time computation.

title: Collaborative Neural Networks significantly Improve Global Aerosol Retrievals From Multi-Angle Polarimeters
abstract: We present the RemoTAP-Hybrid algorithm for global aerosol products retrieved from Multi-Angle Polarimeters (MAP), and apply it to one-year aerosol retrievals from the SPEXone MAP instrument. For the first time, Multiple Collaborated Neural Networks (MCNN) are used to perform global aerosol MAP retrievals over land and ocean. The combined use of MCNN with a full physics inversion in RemoTAP-Hybrid, significantly improves accuracy and computational speed of SPEXone aerosol retrievals. We validate the retrieved Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), Angstrom Exponent (AE), Single Scattering Albedo (SSA), Absorption AOD (AAOD), Fine mode AOD (FAOD), Coarse mode AOD (CAOD), and fine mode effective radius (reff_fine) with AERONET data. The validation suggests that aerosol retrievals can be further improved when extending the aerosol description to include a fine non-spherical mode. For AOD, the Root-Mean-Square Error (RMSE) is 0.051 (0.037) over land (ocean), while 78.3% (80.8%) of the retrievals are within the requirement formulated by the Global Climate Observing System (GCOS). The RMSE is 0.186 (0.207) for AE, 0.038 (0.044) for SSA, 0.023 (0.014) for AAOD, 0.047 (0.031) for FAOD, 0.043 (0.027) for CAOD, and 0.021 (0.026) for reff_fine over land (ocean). Compared to the current RemoTAP algorithm, RemoTAP-Hybrid shows improved agreement with AERONET for AOD, AE, and FAOD over land and ocean while the number of valid retrievals is increased by 4% (3%) over land (ocean) and the computational time is reduced by 43% (32%). Finally, we present the first global seasonal maps of aerosol optical and microphysical properties and chemical composition from SPEXone.

title: Fuelling Natural Enemies: Laboratory Assessment of Sugar Solution on the Longevity of Plutella xylostella and Its Parasitoids From Central Argentina
abstract: The provisioning of non‐host food sources, such as nectar, is a key strategy in conservation biological control to enhance the fitness and efficacy of natural enemies. The diamondback moth, Plutella xylostella (L.), a globally significant crucifer pest, is often regulated by a complex of larval parasitoids. However, the role of carbohydrate availability in shaping the longevity of this specific pest–parasitoid system in South America remains unexplored. This study assessed the impact of a 40% w/w 1:1 glucose: fructose sugar solution on the adult longevity of P. xylostella and its four dominant parasitoids in central Argentina: Diadegma leontiniae , Apanteles piceotrichosus , Oomyzus sokolowskii and Siphona sp. The facultative hyperparasitoid Conura pseudofulvovariegata was also evaluated. Survival analyses using Kaplan–Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models revealed that carbohydrate access significantly increased longevity in all species compared to a water‐only control (starvation condition) (Log‐rank test, p < 0.001 for all). However, the magnitude of the response was species‐specific, with C. pseudofulvovariegata showing the greatest relative benefit and P. xylostella the lowest. Under the sugar solution, C . pseudofulvovariegata achieved an exceptional median longevity of 172 days, significantly outliving all other species (Kruskal–Wallis, p < 0.001). These results demonstrate a shared but unequal dependency on exogenous carbohydrates, with natural enemies—particularly the hyperparasitoid—deriving a disproportionate survivorship advantage. The findings underscore that habitat management providing floral resources can selectively fuel natural enemy populations, potentially improving biological control of P. xylostella by enhancing parasitoid longevity and temporal persistence in the crop environment.

title: Early‐Stage Phenotypic Variation, Repeatability and Multivariate Profiling of Macauba ( Acrocomia spp. ) Hybrids
abstract: Macauba ( Acrocomia spp.) is an underutilised palm, native to Brazil and other tropical regions of the Americas, with substantial potential for vegetable oil and bioenergy production. However, its long juvenile phase delays the identification of promising parents and hybrid combinations. This study characterised the early vegetative performance of 60 individual macauba hybrids derived from intraspecific Acrocomia aculeata crosses and an interspecific A. aculeata × Acrocomia totai cross. Seventeen traits related to plant architecture, leaf morphology and biomass were evaluated over 2 years (2023–2024) using a mixed model fitted by restricted maximum likelihood, with the year as a fixed effect and accession as a random effect. Repeatability, predicted accession effects, trait correlations, principal component analysis, hierarchical clustering and a composite vigour index were also examined. Considerable phenotypic and persistent among‐plant variation was observed, where the number of fallen leaves showed the highest phenotypic and among‐plant coefficients of variation (78.2% and 55.9%, respectively). Repeatability was moderate for all traits ( R = 0.42–0.52), except central pinna width ( R = 0.11). Fresh mass of pinnae was strongly correlated with dry mass of pinnae ( r = 0.90) and moderately correlated with other vegetative and biomass‐related traits, including central pinna length ( r = 0.67), indicating that fresh pinna mass may serve as a practical proxy for pinna dry mass. The first two principal components explained 61.9% of the multivariate variation, driven mainly by biomass and structural traits. The vigour index identified 10 putative hybrid candidates, with H19‐14, H20‐5 and H17‐9 receiving the highest scores. These outcomes provide useful phenotypic information for early screening in macauba, although the selected plants require further validation through replicated, multiyear evaluations that include fruit and oil‐production traits. This work offers a practical starting point for accelerating early‐stage selection in macauba breeding to enhance its productivity as a sustainable bioenergy crop.

title: Operational integration of FT-IR spectroscopy into a genomics-based surveillance algorithm for Listeria monocytogenes
abstract: Rapid and cost-effective tools are needed to complement whole-genome sequencing (WGS) in Listeria monocytogenes surveillance, particularly in settings with limited sequencing capacity. We evaluated the operational integration of Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy as a first-line screening method within a genomics-based surveillance algorithm. A total of 24 L. monocytogenes isolates, including two epidemiologically confirmed outbreaks (n = 15) and unrelated sporadic isolates (n = 9), were analyzed. Species identification was performed by matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization–time-of-flight mass spectrometry, and genomic characterization was conducted using WGS, including multilocus sequence typing and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) analysis. FT-IR spectra were acquired using the IR Biotyper system, and serogroup prediction and clustering were assessed using artificial neural network-based classification and multivariate analysis. FT-IR achieved 100% concordance with WGS for serogroup assignment, with consistently high confidence scores. Clustering analysis generated FT-IR groupings broadly concordant with WGS-defined outbreak clusters, correctly grouping isolates differing by ≤9 SNPs within the same outbreak-associated clusters while differentiating most genetically unrelated strains. FT-IR excluded seven of nine unrelated isolates from outbreak-associated clustering, although partial overlap was observed among highly clonal CC1 isolates. Operationally, FT-IR enabled preliminary results within 48–72 h after isolation, significantly reducing turnaround time compared to WGS. This tiered approach improves cost-efficiency by optimizing sequencing resource allocation, which is particularly relevant for low- and middle-income settings. These findings demonstrate that FT-IR spectroscopy provides rapid and reliable preliminary typing and can be effectively integrated into routine workflows, enhancing early outbreak detection and supporting more efficient measures. To our knowledge, this is among the first studies describing the structured integration of FT-IR into a genomics-based national surveillance workflow for L. monocytogenes, including its use as a real-time triage tool to optimize WGS allocation and accelerate epidemiological response in a public health reference laboratory setting. IMPORTANCE Using a well-characterized data set, including two epidemiologically confirmed outbreaks and sporadic isolates, we demonstrate complete concordance (100%) between Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR)-based serogroup prediction and whole-genome sequencing, along with the capacity of FT-IR to support rapid preliminary clustering. Notably, this study was conducted following the implementation of the first FT-IR system installed in Argentina, representing a major step forward in the incorporation of innovative technologies into national surveillance programs. To our knowledge, this is the first manuscript reporting the combined use of FT-IR spectroscopy, matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization–time-of-flight mass spectrometry, and genomics within an integrated surveillance framework for Listeria monocytogenes. This approach provides a novel and pragmatic model for strengthening microbiological surveillance in resource-constrained settings. Beyond analytical performance, this work provides a real-world, operational framework for integrating rapid phenotypic screening with genomic confirmation, enabling earlier outbreak detection, optimized use of sequencing resources, and the potential to accelerate source-tracking investigations. title: Does Retrieval Relevance Matter for AI-Generated Book Introductions? A Matched-Random Memory Evaluation
abstract: Digital libraries are exploring LLMs for reading-promotion services such as automatically generated book introductions. A tempting design is to retrieve relevant accumulated reader feedback at generation time. We test this in a zero-human-subject controlled experiment: a librarian agent generates introductions for 32 held-out test books under three conditions (No Memory, a composition-matched random-memory control, and Relevant Memory, operationalized through embedding similarity and genre matching), judged on four criteria by a separate-model LLM (GPT-4o). The key methodological device is the composition-matched random-memory control, which isolates retrieval relevance from mere context presence. Lexical uptake checks confirm that retrieved memory is incorporated into generated introductions. Relevant Memory shows no LLM-judged advantage over No Memory on the composite outcome, but outperforms Matched-Random Memory on hook quality (Δ = 0.125, 95% CI [0.023, 0.250]). This pattern suggests that retrieval selection may matter when additional memory is introduced, rather than providing a general improvement over a strong no-memory baseline. We frame the study as pipeline validity evidence rather than evidence of improved human-perceived quality.
journal: Proceedings of the 26th ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries

title: Applications of Generative AI for Advancing Scientific Content Production, Evaluation and Dissemination
abstract: Generative AI is becoming part of how scientific content is being produced, evaluated and communicated. Large language models (LLMs) can write science news, simulate readers, retrieve evidence, generate scientific hypotheses, write code, and execute research workflows. These capabilities create opportunities for accelerating scientific discovery and broadening access to scientific information, but they also introduce risks related to hallucination and trustworthiness. This doctoral dissertation studies how generative AI can support scientific content production and dissemination, while preserving trust, comprehension, and replicability. The completed work includes three components: (1) detecting LLM-generated science news through SANews and GFS, (2) evaluating science communication through reader learning using KnowledgeGain and LLMSim, and (3) benchmarking LLM agents for research replication with ReplicatorBench and ReplicatorAgent. The proposed work extends these directions toward learning-optimized science news generation, MESH for multimodal evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, and MERIT, a simulation-grounded framework for evaluating autonomous AI co-scientists and hypothesis testing in computational materials discovery. The overarching goal is to develop evaluation methods and AI systems that make scientific outputs not only fluent and scalable, but also grounded, useful, and interpretable.
journal: Proceedings of the 26th ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries

title: Towards Automated Analysis of Scientific Limitations and FutureWork
abstract: Scientific progress relies on acknowledging epistemic boundaries and charting forward directions. However, limitations and future work are systematically omitted or hedged to improve publication prospects. With escalating submission volumes, reviewers increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs), yet zero-shot models generate superficial, hallucinated, or author-echoing feedback. This thesis presents a unified framework to discover, evaluate, recommend, and generate scholarly limitations and future work. First, we introduce LimTopic and FutureScope, using hybrid BERTopic, LLM pipelines to uncover thematic limitation patterns and model thirteen years of NLP future work trajectories. Second, to resolve metric inflation from surface metrics, we establish BAGELS and FutureGen, introducing atomic Limitation Units (LUs) for fine-grained PointWise evaluation and RAG-based future work generation with iterative critique loops. Third, we construct citation knowledge graphs with GraphSAGE to recommend paper-specific limitations. Finally, SciLimAgents couples intrinsic (LimitAgents) and novelty (NovAgents) specialist agents over a 120K-paper shared memory, aligned via on-policy preference optimization and composite process rewards. Across extensive benchmarks, our frameworks demonstrate substantial gains over frontier baselines, establishing a principled foundation for AI-assisted scientific quality assurance.
journal: Proceedings of the 26th ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries

title: Bi-allelic variants in the secretory pathway gene SEC16A are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
abstract: SEC16A encodes a scaffold protein that organizes the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) exit sites, specialized ER subdomains that mediate export of newly synthesized proteins and regulate early secretory pathway steps. The role of SEC16A in human nervous system diseases has not been established yet. Here, we report six individuals with bi-allelic SEC16A variants who presented with early-onset neurological symptoms, including cognitive impairment, motor delays, and seizures. Using Drosophila, we show the Sec16 ortholog is essential for normal development and that its loss causes early lethality. Neuron-specific knockdown of Sec16 causes neurological phenotypes including locomotor defects, seizure-like bang sensitivity, and impaired synaptic transmission, which can be associated with the clinical features observed in affected individuals. Neurons differentiated from patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) carrying SEC16A variants display reduced SEC16A protein, impaired neurite outgrowth and increased excitability, which are rescued in isogenic control neurons when the variants are corrected, consistent with a loss-of-function mechanism. Increased ER stress was observed in both patient iPSC-derived neurons and fly models. In summary, our findings indicate a conserved requirement for SEC16A in neurodevelopment and neuronal function and implicate ER stress as a key cellular phenotype underlying the SEC16A-associated neurodevelopmental disorder.

title: Competitiveness and Trade Dynamics of Apricot in Afghanistan
abstract: Afghanistan possesses strong agro-climatic advantages for apricot cultivation, making it one of the most economically and culturally significant horticultural crops in the country. Despite this, the performance of its exports, particularly fresh and dried forms, remains limited due to infrastructural bottlenecks, post-harvest inefficiencies and market volatility. This study analyzed the export competitiveness and trade direction of apricots in Afghanistan using two complementary methods: the revealed comparative advantage (RCA) and Markov chain analysis. RCA values calculated for the top 10 apricot export markets in Afghanistan from 2008 to 2019 revealed strong comparative advantage in India and Pakistan, but weak competitiveness in high-income markets, namely the USA and Germany. The results also demonstrated fluctuating competitiveness across years and destinations, underscoring dependency on a narrow set of regional markets. To examine trade direction and structural shifts, Markov chain models were applied. Transition probability matrices showed high export retention with key partners such as India, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, indicating stable trade relationships. However, markets such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kazakhstan and the USA exhibited volatility, with exports frequently redirected to more accessible or politically aligned destinations. The findings highlighted that while regional markets provide a reliable foundation, diversification into non-traditional destinations remained limited and inconsistent. Policy recommendations include improving cold chain logistics, standardizing quality and adopting certification mechanisms like organic and geographic indication labelling. JEL Classification: F14, Q17, C22

title: Understanding the wildfire adaptation communications landscape in the western United States: examining actors, media type, and geographies
abstract: Adaptations to living with fire are multifold, and U.S. wildfire policy has increasingly shifted toward proactive management. The U.S. Forest Service’s Wildfire Crisis Strategy (WCS) provides coordination and funding for landscape-scale adaptation, yet little is known about how wildfire adaptation is communicated in public online discourse. We analyze press releases, news media, and social media texts from September 2022 to February 2024 to characterize the salience and framing of wildfire adaptation concepts, identify which organizational types are most associated with major themes, and examine geographic variation across ten initial WCS landscapes. Using paragraph-level topic modeling and thematic clustering, we find that wildfire adaptation communication is dominated by prescribed fire, but that most adaptation concepts represented in the Fire Adapted Communities wheel appear across channels. Prescribed fire discourse is internally differentiated (operations, weather windows, and risk/safeguards), and thematic emphasis varies by platform and communicator type. We also observe meaningful state-level variation in adaptation themes within Twitter/X data, consistent with differences in fire history, governance context, and public attention. Together, these findings map a distributed wildfire adaptation communication ecosystem and highlight where key adaptation elements (e.g., codes, ordinances, and continuity planning) remain comparatively absent from public-facing discourse.

title: Machine learning-guided leaf margin classification and discovery that BcPHB promoter selection rewires a BcPHB–BcLMI1 module to shape leaf margins in Brassica campestris
abstract: The morphological diversification of leaf margins reflects the evolutionary reshaping of conserved developmental programs. However, fully deciphering the underlying molecular basis remains challenging due to difficulties in phenotype quantification and the incomplete characterization of complex regulatory networks. In this study, we established a computer-vision framework to decode leaf lobe trait and identified the HD-ZIP III factor PHABULOSA (BcPHB), combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and selective sweep analysis in Brassica campestris. We found that promoter variation defines two major haplotypes, BcPHBHapI and BcPHBHapII, driving divergent expression levels associated with entire and lobed leaves. Functionally, BcPHB knockdown lines (BcPHBami) exhibited lobed margins, whereas complementation of lobed accessions with the BcPHBHapI promoter partially restored the entire-leaf phenotype. Similarly, overexpression of LATE MERISTEM IDENTITY 1 (BcLMI1), a conserved regulator of leaf lobation, phenocopied the BcPHBami lines. Mechanistically, BcPHB and BcLMI1 form a reciprocal negative feedback loop that stabilizes margin patterning. Furthermore, domestication-driven selection of BcPHBHapI facilitated the transition from ancestral lobed leaves to cultivated entire forms. This study reveals a pivotal developmental module and illustrates how regulatory evolution drives morphological diversification in crops.

title: Routine laboratory data are decoupled from symptom phenotype and prognosis in Long COVID: within-cohort variation is dominated by age
abstract: Objectives Long COVID is defined by persistent multi-organ symptoms without an alternative diagnosis. This study evaluated whether routine laboratory data collected under real-world conditions differentiate symptom-defined subgroups within an outpatient cohort and predict the course. Methods In this single-center cohort study of 564 Long COVID patients (1,452 visits), symptom phenotypes were derived by latent class analysis of 19 organ-system domains at baseline. Structure in 89 routine analytes was sought by k-means clustering, confirmed with alternative algorithms, and repeated after age residualization. Analytes were compared across phenotypes using Kruskal-Wallis tests with false-discovery-rate control and adjustment for confounders. Equivalence testing was performed against reference change values. The course was modeled by count models. Prediction of improvement used a nested cross-validated elastic net with a baseline-independent endpoint. Results Clustering showed no convincing structure (silhouette ≤0.09, two to eight clusters); the weak split tracked age (50.5 vs. 38 years) and vanished after residualization. Three age-independent phenotypes (n=503) had no laboratory correlate: none of 89 analytes survived FDR correction, with or without adjustment, or across 50 pseudo-class draws. Equivalence held for 86/89 analytes within ±0.5 SD and 63/70 within the reference change value. Symptom burden declined (median 4 to 2 organ systems, p=2.5 × 10−19); however, no analyte predicted the course (AUC 0.46). Conclusions Routine laboratory variation in this cohort was dominated by age and decoupled from symptom phenotype in both directions. Routine testing in a real-world setting could not provide an age-independent diagnostic, subtyping, or prognostic signature in a cohort of patients suffering from Long COVID.

title: UAV-based disease detection in strawberry by multispectral image segmentation invoking deep learning
abstract: Accurate and timely diagnosis of strawberry diseases is crucial for minimizing crop loss and reducing the cost of plant treatment. The use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with multispectral cameras opens up new possibilities for noninvasive plant health monitoring. The objective of this research is to explore the feasibility of detecting diseases in strawberries through multispectral imagery obtained from UAVs combined with deep learning techniques. Leaf spot disease, caused by Ramularia tulasnei Sacc., was chosen as a case study. A DJI Phantom 4 Multispectral quadcopter was used to survey an experimental plot (37 × 22 m) from an altitude of 3 m, achieving a resolution of 2.2 mm per pixel. Preprocessing of the acquired data involved orthomosaic building using Agisoft Metashape Pro and manual region-of-interest (ROI) extraction in ENVI 5.2. A dataset comprising 360 multispectral images, each of size 64 × 64 × 5 (with spectral bands at 450, 560, 650, 730, and 840 nm), was created and separated into three classes: healthy plants, diseased plants, and soil. Using this dataset, a U-Net-based model – supplemented with the attention gate, squeeze-and-excitation, and residual connections modules – was trained. Additionally, to assess the contribution of multispectral channels, another U-Net model was trained on RGB images, as well as a classic Random Forest model based on 40 GLCM texture features. The U-Net model trained on multispectral data achieved an overall classification accuracy of 96.04 %, which is significantly higher than the performance of Random Forest (76.64 %) and the U-Net on RGB images (94.14 %). The resulting disease distribution maps enable site-specific fungicide application. The proposed approach confirmed the effectiveness of deep learning for diagnosing leaf spot disease in strawberries. Future research will focus on expanding the dataset (different cultivars and disease stages), testing more advanced segmentation architectures, and scaling the method to commercial plantations.
journal: Vavilov Journal of Genetics and Breeding

title: Dominant Source Identification in the Propagation of Ocean Observation Uncertainty to Underwater Detection Performance: A Differentiable End-To-End Framework
abstract: Underwater detection performance is constrained by ocean observation uncertainties that propagate nonlinearly through sound speed profile (SSP) inversion, acoustic transmission-loss (TL) prediction, and sonar performance estimation. We develop a differentiable end-to-end framework that traces observation uncertainty through SSP inversion, acoustic propagation, and passive sonar detection probability (Pd), enabling a quantitative ranking of the dominant uncertainty sources. The framework comprises a Bayesian deep ensemble for SSP inversion, a physics-constrained Fourier neural operator for acoustic propagation, and an analytic sonar-equation module, all implemented in PyTorch with automatic differentiation. Applied to the eddy-active northern South China Sea using the SCSORA reanalysis and validated against independent glider observations, bias-corrected Sobol' first-order indices show that satellite SST observation uncertainty dominates detection-performance uncertainty in deep water (S1 ≈ 0.38–0.52, conditional on the upper-200 m water column), exceeding the acoustic model structural error (S1 ≈ 0.10–0.19). The ranking is robust to a factor-of-two variation in the assigned acoustic structural-error variance and to the choice of attribution scheme (Sobol' vs. Shapley). A paired bootstrap test of a cross-training experiment indicates a small but significant sensitivity of the SST index to the training configuration (ΔS1 = 0.052; 95% CI [0.018, 0.086]), which does not alter the qualitative ranking. In shallow-shelf environments, seabed geoacoustic uncertainty prevails (S1 ≈ 0.41). The framework operates entirely on publicly available data and provides a quantitative basis for prioritizing environmental-observation resources in naval environmental support. Limitations include the absence of independent winter glider observations and the use of a 200-m SSP truncation in deep-water regimes; both are discussed in the paper.

title: Deep Learning–Based Rapid Prediction and Optimization of Outdoor Wind Environment for Campus Buildings
abstract: Courtyard-style campus buildings often suffer from poor outdoor wind environments affecting pedestrian comfort. This study proposes a deep learning-based rapid prediction and optimization framework to bypass the computational expense of traditional numerical simulations. A parametric dataset of 216 pedestrian-level wind fields is constructed via CFD simulations, varying building width-to-height ratio and wind incidence angle. A pix2pix conditional generative adversarial network is trained as a surrogate model to learn the direct mapping from building geometry to wind speed distribution. Unlike conventional regression networks that produce over-smoothing, the adversarial training preserves sharp velocity gradients and local extremes—features critical for comfort assessment. The model achieves a single-case inference time of 1.4 seconds. Results reveal that summer comfort coverage reaches 98.4%, while winter coverage drops sharply to 19.5%, identifying winter as the critical season for intervention. Parametric analysis shows that wind incidence angle exerts a pronounced effect: comfort area increases from 12.9% at perpendicular incidence to 24.1% at 45°. The optimal design is W/H = 1.4 and θ = 45°. The framework has been implemented as a prototype software system. This study provides a valuable reference for climate-adaptive design of campus courtyard buildings.

title: Decommissioning Enterprise Software: AI Agents and the Collapse of the Replication Moat
abstract: I have spent the last six years building software for a living. For most of that time, one rule held: if a company bought a big piece of business software, it was stuck with it, because rebuilding that software would cost far more than just paying for it year after year. This paper is about why that rule is breaking. With an AI coding assistant that costs a few hundred dollars a month, tools that can take apart almost any program, and open models you can run on your own hardware, a single developer can now rebuild the part of a product that a business actually uses, in weeks instead of years. I walk through three real cases from October 2026, the plain economics behind them, what the law does and does not protect, why hiding how your systems work no longer keeps them safe, and who ends up controlling these tools. I am not saying software has lost its value. I am saying the industry can no longer charge people for how hard it is to leave, and the change is going to be messy.

title: Comparative Analysis of Simple Moving Average and Single Exponential Smoothing Methods for Forecasting Readymix Concrete Demand
abstract: General Background Ready-mix concrete represents a vital material in construction projects, yet its rapid setting characteristic prevents long-term inventory storage and creates operational vulnerabilities. Specific Background Demand fluctuations driven by unpredictable project schedules and external factors such as weather cause severe challenges in production planning for batching plants like PT X Sidoarjo. Knowledge Gap Although short-term time-series forecasting is widely recognized, comparative evaluations combining error metrics and tracking signal analysis for daily ready-mix concrete production remain limited. Aims This study evaluates and compares the Simple Moving Average and Single Exponential Smoothing methods to identify the optimal forecasting model with minimal error for daily ready-mix concrete demand. Results Quantitative analysis of historical sales data from April 2026 demonstrates that the Single Exponential Smoothing model with a smoothing constant of 0.7 outperforms the Simple Moving Average model, achieving lower error rates with Mean Absolute Deviation of 40.606, Mean Squared Error of 2373.946, Mean Absolute Percentage Error of 44.99%, and superior tracking signal stability within safety control limits. Novelty This research incorporates daily tracking signal evaluation into short-term ready-mix concrete forecasting, proving that exponential smoothing mitigates cumulative bias during severe demand shifts. Implications Applying the selected Single Exponential Smoothing model yields a daily demand projection of 33.771 m3 for May 2026, establishing an operational safety baseline to prevent overproduction losses and optimize raw material inventory management. Key Findings Highlights Single exponential smoothing with a smoothing factor of 0.7 achieves superior forecast accuracy compared to simple moving average. Tracking signal testing confirms that exponential smoothing maintains cumulative bias stability within acceptable control limits. The projected daily demand of 33.771 cubic meters serves as a safe operational baseline for batching plant production scheduling. Keywords Readymix Concrete, Demand Forecasting, Single Exponential Smoothing, Time Series Analysis, Tracking Signal

title: EthnoPulse: A Multi-Task Deep Learning Framework for Traditional Music Emotion Recognition and Online Engagement Prediction
abstract: Traditional-music emotion recognition and online engagement are usually studied separately, although both depend partly on acoustic structure. EthnoPulse formulates the two problems as a partial-label multi-task setting in which disjoint affect and engagement corpora can share an encoder without imputing missing labels. The model combines dual-resolution log-Mel inputs, a multi-scale residual encoder, squeeze-and-excitation recalibration, task-specific gates, uncertainty weighting, an emotion–valence/arousal consistency term, and CORAL alignment. CTIM and FMA define the raw-audio tasks, with composition-and artist-disjoint splits used to reduce identity leakage. CCMED and WCMED provide an independent feature-level test of the evaluation protocol. Under composition-grouped five-fold validation, the lowest arousal MAEs are 0.286 on CCMED and 0.282 on WCMED, and the strongest rank correlations are 0.773 and 0.806, respectively. Random excerpt splitting raises CCMED valence correlation from 0.318 to 0.527. Cross-domain arousal transfer reaches ρ = 0.808, whereas valence transfer is weaker and the effect of CORAL depends on both direction and target. The results underline the importance of group-disjoint evaluation and dimension-specific reporting in cross-cultural music analysis.

title: Simulating historical and future rainfall and temperature variability and trends in Fedis district, Eastern Ethiopia
abstract: Climate change, driven by human activities, is causing rising global temperatures and rainfall variability. Africa, especially eastern Africa, faces severe impacts due to warming trends, declining rainfall, and reliance on rain-fed agriculture. This research article aimed to analyze past and future climate variability and change in Fedis, Eastern Ethiopia. Historical data were obtained from the Ethiopian Meteorological Institute for the period 1992–2022. For future projections, Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 datasets were used under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. The quantile mapping statistical method was used for future climate downscaling and bias correction. The standardized variable index was used for climate variability analysis. Mann–Kendall test was used for trend assessment. The findings revealed that the district experienced an increase in annual minimum temperature (0.02 °C/year), although not significant, while maximum temperature increased by 0.06 °C/year, and annual rainfall decreased by −2.14 mm/year over the last three decades. Similarly, seasonal trends in rainfall were not significant for both March–May and June–September seasons. Projections showed an increase in annual and seasonal rainfall and minimum and maximum temperatures under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 by the 2050s and 2080s in the district under both SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Future research should integrate crop modeling, extreme climate projections, and socioeconomic vulnerabilities to develop localized adaptation policies.
journal: Journal of Water and Climate Change

title: Mathematical modelling of sequential DRM and catalyst regeneration in a fixed-bed reactor
abstract: Dry reforming of methane is an attractive route for syngas production because it enables the simultaneous utilisation of methane and carbon dioxide. However, its practical application is limited by high energy demand, catalyst deactivation and, in particular, carbon deposition on the catalyst surface. In this work, a mathematical model of sequential dry reforming of methane and CO2-assisted catalyst regeneration in a fixed-bed reactor is proposed. The carbon formed during the reforming stage is treated not only as a deactivating deposit, but also as a reactive intermediate that can be converted into carbon monoxide during the subsequent regeneration step. The axial distribution of carbon obtained from the DRM model is used as the initial condition for the transient regeneration model. To avoid dependence of the total carbon mass on the spatial discretisation adopted for regeneration, the carbon distribution from the DRM stage is recalculated into the mass of carbon assigned to reactor intervals ΔmC, and then transferred to the regeneration grid using a local linear carbon-mass density reconstructed by cubic spline interpolation and integrated numerically over the new grid intervals. The regeneration model describes transient changes in CO2 and CO concentrations and in the local mass of deposited carbon along the reactor. A thermodynamic constraint based on the reaction quotient and the equilibrium constant of the reverse Boudouard reaction is introduced to limit carbon gasification to conditions favourable for CO formation. The resulting system ofmequations is solved numerically using the method of lines and a stiff ODE solver. The influence of spatial grid discretisation is analysed, and a discretisation level is selected to strike a balance between numerical accuracy and computational cost. Regeneration simulations are performed over a temperature range of 973 to 1270 K. The results show that the proposed model enables the local course of catalyst regeneration to be followed, preserves the carbon mass balance when the regeneration grid is changed, and provides a basis for assessing CO2-assisted regeneration as part of cyclic DRM–regeneration operation.
journal: Chemical and Process Engineering: New Frontiers

title: An Empirical Study of Digital Marketing Strategies and Consumer Purchase Behaviour Towards Value-Added Orange Products of Vidarbha Agro-Processing Industry
abstract: The agro-processing industry plays a significant role in enhancing the value and marketability of agricultural produce through product diversification and innovative marketing practices. In the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra, oranges constitute one of the major horticultural crops, and the development of value-added orange products such as juices, jams, candies, squashes, and marmalades has created new opportunities for agro-processing industries. The increasing penetration of digital technologies has transformed the way these products are marketed and consumed. This study examines the impact of digital marketing strategies on consumer purchase behaviour towards value-added orange products in the Vidarbha agro-processing industry. The research investigates the influence of social media marketing, online advertisements, e-commerce platforms, digital promotions, and electronic word-of-mouth on consumers' awareness, preferences, and purchasing decisions. Primary data were collected from consumers through a structured questionnaire, and appropriate statistical tools were employed to analyse the relationship between digital marketing practices and consumer buying behaviour. The findings reveal that effective digital marketing strategies significantly influence consumer awareness, brand engagement, and purchase intentions towards value-added orange products. The study provides valuable insights for agro-processing enterprises to design effective digital marketing initiatives and enhance market penetration and consumer satisfaction.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Performance Evaluation and Voltage-Domain Error Decomposition of the Single-Diode Photovoltaic Model Under Dynamic Operating Conditions
abstract: Accurate modeling of photovoltaic array performance under dynamic field conditions is essential for power forecasting and electrical grid integration. Despite the widespread use of five-parameter single-diode models for annual yield estimation, their instantaneous predictive fidelity under operational extremes remains unconstrained. This study evaluates the dynamic accuracy of the standard single-diode framework using a 21-day telemetry dataset (2,909 active daylight observations, plane-of-array irradiance > 50 W/m²) from a 648-module SunPower SPR-327 photovoltaic array (System 1283, Golden, Colorado). All reported voltages and currents are array-level maximum-power-point quantities measured at the inverter DC input. Across all records, the model predicted DC power with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 5.29 kW (5.57%), a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 5.95 kW (6.26%), and a net bias of −3.98 kW (−4.19%). Under high-irradiance conditions (>800 W/m²), with module temperatures predominantly exceeding 55°C, systematic power under-prediction reached −6.29 kW. Error decomposition revealed that current predictions remained accurate to within 0.4% (bias of −1.91 A), while a 3.1% voltage deficit (−12.02 V) drove the power error. Conversely, low-irradiance (50–200 W/m²) discrepancies were highly sensitive to sensor selection, with voltage bias shifting from −0.84 V (reference cell) to +5.11 V (pyranometer). The deficit in high-irradiance voltage prediction points toward physical mechanisms in the voltage domain, such as the model's assumption of a temperature-independent series resistance or standard silicon thermal coefficient adjustments; however, these proposed mechanisms represent hypotheses generated by this analysis rather than confirmed causes. These results isolate the primary source of high-irradiance modeling error and establish target parameters for future calibration.

title: Semiempirical Quantum Chemistry in the Age of ab initio Data and Differentiable Programming: II. Parameter Optimization
abstract: Semiempirical quantum chemistry (SQC) represents an invaluable asset in the toolbox of molecular and materials modeling. Thanks to their explicit quantum-mechanical treatment of electrons, they allow to capture an array of local and non-local interaction mechanisms and offers access to electronic structure properties, which can be of crucial importance in order to better understand and design molecular systems and materials. In a previous publication, we presented our recent advances within the PySEQM package, enabling rapid gradient evaluations for SQC parameters and thus developing an efficient and reliable back-end for SQC parametrizations. In this work, we detail our implementation of this parametrization procedure, SQCFit, and its features. Offering a high degree of automation, SQCFit implements a suite of tailor-made tools for the optimization of SQC parameters. Specifically, we present local versus global parametrization schemes, the use of train-validation splits and early stopping to avoid overfitting, and advanced scoring/loss functions including appropriately standardized quantitative error measures as well as more qualitative measures such as the performance in ranking candidate systems according to a given molecular property. Based on a set of test applications, we highlight how SQCFit allows to obtain performant parametrizations tailor-made for the modern use cases of SQC.

title: Semiempirical Quantum Chemistry in the Age of ab initio Data and Differentiable Programming: III. Differentiable Complete Active Space Configuration Interaction
abstract: We present an efficient, differentiable complete-active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) framework for GPU-accelerated electronic-structure calculations. The approach is integrated into the PyTorch-based PYSEQM package together with orthogonalization-corrected OM2 and OM3 semiempirical Hamiltonians and floating-occupation molecular orbitals. By combining determinant-based direct CI with matrix-free eigensolution and custom reverse-mode differentiation, the method retains the memory efficiency of the forward calculation while providing derivatives with respect to continuous model parameters and molecular coordinates. Its modular formulation separates the CASCI treatment from the underlying one-and two-electron quantities, facilitating use with different electronic-structure backends. The resulting framework provides state energies, density and transition density matrices, transition properties, and analytic response information for multiconfigurational electronic states. In combination with semiempirical effective Hamiltonians, it offers a computationally economical route to differentiable multireference electronic structure for bondbreaking processes and electronically excited systems. We illustrate this formalism studying minimum-energy conical intersections, solvent effects on the intersection seam energetics, and a proof-of-concept inverse design problem of excitation energies in an external electric field.

title: INTEGRATED HYDROLOGICAL ASSESSMENT FOR THE DESIGN OF A MULTIPURPOSE SMALL RESERVOIR IN THE SIRBA RIVER BASIN, NIGER
abstract: Water scarcity and increasing hydroclimatic variability represent major constraints to sustainable development in the Sahel, where rural livelihoods depend largely on rain-fed agriculture and seasonal water availability. In southwestern Niger, the Sirba River watershed experiences recurrent floods during the rainy season and severe water shortages during the prolonged dry season, highlighting the need for efficient water storage infrastructures. This study assessed the hydrological feasibility of constructing a multipurpose small dam in the Sirba River watershed using an integrated hydrological and geomorphological approach. Long-term rainfall and hydrological data (1960-2020), a 30-m Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) Digital Elevation Model, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and regional empirical hydrological methods (ORSTOM, CIEH and Gradex) were employed to characterize the watershed, estimate design floods and evaluate the reservoir water balance. Rainfall frequency analysis using the Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) distribution indicated design rainfall depths ranging from 210 mm for the 5-year return period to 289 mm for the 100-year return period. Morphometric analysis showed that the watershed covers 39091 km², with an elongated geometry (Gravelius coefficient = 2.04) and a low drainage density (0.06 km km⁻²), characteristics that contribute to moderate flood concentration. The estimated 10-year design flood reached 100.04 m³ s⁻¹, while the mean annual runoff volume was estimated at 86.12 × 10⁶ m³, decreasing to 40.36.10⁶ m³ under 10-year dry conditions. Although evaporation and sedimentation constitute the principal water losses, the reservoir water balance remained positive under average hydrological conditions, indicating sufficient water availability to satisfy projected domestic, livestock and agricultural demands. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed small dam is hydrologically feasible and could significantly enhance water security, support irrigated agriculture, reduce flood risks and strengthen climate resilience in the Sirba River watershed. Future studies should incorporate physically based hydrological modelling, sediment yield assessment and climate change scenarios to optimize reservoir design and long-term operation.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Integrated Electrochemical Process Modelling and Techno-Economic Assessment of Micro-Mesh Alkaline Seawater Electrolysis for Green Hydrogen Production
abstract: This study couples an experimentally calibrated electrochemical model with a techno-economic assessment of expanded nickel micro-mesh electrodes for alkaline electrolysis of seawater (M-SWELT). A zero-gap cell model with explicit thermodynamic, kinetic, bubble and ohmic terms is anchored to commercial alkaline performance, checked against published resistance measurements and calibrated to a like-for-like two-electrode comparison of micro-mesh and woven Ni-mesh cells in natural seawater with 5 M KOH. Because one operating point cannot separate kinetic from resistive contributions, the transferred voltage saving at 0.4 A cm⁻² and 80 °C is bounded at 20–187 mV (central 89 mV). The model is coupled to two seawater feed routes, reverse-osmosis (RO) desalination and direct feed with softening and a chloride bleed, and to a cost model of a 10 MW plant. The RO-fed micro-mesh plant reaches a levelised cost of hydrogen (LCOH) of £4.35 kg⁻¹, against £4.51 kg⁻¹ with woven mesh, and the micro-mesh breaks even at an electrode premium of up to £950 m⁻² (range £217–1,985 m⁻²). Even without chloride oxidation and with electrodes that last as long as the stacks, direct feed costs £4.95 kg⁻¹, because the chloride bleed discards KOH and forces a dilute electrolyte; crediting the chloride’s conductivity narrows the gap to RO feed without closing it, and short electrode life widens it. Across 10,000 Latin-hypercube Monte Carlo samples, the RO-fed micro-mesh plant averages £4.72 kg⁻¹ (P5–P95 £3.95–5.59 kg⁻¹); it is cheaper than woven mesh at equal electrode cost, and direct feed is dearer than RO feed, in every sample.

title: Perceptions and Interests of Polines Business Administration Students Regarding Careers in the Agricultural Sector
abstract: The regeneration of human resources in the agricultural sector requires the involvement of young people with diverse competencies, including those from non-agricultural disciplines. This study aims to describe the perceptions and interests of Business Administration students at Politeknik Negeri Semarang regarding careers in the agricultural sector. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed, involving 113 students as respondents. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale and analyzed descriptively by calculating perception and interest indices. The results show that students had a positive perception of careers in the agricultural sector, with an overall index of 74.99%. The highest perception scores were found for technological development (87.79%) and the applicability of business and administrative competencies (85.49%). Students also demonstrated a high level of interest in engaging in the agricultural sector, with an overall index of 74.16%. The use of digital media for marketing agricultural products was the most preferred form of engagement (81.24%), while considering agriculture or agribusiness as a career choice after graduation received the lowest index (70.97%), although it remained within the high category. These findings indicate that the agricultural sector becomes particularly attractive to Business Administration students when it is associated with technological development and activities relevant to their business competencies. The study highlights the potential for agricultural human resource regeneration to extend beyond agricultural disciplines by involving young talent with business, marketing, and digital competencies in supporting the agribusiness system.

title: AI Based Crop Recommendation Using Machine Learning Model
abstract: Small farmers often choose their crop, their fertilizer dose and their disease treatment by habit rather than by measurement. That costs them yield and money, and it puts extra chemicals into soil and water. This paper presents one tool that supports all three decisions. A crop model takes seven soil and weather readings (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, temperature, humidity, pH and rainfall) and was tested on 2,200 field records covering 22 crops. A 100-tree Random Forest and a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier both reached 99.55% test accuracy, and rainfall and humidity turned out to be the most influential inputs. A fertilizer module then calculates how much Urea, DAP and MOP is needed to bring the soil up to the target of the chosen crop, counting the nitrogen that DAP already supplies, and adds a farmyard manure dose. A four-block convolutional network trained on 15,000 leaf images identifies common leaf diseases with 98.40% validation accuracy and returns a treatment suggestion. On a standard Intel Core i7 CPU a crop recommendation takes about 14 ms and a leaf diagnosis about 43 ms, so the whole system runs comfortably as a small web service.
journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology

title: Benchmarking time-series foundation models for multitask predictive maintenance in digital twins
abstract: Digital twins provide a comprehensive virtual representation of physical assets, distinguishing themselves from traditional control systems through long-term diagnostic and prognostic capabilities. However, current digital twin architectures face a critical scalability barrier: they rely on dedicated, single-purpose models for every distinct query, task, physical scale, and operating context, resulting in unsustainable engineering overhead. To address this limitation, there is an urgent need for flexible, general-purpose analytical backbones capable of interpreting diverse time-series data without constant reconfiguration. While time-series foundation models (TSFMs) offer a potential solution through large-scale pre-training, their capacity to generalize beyond forecasting to the complex, multi-objective downstream requirements remains largely unverified. Addressing this challenge, this study utilizes the Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) dataset to benchmark three representative multi-task TSFMs (MOMENT, UniTS, and FFTS) across four downstream tasks (imputation, anomaly detection, classification, and regression) within a predictive maintenance context. We frame this evaluation as a rigorous test of generalization, assessing whether architecturally distinct TSFMs can adapt to distinct downstream tasks such as regression for remaining useful life estimation. Our benchmark reveals that although TSFMs generalize across all evaluated tasks, they do not yet match specialized baselines trained only on the C-MAPSS dataset. We further find that the three backbones separate most clearly when adaptation is restricted to a small set of parameters, where the model combining channel-mixing with explicit task tokens adapts best to multi-objective use, including regression, a task absent from all three pre-training objectives; in the zero-shot regime no single backbone leads across tasks. Because the models differ simultaneously in architecture, capacity, pre-training corpus, and patch size, we report these as patterns observed under one shared benchmarking framework rather than as isolated causes. The evaluation is conducted on raw sensor series alone, without the semantic or physics-based components of a mature digital twin, so these findings provide an empirical baseline for the analytical layer such a system would host rather than an evaluation of digital twin integration itself.
