We argue that this approach presents three profound dangers. The first two are familiar from past arms races: being overtaken by a rival or triggering a war. The third is new: losing control of human beings' future to agents far more intelligent than we are, which could endanger our very survival. Striving to get to AGI first risks a race to the bottom on safety practices and regulation concerning them. China does not yet appear bent on racing to superintelligence. The United States should prioritise both unilateral and co-operative efforts to improve AI safety and avoid provoking a race that all humanity could lose.

title: Masked Diffusion for Travel Diaries Synthesis
abstract: Because household travel surveys combine household characteristics, variable-length person rosters, vehicle rosters, and trip chains, existing synthesis pipelines split them across separate models or flatten them into cropped fixed-length vectors. Representation, rather than modeling, becomes the bottleneck: splitting severs cross-segment dependence, and cropping truncates the household-structure distribution. We instead tokenize the diary and keep the object whole: each household-day becomes one token sequence with count tokens for vehicles, persons, and trips, and distinct symbols for padded, hidden, unobserved, and inapplicable positions. We introduce DiaryBridge, a masked diffusion model that bridges the fully hidden sequence to the distribution of complete diaries by unmasking positions in any order. One trained model, conditioned on any observed subset, performs synthesis and partial-diary completion alike. Experiments on real data extracted from the 2017/2018 Regional Travel Survey of the Baltimore region show that DiaryBridge generates travel reflecting vehicle availability and employment status, recovers shared trips using other household members' observed diaries, and better reproduces aggregate demand across modes, purposes, and departure periods than the learned baselines.

title: When LLM Agents See a Conflict but Still Proceed: Cross-Domain Dependencies in Network Slicing
abstract: Future AI-native networks are being designed to apply autonomous agents built on large language models (LLMs) in network management through intents. When intents from different domains meet on the same resource, an agent must recognize the cross-domain dependency before taking an irreversible action. We investigate this problem through a smart-grid use case, in which a power utility holds an active intent on a backup slice for protection traffic. This slice appears idle by design, which is precisely the profile targeted by a cost-reduction intent. We built a tool-based environment in which the dependency must be either queried by the agent or read from an inventory annotation, together with a negative control, and evaluated ten models from four different providers in 600 runs. Most models acted against the dependency they had observed: seven of the ten models removed the protection slice at least once after receiving the cross-domain dependency, and in the high-harm tier the slice was removed in 76% of the exposed runs, while four models practically never did. Only one of ten models never removed the slice. We identify two failure modes, not querying the dependency and querying it but proceeding anyway, and show that agents often reported no conflict after observing it. These results indicate that, in AI-native networks, visibility of cross-domain dependencies is not a sufficient safeguard, and that dependency verification should be enforced by the management architecture before irreversible actions rather than delegated to the LLM's judgment.

title: Who is the'I'in AI? Establishing Decentralized Identity and Accountability for Autonomous Agents
abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomous AI agents in decentralized ecosystems challenges existing identity paradigms. While human identity is traditionally anchored in biological and/or self-asserted attributes and government credentials, AI agents lack a standardized definition of selfhood, creating critical gaps in trust and accountability. This paper introduces a novel framework for establishing Decentralized AI Identity rooted in Self-sovereign identity (SSI) principles. We propose a formal model that clearly distinguishes human users and AI agents, enabling distinct verification logic for each class while maintaining a unified identity calculus. The central to our contribution is the ABCD Framework, a multi-layered approach to agent identification and verification: (A) Algorithmic Fingerprint, which binds the identity to static model architectures and provenance; (B) Behavioural Fingerprint, which verifies dynamic performance metrics over time; (C) Cryptographic Identity, which anchors the agent via Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) and (D) Delegation, which cryptographically binds agent actions to respective human accountability. By orthogonalizing these dimensions, we model how systems can enforce granular trust policies ranging from simple authentication to complex liability assignment, thereby solving the black box identity problem in the autonomous economic activities of AI agents.

title: EgoProbe: Benchmarking Long-Range and Exact Memory in Streaming Egocentric Videos
abstract: Egocentric video provides a continuous first-person record of everyday activities, making it a natural foundation for wearable AI assistants. Unlike offline video understanding, streaming systems must process observations as they arrive, while queries may refer to experiences from the distant past. Recent work has begun to explore whether information can be recalled across long temporal gaps. Yet remembering how far is only part of the challenge: recurring objects, actions, and locations also require models to remember exactly which detail belongs to which event. We introduce EgoProbe, a benchmark that evaluates streaming egocentric memory along these two complementary dimensions: long-range retention, i.e., how far, and event-specific recall under interference, i.e., how exact. Built on long-form egocentric videos, EgoProbe uses an event-grounded data engine to extend recall intervals, identify related events, and construct event-grounded distractors, followed by human verification. It contains two subsets: EgoProbe-Base, which evaluates long-range recall without intervening related events, and EgoProbe-Echo, which challenges models with similar intervening events and event-grounded distractors. EgoProbe-Echo adopts coarse-to-fine multi-turn probing: the first turn evaluates coarse-grained event recall, while the second tests whether the model can retrieve the target-specific detail associated with the designated event. Extensive evaluation across diverse models reveals substantial limitations in long-range recall, with further challenges in recovering target-event details among related experiences. Even when models correctly answer coarse-grained questions, they often fail to recall the specific details of the designated event. EgoProbe exposes this underexplored failure mode and provides a testbed for advancing long-range and exact memory in streaming egocentric video understanding.

title: OASIS: On-the-fly ASynchronous Image Stream classification -- Transformer-based models for the early detection of strongly lensed supernovae
abstract: Time-domain surveys often produce asynchronous image sequences across irregular observation times and photometric bands. In many applications, predictions are needed after each new observation, particularly when transient sources must be identified early to trigger follow-up. Strongly lensed supernovae (LSNe), for which follow-up is particularly time-critical, provide a useful example. We formulate this setting as On-the-fly ASynchronous Image Stream (OASIS) classification and explore reusable transformer architectures for causal, on-the-fly classification. We demonstrate these architectures on the lensed-transient classification problem studied by Bag et al. (2026a,b), distinguishing LSNe Ia from unlensed astrophysical transients. We compare them with the recurrent baseline adopted by Bag et al. (2026b), which combines a ConvLSTM branch for image processing with a separate LSTM branch for encoding observation times. The baseline maps asynchronous observations onto a fixed band-by-observation grid, filling unobserved bands with zeros. Using a common training setup, we compare two transformer-based approaches to modeling interactions among spatio-temporal tokens: factorized attention, which separates spatial and temporal interactions, and joint attention, which models them together. On the demonstration dataset, factorized architectures achieve mean losses of $0.095$--$0.100$, compared with $0.128$ for the recurrent baseline and $0.107$ or higher for joint architectures. A selective readout further reduces the best loss to $0.089$ for a factorized model. These results suggest that factorized attention suits this dataset better, without implying universal architectural superiority. We release the architectures as reusable foundations for time-domain astronomy and other applications involving evolving spatial features that require on-the-fly predictions.

title: Comprehensive Workflow for Uncertainty-Aware Ionic Liquid Solvent Discovery
abstract: Designing synthesizable materials with targeted properties remains one of the central objectives in materials sciences. Ionic liquids (ILs) are well suited to this goal due to their "tunability", where physical and chemical properties can be precisely customized by modifying their molecular structure, specifically by varying the combination of cations and anions. At the same time, current data-driven property models for ionic liquids often degrade in scarce, noisy, and uneven data regimes, where measurements cover only a small fraction of chemical space and a limited range of thermodynamic conditions. This makes out-of-distribution screening brittle: even when point predictions look plausible, it is difficult to compare candidates consistently, quantify downstream implications, or trust rankings enough to guide molecular discovery. We present a property-prediction and optimal candidate selection workflow that treats data processing, deep learning modeling, and physics-based calculations as a coupled system, linking property prediction with uncertainty estimation and physics-based filtering. By tightening the link between predicted properties and the criteria used for down-selection, the workflow supports reliable out-of-distribution ranking and enables prioritization of previously untested ionic liquid candidates with favorable predicted trade-offs. We demonstrate the application of our workflow by designing novel ionic liquids for CO2 capture from flue gas, predicting their properties and selecting Pareto-optimal candidates based on CO2 solubility, IL viscosity and working capacity.

title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
abstract: Evaluation has been central to advances in AI, and it is equally critical to autonomous discovery. Yet scaling autonomous discovery to real-world engineering challenges faces a fundamental bottleneck: the cost of evaluating progress. In real settings, a single true evaluation, such as a full benchmark or serving trace, can take hours, so a search can afford only a handful of true evaluations. We present DuoDiscover, a search system that jointly discovers what to optimize and how to evaluate progress efficiently, through three mechanisms. First, each worker in a fleet of coding agents co-discovers an optimization target and a fast, tailored proxy evaluator, which we call a yardstick. The agent then hill-climbs the yardstick rather than the true evaluation. Second, since search can exploit gaps between a yardstick and the true objective, fidelity tests continually recheck each yardstick's ranking and invalidate any that drift. Third, the fleet is bottom-up, with no central decomposition of the problem. A lightweight orchestrator spawns and terminates agents, briefs running ones, and seeds new agents with others' confirmed work. DuoDiscover enables autonomous optimization from software to chip architecture. We demonstrate DuoDiscover on two repository-level benchmarks and four GPU and TPU kernel suites covering hundreds of kernels. On SWE-fficiency, it doubles the average speedup of human experts. On SOL-Exec, it ranks first on 121 of 235 kernels and in the top three on 212. On the heavily optimized vLLM and SQLite engines, DuoDiscover achieves 1.92$\times$ and 1.38$\times$ gains over the base code. On a CPU microarchitecture optimization task with evaluations of up to 28 hours, DuoDiscover surpasses both AlphaEvolve-based ArchAgent v2 and the best human design, with 1.65$\times$ ArchAgent v2's gain in 16.7 days versus more than 40 days, advancing the frontier of autonomous chip design.

title: Principles and Techniques for Agentic Research in Experimental Physics
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in physics research is increasingly common, yet few guidelines exist for its effective use. Starting with a principles-based approach, we outline a set of ten requirements for collaborative AI agents in experimental physics, spanning scientific norms, effective agent use, and domain expertise. We take a human-centered approach in which agents act as collaborators that amplify rather than replace the expertise of a human researcher (user) who directs the work and is responsible for its results. We then present a framework designed to enforce these requirements, detailing methods for improving off-the-shelf behavior of large language models (LLMs) with custom scaffolding and describing general-purpose scientific workflows and skills. In particular, we highlight the power of closed-loop campaigns where agents work iteratively toward a well-defined goal. We demonstrate the potential of this mode of research through six case studies in experimental physics, covering device design, hardware control, neural network optimization, physical model identification, and data analysis. All six case studies result in useful work products that add utility to our research, including a neural network architecture and solid-state quantum defect photodynamic model that substantially outperform our published work; a microwave waveguide design that extends a published design concept to a fabrication-ready device meeting our experimental constraints; a quantum control pulse sequence candidate that improves simulated performance by more than an order of magnitude; commissioning of an NMR spectrometer to $\sim$1~Hz frequency precision on live hardware; and finally a data-fitting pipeline that achieves, to our knowledge, the first reconstruction of the Ising microstate of an artificial spin-ice array from diffraction-limited magnetic imaging.

title: Welcome to the Age of Agent Ads: Using On-Policy Attacks to Steer Agentic Decisions
abstract: People increasingly delegate option-ranking tasks (e.g., shopping, job search, travel) to AI agents, which creates incentives to steer agentic decisions via "agent ads." To defend against such steering attacks, people count on models' alignment training and platforms' terms of service, and consequently the most effective existing attacks are designed to trigger off-policy behaviors. Exposing a new attack surface, we introduce on-policy attacks, which steer agentic decisions without pushing individually aligned behaviors off policy. Our example attack consists of two steps: To remain compliant with platforms' terms of service, we first inject a truthful negation about a fictitious concept ("Does not contain blizyester") into a product description. This triggers an agent to search the web ("What is blizyester?"), which surfaces planted websites full of fabricated information associating the fictitious concept with harmful implications ("Blizyester linked to dementia"). Trained to keep users safe from harm, the agent penalizes every option missing the truthful negation. Evaluating our attack across four real-world listing datasets, we find some frontier models exposed, enabling an adversarial actor to penalize competitors without violating existing platform-listing guidelines. We discuss the broader challenge of regulating advertising aimed at AI agents and provide recommendations to model developers and platform providers.

title: Compute-optimal data scaling for neural surrogates via multi-fidelity training
abstract: Neural surrogates for Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) are usually trained on synthetic data from numerical simulators. As models grow and scaling laws demand larger datasets, the cost of data generation often outweighs the training cost and becomes the bottleneck in the scaling quest. Unlike data in other domains, however, each PDE sample has a tunable cost that depends on its numerical fidelity, with the resulting cost-accuracy trade-off governed by known convergence rates. We exploit this property by formalizing neural surrogate training as a function of both data quantity and fidelity under a fixed data generation compute budget, treating fidelity as a fine-grained discrete spectrum rather than a binary distinction. Building on this, we show that multi-fidelity training enables Pareto-optimal error scaling against data generation compute. By using simulations at lower fidelities as an additional training signal, training on the optimal fidelity mixture matches the accuracy of high-fidelity-only training, with up to $6.3\times$ less data generation compute across our settings. We validate these findings across six PDE problems spanning structured grids and unstructured meshes, two distinct error sources (discretization and iterative-solver error), and four surrogate architectures, totaling over 7,000 training runs.

title: From Conceptual EneMonIE to an Executable Backend: A Modular Architecture for Energy Information Extractionand Grounded Question Answering
abstract: The original EneMonIE proposal describes a Web-based semantic system for continuously monitoring energy trends through targeted information extraction from heterogeneous online media. This article presents EneMonIE-Backend, an implementation-derived redesign that converts that conceptual pipeline into a modular, executable, and application-independent backend. The architecture separates five concerns: data sources, acquisition and normalization, semantic processing, knowledge organization, and persistent storage. It operationalizes configurable connectors for RSS feeds, URL collections, arXiv, social-media JSON files, and open-data CSV files; it also introduces question-driven Web search and scraping. Relevant documents pass through energy categorization, named entity recognition, temporal and event extraction, source sensitive sentiment analysis, and extractive summarization. The resulting semantic representations support entity co-occurrence graphs, cross-document interlinking, cluster-level information fusion, and relational persistence in SQLite. Three grounded question-answering paths are exposed at the backend level: live Web evidence, the stored corpus, and selected configured resources. Answer generation uses a language model when configured and otherwise falls back to deterministic extractive output. Unlike the original proposal, the presented architecture deliberately excludes the user-interface and server-side application layers, allowing the semantic core to be embedded in different applications. A deterministic smoke validation confirms relevance filtering, persistence, clustering, evidence retrieval, and document deletion. The work provides a reproducible architectural basis for future evaluation on larger multilingual energy corpora.

title: Reduced-Order Backstepping Control of Nonlinear Mechanical Systems with Input Delay via Galerkin Projection
abstract: This paper addresses trajectory tracking for a class of nonlinear mechanical systems with input delay. The delayed actuator channel is represented as an equivalent transport partial differential equation, thereby transforming the original delayed system into a coupled plant-channel representation. A finite-dimensional approximation of the delay channel is then constructed through Galerkin projection, resulting in an explicit ODE model of the delayed actuator dynamics. Using this reduced-order plant-channel model, a backstepping controller is developed, and Lyapunov analysis establishes uniform exponential stability of the nominal tracking error dynamics for the reduced-order Galerkin model. To enhance practical implementation, a command-filtered version is also introduced to avoid direct differentiation of virtual controls, for which a corresponding uniform ultimate boundedness result is obtained. Simulation studies are provided to validate the proposed design and illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

title: Colored Graph Signal Diffusion Models
abstract: Standard diffusion processes with isotropic noise corruption are not spectrally neutral. They inherit a coarse-to-fine generation hierarchy from the nonuniform data spectrum, because each frequency band loses signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at its own rate. For signals on a graph, the relevant spectrum is that of the graph shift operator (GSO). A natural construction, therefore, builds both the diffusion dynamics and the denoiser from graph filters of the GSO, and any such design also takes a position on this hierarchy. We expose this hierarchy as a tunable axis through a family of colored score-based diffusions. Fixing the terminal prior to a Gaussian colored by the GSO couples the drift and diffusion through a positive spectral rate, which acts as a clock for each graph-frequency band. The clock sets when a band loses and recovers information, and the forward processes of standard and certain graph-aware diffusions appear as members of this family. A GSO-valued EDM preconditioning splits the denoiser into an analytic Wiener head that carries the Gaussian second-order structure and a graph neural network (GNN) that learns the remaining non-Gaussian dependencies. Numerical experiments show that colored diffusions reach a given generation quality in far fewer sampling steps than standard diffusion.

title: Stabilizing Low-Stiffness Soft Robots at Unstable Equilibria: A Model-Based Optimal Control Approach
abstract: Continuum soft robots are highly nonlinear and underactuated systems, which makes stabilizing them around unstable equilibrium points difficult. This challenge becomes even greater in low stiffness regimes, where gravitational forces dominate elastic forces. In this letter, we explore whether optimal control can address these challenges using a computa- tionally efficient method suitable for real time use. We propose a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) approach based on Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), combined with an accurate reduced order Variable Strain model with analytical derivatives. This results in an efficient control framework for addressing the stabilization problem. Tested on a soft inverted pendulum and other hybrid soft rigid systems, the method outperforms traditional controllers, stabilizes more challenging configurations, and operates reliably at real time speeds (50 150 Hz), demonstrating both effectiveness and practical feasibility in experimental settings.

title: Do Theorem Provers Need Theorem-Proving Agents? mini-Lean-agent: A Coding-Agent Baseline for Lean
abstract: General-purpose coding agents use standard shell and file interactions, yet formal theorem-proving agents often rely on specialized, ad-hoc tooling. This makes it difficult to determine which components of theorem-proving agents provide benchmark gains: an improved base model, a specialized harness, a specific tool, or a combination of any of them. We introduce mini-Lean-agent, a deliberately minimal agent for Lean tasks whose only model-visible tool is bash. The model must use bash to inspect and edit the repository, search local libraries, invoke Lean, and manage its own intermediate work, while a separate trusted evaluator verifies the final artifact. We compare mini-Lean-agent against AxProverBase and Numina-Lean-Agent on the Putnam 2025 benchmark. Experiments with Gemini 3.8 Flash as the base model show that mini-Lean-agent solves 7/12 problems at \$2 per problem limit, compared with AxProverBase's 4/12. With Astra as the base model, mini-Lean-agent solves 12/12 problems at an average cost of \$1.28 per problem. This suggests that a generic coding agent with a minimal harness can already achieve strong performance on Lean benchmarks. Our results motivate using mini-Lean-agent as a standard baseline when evaluating theorem-proving infrastructure.

title: An Introduction to Contract Theory for Computer Scientists
abstract: This survey introduces contract design to computer scientists: using outcome-based payments to incentivize effort. We discuss applications that motivate a computational approach to contract design, ranging from online labor markets, to incentive-aware algorithmic classification, to emerging ecosystems of AI agents. We present the classic principal-agent model and introduce basic concepts. We show how optimal contracts are computable via linear programming, and why they can be opaque and brittle. Motivated by this we turn to simpler contract formats, specifically linear contracts. We discuss approximation guarantees, and robust (max-min) optimality of such contracts. We then move beyond the single-agent setting to combinatorial contract settings with multiple agents, mapping the algorithmic landscape of tractability and approximation. Finally, we discuss partial information settings through the lens of learning algorithms, and outline open directions. The goal is a concise, accessible entry point that connects economic foundations with algorithmic tools and highlights opportunities for new theory and applications.

title: Large Network limit for Latent Variable Process Models with Endogeneously Evolving Interactions among Multiple Types
abstract: Motivated by the opinion and social dynamics literature, we rigorously study dynamically co-evolving latent space network models, where agent opinions evolve based on a latent state space model influenced by and influencing an underlying dynamically evolving graph determining their interactions. In contrast to earlier work, see [18], agents are allowed to be heterogeneous, i.e., of different types, and their dynamic evolution can capture behaviors like attraction and repulsion between and within groups. In addition, the model encodes bidirectional feedback between the latent process and the underlying interaction network, persistence effects are included, and the interactions are localized, i.e., individual agents do not have global information. We produce weak and empirical limit theorems that encode the asymptotic joint distribution of agent opinion trajectories and their interaction network. In doing so, we describe and exploit the complex dependence structure of the model.

title: Get In, Decide, Prove: A Merchant-Side Readiness Benchmark for Agentic Commerce
abstract: AI agents now browse and buy on people's behalf, and benchmarks measure how well the agents perform. Far less is known about the other side of the transaction: whether a merchant's website lets an agent in, publishes terms precise enough to decide a purchase, and leaves evidence of what was agreed. This paper presents a merchant-side benchmark built on those three questions and reports a pilot of it. The central measurement, decision sufficiency, rates each criterion of a concrete buyer mandate (total cost, cancellation or return terms, service date, variant identity) as determinate, indeterminate, or unknown from the merchant's own published evidence. Readiness scores carry their evidence coverage and missingness bounds; access is reported separately for a declared bot, a declared headless browser, and a user-present browser; and each observed term is mapped to the RAILS admissibility class of the evidence that could support it in a dispute. Four large merchants received the full assessment: three refused the declared profiles at their offer pages, and no mandate could be confirmed as met, because each merchant left a total or a refund term undetermined. An access census of 555 sites of merchants that two payment processors publicly name as clients found the home page unreadable to both declared profiles at 105 sites (18.9%). A declared assessment of 330 merchants, scored by deterministic rules without a rater, found that evidence coverage rather than the score decides who can be ranked: 115 merchants (35%) reached the ranking threshold, rankable profiles scored a median of 89 to 90, and material terms was the one pillar well below the others, because the all-in total was decidable at 18 merchants. The pilot shows that the measurements can be taken; it does not validate them or rank merchants, and the weights and the projected clearing band await validation against outcomes.

title: Variable Input Masked Autoencoders for Wrist-Worn Accelerometry
abstract: Large-scale repositories of wearable sensor data have enabled the development of foundation models for human activities and behavior. However, existing models are pretrained using fixed input durations and sampling rates, despite substantial heterogeneity in recording conditions, downstream tasks, and deployment constraints. We introduce VarMAE, a variable input masked autoencoder that learns a single representation across sampling rates and temporal contexts. During pretraining we construct two views of the same signal: a long duration high frequency view, and a short duration lower frequency view, obtained via random cropping and downsampling. We perform masked reconstruction within each view and introduce a cross-resolution masked reconstruction objective that uses visible tokens from the long view to predict masked tokens from the short view. Cropping and downsampling impose complementary information bottlenecks, encouraging the model to learn representations that remain effective across input durations and sampling rate changes. We pretrain VarMAE on the large-scale NHANES dataset, producing a single pretrained encoder matching or outperforming controlled foundation model baselines on eight benchmark datasets. With only 3.82M parameters, VarMAE is parameter efficient and shows that a single foundation model can achieve broad transfer capabilities across sensing configurations.

title: JustOPD: On-Policy Distillation from Autoregressive to Diffusion Language Models
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is a post-training approach for large language models (LLMs) that enables a student model to learn a teacher model's distribution from sequences sampled from the student's own policy. Despite its promising capability, OPD for diffusion language models (DLMs) remains underexplored and existing studies primarily focuses on DLM-to-DLM distillation. The limited availability of strong teacher DLMs and the flexible generation order of DLMs impose additional technical challenges as well. However, it remains unclear how to effectively distill knowledge from a strong autoregressive language model (ARM) into a weaker DLM, given the mismatch between the left-to-right decoding of ARMs and the flexible decoding order of DLMs. Inspired by Ni et al. (2026), we propose JustOPD, an ARM-to-DLM on-policy distillation method that uses autoregressive rollouts during training to align the student's generation process with the ARM teacher's left-to-right decoding. This alignment enables effective distillation from ARM teachers while preserving the DLM's flexible generation-order capability at inference time. Experiments using Qwen3-14B as the teacher and Dream-7B as the student demonstrate that JustOPD consistently improves mathematical reasoning performance over the base DLM across multiple divergence choices.

title: Agency as a New Organizing Abstraction for Computer Science
abstract: Advances in large-scale machine learning have enabled agentic AI systems: persistent, autonomous computational entities that pursue goals, initiate actions, and interact with open environments. These systems are often framed as applications of foundation models. We argue that this framing is incomplete: agency is also a candidate new organizing abstraction for computer science. What is new is not the concept of an agent, nor runtime policy generation per se, but its general-purpose, open-ended form, in which systems can synthesize courses of action from goals, observations, and memory, over tools and environments for which no complete task-specific model was specified in advance. Thus agency becomes a systems-level abstraction as well as an AI modeling concept. Where the process abstraction organizes computation around executing programs, agency organizes it around pursuing goals under bounded resources: a process executes a program; an agent pursues a goal. From this perspective, the recurring failures of deployed agentic systems (runaway resource consumption, behavior redirected by adversarial content, opaque continuous operation) are symptoms of structural abstraction gaps, not isolated engineering defects. We examine these gaps across six dimensions (execution, interfaces, correctness, oversight, coordination, and persistence) and argue that closing them requires coordinated advances in systems,

title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning
abstract: Clinical decision-making is a sequential process of information collection, clinical inference, and forecasting under partial observability, often without a uniquely correct treatment decision. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong medical question-answering capabilities but extending these advances to clinical reasoning remains challenging because many clinical tasks are only partially verifiable. Recent clinical reinforcement learning (RL) work has therefore largely focused on diagnostic endpoints, where correctness can be more directly verified. Oncology treatment decision making is a particularly challenging instance of this problem that extends beyond medical question-answering in which multiple decision trajectories can be clinically defensible for the same partially observed patient state. We formulate oncology treatment planning as an interactive RL problem under partial observability and construct patient-specific, process-aware rewards from decision processes observed in real world clinical records. The agent must learn to sequentially acquire information from a structured patient representation before committing to a first-line treatment recommendation, and is evaluated on information gathering, treatment selection, and reasoning alignment. Using GRPO and GDPO to optimize Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct within this environment, RL substantially improves the base policy beyond frontier model capabilities. The GDPO-trained policy increases Mean@3 scalar clinical reward by $79.60\%$ over base Llama and exceeds GPT-5.2 by $18.82\%$ under the same interactive environment, while reducing query count during training. Overall, our results show that patient-specific, partially verifiable rewards can provide an effective learning signal for interactive clinical RL when both the patient state and the underlying clinical decision process are only partially observed.

title: SchemaWeaver: Accelerating On-Device Mobile Agentic AI via Schema-Guided Parallel LLM Decoding
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) on mobile devices can act as agents that call external software tools to complete complex tasks, but the major challenge of supporting on-device mobile agentic AI with LLMs is the long latency of LLM tool calling on mobile devices. In particular, the decode phase is the main contributor of such long latency, but is hard to speed up on mobile processors as it is bound by memory bandwidth rather than compute power. To address this limitation, in this paper we present SchemaWeaver, a new on-device mobile agentic AI technique that enforces schema-guided parallel decoding in the decode phase of LLM tool calling, to reduce its latency by producing multiple tokens in each decode pass. SchemaWeaver can be generically applied to the LLM inference engine on mobile devices without involving any training efforts or changes on LLMs, and our experiment results on major mobile SoCs and LLM families show that SchemaWeaver can reduce the LLM tool calling latency by up to 3.9 times, compared to the competitive baselines.

title: A Stochastic Growth Model for Online Platforms
abstract: We investigate the growth trajectory of online platforms operating as market makers in two-sided matching markets. Their expansion, often referred to as the ``chicken-and-egg dilemma'' in the literature, poses an inherent challenge: service providers find value in joining the platform because of the presence of customers, while customers are drawn to the platform by the availability of service providers. Much of the existing literature addresses this expansion challenge through either a static market-clearing lens or aggregate dynamic models, emphasizing how network externalities shape a platform's growth trajectory and equilibrium size. These approaches do not fully capture how gradual growth must be implemented through server-level admission, assignment, and compensation decisions. Embedded in this growth process are intertemporal participation constraints that the platform must satisfy to attract and retain forward-looking servers. To explicitly account for the stochastic dynamics of a platform's gradual growth, we model the system as a Markov process. Potential servers and customers arrive according to Poisson processes, and customer demand is non-decreasing in the number of active servers. Under mild conditions, we characterize the platform's optimal admission, assignment, and compensation policies. The platform admits servers at the maximum feasible rate until it reaches an endogenous target size, which can be smaller than the static market-clearing optimum. In the baseline model, seniority-based compensation acts as an operational substitute for financially subsidized growth: instead of using upfront subsidies to induce early server participation, the platform uses future cash flows to reward early servers for joining when demand is limited and for helping the platform reach later, higher-demand states.

title: Structure-preserving fidelity diagnostics for partial differential equations
abstract: Machine learning surrogates of partial differential equations (PDEs) are commonly trained on data generated by numerical solvers. Therefore, the training data obey not the PDE but the modified equation of the numerical scheme, and the test loss, computed on data from the same solver, cannot distinguish a model that learned the physics from one that learned the discretization error. Here, we show that the difference is nevertheless visible in the trained model. We propose a suite of structure-preserving fidelity diagnostics, simple scores that measure whether a learned model respects one known property of the physics, such as a conserved quantity, a symmetry or a Hamiltonian structure, without access to the training data or the governing equation. Over five systems, the diagnostics track the error with respect to the true dynamics with a rank correlation of up to $0.94$, while the test loss is uncorrelated or anti-correlated with it. For the Burgers, Korteweg-de Vries and Navier-Stokes equations, the diagnostics separate numerical schemes that the test loss ranks as equivalent, including schemes of the same order. order.

title: Physiology-Informed Sparse Identification of Dynamic Crop Models
abstract: Developing resilient crops requires models that accurately capture how plant growth dynamics emerge from the continuous interplay between genetic and environmental factors. While high-throughput phenotyping platforms generate data for dynamic growth models, current modelling approaches show limitations: process-based crop growth models (CGMs) capture environmental dynamics but are difficult to scale across many genotypes because they require calibration of many parameters, while quantitative genetic models allow modelling many genotypes but often summarise time-varying environments using static covariates. To address this gap, we propose a data-driven framework to identify reduced systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) describing crop growth dynamics as functions of environmental variables and a controllable number of genotype-specific coefficients (GSCs). Using the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) method, we infer model structure directly from data via sparse regression on a physiologically informed library of candidate functions. In this framework, GSCs parameterise cultivar-specific differences in response to environmental conditions. The resulting models are linear in these GSCs, making them compatible with mixed-model and genomic prediction approaches. We evaluate the approach on an in silico dataset generated with WOFOST for five potato cultivars across twelve growing seasons. Our identified ODEs generalise to held-out years and achieve $R^2 > 0.9$ for end-of-season yield prediction across held-out years when compared to full-scale WOFOST simulations. These results provide a proof of concept for SINDy-based identification of parsimonious dynamic crop models from longitudinal crop-growth data.

title: Creative destruction: Human-AI competition in an experimental market
abstract: We study two hypotheses for how a human role in production could persist despite growing AI capabilities. Humans might have a durable advantage in taste, designing better products even as AI agents automate routine tasks, or consumers might intrinsically prefer that humans have a hand in production. In our experiment, participants act as producers, designing computer games with an AI coding agent, and as consumers who buy them. Across three studies (N = 1,025), we find no evidence for either hypothesis. Games designed by an AI on its own outperform those of human producers, including both amateurs and professional creatives. Human producers do not anticipate the AI's advantage. Revealing whether a game is human-designed does not raise consumers' willingness to pay for the product.

title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
abstract: Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulation and fitting methods, but these calculations are not generally available as differentiable components within machine-learning workflows. We present TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework that ports the organization and numerical conventions of EasySpin into a tensor-based computational environment. Representative calculations spanning continuous-wave EPR, ENDOR, pulse EPR, spin dynamics, trajectory simulation, and magnetometry closely reproduced corresponding EasySpin results. In matched benchmarks, TorchSpin CPU execution was faster than EasySpin for six of nine workloads although performance depended strongly on the calculation. We therefore focused on the capabilities enabled by automatic differentiation in PyTorch. In a Cu(II) powder-spectrum demonstration, feedback propagated through TorchSpin improved the quality of a supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) without using parameter labels during refinement. Models trained from randomly initialized CNNs using only noisy spectra and TorchSpin reconstruction loss achieved median similarities of $\geq$ 0.99. CNNs trained on TorchSpin-generated libraries also transferred without adaptation to independently generated EasySpin spectra with performance comparable to EasySpin-trained controls. Once trained, the CNN produced initial parameter estimates in approximately 1 ms per spectrum while a batch of 512 was processed in approximately 1.3 ms with GPU acceleration. TorchSpin therefore provides both a tested Python implementation of established EPR calculations and a differentiable physical layer for rapid learned inference, spectral refinement, and parameter-label-free training.

title: KEPUASAN KERJA DOSEN: PERAN BEBAN KERJA, STRES KERJA, DAN PENGALAMAN KERJA SEBAGAI MODERATOR
abstract: The increasingly complex demands of the higher education tridharma frequently trigger dynamic psychological pressures and work evaluations among lecturers; however, the mechanisms explaining these relationships continue to show inconsistent findings, particularly regarding how tenure or individual work experience differentiates the impacts of various types of workload. To address this research gap, this study aims to analyze the effects of workload and job stress on lecturers' job satisfaction and to examine work experience as a moderating variable in both relationships, using the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) Theory as a theoretical framework. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed, involving 148 lecturers at Universitas Negeri Semarang (UNNES) selected through proportionate stratified random sampling. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4.0 by evaluating the measurement model, structural model, and moderation effects. The results indicate that workload has a positive and significant effect on job satisfaction (β = 0.272; p = 0.002), whereas job stress has a negative and significant effect (β = −0.384; p < 0.001). Work experience does not moderate the relationship between workload and job satisfaction (β = 0.031; p = 0.702), but it significantly moderates the relationship between job stress and job satisfaction (β = 0.198; p = 0.026), indicating an attenuation of the negative relationship. These findings provide additional evidence that the role of work experience within the JD-R framework is not uniform across different work relationships. Practically, higher education institutions need to strengthen stress management, professional support, mentoring, and workload allocation that is proportional to lecturers' capacities. ABSTRAK Tuntutan tridarma perguruan tinggi yang semakin kompleks kerap memicu dinamika tekanan psikologis dan evaluasi kerja dosen, namun mekanisme yang menjelaskan keterkaitan tersebut masih memperlihatkan inkonsistensi temuan, khususnya terkait bagaimana tenure atau masa kerja individu membedakan dampak dari berbagai jenis beban pekerjaan. Guna mengisi celah penelitian tersebut, penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh beban kerja dan stres kerja terhadap kepuasan kerja dosen serta menguji pengalaman kerja sebagai variabel moderasi pada kedua hubungan tersebut dengan menggunakan Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) Theory sebagai landasan teoretis. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain cross-sectional yang melibatkan 148 dosen Universitas Negeri Semarang (UNNES) yang dipilih melalui proportionate stratified random sampling. Data dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) melalui SmartPLS 4.0 dengan pengujian model pengukuran, model struktural, dan efek moderasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa beban kerja berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan kerja (β = 0,272; p = 0,002), sedangkan stres kerja berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan (β = −0,384; p < 0,001). Pengalaman kerja tidak memoderasi hubungan beban kerja dengan kepuasan kerja (β = 0,031; p = 0,702), tetapi secara signifikan memoderasi hubungan stres kerja dengan kepuasan kerja (β = 0,198; p = 0,026), yang mengarah pada pelemahan hubungan negatif tersebut. Temuan ini memberikan bukti tambahan bahwa peran pengalaman kerja dalam kerangka JD-R tidak seragam pada setiap hubungan kerja. Secara praktis, perguruan tinggi perlu memperkuat pengelolaan stres, dukungan profesional, mentoring, dan pengaturan beban kerja secara proporsional.
journal: PAEDAGOGY : Jurnal Ilmu Pendidikan dan Psikologi

title: What matters when? Temporal development of drivers and sources of nitrous oxide emissions in winter wheat
abstract: Agriculture is the largest anthropogenic source of nitrous oxide (N 2 O), primarily due to nitrogen (N) fertilization. Understanding how the influence of key drivers and the relative contribution of source processes change throughout cropping seasons is crucial for developing effective strategies to mitigate N 2 O emissions. In this study, we combined high-resolution eddy covariance (EC) flux measurements and explainable machine learning (ML) across the 2022–2023 winter wheat season and the subsequent summer cover crop at a temperate site in Switzerland, complemented by stable isotope analyses conducted in March 2023 following a fertilization event. We used Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to interpret an XGBoost model trained to predict N 2 O fluxes, enabling a time-resolved assessment of driver contributions. Crop establishment and early spring emerged as particularly vulnerable periods, characterized by mismatches between N supply and plant demand that led to surplus soil mineral N and elevated N 2 O fluxes under favorable moisture and temperature conditions. Elevated gross primary productivity (GPP, used as a proxy for crop activity and N demand) showed a consistent negative effect on N 2 O fluxes, supporting the role of active vegetation as a competing N sink. Stable isotope source partitioning identified denitrification as the dominant N 2 O production pathway during the early-spring post-fertilization period, consistent with poor soil drainage and high soil moisture. Cumulative N 2 O emissions over the nine-month winter wheat season reached 5.5 kg N 2 O-N ha −1 , with yield-scaled emissions of 1.1 kg N 2 O-N Mg −1 grain, both values exceeding those typically reported for wheat. Our findings highlight the value of combining EC, explainable ML, and stable isotope approaches to resolve the temporal dynamics of N 2 O emissions and identify vulnerable windows for targeted mitigation in cropping systems.

title: Visual Transformation and IP Development as Approaches to Agricultural Heritage Conservation: A Case Study of the Hani Rice Terraces
abstract: This paper asks whether visual transformation and intellectual property (IP) development can provide new ways to address the central challenge in Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS) conservation—how to keep heritage "alive" while also making it sustainable. We use the Honghe Hani Rice Terraces in Yunnan as our case. The analysis looks at the composite and dynamic nature of agricultural heritage, and the practical problems that conservation efforts are now facing. We argue that design-based translation and cultural branding can be useful tools for heritage protection. We propose a four-stage pathway: collecting cultural landscape resources, refining and symbolizing them, designing a core IP image and system, and finally embedding that IP system into the local community. The key idea is to re-express the ecological and cultural values of heritage through modern visual language and brand stories, and spread these through digital media. This approach keeps the "living" quality of heritage while allowing change, encourages community involvement and benefit sharing, and gives both a new theoretical view and practical guidance for adaptive management of agricultural heritage.
journal: Scientific Journal Of Humanities and Social Sciences

title: The Spatial Representation of Invisible Labour: A Gender-Responsive “Productive Neighbourhood” Model for Urban Agriculture
abstract: Increasing urbanisation raises urban food demand, while the ecological costs and crisis vulnerability of conventional agriculture necessitate reconsidering food production within urban environments. Literature shows that women, especially low-income women, play a crucial role in urban food production and in sustaining urban populations through subsistence agriculture. Nevertheless, women’s essential contributions to urban food production are often overlooked and remain spatially invisible in urban planning. This study evaluates the mainstreaming of gender in urban agriculture and food justice as issues of land use and spatial planning. It uses critical document analysis of zoning legislation, urban transformation, and public property regulations in Türkiye. Accordingly, it introduces a productive spatial model at the neighbourhood scale through a gender-responsive planning approach. The model proposes incorporating neighbourhood gardens into legislation as Land Readjustment Contribution Share (LRCS) areas. It also recommends designing educational spaces as multifunctional production areas, such as greenhouses and orchards, transforming residential complexes into productive landscapes, and integrating micro-livestock practices in peri-urban neighbourhoods. These strategies link neighbourhood markets with women’s cooperatives and are supported by local urban agriculture regulations. Integrating urban agriculture into the planning system provides a strategic foundation for building resilient cities, advancing gender-responsive urban agriculture policies, and promoting equity in urban nutrition.

title: The Authority of the Living Plot: Unlearning, Socio-Technical Divides, and Lifelong Learning Ecologies Among Aging Thai Smallholders
abstract: This qualitative instrumental case study explores how aging, low-literacy vegetable smallholders in Wang Thong Sub-district, Northern Thailand, learn, hesitate, negotiate, and adapt while moving from chemical-heavy cultivation toward national Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) standards. Drawing on semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions, and naturalistic participant observations, the study shows that the shift toward safe farming was not experienced as a simple technical adjustment. For many farmers, change began with embodied pressures, including declining health after long-term chemical exposure, rising household debt, and fear of crop failure if familiar practices were abandoned. The findings also reveal that formal training sessions, written GAP logbooks, and digital platforms often intensified anxiety among older farmers with limited schooling. In contrast, practical learning in village demonstration plots, locally understood as “Living Plots,” created safer spaces where farmers could observe, test, fail, ask questions, and rebuild confidence through hands-on experimentation. Peer mentoring, community sages, and everyday exchanges through local networks, including LINE groups, helped sustain learning beyond formal state-led training. Rather than presenting lifelong learning as an individual process of acquiring new knowledge, this study demonstrates how unlearning and relearning occur through bodily experience, shared risk, local trust, and community-based support. Based on these empirical patterns, the study proposes The Evolving Rural Lifelong Learning Ecosystem Model as a field-grounded framework for supporting age-responsive, care-based, and community-embedded agricultural learning in rural contexts.

title: Cataloging the alien flora of Portugal: New findings and updates
abstract: During recent fieldwork in Portugal – mainly in the regions of Estremadura and Ribatejo in the autumn of 2024, but also earlier and elsewhere in the country – many interesting non-indigenous taxa were recorded. The following 25 taxa were not yet known from Portugal: Amaranthus blitum subsp. pseudogracilis, Amaranthus palmeri, Bassia indica, Cardiospermum grandiflorum, Casuarina cunninghamiana, Chloris gayana, Crepis bursifolia, Cyperus papyrus, Elatine ambigua, Eleocharis obtusa, Eragrostis mexicana, E. pectinacea, Guizotia abyssinica, G. schimperi, Hedera algeriensis, Hydrocotyle bowlesioides, H. sibthorpioides, Ipomoea hederacea, Megathyrsus maximus, Nassella tenuissima, Physalis angulata, Sida spinosa, Solanum bonariense, Vitisriparia and V. × ruggerii. Among these, Hydrocotyle bowlesioides is especially noteworthy as this record represents the first confirmed occurrence on the European mainland, extending the known non-native range of the species. In addition, several other taxa were recorded for the first time in particular regions, especially Estremadura and Ribatejo. Most newly recorded species belong to Poaceae and Asteraceae, families that dominate alien floras in Mediterranean regions. Biogeographically, they originate mainly from tropical and subtropical America and Africa, reflecting both climatic affinity and strong anthropogenic dispersal. Regional analyses highlight contrasting patterns: Estremadura, with its urban and coastal environments, acts as a primary entry zone linked to horticultural and transport activities, whereas Ribatejo – especially along the Tagus River (Rio Tejo) valley –functions as a linear dispersal corridor for riparian and agricultural invaders. Several taxa are clearly naturalised, and some show localdominance, underlining an accelerating transition from casual to established status. These findings illustrate the ongoing dynamism of Portugal’s alien vascular flora under the combined influence of globalisation, urbanisation and climate change, and emphasise the need for continued monitoring and documentation through co-ordinated fieldwork and digital biodiversity platforms, particularly in light of the high invasive potential demonstrated by many of the species involved.

title: Occupational burnout and self-reported nonverbal immediacy: A quantitative study of primary education teachers in Greece
abstract: This quantitative, cross-sectional study examined associations between the three dimensions of occupational burnout and primary education teachers' self-reported nonverbal immediacy in the Greek educational context. Data were collected from 76 teachers using the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Educators Survey (MBI-ES) and the Nonverbal Immediacy Scale–Self Report (NIS-S). In accordance with the multidimensional structure of the MBI-ES, emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and personal accomplishment were analysed separately rather than combined into a total burnout score. Depersonalization was negatively associated with self-reported nonverbal immediacy (ρ = −.397, p < .001), whereas personal accomplishment showed the strongest positive association (ρ =.499, p < .001). Emotional exhaustion was not significantly associated with self-reported nonverbal immediacy (ρ = −.170, p = .142). The simultaneous multiple regression model was statistically significant, F(3, 72) = 6.97, p < .001, R2 = .225, adjusted R2 = .193; personal accomplishment was the only dimension with a statistically significant unique association (β = .394, p = .003). Because the study is cross-sectional and all focal variables were self-reported, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects and do not represent direct observation of classroom behaviour. The study extends existing research by demonstrating that different dimensions of burnout are differentially associated with teachers’ perceived nonverbal communicative behaviour, with personal accomplishment and depersonalization emerging as particularly relevant to perceived communicative presence. The differentiated pattern across burnout dimensions suggests that emotional depletion, relational distancing, and positive professional self-evaluation should not be treated as interchangeable when examining teachers’ perceived communicative presence.
journal: Research on Preschool and Primary Education

title: Computer Simulation of Marghi Cultural Symbols as Source of Unified Motifs for Textile Design and Production
abstract: This study explores the application of computer simulation techniques to transform Marghi cultural symbols into unified motifs suitable for textile design and production. The Marghi people of northeastern Nigeria possess rich cultural heritage expressed through symbolic art forms that risk erosion due to modernistion and limited documentation. Employing Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and digital simulation techniques, this research digitises and synthesises key Marghi symbols traditionally found in war weapons, marriage accessories, musical instruments, and agricultural implements. A mixed-methods approach combining ethnographic research and survey design was adopted, with data collected from 399 respondents in Madagali Local Government Area, Adamawa State. Visual observations and oral interviews revealed 70 distinct motifs, from which 20 were purposively selected and developed into 10 unified textile designs using CorelDraw X7. The digitally printed fabrics were evaluated for cultural authenticity and aesthetic appeal. Results indicate that 65% of respondents were unfamiliar with Marghi cultural symbols, yet 82.7% emphasized the importance of preservation. The Dala pattern achieved the highest overall acceptance rating (94.9%), followed by the Knundai basket pattern (93.3%). The study demonstrates that digital tools can effectively bridge cultural preservation and modern design innovation, enabling scalable and aesthetically rich reproduction of traditional motifs while maintaining cultural significance.
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory

title: Digital Infrastructure Access, Fintech Adoption, And Financial Inclusion Among Smallholder Farmers in North Central Nigeria: A PLS-SEM Analysis
abstract: Purpose: Smallholder farmers account for the majority of Nigeria's food production yet remain largely excluded from formal financial services, constraining productivity and rural economic development. This study examines whether access to digital infrastructure drives FinTech adoption among smallholder farmers, and whether FinTech adoption, in turn, translates into meaningful financial inclusion. Design/Methodology/Approach: A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed. Structured questionnaires were administered face-to-face to smallholder farmers across Benue, Nasarawa, Plateau, and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Abuja in Nigeria's North Central region, using a stratified multi-stage sampling procedure. Of 445 questionnaires distributed, 392 valid responses were obtained (88.1% response rate). Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS was used to assess the measurement model and to test the hypothesised structural relationships between digital infrastructure access, FinTech adoption, and financial inclusion. Findings: All constructs demonstrated strong reliability and convergent validity (Cronbach's alpha, composite reliability, and AVE values exceeding recommended thresholds). Digital infrastructure access exerted a strong, positive, and statistically significant effect on FinTech adoption (β = 0.934, t = 138.009, p < 0.001), explaining 87.2% of the variance in adoption. FinTech adoption, in turn, had a strong positive effect on financial inclusion (β = 0.873, t = 50.832, p < 0.001). Both hypothesised paths were robustly supported, with effect sizes considerably larger than those typically reported in comparable technology-adoption studies. Practical Implications: The findings indicate that digital infrastructure functions as a threshold precondition rather than a marginal enabler of FinTech adoption in resource constrained rural settings. Policymakers, mobile network operators, and FinTech providers should therefore prioritise rural connectivity and infrastructure investment as a precondition for financial-inclusion programming, rather than treating infrastructure and adoption facilitation initiatives as parallel, independent workstreams. Originality: This study provides rare, statistically robust, empirically grounded evidence of the infrastructure–adoption–inclusion pathway among smallholder farmers in a developing economy agricultural setting, using a large, regionally stratified sample and rigorous PLS SEM validation. It extends Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation theory by demonstrating that communication-channel access can function as a binding constraint rather than a merely facilitating condition in infrastructure-scarce rural economies.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH

title: Agro‑Governance: Institutional and Digital Transformation in Agricultural Contracts and the Role of Third Parties in Bulgaria
abstract: The article analyses the evolution of governance structures in Bulgarian agriculture during the period 2000–2024, with particular focus on the role of institutional intermediaries (“third parties”) and the impact of digitalisation on agricultural contracts. The study applies the framework of the New Institutional Economics (NIE) and draws on 1,027 empirical observations to trace how the interaction between state administration, private agents and rights holders shapes transaction costs and property protection. The results show a fragmentation of functions reflected in the growing variety of contract types, accompanied by an increase in the number of documents and procedural complexity. Digitalization optimizes certain processes but increases dependence on adaptation to information systems, which in turn raises the time and costs required to process contracts. The analysis reveals that institutional transformation leads to greater formalisation, which does not always translate into higher economic efficiency, especially for small farmers. The study highlights the dual nature of institutional and digital reforms, which tend to transform rather than reduce the complexity of agro-governance.

title: A Study on the Challenges and Optimization Strategies for the Development of Cross-Border E-Commerce for Specialty Agricultural Products in County-Level Regions
abstract: Against the backdrop of the digital economy’s deep penetration into the rural revitalization sector, the digital transformation of cross-border trade in distinctive county-level agricultural products has emerged as a new model for foreign trade development—one that unlocks the value of local agricultural resources, opens up domestic and international distribution channels for agricultural products, and fosters a competitive edge in the agricultural industry. The development bottlenecks currently facing the growth of cross-border e-commerce for county-level agricultural products are not merely shortcomings in a single link of the industrial chain. Rather, they represent systemic challenges across the entire industrial chain resulting from the mutual constraints and cumulative effects of six core elements: cold-chain logistics systems, market-oriented brand operations, international trade compliance, port clearance services, multidisciplinary professionals, and cross-border financial services. Development shortcomings across these dimensions are interrelated and mutually restrictive, forming a negative feedback loop that is difficult to break through independently. Taking a full-industry-chain development perspective as its core entry point, this paper systematically analyzes the intrinsic relationships and coupling mechanisms among the six constraining factors. Drawing on practical industrial case studies from typical counties in China, it establishes a multi-stakeholder collaborative governance framework for industrial development and proposes a set of systematic, actionable industrial optimization strategies, including the upgrading of cross-border supply chains and cold-chain systems, the establishment of a dual-track brand cultivation system and a full-chain international compliance empowerment system, the optimization of port customs clearance facilitation mechanisms, the development of a tiered, multidisciplinary talent training mechanism, and the construction of a diversified cross-border financial support system.

title: AI-Based Personalized Travel Planning and Recommendation System: A Unified Framework for Intelligent Trip Planning
abstract: A growing number of travel planning activities involve managing multiple pieces of often competing data about destinations, budget, weather, attractions' availability, transportation options and personal preferences that are typically distributed across a number of isolated online services. Traditional travel-planning tools tackle these issues one at a time: choosing or navigating, and rarely include personalization, predictive analytics, and multi-constraint reasoning within a single interface. We propose a unified framework for personalized travel planning that integrates personal preferences, context-based destination recommendation, budget-and weather-aware filtering, and route and distance analysis, and AI-assisted itinerary generation. The framework is inspired, and to some extent generalized, from the design of the ongoing academic research prototype TripCraft, an AI-powered agent for trip planning. We build upon the state of the art of recommender-systems theory, context-aware recommendation, tourist trip design (route optimization) literature, and recent large language model-based agents for travel-planning to develop a system-level description, a hybrid AI/ML approach, and a step-by-step algorithmic process for creating personalized itineraries that take preference, budget, weather and route constraints into account. We provide preliminary proof of concept based on a synthetic evaluation on fabricated records using baseline comparisons and constraint-compliance metrics. The findings are only indicative of the possible effectiveness, but do not constitute proof of concept. The expected contribution is the conceptual and methodological foundation for unifying preference, budget, weather-and route awareness in intelligent travel planning.

title: Predictive Analytics for Construction Material Procurement, Cost Control and Schedule Performance in Saudi Giga-Projects
abstract: Unprecedented construction activity, tight delivery windows, complex interfaces, global sourcing, and exposure to volatile material markets characterize Saudi Arabia’s giga-project portfolio. These conditions make procurement, cost control, and schedule performance highly interrelated. This review critically discusses how predictive analytics can convert fragmented project, commercial, supply-chain, and progress data into forward-looking decisions for construction material procurement for Saudi giga-projects. An integrative review method integrates recent peer-reviewed evidence on machine learning, construction cost forecasting, schedule prediction, digital supply chains, building information modeling, digital twins, and Saudi project performance. The literature indicates that the predictive value is greatest when models combine material demand, price escalation, supplier reliability, lead times, inventory status, progress quantities, and schedule logic, rather than attempting to predict a single outcome in isolation. Ensemble learning and hybrid models regularly yield better forecasting precision, but their operational-level usefulness depends on data quality, temporal validity, explainability, and integration with procurement and project-control workflows. Saudi studies consistently identify material-price fluctuation, change orders, planning weaknesses, and delayed approvals as major cost and time pressures. Yet, direct evidence of analytics-enabled procurement in giga-project settings remains limited. The review suggests an integrated predictive-control architecture that links 5D BIM, enterprise resource planning, supplier data, market indicators and planning systems. It argues that predictive analytics in giga-project organizations should be seen as a governance capability rather than a standalone algorithm, marrying model outputs with human review, uncertainty ranges and auditable intervention thresholds. Future research directions encompass Saudi longitudinal datasets, cross-project transferability, causal evaluation of interventions, supplier-risk prediction, and explainable models that jointly optimize procurement cost, material availability, and schedule resilience.

title: Parsing the Pediatric Mood Spectrum in U.S. Youth: Transdiagnostic Severity Versus Phenotypic Specificity
abstract: Objective: Emotion dysregulation and irritability occur across pediatric disorders, complicating distinctions between general symptom burden and specific clinical presentations. Person-centered analyses can look at profiles of scores to identify groups with similar presentations. We examined whether modeling shared and domain-specific symptom variance identified differentiated profiles in youth. Method: Caregivers of 2,187 US youth ages 6-18 completed 87 items assessing emotion dysregulation, depression, mania-related symptoms, sleep-related impairment, and attention and behavioral problems. An ordinal bifactor model estimated one general and 13 specific factors. Latent profile analyses used standardized scores on all 14 factors, with an expanded raw-score analysis as a comparator. We examined caregiver-reported diagnoses and functioning and approximately two-week classification agreement among 166 recontacted caregivers. Results: The general factor accounted for 62% of common variance ({omega}H=.94), although model fit was mixed (CFI=.884; RMSEA=.058; SRMR=.092). A provisional four-class solution distinguished population-modal (67.4%), internalizing (11.8%), attention/hyperactivity (11.0%), and unusual-thought/elevated-mood (9.8%) profiles. Entropy was .83, but model enumeration and initialization checks did not establish a unique solution. Profiles showed overlapping diagnostic and functional correlates. Recontact agreement was 78.9% ({kappa}=.60). Irritability-specific reliability was limited, constraining interpretation of its weak profile differentiation. Conclusions: General symptom burden coexisted with differentiated residual symptom patterns. These findings support evaluating severity alongside symptom configuration, without equating profiles with diagnoses or weak residual irritability signals with limited clinical relevance. Measurement refinement, model-selection verification, and confirmation of classification-error-adjusted associations are needed before clinical application, but profiles could simplify clinical interpretation of sets of scales.

title: Computational modelling of decision-making in suicide attempters
Prognostic value of the Hippo signaling pathway in oral squamous cell carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Active teaching-learning methodology in a non-formal teaching environment as a tool to mitigate the ‘plant awareness disparity’ in public school students
abstract: Currently, a significant proportion of young people are discouraged by the teaching of botany and, consequently, show little interest in preserving local biodiversity. On the other hand, with the recurrent use of digital technologies (DTs), young people have shown significant interest in virtual devices. Our project’s tested the hypothesis whether plants awareness disparity in public school students was overcome through active teaching and learning. Thus, the objective was to investigate the use of active methodology in a non-formal teaching environment (e.g., sensory garden, SG) in order to stimulate learning in plant organography based on its evaluation using digital games. Our proposal was investigated at the Lagoa do Sino campus (Buri/SP, Brazil) in partnership with the Public School System of the Municipality of Campina do Monte Alegre/SP, Brazil. Furthermore, students were divided into two teams, which applied qualitative methodologies, such as that one of these (‘Team A’) had “face-to-face” contact with the SG, using the ‘Problem-Based Learning’ (PBL) methodology, digital game and survey. Team B, on the other hand, will only have contact with the game. After collecting the data, we verified statistically significant differences between the teams using the Wilcoxon test and based on the latent traits evaluated. Given this, the literature points out that discouraging students influences their learning and, consequently, their education. In addition, our considerations are based on the latent trait ‘knowledge of botany’ and, thus, we reject our null hypothesis and accept our alternative hypothesis. On the other hand, based on the latent trait of plant perception, we cannot affirm the acceptance or rejection of the hypotheses. It is worth noting that future studies should have a larger number of participants than this research in order to better evaluate what is intended. Societal impact Statement Brazil presents a paradox: it is an agricultural powerhouse with booming production and vast biodiversity, crucial to its economy. However, a significant “plant awareness disparity” exists. The public shows little interest in botany, and the media neglects its importance. This lack of knowledge means people fail to appreciate plants’ economic value in sectors like pharmaceuticals and cosmetics, or their environmental role. Consequently, there is little concern for preserving local biodiversity. Despite having the world’s richest flora, this motivational gap prevents society from valuing its vital botanical heritage.

title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models reveals an advantage in the low-data regime for cell-type and disease-state prediction
abstract: Single-cell foundation models perform well on cell-type classification, but their value for disease-state prediction and their advantage over classical representations remains unclear. We benchmarked cell-representations from four foundation models using logistic regression, on 868 disease-prediction tasks (82 datasets) and 65 cell-type datasets from CELLxGENE. With full data, the baseline (log-normalized counts) outperformed the best model (TranscriptFormer-Sapiens) for cell type and matched it for disease. However, with few labeled cells, TranscriptFormer-Sapiens significantly outperformed the baseline in both tasks up to ~10 2 samples per class. Our comprehensive zero-shot benchmark identifies the data-scarce regime as a domain where Single-cell foundation models truly show advantage.

title: Feature-level fusion of Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery for crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountainous terrain
abstract: Accurate crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountains is challenged by persistent cloud cover, rugged topography, and fragmented smallholder parcels. This study evaluates a feature-level fusion workflow that integrates Sentinel-2 optical indices and Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter for crop-type mapping in Candipuro District, Lumajang, East Java, Indonesia. Sentinel-2 surface reflectance and Sentinel-1 IW data acquired in June–July 2023 were harmonised in Google Earth Engine to a common 10 m pixel grid, so that all comparison maps were evaluated on the same spatial support. The optical component comprised NDVI, NDBI, and NDWI, whereas the radar component used the VH/VV polarisation ratio. A DEM was used only to characterise the mountainous setting and to assist terrain interpretation, and was not included as a predictor in the classifier. The stacked feature image was classified using a Random Forest model trained with 101 field-survey ground control points representing eight land-cover/crop-related classes.
