A strong correlation between measured and estimated values is observed for the plasticity index (R² = 0.73), while moisture content shows a moderate correlation (R² = 0.45). In contrast, cohesion and friction angle exhibit very weak correlations, R² = 0.04 and R² = 0.05, respectively, highlighting the influence of structural and mechanical factors, such as fracturing, cementation, and lithological heterogeneity, that are not directly governed by electrical conduction processes. Three-dimensional modelling of ERT-derived properties reveals the spatial distribution of the main geotechnical units and identifies a three-layered subsurface structure composed of a resistive weathered limestone tuff cap, an intermediate conductive silty-marl horizon, and a deeper fractured limestone unit. Although the estimated parameters show broader ranges due to the spatial continuity of geophysical data, laboratory measurements generally fall within the ranges of these estimates. These results demonstrate that ERT based empirical modelling can provide reasonable preliminary estimates for parameters closely linked to electrical resistivity, particularly moisture content and plasticity index. However, mechanical strength parameters such as cohesion and friction angle require cautious interpretation and must be validated through direct laboratory testing. Overall, the integrated approach offers a cost-effective tool for large-scale preliminary geotechnical reconnaissance, improved identification of potentially unstable zones in karst envi - ronments, and optimization of borehole investigation strategies.

title: Multiple classification of childhood and juvenile autism spectrum disorder from ABIDE-II sMRI using BN-GO-CNN
abstract: Objectives Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) shows heterogeneous neurodevelopmental patterns across childhood, juvenile development, and adulthood, so binary MRI classification may not fully capture age-and sex-related variation. This study proposes a proof-of-concept framework for multiple classification using ABIDE-II T1-weighted structural MRI (sMRI). Methods After image-quality screening, sMRI slices were processed using Canny edge detection, brain-region cropping, 224 × 224 resizing, and augmentation. Images were organized into sex-based four-class, age-based four-class, and combined age-and-sex eight-class datasets, separating child, young, juvenile, adult, male, and female groups. A Batch-Normalized Grid-Optimized CNN (BN-GO-CNN) was developed to learn structural representations directly from preprocessed sMRI, with grid search used to select key CNN hyperparameters. The model was compared with VGG16, DenseNet201, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0 using identical image partitions. Results BN-GO-CNN achieved validation accuracies of 67.0 %, 64.0 %, and 60.5 % for sex-based, age-based, and combined age-and-sex classification, respectively. These outcomes remained above chance but showed limited class separability. Conclusions The modest performance suggests that label-related sMRI differences are subtle, supporting this framework as a preliminary test of CNN-assisted sMRI classification for future research use rather than a clinically reliable ASD diagnostic system.

title: Who Can Undo the Agent? Redressability as a First-Class Safety Property for Tool-Using AI Agents
abstract: Tool-using AI agents increasingly act inside institutional workflows by updating records, sending notices, changing account status, scheduling services, and triggering review processes. Existing agent-safety evaluations largely ask whether agents avoid harmful actions. Deployed institutions must also determine whether affected people and responsible reviewers can discover, understand, contest, reverse, and obtain remedy for consequential actions after they occur. We operationalize redressability, a property grounded in legal doctrine and accountability scholarship, as a first-class safety property of tool-using agents. The framework defines eight scoreable dimensions: detectability, traceability, contestability, reversibility, remedy, recurrence prevention, burden allocation, and value-chain assignability. We instantiate the framework in Agent RedressBench, a benchmark of 40 seed and 24 stress scenarios; Redress Traces, an action-level provenance schema; and Redress Gate, a proposed runtime-enforcement pattern. Diagnostic experiments with GPT-4.1 and Llama 3.1 8B show that guardrails, trace generation, and escalation address distinct failure modes. Guardrails reduced automatic unsafe-action labels without creating redress evidence, whereas trace contracts reliably elicited accountability artifacts. Trace-only outputs nevertheless received unsafe-action labels in 26/40 Llama seed cases, sometimes while documenting that required approval had not been obtained. A blinded single-validator assessment of all 96 GPT-4.1 stress trajectories rated 93 trajectories safe and three ambiguous, while sharply separating trace from non-trace conditions in redressability: mean scores were 19.21/24 and 19.33/24 for trace and trace plus escalation, compared with 4.38/24 and 4.58/24 for baseline and guardrailed conditions. These findings support the separation of substantive action safety from procedural redressability and motivate runtime enforcement as a design implication rather than an evaluated treatment.
journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)

title: Unaccountable Delegation, Fading Skills: Mapping the Risks of Workplace AI Agents
abstract: To anticipate the socio-technical risks posed by AI agents, organizations first need taxonomies to classify them. However, existing AI risk taxonomies focus on broad risks and do not capture the job-specific risks introduced by agents. To address this gap, we make three main contributions. First, we developed a multi-layer framework based on a review of the literature on AI agents. The framework models three core components and their interactions: the agents, their goals, and their environment. Second, we embedded this framework in a structured prompt and applied it to descriptions of 2,078 job tasks from the O*NET occupational database, producing 8,356 risk scenarios labeled by severity and deployment mode (automation or augmentation). We validated these scenarios with 45 workers across 10 job roles and an independent LLM judge, confirming their high plausibility and alignment with the corresponding job tasks. Finally, we extended an existing taxonomy to create a 15-category taxonomy of workplace AI agent risks that covers all our risk scenarios. Our analysis highlights four findings. First, augmentation is not inherently safe because overreliance on agents can gradually erode workers' skills and oversight. Second, erroneous actions of agents account for the largest share of risk scenarios and has the highest number of severe risks. Many of these risks arise at the human-agent boundary. Third, automation is associated mainly with organizational risks (operational failures, financial losses), whereas augmentation is associated mainly with risks to workers (capability erosion, psychological and social risks). Fourth, workers found our taxonomy easier to use for a risk classification task than two other risk taxonomies and preferred it in 64% of non-tied comparisons with a recent generative AI risk taxonomy. Taken together, these findings show that workplace AI agent risks do not arise from agents alone; they also depend on how people work with agents and how agents are deployed. Safer workplaces therefore require not only safer agents but also carefully designed human-AI agent collaboration.
journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)

title: Why Do AI Agents Break Rules? How Framing, Context, and Social Signals Shape Compliance
abstract: Specifying a penalty can turn a legal obligation into a cost-benefit calculation that favors violation. We show that this enforcement information paradox occurs in AI agents. Most AI safety evaluations test whether models fail; we ask why, using compliance theory from law and economics as a diagnostic. We evaluate twelve instruction-tuned language models deployed as enterprise procurement chatbots. Each is given an environmental regulation in its system prompt covering large purchases, and a vendor list on which the certified suppliers cost nearly twice what the uncertified ones do. We test the agents against the predictions of deterrence, legitimacy, and expressive law, and find that each theory accounts for part of what we observe. Under identical conditions, compliance spans 46 percentage points across models, and models differ in which pressure breaks them: some treat the regulation as binding however it is worded, while others fail where theory predicts, under low penalties and non-command phrasing. Benchmark scores and developers' own descriptions of post-training do not predict where a model falls. Across all twelve, financial incentives, managerial demands, peer outcomes, and employee pressure each produce large compliance failures. These agents violate regulatory constraints to satisfy local user objectives in ways standard alignment benchmarks do not measure. Embedding the rule in the system prompt is not on its own enough to produce a compliant agent: model selection is itself a governance decision, and benchmark evaluation is not sufficient for compliance-sensitive deployments.
journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)

title: Agentic Relationship Harm: Benchmarking and Gating Relational Manipulation in AI Agents
abstract: AI agents built on large language models can assist not only legitimate tasks but also relational manipulation. AI agents can be used to help a user maintain a deceptive identity, intensify emotional dependency, isolate a target, or prepare for later extraction. We conceptualise this risk as agentic relationship harm: workflow-level assistance that can exploit recipient vulnerability, persuasive influence, and relational power asymmetry. Existing safety evaluations and generic guardrails often treat harmfulness as a property of isolated outputs, missing role-sensitive interaction patterns. To study this, we introduce a 110-prompt benchmark with balanced attacker-and victim-side cases, a relationship-specific labelling framework, and a lightweight post-generation policy gate for local agent deployments. In our evaluation, the relationship-specific gate outperforms generic safety prompting under automated judging, with no harmful-compliance cases identified on the main benchmark or multi-turn stress test while preserving victim-side protective intervention. These results suggest that relationship harm is a distinct sociotechnical risk surface and that role-sensitive evaluation plus lightweight policy gating offers a practical path beyond generic refusal prompting.
journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)

title: Small-world Networks of Agents Brainstorm AI Risks to Support Ideation
abstract: The ideation phase of participatory AI risk assessment often starts with a blank slate or a limited list of predefined risks, making it difficult to surface indirect or systemic harms. To address this limitation, we propose a three-stage tool to support the ideation phase of AI risk assessment. The tool complements participatory AI, rather than replacing it, and helps focus later engagement with affected communities. First, it dynamically discovers stakeholders depending on the given AI use and recursively expanding outward, allowing overlooked or indirect stakeholders to emerge. Second, it simulates these stakeholders with LLMs (creating in-silico stakeholders), connecting them into a network of a given topology, and having them ideate about risks. Third, it prioritizes risks using network centrality measures (the centrality of in-silico stakeholders in the network). In an initial evaluation, we found that betweenness centrality run through agents connected in a small-world network works best as it elevates risks raised by stakeholders who bridge disconnected groups, surfacing novel, systemic harms that traditional methods often miss. On an AI chatbot companion use case, this approach increased the novelty of the identified risks by approximately 1.1 points over single LLM brainstorming, and by 0.5 points over agentic LLM brainstorming, measured on a normalized five-point Likert scale, without reducing the plausibility or severity of the identified risks. To test whether our framework helps a human-led ideation session using the Futures-Wheel approach, we divided 11 teams of non-western young chatbot users into two types: control (team) and treatment (team) in a participatory AI risk assessment. The control teams started from a list of risks generated by the 45 AI practitioners in the initial evaluation; the treatment teams started from a list generated by our framework. The treatment teams identified more risks overall, and more systemic, human-computer interaction, and environmental risks in particular, categories that practitioners typically find harder to spot.
journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)

title: Virtue by Observation: Social Reinforcement Learning for Intrinsically Ethical Agents
abstract: Reinforcement learning is increasingly deployed in settings with ethical stakes, yet rule-based and scalar-reward alignment approaches remain brittle and prone to proxy gaming. I argue that two of their most persistent failures, hallucination and moral drift, share a single structural cause, which I term \textit{feedback collapse}: the compression of plural human values into a static scalar reward by a fixed evaluation model. My research develops a virtue-centric alternative, Social Reinforcement Learning, in which evaluative authority is distributed across a dynamic population of peer agents. Completed work formalizes feedback integrity as a gradient alignment condition, proposes Epistemic Source Alignment to defend against sycophantic evaluators, introduces the Forager's Dilemma to study peer enforcement, and shows that standard multi-agent metrics cannot distinguish consensus from coercion. Planned work asks whether agents can internalize stable ethical dispositions purely by observing virtuous peers.
journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)

title: Rethinking Agentic AI: A Sociotechnical Framework for Agents in Emergent Social Contexts
abstract: Existing agent-environment frameworks were not calibrated to capture the open-ended social digital environments in which AI agents are increasingly deployed. These contexts continuously evolve as a product of human-agent and agent-agent interactions, rather than through fixed mappings between actions and consequences assumed in much of agentic AI research. I propose a new sociotechnical conceptual framework for studying AI agents in these settings and argue that the agent-environment loop is not merely iterative but recursive: agents do not simply interact with environments, but actively co-constitute them. This recursive dynamic may lead to behavioral and normative drift, defined as systematic divergence from an agent's deployment baseline. The framework is intended to support empirical inquiry into agentic behavior at scale, inform alignment-focused research, and provide a theoretical foundation for governance surrounding multi-agent systems deployed in uncontrolled, real-world settings.
journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)

title: A Web-Based Farmer-Buyer Partnership System for Direct Agricultural Market Connectivity
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in the Indian economy and provides livelihood opportunities for a large rural population. However, farmers often face difficulties in finding suitable buyers, accessing market information, communicating product availability, and managing agricultural sales. Traditional agricultural marketing systems may involve multiple intermediaries, resulting in limited direct interaction between farmers and buyers. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Farmer– Buyer Partnership System, a web-based platform that provides a digital connection between farmers and buyers. The proposed system enables farmers to register, create profiles, list agricultural products, specify available quantities and expected prices, and manage buyer requests. Buyers can register, search and view available agricultural products, access relevant farmer and product information, and submit partnership requests. An administrator manages users, products, and partnership activities through a centralized system. The proposed application is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, Python Flask for the backend, and MySQL for database management. The system follows a structured approach to improve product visibility, communication, request tracking, and information accessibility. The proposed platform provides a foundation for direct farmer– buyer interaction and can be extended in the future with online payments, real-time market prices, logistics management, notifications, and intelligent farmer–buyer matching.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Global Synthesis of Socio-Ecological System Research in Watersheds: A Systematic Review and Dynamic Framework Proposal
abstract: Watersheds are increasingly understood as socio-ecological systems (SES), reflecting the close interaction between ecological processes and human activities. However, research trends, thematic developments, and knowledge gaps in watershed-based SES studies have yet to be comprehensively synthesized. This study aims to examine the evolution of SES research in watershed contexts through a systematic review of the scientific literature published between 1999 and 2025. Following the PRISMA approach, records were retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science. A total of 689 documents were initially identified; 455 remained after duplicate removal, and 96 articles met the final eligibility criteria for analysis. The review reveals a substantial increase in watershed-SES publications after 2018. Earlier studies primarily focused on conceptual development, whereas more recent research has expanded toward governance, climate adaptation, resilience, land-use pressures, and agricultural–water interactions. Geographic patterns indicate that studies conducted in the Global North tend to emphasize institutional and modeling approaches, while research in the Global South more frequently addresses socio-ecological pressures and local environmental challenges. The synthesis also highlights the growing use of spatial analytical tools, particularly Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing, to investigate watershed dynamics and support management decisions. Based on the findings, this study proposes a conceptual Dynamic SES–Watershed Framework that links ecological thresholds, governance processes, adaptive capacity, resilience, and land-use pressures within watershed systems. However, as a review-based study, the framework is intended as a conceptual foundation for future empirical testing rather than a validated model. The findings contribute to a broader understanding of watershed sustainability and provide directions for future SES research and management.

authors.name: Yohanes M. F. Seko Raja Mijang

title: Evaluation of Crop Water Production Functions (CWPF) for Carrot from a Mathematical Modeling Perspective
abstract: Crop water production functions (CWPF), which define the functional relationship between yield and water use in agricultural production, assuming all other production input variables remain constant, are of great importance in defining different irrigation strategies and determining optimal irrigation levels. The aim of this study is to estimate yield in carrot by utilizing the performance of the Stewart, Jensen, Minhas, Blank, and Rao functions (CWPF). Field studies on carrot were conducted in 2019 and 2020 at the Agricultural Production Center of Bursa Uludağ University Bursa Yenişehir Vocational School. The water stress sensitivity indices of crop water production functions (CWPF) were determined using ET and yield values from the first year. The yield values simulated with the crop water production functions in 2019 were compared with the yield values measured in the field in 2020. Using five different crop water production models (CWPF), the water sensitivity indices of carrot at four different crop growth stages were determined. Based on the water sensitivity indices of carrot during four different crop growth periods, the yield formation period (Y) was determined to be the most water-sensitive period. The yield formation (Y) period was followed by the flowering (F) and vegetative (V) periods. The stage at which carrot is least sensitive to water is the ripening (R) stage. When comparing the water stress sensitivity indices calculated for four different crop growth stages of carrot, it can be said that the estimates obtained from the Rao and Blank (Bras-Cordova) models are more accurate and, therefore, are the most suitable models to be recommended within crop water production functions.
journal: Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology

title: A Gateway-Based Approach for Integrating Digital Compass Data into Controller Area Network (CAN) in Precision Farming Systems
abstract: The integration of high precision orientation sensors into resilient communication infrastructures is a key requirement for next-generation autonomous systems. Digital compass sensors typically generate data in the NMEA format, whereas distributed control architectures in mobile robotics predominantly utilize the CAN 2.0B protocol. This study presents the design and implementation of a microcontroller-based hardware-software gateway that enables seamless interoperability between these heterogeneous communication standards within autonomous agricultural platforms. The proposed system operates as a protocol translation layer, acquiring orientation data (heading, pitch, and roll) from a digital compass via serial communication and converting it into CAN-compliant messages. The incoming NMEA sentences are parsed, validated, and filtered before being encapsulated into extended CAN frames. To address the payload limitations of Classical CAN and discrepancies in transmission rates, a multi-frame segmentation strategy and a synchronization mechanism based on handshaking are implemented. Additionally, buffering techniques are employed to ensure temporal consistency and prevent data loss during high-frequency data exchange. Experimental evaluations demonstrated that the proposed gateway achieved reliable real-time communication performance, with an average end to end communication latency of 19.6 ms, a 99.98% message reconstruction success rate, and 0.02% packet loss during continuous CAN Bus data transmission tests. The proposed integration framework effectively bridges the gap between legacy serial sensor protocols and modern CAN Bus-based distributed systems. Consequently, this work offers a scalable and practical solution for protocol interoperability in precision agriculture and contributes to the development of robust sensor integration strategies for autonomous field robotics.
journal: Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology

title: Digital Agricultural Transformation under Climate Risk: A Policy and Financing Perspective within the National Economy Model
abstract: Today, the global food system is undergoing a multidimensional transformation driven by climate change, population growth and rising food demand. Irregular precipitation regimes, increasing water scarcity and ecosystem degradation are making agricultural production increasingly unpredictable and fragile. In addition to these ecological pressures, shrinking arable land, the ageing agricultural labour force and rising input costs further challenge the sustainability of conventional farming systems. The growing frequency of extreme weather events demonstrates the vulnerability of existing production models and highlights the need for structural transformation in agriculture. Digital agriculture offers a potential solution through a technology-oriented paradigm shift. Technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI)-based decision support systems, remote sensing and precision agriculture enable site-specific resource management, reducing environmental impact while improving productivity. However, the adoption of these technologies is constrained by high investment costs and financial uncertainty, particularly for small and medium-scale producers. Therefore, integrating digital technologies into agricultural production depends on reducing financial and operational risks through effective public policy instruments. This conceptual analysis state-led strategic support mechanisms for digital agricultural transformation within the framework of the National Economy Model (NEM). The model’s production-oriented and cost-protection principles provide a stabilisation framework that may facilitate technological adoption. The study argues that public support mechanisms function not only as financial assistance but also as strategic policy instruments that enhance agricultural resilience and production continuity under climate-related risks.
journal: Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology

title: Problems of digitalizing failure analysis of asynchronous electric drives in agriculture
abstract: The paper examines the relevant issue of using neural network diagnostics as an auxiliary element of a set of measures to detect failures of the asynchronous electric drive of a vibratory jaw crusher used for crushing mineral fertilizers. A distinctive feature of this equipment is its ability to generate powerful vibration loads necessary for the effective destruction of the material, while maintaining the reliability and simplicity of the design. According to statistical data, up to 95 % of asynchronous motors installed in vibratory jaw crushers for crushing mineral fertilizers are machines with a power output ranging from 75 to 250 kW. These motors are most susceptible to the effects of aggressive environments, humidity, temperature fluctuations and increased vibration loads, which primarily leads to the failure of the mechanical parts of the equipment and the stator winding bars. The authors demonstrate the main problems of applying the method of neural network diagnostics of equipment and develop an algorithm for predicting failures of the actuator, namely, rod breakage in the phases of the stator of an asynchronous motor that operates as a drive for a vibrating jaw crusher of mineral fertilizers. Moreover, the research presents the assessment methodology with an expanded algorithm that allows eliminating a number of typical failures for this equipment, thereby increasing the efficiency of using an asynchronous electric drive in this industry. The research produced guidelines for operating and configuring the neural network algorithm designed to detect broken stator bars in an asynchronous motor.

title: Fisiología económica del mango: la función de producción en cultivos perennes sinaloense 2000-2023
abstract: The study of mango production in Sinaloa (2000-2023) demonstrates that yield is not a contemporary stochastic event, but a trajectory-dependent process defined by the orchard’s inherited physiological state. The evidence indicates that the crop arrives at each cycle with an energy ‘memory’ accumulated from its recent production history, which conditions its capacity to respond to climate, management, and inputs. Modeling using ensemble algorithms enabled classification of the production regimes with 77%-79% accuracy, achieving a statistical robustness of R²= 0.84 by identifying that physiological memory dominates the hierarchy of predictors with a relative weight of 53%. This finding allowed us to reinterpret the variability in production. The drop in yield is not explained by structural failures or extreme climatic events but by physiological depletion accumulated after previous cycles of high biomass extraction. Similarly, years with favorable climatic conditions may not translate into high yields if the tree arrives energetically compromised. An induction ‘sweet point’ was identified, where the maximum yield (7.78 t ha-1) is only viable under a water stress index between 0.54 and 0.61; outside this threshold, the tree exhibits an inelastic response regardless of its previous load. Based on this logic, operational bioindicators were developed that allow anticipating the crop’s response and differentiating years to intensify production from |those where physiological recovery should be prioritized, optimizing intertemporal decision-making in perennial agricultural systems.

title: LAYER 2 OF THE AI-FIRST SDLC: A PROPOSED AGENT-DRIVEN ARCHITECTURE FOR BUILD, VALIDATION, AND RELEASE READINESS
abstract: This paper proposes Layer 2 of the AI-First Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) introduced in our parent framework and extended through the Layer 1 Product and Designer Layer. Layer 2 is a conceptual Build, Validate, and Release architecture intended to transform a Product Requirement Bundle (PRB) and a Design Artifact Bundle (DAB) into a documented, validated, merge-ready pull request. It defines six proposed specialist agents—Architecture, Coding, Testing, Review, PR, and CI Gate—coordinated by a Layer 2 Sub-Orchestrator. The design includes a bounded Feedback-Driven Repair Loop, revalidation after code modifications, non-overridable CI and security gates, and a mandatory human merge decision. The proposed design draws on the authors' technical analysis, review of existing software-engineering and agentic-AI approaches, and exploratory proof-of-concept work. The integrated architecture has not been implemented or empirically evaluated; potential effects on delivery time, code quality, cost, and compliance remain hypotheses for future evaluation.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Researching Business Models for Building Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Business models are increasingly recognized as key architectures that may help coordinate technological, organizational, social, and territorial innovations in sustainable agriculture. This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 325 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (2002–2026) to map the epistemic, conceptual, and intellectual structure of research on business models for building sustainable agriculture. Using Price’s, Lotka’s, Bradford’s, and Zipf’s laws, along with co-citation analysis, the study examines temporal growth, author productivity, journal concentration, thematic clusters, and foundational literature. Results suggest exponential growth in scientific production, strong alignment with SDGs related to food security, circular economy, climate action, and biodiversity, and a highly concentrated intellectual core centered on business model design, sustainability transitions, and digital transformation. Four thematic clusters emerge: innovation and agricultural systems; management, governance, and business models; sustainability and climate-energy dynamics; and challenges, assessment, and ecosystem services. Co-citation analysis reveals three major axes shaping the field: strategic business model design, circular and sustainable value creation, and digital and territorial transformation of agri-food systems. Overall, the findings suggest that sustainable agriculture may benefit from hybrid business models integrating technological innovation, circularity, governance, and multi-actor collaboration.

title: Theory of the Process of Vibratory Digging of Carrot Root from the Soil
abstract: Mechanical interaction during carrot harvesting can impair root quality, motivating analysis of the lifting stage before damage assessment. Therefore, an important task is the design and research of working bodies that reduce this negative impact on root crops. The aim of this study is to develop a reduced-order analytical model of the bilateral contact between a carrot root and the two digging shares and to establish the corresponding centre of mass velocity and displacement relations. The closed form solution is an approximation to the retained positive-force branch under the assumed bilateral-contact regime. It identifies the formal influence of the effective harmonic contact force amplitude, oscillation frequency, and forward motion terms on root kinematics. For an illustrative, uncalibrated case at 10 Hz, increasing the effective force amplitude per share from 1 to 3 N increases local lift from 2.93 to 39.43 mm. At 2 N, lift is 20.45 mm, peak vertical velocity is 0.821 m·s−1, and the frozen-angle approximation overestimates endpoint lift by 4.05%. Direct calculations quantify amplitude, frequency and forward speed effects within the retained model. The model is intended for preliminary kinematic analysis and does not predict carrot deformation or damage.

title: AgriSkill-Agent: A Skill-Guided and Knowledge-Enhanced Agent Framework for Leaf Disease Diagnosis and Management
abstract: While visual recognition and multimodal language models have improved leaf disease identification, most systems remain focused on recognition rather than integrated diagnosis and management. Practical support must connect symptoms, lesion extent, evidence-grounded diagnosis, and crop-specific guidance. We present AgriSkill-Agent, a skill-guided and knowledge-enhanced single-agent framework for leaf disease diagnosis and management. A central large language model activates task-specific procedural skills to coordinate visual analysis, external knowledge, and structured reporting. The main contribution is a unified diagnosis-to-management workflow integrating stage-specific skill contracts, deterministic lesion measurement, literature retrieval, and a pesticide-use knowledge graph. Image-derived measurements remain separate from language-model interpretation, while literature and structured pesticide-use knowledge provide traceable support. We evaluated AgriSkill-Agent on 140 image-based cases across 10 crops. The framework achieved higher diagnostic accuracy and produced more complete and better-grounded reports than direct multimodal baselines. Ablation analysis indicated that procedural skills primarily improved workflow compliance and report completeness, whereas external knowledge strengthened management grounding. Overall, AgriSkill-Agent provides a structured and traceable approach for integrating visual evidence, diagnostic reasoning, and agricultural knowledge in AI-assisted crop disease diagnosis and management.

title: Transformer-Based Semantic Segmentation for UAV Imagery: Application to Cyanobacterial Bloom Monitoring in Taihu Lake
abstract: Cyanobacterial blooms in eutrophic lakes pose severe threats to aquatic ecosystem health and drinking water safety. Accurate, timely, and spatially explicit monitoring of cyanobacterial distribution is therefore critical for effective water quality management and risk mitigation. This study proposes a transformer-based semantic segmentation framework—built upon Mask2Former—for automated detection of cyanobacterial blooms in Taihu Lake using high-resolution unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery. To support robust model training and evaluation, we constructed a manually annotated semantic segmentation dataset comprising 942 images acquired from both UAV platforms and fixed shoreline monitoring cameras. The dataset encompasses diverse real-world conditions, including variable bloom densities, heterogeneous lighting environments, and dynamic water surface disturbances (e.g., waves, reflections, and floating debris). The Mask2Former architecture—featuring a Swin Transformer backbone, a multi-scale pixel decoder, and a masked-attention transformer decoder—was trained to perform three-class pixel-wise classification: background, open water, and cyanobacterial bloom. Quantitative evaluation on the independent test set yielded a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 85.63%, a frequency-weighted Intersection over Union (fwIoU) of 86.69%, and a pixel accuracy of 92.09%. For quantitative bloom coverage estimation, the model achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.973, a mean relative error (MRE) of 13.5%, and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.056 (normalized to [0, 1] coverage scale). These results indicate that the framework can provide automated, spatially explicit bloom monitoring for Taihu Lake, supplying quantitative information for water quality assessment, ecological forecasting, and early-warning systems.

title: An Integrated ResNet-WOFOST Framework for UAV-Based Kiwifruit Leaf Area Index Retrieval and Dynamic Growth Assessment
abstract: Leaf area index (LAI) is an important indicator of canopy structure and growth status in kiwifruit. To address the high cost of field LAI measurements, limited deep-learning generalization under small-sample conditions, and the lack of quantitative growth-assessment criteria, UAV multispectral imagery and field-measured LAI data from ‘Xuxiang’ kiwifruit orchards in Mei County, China, were integrated to develop an improved ResNet-based LAI retrieval model with an LAI-constrained Mosaic augmentation strategy. The WOFOST crop growth model was parameter-localized using EFAST sensitivity analysis and field observations to simulate multi-year kiwifruit LAI dynamics. A five-level growth assessment system was then established using LAI anomaly percentage. The LAI retrieval model achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.893, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.604, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.447. The localized WOFOST model reproduced LAI dynamics across key phenological stages, with R2 values of 0.744–0.821. The stage-specific growth assessment system characterized spatial variation in orchard canopy growth status. Overall, integrating UAV multispectral remote sensing, deep learning, and process-based crop modeling provides a quantitative framework for spatiotemporal monitoring and growth-status assessment in kiwifruit orchards.

title: Impact of Well-Facilitated Farmland Construction on Farmers’ Adoption Behavior of Improved Agricultural Machinery
abstract: Well-facilitated farmland construction provides a material foundation for the application of improved agricultural machinery, and the in-depth integration of the two can contribute to a new breakthrough in improving grain yield per unit area. Based on 371 farm household survey samples from Heilongjiang Province, this study employed the Poisson regression model, mediation pathway test model, and moderating effect model to explore the effect of well-facilitated farmland construction on farm households’ adoption behavior of improved agricultural machinery. The main finding shows that well-facilitated farmland construction can significantly promote farm households’ adoption behavior of improved agricultural machinery, and this conclusion remains valid after a series of robustness and endogeneity tests. In terms of the heterogeneous impact of project types on adoption behavior, farmland road construction is the only type that generates a significant positive effect on adoption, while drainage facility construction and shelterbelt construction show significant negative effects; the other five types, including irrigation facility construction, gully erosion control, power facility construction, soil fertility amelioration, and farmland morphology remediation, have no statistically significant impacts. This study preliminarily identifies that the farmers’ organization level serves as a potential mediation pathway through which well-facilitated farmland construction facilitates farmers’ adoption of improved agricultural machinery, and both farmland fragmentation and poor traffic conditions exert significant negative moderating effects. In the future, machinery-oriented differentiated construction should be promoted based on local conditions, the farmers’ organization level should be improved, and targeted measures should be adopted to address farmland endowment constraints; this has the potential to further enhance the policy precision and implementation efficiency of well-facilitated farmland construction.

title: Reference Data Generation for Remote Sensing Image Classification: A Comprehensive Review of Methods, Challenges, and Recent Advances
abstract: Image classification is a fundamental technique that has been broadly adopted in remote sensing, computer vision and related areas. High-quality annotated datasets are necessary for the development and reliable evaluation of classification and segmentation algorithms for accurate thematic mapping. Reference data are critical in this sense, as their quality has a direct impact on the performance, accuracy and generalization of the model. However, generating reliable reference data remains challenging due to methodological, technical, and annotation-related uncertainties. This study reviews the principal challenges in reference data generation, and the solutions proposed in scientific literature. A total of 100 papers indexed in the Web of Science were examined. The review covers traditional reference data generation methods as well as emerging approaches based on semi-supervised, self-supervised, and active learning, segmentation- and post-processing-assisted labeling, benchmark dataset construction, sampling and accuracy assessment, and deep learning and automated label generation. Major challenges and emerging research directions are also discussed. The results indicate a clear shift from traditional manual techniques to more automated, learning based and accuracy driven methods. The study provides a framework of existing techniques and future research areas in image classification.

title: Banking on the soil: Opportunities and obstacles in Financial Inclusion of Farmers in Anantnag, Kashmir
abstract: Financial inclusion is vital for inclusive economic growth, particularly within agricultural regions. This study examines the determinants and barriers of financial inclusion among farmers in District Anantnag, the largest district in the Kashmir Valley of Jammu and Kashmir. Utilizing primary data from a survey of 300 agricultural households across six blocks alongside secondary institutional data, the paper evaluates the adoption of savings accounts, institutional credit, crop insurance, Kisan Credit Cards (KCC), digital payments, and Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT).The findings reveal that while the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) has successfully driven near-universal bank account ownership, meaningful financial inclusion remains low. Key barriers include a deficit of rural banking infrastructure due to scattered, mountainous terrain, low financial literacy (especially among women and elderly farmers), rigid collateral demands, and a persistent reliance on informal lenders (arthiyas). Furthermore, the district's dominant horticulture sector (apple and walnut cultivation) faces severe gaps in tailored credit and insurance products. To bridge these gaps, this study recommends expanding Business Correspondent networks aligned with horticultural credit cycles, launching localized financial literacy campaigns, simplifying KCC renewals, leveraging Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) as credit intermediaries, and deploying digital technology to ensure last-mile connectivity.

title: Burning the Black Dragon, Creating Dongbei: Fire Social Ecological History in Northeastern China, 1945–2005
abstract: Modern China’s understanding of wildfires is primarily applied science aimed at resolving issues related to fire management. Dominant conceptions of fire focus on physical processes and interactions – a physical paradigm. This was not always the case and this historical survey and analysis of fires in northeast China (Dongbei) seeks to unpack a more biological and cultural wildfire paradigm based on key policy evolutions and wildfire events. Northeast China was transformed over the course of the twentieth century from mixed and boreal forest-grassland-wetland interface into one of the major ‘breadbaskets’ of China through migration, infrastructure and agricultural development, and extensive fire use and wildfire outbreaks. China’s understanding of fire, firefighting and fire policy evolved in tandem with this transformation, and increasing experience with major wildfire disasters in the region, leading to a more applied science and professionalised wildfire management approach. Based on historical analysis of settlement and landscape management trends, use of fire in land reclamation, together with evolving wildfire suppression and firefighting administrations in northeastern China, fostered a range of fire policy frameworks – from limited colonial regulation to socialist revolution and collectivisation approaches – and, overall, a total war on wildfire with varying success, through current wildfire management models.

title: Modelling the broken age-[Fe/H] relation and metallicity distribution function of mono-age populations
abstract: This study investigates the chemical evolution history and radial migration in the Milky Way utilizing high-precision age measurements based on large-scale stellar spectroscopic surveys. Recent observational data have revealed a distinct break in the age-metallicity relation of stars in the solar neighborhood, suggesting that stellar populations of the Milky Way can be divided into two evolutionary sequences. Based on galactic chemical evolution models, we confirm that this break in the age-metallicity relation can be explained by a recent major gas accretion event, which diluted the metallicity in the disk and triggered a starburst, leading to the formation of an independent age-metallicity sequence. To assess the impact of stellar radial migration, we incorporate a simplified treatment of this process into our multi-zone chemical evolution model. Radial migration is modeled as a probabilistic diffusion process, characterized by a Gaussian distribution. By fitting the model-predicted metallicity distribution functions (MDFs) of mono-age stellar populations to observations, we infer a migration strength of $σ= 2.15^{+0.100}_{-0.103}\,{\rm kpc}$ for stars with ages between 2 and 6 Gyr located at 9.5-11.5 kpc, corresponding to an average radial displacement of 1.92 kpc over 10 Gyr. This result is lower than previous estimates of stellar radial migration, suggesting that the role of radial migration in shaping the chemical structure of the Milky Way is less important than previously estimated.

title: CHEAR: Confusion-Hierarchy Evidence-Aware Reasoning for Cost-Efficient Human Activity Recognition
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a new approach to wearable-sensor-based human activity recognition. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) further introduces similar motion examples and discriminative sensor knowledge, enabling decisions grounded in observations relevant to the current query. More evidence, however, does not necessarily mean better-organized evidence. When online prompts and LLM agents primarily orchestrate inference, decisions about which activities to compare and when to invoke discriminative knowledge remain concentrated at inference time. As the activity vocabulary grows, the model must repeatedly process more candidates and associated knowledge, whereas pruning candidates too early risks excluding the true activity. We propose confusion-hierarchy evidence-aware reasoning (CHEAR), which moves part of this knowledge organization offline. CHEAR constructs and validates an activity hierarchy from recurrent cross-subject retrieval errors and builds corresponding activity-pair knowledge. At inference time, the hierarchy orders candidate comparisons; the LLM retains candidates progressively, and local discriminative knowledge is accessed only for the remaining activities. Across eight datasets, CHEAR achieves 86.79\% mean cross-subject accuracy, a 75.91\% candidate reduction rate, and 96.44\% true-activity retention. Per-sample token use is 85.15\% lower on average than in a variant without the hierarchical structure. Mean accuracy across eight cross-dataset transfer directions is 88.81\%. These results show that organizing candidates and discriminative knowledge around observed activity confusions reduces online LLM input while maintaining recognition performance.

title: Siam-ALS: An Explainable Siamese Deep Learning Framework for Early ALS Detection Using EEG and Eye-Tracking Signals
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) diagnosis remains challenging due to heterogeneous symptoms and reliance on clinical assessment, underscoring the need for objective, data-driven approaches that leverage patient-generated physiological signals. We propose Siam-ALS, an explainable Siamese deep learning framework that jointly models synchronized electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-tracking (ET) signals. EEG captures ALS-related changes in brain activity, while ET provides information about oculomotor control, allowing the model to learn complementary patterns associated with ALS. The framework employs two modality-specific encoders: a convolutional EEG encoder that captures spatiotemporal neural patterns and an MLP-based ET encoder that models oculomotor dynamics. These modality-specific features are processed through weight-sharing Siamese branches and fused into a compact 64-dimensional joint embedding. A lightweight classifier is used to predict ALS, while pairwise metric learning helps the model learn more effective patterns from the small, diverse ALS datasets. Performance was evaluated on the public EEGET-ALS dataset using strict subject-level cross-validation, where Siam-ALS achieved an accuracy of 0.988 and an AUROC of 0.998, demonstrating strong performance compared with classical machine learning, DL, and non-Siamese fusion approaches. Cross-dataset evaluation on the independent BigP3BCI dataset achieved an AUROC of approximately 0.98, supporting the generalization capability of Siam-ALS across different BCI paradigms. To enhance interpretability, six XAI methods were evaluated in the learned embedding space, with SHAP achieving the highest, though statistically comparable, fidelity in identifying important EEG and ET patterns that contribute to ALS predictions. Overall, Siam-ALS provides an accurate, generalizable, and explainable framework for multimodal ALS detection.

title: LERR-Nav: Learning to Coordinate Exploration, Recovery, and Reminiscing for Object Navigation
abstract: Object Navigation in unseen environments remains a fundamental challenge in embodied AI, as it requires agents to generalize visual and spatial reasoning to novel layouts. While recent advances in large language model (LLM) and vision-language model (VLM) have enhanced semantic mapping, spatial memory, and waypoint selecting for navigation, successful navigation requires more than selecting the next promising waypoint. A robot must also recognize stalled progress, escape unproductive behaviors, and revisit overlooked target cues. Addressing these challenges requires both specialized navigation strategies and a high-level policy that coordinates their execution. Motivated by the analysis of failed navigation episodes, we propose LERR-Nav, an object navigation framework that coordinates exploration, recovery, and reminiscing through a learned high-level policy. The framework comprises four complementary navigation strategies: value-function-guided exploration, LLM-guided exploration, recovery from stalled or repetitive behavior, and memory-guided reminiscing. To support history-aware coordination, we maintain the execution memory that preserves textual summaries of all strategy executions alongside a sliding window of map sequences. To learn the coordination policy, we initialize a high-level vision-language agent from Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and train it through a two-stage curriculum. The first stage uses map-centric supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to establish spatial grounding. The second stage performs SFT on variable-length navigation segments to learn which navigation strategy to invoke next based on current maps and the hybrid execution memory. Experiments on HM3D and MP3D demonstrate state-of-the-art navigation performance, while ablation studies validate the contributions of individual components.

title: A Decade of PhotoMappers: A Longitudinal Study of Crowdsourced Disaster Photos Geolocalization with Vision-Language Models and Geospatial Reasoning
abstract: Crowdsourced disaster imagery provides timely, ground-level observations when conventional disaster mapping is delayed or incomplete, yet its geographic value depends on where observations are produced, how they are interpreted, and whether they can be reliably located as actionable Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT). Using more than a decade of PhotoMappers, a crowdsourced disaster-mapping initiative, this study examines the changing geography of disaster information and asks how emerging GeoAI models compare with human geographic interpretation. We combine longitudinal spatial analysis with cross-view geolocalization using street view imagery (SVI) and remote sensing imagery (RSI), and evaluate vision-language models (VLMs) reasoning through 30 indicators spanning geographic cues and reasoning evidence. The results reveal a geographically and temporally uneven archive shaped by changing disaster types, Community Lifelines, and operational priorities. Integrating VGI, SVI, and RSI with Sinkhorn re-ranking achieves 40.90% R@1, 61.10% R@5, and 69.45% R@10, while yearly R@1 varies markedly from 25.00% to 65.07%. Geographic reasoning is similarly uneven: Qwen3.6-27B achieves an overall agreement of 67% compared with 51% for InternVL3-8B, with both models showing greater difficulty with localized and place-specific evidence than broad spatial configurations. We argue that the value of GeoAI lies less in replacing volunteered geographic interpretation than in complementing it, scaling candidate retrieval while retaining human judgment for ambiguous and consequential cases. This provides a pathway toward more human-centered and responsible GeoAI for disaster mapping. All data and code are openly available at https://github.com/bobleegogogo/PhotoMappers-VLM.

title: OmniRSI: Taming Latent Diffusion for Unified Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Generation
abstract: Multimodal remote sensing image generation emerges as a promising paradigm for recovering complete and complementary observations from heterogeneous and partially observed remote sensing data. However, existing methods predominantly depend on sensor-specific fine-tuning of natural image generation models, limiting unified multimodal generation capacity due to the absence of shared representations and robust conditioning mechanisms. To address these challenges, we propose OmniRSI, a unified multimodal remote sensing image generation model. Specifically, we develop a remote sensing-specific variational autoencoder that captures multimodal priors and promotes a locally smooth latent space for unified representation and robust reconstruction across diverse observed data. Building upon that, we fully adapt Stable Diffusion 3.5 with a ControlNet branch to support unified multimodal generation and translation conditioned on textual and visual cues. Besides, we devise a training-free cyclic latent alignment mechanism that iteratively enriches incomplete visual conditions with generated multimodal information, progressively improving guidance reliability while preserving observed measurements. We also construct RSI-MM, a large-scale dataset comprising 11.5M multi-resolution images with text annotations and partially paired data for training and evaluation. Extensive experiments verify that OmniRSI achieves superior performance in multimodal reconstruction, generation and translation.

title: Verifying Autoware Controller Node by Combining Model Verification and Runtime Monitoring
abstract: Formal modeling and verification of autonomous driving systems remain challenging due to the vast operational space and the complexity of the control logic. We propose a hybrid verification approach that combines formal model verification and runtime monitoring for the trajectory-following control node of Autoware, an open-source autonomous driving platform. We formalize the controller as a hybrid system in differential dynamic logic (dL), and introduce an abstract model that captures the essential control dynamics. We then prove safety and liveness properties of the model using the KeYmaera X proof assistant. Complementarily, we monitor the constraints that assure the compatibility between the model and the Autoware implementation across numerical simulation runs using the Autoware toolchain, quantifying to what extent the implementation's behavior is subsumed by the verified model. The experimental results confirmed that (i) monitoring provides a sound evaluation of target following with accuracy bounds, and (ii) the Autoware implementation reaches the target with an accuracy of approximately 0.2-0.4 (m) in position and 0.8 (m/s) in velocity.

title: When Messages Go Wrong: Understanding Communication Faults in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS) use specialized agents that exchange messages to accomplish complex tasks. Their reliance on networked protocols, remote tools, and model endpoints exposes communication to message loss, delay, and context expiration. Because agents often exchange open-ended natural language, anomalies can alter task-relevant information while leaving messages processable, allowing semantic errors to propagate through subsequent interactions. Systematic studies of faults in inter-agent communication remain limited. This paper presents a large-scale empirical study of how communication faults manifest, propagate, and affect task outcomes in LLM-MAS. We construct a cross-layer taxonomy linking lower-stack disturbances to application-visible faults and develop a fault-injection and tracing pipeline. Our evaluation covers more than 29,000 executions across 100 tasks, five domains, three workflow topologies, and three model configurations. We find that 20.7% of failures with complete detection records occur without an immediate failure signal, reaching 76.2% for partial-content faults. Flat maintains 53.0% task success under communication faults, compared with 3.3% and 3.2% for Sequential and Hierarchical, respectively. This advantage primarily arises when an alternative information path preserves the evidence required by downstream agents. We also evaluate execution-side and evidence protection mechanisms and find that they recover different failure cases. Evidence recovery depends on whether trustworthy information remains accessible through an unaffected path. These observations provide empirical insights into communication-fault propagation, workflow resilience, and protection design for LLM-MAS.

title: Toward Explainability in Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: Multimodal recommender systems effectively alleviate data sparsity and cold-start problems by integrating heterogeneous information, yet complex cross-modal representations and model decision-making processes also introduce new interpretability challenges. Despite the rapid growth of research on the interpretability of multimodal recommendation in recent years, relevant methods and evaluation criteria remain relatively fragmented, lacking a unified conceptual framework. To address this gap, this paper categorizes existing methods into modality explanation and post-hoc explanation based on the timing and manner of explanation generation, and further constructs a progressive system for each category. Building on this foundation, this paper synthesizes four categories of evaluation metrics from both objective quantitative and subjective perceptual perspectives, and reviews relevant datasets along the dimensions of application domain and data source. Through a comprehensive analysis of existing research, we further propose future research directions. This paper aims to establish a unified analytical perspective across multimodal representation, recommendation decision-making, and user preferences, providing a research foundation for building transparent and trustworthy multimodal recommender systems.

title: Revisited Support Vector Machines: A Unified Joint Optimization Framework with Nyström Approximation for Scalable Adaptive Learning
abstract: The theoretical elegance of Support Vector Machines (SVMs), grounded in statistical learning theory, establishes them as a reference for robust classification. However, in the era of Big Data, classical SVMs face two major bottlenecks: the prohibitive cubic complexity $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$ of training and the rigidity of static kernels. Traditional methodologies treat kernel selection as a discrete, "brute-force" GridSearch problem, effectively decoupling the learning of data representation from the optimization of the decision boundary. This paper proposes a paradigm shift with a so-called "Revisited SVM", a unified framework that recasts the learning process as a continuous %bi-level joint optimization problem. We derive a novel objective function $J(α, θ)$ that allows for the simultaneous optimization of dual Lagrange multipliers and kernel hyper-parameters. To solve this challenging non-convex problem efficiently, we introduce a hybrid Block Coordinate Ascent (BCA) algorithm, tightly integrated with Nyström-based low-rank approximation, which drastically reduces computational complexity to $\mathcal{O}(Nm)$. Extensive experiments conducted across four heterogeneous domains (Bioinformatics, Finance, Cybersecurity, and Computer Vision) demonstrate that our approach not only matches but often exceeds exhaustive GridSearch accuracy, while delivering training speedups of up to 100x. Notably, on the complex NSL-KDD intrusion detection dataset, our adaptive kernel approach achieves 96.25\% accuracy compared to a mere 50\% for standard baselines, proving its unique ability to model complex non-linear manifolds in high-dimensional spaces. We validate our results using rigorous statistical tests and provide a theoretical convergence analysis of the proposed algorithm.

title: Identification of effective transport physics and optimal feedback control: Experimental demonstration on a 1600-fan wind generator
abstract: Distributed-input distributed-output (DIDO) systems arise in numerous engineering applications where large numbers of actuators generate spatially distributed physical fields that are monitored by distributed sensors. Developing physically interpretable models that enable real-time optimal control of these systems remains challenging because of the high dimensionality and strong spatial coupling between inputs and outputs. In this work, we propose a physics-based framework for modeling and closed-loop optimal control of DIDO systems from experimental input-output data. First, an effective partial differential equation (PDE) is selected among candidate transport models and discretized on the actuator grid to obtain a minimum-grid representation. Second, the PDE is solved in closed form, which yields an input-output operator with only four physically interpretable parameters. Third, the operator is incorporated into an iterative, constrained quadratic program that accounts for the actuator limits. The framework is demonstrated on the inner 40 x 40 section of the world's highest-resolution Fan Array Wind Generator (FAWG), comprising 1600 independently controlled fans with 36 distributed velocity measurements. The model describes the spatial interaction between the 1600 actuators and the measured velocity field with normalized mean absolute prediction errors of 11-20% for representative actuation patterns. The closed-loop controller reproduces all three prescribed two-dimensional velocity fields with a normalized mean absolute error below 2.3% in fewer than 10 iterations.

title: Stereo-Planner: Learning Stereo-to-Trajectory Planning for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Quadrotor Navigation
abstract: Existing navigation systems commonly rely on dedicated depth sensors or explicit depth reconstruction, while learning to generate trajectories directly from RGB images remains challenging due to the sim-to-real domain gap. In this work, we propose Stereo-Planner, an end-to-end vision-to-trajectory framework that enables zero-shot sim-to-real planning from stereo RGB observations. The key idea is to formulate trajectory generation as state- and scale-conditioned querying of latent stereo geometry. A Scene Representor incorporates a pretrained vision grounding foundation model to extract geometric cues shared across simulated and real-world environments, supporting generalization across visual domains. A lightweight Trajectory Decoder then translates these representations into trajectories through interleaved attention, separating trajectory-state interaction from scene-feature retrieval and incorporating the stereo baseline as a metric-scale cue. With these designs, Stereo-Planner is trained entirely on simulated data by minimizing differentiable trajectory costs and deployed directly in real-world environments without fine-tuning. Benchmark results demonstrate strong cross-scene generalization, with a 95% success rate in simulation environments at a commanded speed of 8 m/s, and competitive performance against depth-based planners using only stereo RGB observations for scene perception. Furthermore, deployment on a compact quadrotor equipped with an NVIDIA Orin NX enables autonomous flight at speeds of up to 7 m/s, with a mean onboard vision-to-action inference time of 24.27 ms. The software, simulation environments, and hardware designs will be open-sourced at https://github.com/Stereo-Planner/Stereo-Planner.

title: Genesis: Visual Augmentation Primitives for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
abstract: Recent multimodal large language models achieve promising results on visual reasoning tasks, approaching human-level performance on existing STEM benchmarks. However, these capabilities degrade under complex real-world scenes. We identify that chain-of-thought reasoning remains largely confined to the linguistic space, rarely anchoring each step in visual evidence. The main cause is the absence of such data during training. In this work, we introduce a training data augmentation pipeline, \textbf{Visual Augmentation Primitives} (VAP), which leverages state-of-the-art vision generative models to synthesize diverse photorealistic training samples and corresponding reasoning text. VAP introduces some basic operators and applies them to a seed image and gets a variant. It also constructs coherent multimodal reasoning chains throughout the generation process. Such training data force models to perceive visual content and perform logical reasoning according to them at every step. We further introduce multimodal chain-of-thought rubric-based reinforcement learning to enhance this. It rewards not only text reasoning but also visual reasoning by scoring intermediate reasoning steps for logical validity, completeness, and consistency. Moreover, we construct the UNREAL benchmark to systematically evaluate visual reasoning on hyperrealistic scenes across controllable difficulty levels. Experiments show that a 4B model built on this framework surpasses 8B baselines, with performance improving consistently as the model scales to 32B, validating the scaling law for visual reasoning.

title: Riemannian Formulation of Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Solvers for Elliptic Problems: Energy-Norm Guarantees and Duct-Flow Applications
abstract: Sample-based quantum linear solvers measure quantum Krylov states $e^{-iAT}|b\rangle$ and reconstruct the solution of $Ax=b$ classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for positive-definite systems that arise from elliptic partial differential equations. We show that the sampling guarantees hold in any fixed basis with an efficient transform. We then replace the variational reconstruction by a Galerkin solve on the sampled set. For this reconstruction we derive expected and high-probability energy-norm error bounds, a sample complexity in terms of the smallest sampling probability on an essential set, a computable residual certificate, and a support-completeness theorem for the dephased outcome law. We formulate the method for elliptic problems on Riemannian cross sections. In two dimensions the stiffness matrix is metric-independent in conformal coordinates, and curved vessels lead to the same matrix class. Killing symmetries of the cross section give selection rules for the measurement outcomes, and the Lie derivative of the metric gives first-order bounds for geometric perturbations. We separate operator approximations, whose effect we bound, from sampler approximations, which affect coverage but not the target. As examples we treat the implicit step of pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts. In simulations of up to 12 qubits, the number of Fourier modes required for 1% error grows from 14 to 60 while the number of unknowns grows from 64 to 4096. A classical residual-greedy selection is nevertheless more efficient than quantum sampling in all cases studied, consistent with the low measured sampling efficiency. On a six-qubit trapped-ion processor, the measured outcome laws follow a replacement-noise model whose strength grows by about 0.6% per two-qubit gate, and a parity selection rule rejects shots at the predicted rate.
