title: An Attention-Guided Graph Neural Network Surrogate for Boundary Integral Computation in Physical Field Reconstruction
abstract: In practical engineering and scientific computing, a real physical system can be reduced to a boundary value problem, and the adequate boundary information to determine the interior spatial distribution and evolutionary state of the physical field can be solved with linear equations, alternatively, the the real physical problem can be treated with boundary problems with in adequate information problems in field of machine learning. This paper proposes a deep learning framework for the recovery of missing boundary information using an attention-guided graph neural network (GNN) surrogate. The framework extracts features from the physical information on the discretized boundary into a latent space, and the missing boundary quantities are then predicted by the network. Thus, the nonlinear mapping from known boundary quantities to missing boundary quantities is learned using a variational autoencoder (VAE) architecture, while an attention mechanism is incorporated to better model the correlations among different types of boundary information. Furthermore, the interior physical field can be reconstructed using the conventional boundary element method (BEM) integral formulation. The effectiveness of the GNN-BEM framework is evaluated using numerical examples of the two-dimensional Laplace and Poisson equations, which demonstrate good performance in reconstruction accuracy, local detail preservation, and model stability. The results show that GNN-BEM provides a feasible computational framework for boundary information recovery and fast interior physical field reconstruction for partial differential equations under complex boundary conditions.

title: Physical Layer Security for Movable Antenna-Aided Mixed-Field ISAC
abstract: Movable antenna (MA) can enhance the physical layer security (PLS) performance of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). However, most existing works assume either near-field (NF) or far-field (FF) propagation models for both communication users (CUs) and targets. This paper considers a more practical scenario where multiple CUs, an eavesdropper (Eve), and multiple targets are in a mixed near- and far-field environment due to the changes in the propagation field caused by antenna position updates in MA with a unified array response and continuous NF/FF weights. To evaluate the PLS performance of MA-aided ISAC in mixed-field environments, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the sum secrecy rate (SSR) of CUs by jointly designing the transmit beamforming and antenna positions at the transmitter. The problem is highly non-convex, so a two-layer algorithm is proposed to iteratively solve the problem using the projected gradient ascent (PGA) method and the Lagrangian dual transform. Since the abrupt switch between the NF and the FF models during antenna movement can cause the objective function to oscillate during iteration, the unified array response is combined with the Barzilai-Borwein step, Armijo line search, and precise projection to ensure that the SSR does not decrease during the iteration and the objective function is differentiable on the Rayleigh boundary. Numerical results show that the MA-ISAC using the mixed-field model achieves almost identical PLS performance to that of using the full NF model in terms of SSR, and both outperform the FF model. Using the mismatched FF model during antenna position updates results in a loss of MA gain, potentially making MA inferior to the FA-based system using the correct model.

title: From Dirac Neutrino Mass to Dark Radiation: An $A_4$-Symmetric FIMP Dark Matter Framework
abstract: We propose a unified $A_4\times Z_2\times U(1)_L$ framework for generating small Dirac neutrino masses and address dark matter through feeble interactions in an extended particle physics model. The model extends the Standard Model with a pair of heavy vector-like neutral $A_4$ fermions $N(N_{L,R})$, two additional flavon fields $η$ and $φ$, among which $η$ being a $Z_2$-odd inert scalar and a dark-sector vector-like fermion field $χ$. We numerically explore the Dirac-sector Yukawa couplings and identify the parameter region that is consistent with the {\tt NuFit 6.1} neutrino oscillation data at the $3σ$ level. The dark matter candidate $χ$, stabilized by the $Z_2$ symmetry, is produced non-thermally through the decay $N_L\rightarrowχ+η$. By solving the Boltzmann equation, we find that the observed relic abundance, $Ω_{\rm DM}h^2\simeq0.12$, can be reproduced for freeze-in couplings of order $λ\sim10^{-5.5}$--$10^{-7.5}$ over the considered dark matter mass range. For the chosen parameter space, we also verify the interaction rate remains below the Hubble expansion rate, confirming $χ$ never reaches thermal equilibrium. Thus, our results demonstrate that the model provides a consistent realization of Dirac neutrino masses and FIMP dark matter within a common symmetry-based setup. The presence of light Dirac RH neutrinos can contribute to the dark radiation and hence the effective degrees of freedom via thermal and non-thermal processes. We further estimate the contribution of the light right-handed neutrinos to \(ΔN_{\rm eff}\), finding a maximum characteristic value of \(ΔN_{\rm eff}\simeq0.14\) in the benchmark parameter region.

title: Aspects of $\mathcal{N}=2$ SUSY gauge theories and applications to Quantum Field Theory and Gravity
abstract: This thesis investigates the application of techniques developed in supersymmetric gauge theories to physical problems in Quantum Field Theory and Gravity, focusing on the Seiberg-Witten (SW) curve and its quantum version. After reviewing the essential concepts of Supersymmetry and the derivation of the SW curve, we explore its applications in both fields. In Quantum Field Theory, we investigate the emergence of Argyres-Douglas theories in the moduli space of supersymmetric models, focusing on extremal correlators. We analyze a conformal model to compute their instanton corrections, finding agreement with predictions from Effective Field Theory, and discuss the implications for analogous observables in Argyres-Douglas theories. In Gravity, we exploit the quantum SW curve and its relation to differential equations describing physical systems. We establish the linear stability of Topological Stars, arising in the fuzzball proposal, under massive charged scalar perturbations. We also investigate charge superradiance in configurations with a horizon and derive a novel hypergeometric representation of the confluent Heun function, relevant to gravitational-wave propagation in the Schwarzschild background. This result yields a new resummed expression for waveform tail contributions, in excellent agreement with numerical data. Finally, beyond the SW formalism, we develop a Machine Learning algorithm based on Hamiltonian Neural Networks to reproduce the geodesics of a neutral particle in a fuzzball geometry. For critical trajectories, our method outperforms standard numerical integrators in both efficiency and accuracy.

title: From Stages to States: Unified Iterative Reasoning for MLLMs
abstract: Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (MCoT) substantially enhances the complex reasoning capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by explicitly modeling intermediate reasoning processes. However, most learning-based MCoT methods follow a stage-centric paradigm, where different reasoning behaviors are assigned to predefined stages and optimized separately. This results in fragmented reasoning and a training-inference reasoning-state gap. To address these limitations, we propose ReState, a unified iterative reasoning framework that reformulates multimodal reasoning from a stage-driven pipeline into a state-driven dynamic process. It comprises two complementary components: Unified Reasoning State Modeling (URSM) and Closed-Loop Reasoning-State Learning (CRSL). URSM unifies reasoning construction, correct reasoning preservation, and erroneous reasoning correction as reasoning-state transitions within a shared state space, enabling these heterogeneous reasoning behaviors to be learned jointly. CRSL further incorporates self-generated historical reasoning states during training and recursively updates the current state during inference, thereby mitigating the reasoning-state gap and enabling iterative self-refinement without requiring an additional reflection module, critic, or independent correction stage. Furthermore, we construct VersaCoT-10K, a high-quality CoT dataset spanning eight visual reasoning domains, which provides diverse supervision for multi-domain reasoning and reasoning-state refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ReState exhibits strong adaptability across different MLLM backbones and achieves strong performance on multiple public reasoning benchmarks, supporting the shift from stage-centric reasoning toward state-centric reasoning. Our data and code are available at https://github.com/YuChuang1205/ReState

title: Imitation Learning via Discrete and Rhythmic Primitive Composition
abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation is inherently composed of semantically meaningful sub-tasks. While Movement Primitives (MPs) can model these components, their composition typically relies on manual engineering or sample-inefficient reinforcement learning. Existing supervised methods are limited by the lack of MP labels in standard datasets and often fail to generalize across discrete and rhythmic movements. We propose Neural Dynamic Composition (NDC), a supervised framework to compose Dynamic Movement Primitives (DMPs) using only raw trajectories for supervision, given a single example of each primitive. Our approach exploits parallel combinations of DMPs as a differentiable relaxation of categorical primitive selection, and utilizes a warp-invariant loss formulation to identify primitives despite spatial or temporal variations. A staged training curriculum is employed to learn the selection policy and DMP parameters, unifying discrete and rhythmic movements in one framework. Evaluated on 2D handwriting and 3D robotic tasks, our method outperforms baselines on most tasks and metrics. An ablation study demonstrates how each design choice contributes to the system's performance.

title: Broadband 600- and 1200-GHz Subharmonically Pumped Schottky Diode Mixers
abstract: A subharmonic mixer topology is introduced that uses quarter-wave stubs to create virtual RF/LO grounds and provide impedance matching in close proximity to the antiparallel Schottky barrier diode pair, thereby reducing the electrical length and enabling broadband operation. The RF/LO matching topology is demonstrated at 600 GHz and 1200 GHz, with good agreement between measured and simulated performance. The 600-GHz mixer demonstrates approximately 20% RF bandwidth with a DSB receiver noise temperature below 1300 K across most of the measured band, while the 1200-GHz implementation achieves DSB receiver noise temperatures below 3000 K over a broad frequency range. Both mixers are characterized at room temperature with approximately 2 mW of LO power. The 600-GHz mixer is used in the Submillimeter Wave Instrument (SWI) onboard ESA's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer. Overall, these results demonstrate state-of-the-art room-temperature performance for broadband receiver front ends targeting atmospheric research and remote-sensing applications.

title: RSAJEV: Training-Free Abstaining Prototype Memory for Eliminating Silent Hallucination in JEV-Based Remote Sensing Classification
abstract: Scene classification of remote sensing imagery with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is formulated as a single-forward-pass decision problem: candidate class names are lettered options in the prompt, a registered answer slot is conditioned on the prompt, and classification is read out by scoring letter tokens with the language-modeling head. We show that although this letter binding is highly effective within its training vocabulary (97.71% OA on UCM), it behaves erratically out of vocabulary: zero-adaptation accuracy across four cross-dataset directions fluctuates between 7.35% and 96.40%, and under out-of-vocabulary weights its confidence fails inversely on open-set evaluation, assigning higher confidence to unseen than to seen classes (AUROC 0.38), a failure we term silent hallucination. We retain the slot representation and replace the readout with RSAJEV, a training-free abstaining prototype memory that performs retrieval-based prototype matching: K reference images per class are cached as prototypes via their slot representations under the same prompt, and classification becomes nearest-neighbor retrieval over the prototypes, refined by a shrinkage-Mahalanobis geometric correction. This readout is mechanistically isomorphic to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) but operates on discriminative decisions; it is the first retrieval-based readout for MLLM slot representations. The retrieval readout reaches 89.43% on the UCM cross-dataset gate with 16 references per class and zero gradient updates, and 96.90% on AID. Its ID-ness scores attain 0.91-0.99 AUROC on open-set evaluation over two datasets, exceeding symbolic confidence (0.38-0.96) in all four open-set settings, restoring a calibratable abstention channel and supporting class addition/removal at zero extra inference cost via offline rescoring of the cached matrix.

title: Google Earth AI Geospatial Reasoning Agent: Capabilities and a Systematic Evaluation
abstract: Google Earth AI is a family of geospatial AI models, together with an agent that orchestrates them. We present this agent, Google Earth AI's Geospatial Reasoning agent (GRA), a Gemini-powered research system that combines geospatial data sources, foundation models, and tools to answer questions about our planet. GRA organizes these into modular domain skills and pairs them with upfront geospatial planning to decompose complex queries into multi-stage workflows. Evaluating such systems is hard: real-world problems admit multiple valid workflows, require data discovery across large catalogs, and rely on evolving ground truth. We introduce two benchmarks and release their development splits. GeoExpertQueries poses complex analytical problems grounded in practitioner use cases and refined by geospatial experts; each is paired with a consensus golden workflow from three independent experts and scored by a human-validated, tool-agnostic autorater. GeoKTools consists of templated queries with deterministic reference solvers that systematically vary the number of required tool types. We also use two external benchmarks, CBGB and UnivEARTH; the latter we find to be saturated. To isolate the contribution of GRA's tools and its agentic orchestration, we compare four configurations, each with Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3.8 Flash: a standalone LLM, the LLM with basic tools, the LLM with GRA's skills and tools but without its upfront planning and execution guidance, and GRA itself. With at most basic tools, an advanced model recovers much of the answer on templated queries but satisfies only a small fraction of the expert workflows on open-ended problems; GRA performs well on both. The largest step comes from GRA's skills and tools; on open-ended problems, its planning and execution guidance add a further gain with Gemini 3.8 Flash, letting Flash match or exceed Pro at lower cost.

title: RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution
abstract: Recent focus in agentic reinforcement learning (RL) seeks to improve credit assignment in long-horizon tasks. One promising direction combines reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), integrating trajectory-level advantages with dense token-level supervision. This line of work often conditions a teacher model on privileged context, such as agentic skills, to score tokens generated by the student policy. Despite their progress, they largely overlook the on-policy evolution of agentic skills and the reliability of teacher supervision. Towards this end, we introduce Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization (RSIPO), a self-evolving agentic RL framework that enables agentic skills and the policy model to co-evolve throughout the training process. Specifically, RSIPO enables the policy itself to extract skills from completed trajectories and explicitly optimizes its skill-generation capability through trajectory replay. It further employs empirical Bayes shrinkage to dynamically calibrate the student's trust in teacher scores, accounting for the fact that skill-enhanced teacher guidance can sometimes be less reliable. Experiments with Qwen-family models on embodied interaction and search-based agentic tasks demonstrate that RSIPO outperforms all the compared baseline approaches. With Qwen2.5-7B as the base model, RSIPO achieves an average success rate of 98.6\% on ALFWorld, yielding absolute improvements of 2.5\% and 17.4\% over the second-best baseline and standard GRPO, respectively.

title: FlowGRPO for Vocal Separation: From Reward Analysis to Reward Design
abstract: The Flow Matching objective supervises the velocity field at intermediate states, whereas waveform metrics are evaluated after decoding and may be non-differentiable. To align Flow Matching models with waveform-level and perceptual quality objectives during post-training, FlowGRPO optimizes their trajectories using endpoint rewards. In this work, we focus on music separation and use multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform (MRSTFT), scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio (SI-SDR), and Virtual Speech Quality Objective Listener (ViSQOL) as reward components. Before policy optimization, we analyze the relationship between data quality factors and the within-group gap between the maximum and mean rollout rewards for each component. This analysis motivates a revised ViSQOL reward that matches channel-wise root-mean-square (RMS) levels and evaluates the interval from the first to the last active frame, retaining inactive frames within that interval. We also apply a sample-quality filter based on predefined waveform checks. Together, the revised reward and quality filter enable FlowGRPO to improve the pretrained vocal separator in both separation performance and perceptual quality.

title: Heterogeneous Structured Pruning Under Resource Constraints for Hardware-Efficient Large Language Models
abstract: Training-free pruning removes weights from pretrained large language models to reduce their deployment cost. However, existing approaches typically consider only the total number of retained weights. Consequently, their pruning decisions do not account for how target hardware stores and processes those weights. These methods select a sparsity structure in advance and apply it uniformly to all projections, rather than accounting for how each structure trades pruning error against latency and memory across sublayers. We propose Heterogeneous Structured Pruning (HSP), a hardware-aware pruning framework that combines two components: (i) a heterogeneous search space of dense, unstructured, 2:4, block-sparse, and head / channel (H/C) pruning options and (ii) structure-regularising constraints based on latency and memory models. Our contribution generalises existing importance-based methods: a global solver selects one option per sublayer to minimise proxy pruning loss under a resource budget, thereby assigning each projection a structure and density. We evaluate HSP on OPT and LLaMA models for an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super edge device, where it improves the quality-resource frontiers over training-free baselines. A project page and updated links for the related code is maintained at: cameronbarker.me/publications/hsp.

title: A Robust Numerical Framework for Multi-Strain Epidemics
abstract: Epidemiological models often take the form of systems of differential equations of varying levels of complexity. In multi-strain models, complexity arises from the interaction of diverse pathogen types that may exhibit different patterns of cross-immunity due to the host's immune system. Where previous work has tended to focus on theoretical analysis of this complexity, or model simplification, less effort has been given to efficient numerical exploration of full multi-strain disease dynamics. Here, we propose a computational framework for representing multi-strain disease transmission models, through a mathematically transparent hard-coded mapping between sets and integers. By mapping infection histories into Boolean matrices, the framework eliminates explicit iteration over strain combinations while preserving key biological processes, including sequential infection and partial cross-immunity. Benchmark comparisons of numerical solutions of our matrix formulation and a set-indexed implementation demonstrate substantial performance gains. Across models with increasing numbers of strains, the matrix formulation consistently reduces runtime, with a speedup exceeding two orders of magnitude for systems with 11 strains. We present an application of this approach to the case of COVID-19 in Indonesia, focusing on the replacement of the Delta variant by Omicron. We hope that our approach represents a robust computational approach to automatically generate diverse multi-strain epidemic models that can be solved in a computationally efficient manner for a variety of scientific and public-health questions.

title: High-Fidelity Song Generation with Joint Discrete and Continuous Modeling
abstract: Generating a full song from lyrics and a style description requires long-range musical planning without sacrificing vocal and instrumental detail. Low-rate discrete semantic tokens make this tractable, but quantization constrains the information available to acoustic rendering, while separately optimized stages prevent downstream generation objectives from shaping the planner. We propose joint discrete and continuous modeling for high-fidelity song generation. A VQ tokenizer supplies tokens for autoregressive planning, and a separately trained SSL-derived variational encoder supplies continuous semantic targets. Conditioned on the completed token plan and differentiable readouts of the planner's predictive states, a full-sequence flow model generates semantic features for acoustic rendering. Its flow-matching gradients reach the language model through the readouts, without differentiating through token sampling; the standard pathway keeps continuous features out of autoregressive feedback. On 192 shared prompts, its 48D configuration improves SongEval from 4.152 to 4.269 and reduces micro-PER from 20.26% to 14.47% relative to a discrete baseline, while receiving substantially higher expert listening scores. We further analyze the system through downstream semantic probes and conditioned reconstruction.

title: Grounding Deep Learning Framework Testing in Data Flow
abstract: Data flow underlies deep learning (DL) framework execution, including automatic differentiation and operator-fusion optimization. Bugs involving data flow can cause incorrect results or unexpected behavior. Existing testing methods represent models primarily by operator topology, omitting runtime tensor values and properties and operator input requirements. They therefore cannot distinguish data flows in models with similar topologies, even when these differences affect framework behavior. We introduce the Tensor Flow Graph (TFG) to capture runtime tensor states and operator input requirements. Its nodes represent operators and their input requirements, while its edges record tensor values and properties. Building on the TFG, we propose FlowMuT, a mutation-based testing method grounded in data flow. Mutations are represented as constrained subgraph replacements, with mutation operators derived from prior work and an analysis of mutable data flow objects. In each round, FlowMuT builds a TFG for the seed model, pairs mutation operators with TFG sites, and filters illegal candidates using data flow constraints. It uses LinUCB to select a candidate based on coverage and impact, executes the mutant, updates selection feedback, and uses each accepted mutant as the next seed. We evaluate FlowMuT on PyTorch and MindSpore using representative models from diverse application scenarios. FlowMuT submitted 55 bug reports for cases missed by all baseline methods; developers confirmed 41 reports and fixed the bugs described in 7 reports. FlowMuT achieves 43.4% higher data flow diversity than the strongest baseline and a legal mutant rate of 96.7%, compared with 86.4% without constraints. These results show that testing from a data flow perspective is practical and effective.

title: Occultation polarimetry as a probe of unresolved polarization
abstract: Context: Low polarization in an unresolved source may reflect weak local polarization or spatial cancellation between strongly polarized regions. An occultation can break this spatial degeneracy by differentially sampling the source as the occulting boundary moves. Aims: We develop a general theoretical framework for occultation polarimetry and determine what information can be inferred directly from unresolved full Stokes light curves, without reconstructing a polarization image or prescribing a source model. Methods: For a stationary, spatially incoherent source undergoing monotonic occultation, we relate Stokes variations to the polarization sampled by an arbitrarily curved occulting boundary and derive an exact variance decomposition of the normalized Stokes vector. Results: The polarization deficit decomposes exactly into three non-negative contributions: local polarization deficit, mixing within limb samples, and mixing between their mean polarization states. The last is directly measurable and provides a sharp, model-independent lower bound on total spatial mixing. The associated covariance tensor further characterizes the direction and correlations of the resolved polarization variations, including those between linear and circular polarization. Finite sampling preserves the bound, which can be strengthened through complementary occultation trajectories. Conclusions: Occultation polarimetry provides a powerful observational technique for extracting quantitative, model independent constraints on spatial polarization mixing directly from unresolved Stokes light curves. It offers a means to reveal both the extent and the form of polarization structure otherwise inaccessible at the available angular resolution.

title: ChangeT$^3$: Evaluating Vision Test-Time Training for Remote Sensing Change Detection
abstract: Bitemporal remote sensing change detection requires representations that preserve spatial detail while capturing contextual information relevant to changes between acquisitions. Visual test-time training offers an alternative to explicit token-to-token attention by adapting a compact inner model to each image. This letter describes ChangeT$^3$, a vanilla Siamese configuration combining the existing hierarchical ViT$^3$-Tiny encoder with the multiscale ChangeFormer decoder. The two image streams share learned encoder parameters, while their fast weights are computed independently from their respective spatial features. Each encoder block retains the inherited global simplified SwiGLU and local adaptive depthwise-convolution branches. Temporal comparison is performed by the decoder through learned fusion of paired features at four resolutions, followed by coarse-to-fine aggregation and binary prediction. This separation provides a direct setting for examining image-conditioned inner updates without introducing an additional temporal interaction module. Trained from scratch on LEVIR-CD+ with the same decoder, recipe, and budget as a ChangeFormer control, ChangeT$^3$ reaches an F1 of 80.61$\pm$0.90 against 78.84$\pm$0.21 for ChangeFormer (three seeds each); as in the standard protocol for this dataset, checkpoints are selected on the test split. Trained with both inner updates disabled, the same encoder reaches 78.63$\pm$0.20. Neither model transfers zero-shot to SYSU-CD, DSIFN-CD, or WHU-CD, and ChangeT$^3$ is the slower of the two at small inputs despite similar parameter and operation counts.

title: Attention Sinks in VLMs Are Borrowed, Not Seen
abstract: We study how to detect and mitigate visual attention sinks in vision-language models (VLMs). Visual attention sinks are image tokens that absorb a large share of attention over the image regardless of the query or task, and they mislead methods that treat attention maps as a record of where the model ``looked.'' Prior work has detected sinks through massive activation dimensions and proposed redistributing their attention, but none have addressed what makes a token become a sink. Comparing six candidate detectors on ten VLMs from four families, we find that only the centered cosine similarity between an image token's key and the key of the language model's text-sink detects visual sinks. Thus, a visual sink is an image token whose key aligns with the text-sink's key. Moving a sink's key component along this direction to the median of the image keys sends its attention back to the text-sink (\textbf{Are Borrowed}) while leaving model answers unchanged~(\textbf{Not Seen}). Building on this, we propose a training-free, entropy-triggered re-look that first cleans the attention map, then crops the most-attended region of the cleaned map and inserts it into the reasoning trace. Cleaning adds negligible computation to the forward pass, and the re-look improves accuracy with a mean gain of $+4.3$ points on fine-detail VQA benchmarks across model families.

title: A Hybrid Gaussian Process-Extreme Gradient Boosting Machine Learning Framework for Robust Knockdown Factor Prediction and Reliability-Based Design of Thin Spherical Shell Caps
abstract: Elastic buckling remains a critical concern in the design of deep spherical shell caps, given that experiments reveal a significant reduction of critical loads from those predicted by linearized eigen-buckling analysis. This discrepancy has been attributed to initial geometric imperfections and is often reconciled through a dimensionless parameter, namely the knockdown factor (KDF). However, conventional KDFs (NASA SP-8007; Eurocode 3) are highly conservative, as they represent the lower bound of an extensive body of experimental data. This study aims to narrow the conservatism in the KDFs for spherical shell caps through machine learning (ML) regression models trained on experimental data on spherical shell buckling. A hybrid model is proposed by combining Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and its improved performance is demonstrated over conventional ML algorithms, i.e., the Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), Random Forest Regressor (RFR), and Histogram-based Gradient Boosting (HGBoost). Each of these models uses six input features and a single output, i.e., the KDF. The most critical feature affecting the KDF is ascertained through a sensitivity analysis. The study concludes with a reliability-based design framework that relies on the predictive ML model to obtain safety-consistent, yet less conservative, KDFs.

title: Assessing the impact of background subtraction on a dust-free corona
abstract: Context. White-light observations of the solar corona contain contributions from both the electron-scattered K-corona and the dust-scattered F-corona. Because the diffuse F-corona dominates the measured intensity at altitudes of approximately 4 $R_{\odot}$ and above, background subtraction techniques are routinely employed to isolate the electron corona in coronagraph observations. Aims. Since no direct observational "ground truth" for the K-corona exists, the amount of coronal signal that is inadvertently removed by background subtraction methods remains unknown. We aim to quantify, for the first time, the impact of background subtraction on the inferred large-scale structure and brightness of the solar corona. Methods. We use a 32-day simulation based on a novel near-real-time, data-assimilative, time-evolving magnetohydrodynamic model to generate synthetic white-light observables. Because these synthetic observations are free from dust and instrumental stray-light contributions, they provide direct access to the "true" K-corona and enable a quantitative assessment of the effects of background subtraction. Results. We find that background subtraction generally preserves the large-scale morphology of the electron corona, including the locations and shapes of major coronal structures. However, the procedure systematically modifies the relative brightness of different features and removes a non-negligible fraction of the K-coronal signal. Conclusions. Although standard background subtraction techniques successfully recover the overall appearance of the electron corona, they can alter its quantitative photometric properties. These findings should be considered when interpreting coronal brightness measurements and deriving physical properties from processed white-light observations.

title: Social Learning of Ranking: Getting the Top Right despite Local Herding
abstract: In sequential learning, a group of agents sequentially receives a noisy private signal and observes the predictions of prior agents to estimate a hidden ground truth. While extensively studied for binary signals, we formalize and analyze sequential learning when the hidden ground truth is an ordering of $n$ items, and both private signals and inferences involve pairwise comparisons. A key focus in sequential learning is herding, where agents disregard their private signals to follow the crowd. We show that, while local herding in our model may lead agents to make incorrect pairwise inferences, the global hidden order can still be approximated. Specifically, by aggregating all pairwise comparison outputs, the highest-ranked items can be retrieved. We investigate top-$k$ retrieval across three scenarios: (1) passive aggregation, where information is gathered from the social learning process without intervention; (2) strategic selection, where agents choose their pairwise comparisons dynamically; and (3) aggregation with stubborn nodes, where a very small set of stubborn agents, who base their inferences solely on their private signals, join the mechanism. With query complexity as the number of agents needed for a high-probability estimation, we propose top-$k$ retrieval algorithms with query complexities sublinear in $O(n^2)$, the total number of pairs.

title: Mesh-Free Convolution: Learned Spectral Attenuation and Transport
abstract: Learning solution operators for partial differential equations (PDEs) requires models that can represent spatial structure across grids and scales. This becomes especially important in time-dependent problems, where the learned operator is often used autoregressively: each predicted state is fed back as input to predict future states. In this setting, small spatial errors can be repeatedly propagated through the learned dynamics, leading to instability and drift, vitiating long-term solution fidelity. We propose Mesh-Free Convolutions (MFCs), filters defined in continuous space and discretized only at evaluation time. This allows the same learned filters to be applied across resolutions. Rather than imposing a grid-dependent stencil or a fixed spectral cutoff, MFCs learn smooth scale-dependent filtering and include directional terms for transport-like behavior. Across fluid-dynamics and weather-forecasting benchmarks, MFC-based models produce stable long-horizon rollouts, transfer reliably across resolutions, and better preserve long-time statistics. These results suggest that continuous, mesh-free filtering is a useful inductive bias for PDE operator learning, especially in autoregressive prediction.

title: Natural Language Processing for Aligning Readings with Learning Objectives and Assessing Topic Balance in Dental Education
abstract: Curriculum teams often lack time to check whether assigned readings support learning objectives (LOs) and whether topic coverage is balanced. We present a natural language processing (NLP) workflow to support evidence-informed curation of reading lists. The workflow combines PubMedBERT sentence embeddings and cosine similarity for retrieval, natural language inference (NLI) for evidence checking, and topic modeling for coverage analysis. We tested the approach in dental education using 13 course-level LOs and a PubMed-derived corpus of 3,837 LO-abstract pairs. Median cosine similarity ranged from 0.86 to 0.91 across the 13 LOs, showing generally high semantic similarity. Topic modeling showed broad but uneven coverage, with one or two dominant topics per domain. Similarity alone was not enough for selecting readings: among high-similarity pairs (cosine 0.90-1.00), 22.9% were classified by NLI as neutral or contradictory. In a 49-pair expert-labeled validation set, cosine-based retrieval (cosine >= 0.90) achieved 0.69 accuracy, while the combined cosine and NLI approach achieved 0.73 accuracy against expert alignment labels. Overall, the workflow shows how AI can support curriculum alignment by reducing false positives and helping select readings that better match intended LOs.

title: Distributed Observation Scheduling and Sensor Fusion For Large Agile Constellations
abstract: With the rapid increase in interest towards large scale earth observing satellite constellations, the problem of properly commanding and utilizing these systems has become increasingly relevant. This work focuses on a complete distributed approach to this problem, incorporating an observation task allocation and scheduling algorithm in addition to a sensor data fusion algorithm for end-to-end target coverage and processing. Observation task allocation and scheduling is performed in this work through the combination of the bid warped consensus based bundle algorithm (BWCBBA) and a lightweight observation scheduler for bid scoring. This method produces a unique mapping of tasks to command agents when allowed to iterate sufficiently. The approach to distributed data fusion in this work occurs primarily through an ownership model in which one satellite takes ownership of a system track in the constellation. After local information is shared between the sensing nodes to create the system tracks, the dedicated fusion nodes assume ownership for further information fusion and track information is disseminated throughout the constellation for data association. This paper analyzes the performance of these two algorithms over a set of increasingly decentralized architectures to highlight the performance losses compared to more traditional centralized methods.

title: Small but Mighty: Test Suites as Improvement Signals for Self-Evolving Agents
abstract: A self-evolving agent rewrites its own harness and must decide which rewrites to keep, so its improvement signal is the check a rewrite has to pass. Verifying a rewrite by agent rollout is expensive and subjective, while executable checks such as the repository's own tests are too sparse to catch behavior-changing rewrites, rejecting only a quarter of them. We instead take test feedback as the executable signal, and search for test suites that are both small and strong with a quality-diversity evolutionary algorithm, so that the signal is dense and informative. TeSearch treats suite size as a behavior descriptor, so that quality is pursued at every size and a small, strong suite is reachable, and learns a transition kernel during the search that denoises the LLM as an actuator on that descriptor. Across 129 real-world modules and three backbones, TeSearch delivers the highest-quality suites of any method compared, LLM-driven evolutionary search included, and the smallest of any LLM-based one. Used as the improvement signal of a self-evolving agent, it rejects 59.9% of behavior-changing rewrites against 25.3% for the repository's tests, at a 4.0% false-alarm rate and 3.5 s per decision. The code and data are available at https://github.com/ccsnow127/TeSearch.

title: A Hardware-Partitioned micro-ROS Mini-Vehicle for Operator-Supervised Neural Driving
abstract: We present a low-cost miniature Ackermann vehicle for embedded neural-driving research, organized as a hardware-partitioned perceive-decide-act agent: an ESP32 camera node streams frames over Wi-Fi to a host computer, where neural inference and state estimation run, while an ESP32-S3 chassis controller executes safety-critical actuation in a 100 Hz per-wheel proportional-integral-derivative (PID) loop beneath a micro-ROS client. The partition isolates real-time control and safety on the vehicle while learning-based components run off-board, supervised by an operator from a gamepad. We characterize the complete pipeline during real closed-loop neural driving. Wireless sensing, rather than neural inference, dominates latency, with a 59.5 ms median capture-to-actuation delay; the platform absorbed wireless variability by holding the last safe command under a firmware watchdog, operating across twelve autonomous sessions with zero collisions or manual interventions; and encoder-inertial-measurement-unit (IMU) fusion cut odometry loop-closure error by 22%. These results indicate that carefully partitioned microcontroller-class vehicles support reproducible experiments in embedded AI, wireless control, and operator-supervised autonomous driving. The platform software is open source.

title: Requested, Executed and Recoverable Credit: Shared Action Ordering among LLM Borrowers in a Simulated Lending Market
abstract: AI agents built on different language models can still share the software that presents their choices. We study one shared component, the order in which a borrowing agent's actions are listed, in a simulated collateralized lending market populated by three open-weight model families. In fixed decision states, moving the borrowing action from last to first raises valid borrowing requests by 27 percentage points. In 12 matched pairs of 15-agent markets, all agents in one market see the same order; the other spreads the six possible orders across agents. A common order moves whole markets: the four markets that listed borrowing first raised net debt by 1.8 to 2.7 times their initial unused borrowing capacity, while those that listed debt reduction first cut debt. These groups account for 96 percent of the sample variation among common markets, whose standard deviation is three times the balanced one. The borrowing cap stops 40 percent of valid borrowing requests made when borrowing is listed first, but it values collateral at the pool price, so correlated purchases raise borrowing capacity and leave positions above 70 percent of reference value. Under a 30 percent shock, an 8 percent liquidation bonus produces write-offs on loans that are fully collateralized before liquidation, and liquidation triggers that read the pool price add exposure. Common ordering does not put more borrowers into the write-off zone; it concentrates them in the markets whose shared order favored borrowing. Collateral valuation and liquidation rules determine how much of it creditors fail to recover.

title: Geo-vision: Native-Resolution Geometry and Sampled Topology for Vehicle-Part Damage Classification
abstract: Geo-vision classifies vehicle-part damage using a fixed representation combining appearance, multiscale geometry, orientation, and sampled digital topology. Connected components, holes, Euler characteristics, and spatial arrangement complement amplitude-sensitive pooling and a supervised tree classifier. We establish amplitude preservation, axial sign invariance, and conditional operator stability. Retrospective checkpoint evaluation on 55,303 crops from 4,916 source groups yields average precision 0.7577, exceeding 0.7458 for an ImageNet-pretrained frozen YOLO11n comparator on identical crops. The complete added structural block, comprising topology, occupancy, and component location, improves average precision by 0.00493 beyond appearance and geometry. Geo-vision uses no external encoder pretraining and has higher AP point estimates at every matched label budget. With approximately 25% fewer task labels, its AP point estimate exceeds full-data YOLO, although the adjusted interval includes zero. Complete serial CPU inference requires 26.98 ms per crop versus YOLO's 11.20 ms, with peak memory 185 versus 437 MiB. Independent external validation remains necessary.

title: Reliability diagnostics for learned input-to-parameter relationships in differentiable hybrid models: RELIP v1.0 with a large-sample hydrologic evaluation
abstract: Predictive performance remains the usual basis for assessing geoscientific models, but neural-parameterized mechanistic models expose another object that may be interpreted: the learned mapping from inputs to parameters. RELIP v1.0 evaluates whether that mapping is reproducible. It proceeds through four linked levels: predictive adequacy, stability across random seeds and loss functions, consistency of dominant controls across parameter-learning formulations, and compactness of the full relationship matrix. We apply RELIP to differentiable HBV parameter learning for 531 CAMELS-US catchments, comparing deterministic, Monte Carlo dropout, and distributional formulations under three losses and five seeds. The three formulations produced closely comparable streamflow skill, so predictive metrics alone offered little basis for choosing among them. RELIP distinguished them at the level of relationship structure. The distributional formulation had lower cross-seed variability in Spearman correlations, more reproducible dominant controls, and the most compact relationship matrix. Seven of fourteen mechanistic parameters formed a shared dominant-control core. Parameter spread also contained structured information, although several gradients were coupled to parameter means or boundary proximity. These results identify learned parameterization structure as a separate target of model assessment and provide a practical diagnostic for formulations that appear similar in prediction.

title: Hybrid CNN-LSTM Techniques for Plant Leaf Disease Detection and Farmer-Based Agricultural Practice Analysis in Western Tamil Nadu
abstract: Plant diseases greatly affect crop productivity and agricultural sustainability, making early and accurate disease detection essential. This study investigates hybrid deep learning techniques for plant leaf disease detection and classification, focusing on combining Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory networks. A review of existing studies revealed that the CNN-LSTM hybrid model achieved over 98% accuracy, outperforming several other hybrid approaches. In addition, a survey of 140 farmers from the western districts of Tamil Nadu analyzed farming practices, disease identification methods, and management techniques. The findings indicate that younger farmers are gradually adopting modern agricultural technologies, while older farmers continue to rely on traditional practices. The study highlights the effectiveness of CNN-LSTM models for smart agriculture and emphasizes the importance of farmer awareness and technology adoption for sustainable crop management.
journal: ASEAN Journal of Scientific and Technological Reports

title: Implementasi Konsep Ekonomi Kreatif Pada UMKM Kuliner Tradisional Ubi Bakar Madu Jangkat
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis penerapan konsep ekonomi kreatif pada UMKM kuliner tradisional melalui studi kasus pada usaha Ubi Bakar Madu. Menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan pendekatan studi kasus, penelitian ini menelusuri faktor non-finansial seperti kreativitas, inovasi produk, strategi pemasaran berbasis budaya, dan pelestarian nilai tradisional sebagai elemen utama keberlanjutan usaha. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis dengan model Miles dan Huberman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Ubi Bakar Madu berhasil mengimplementasikan konsep ekonomi kreatif melalui inovasi produk berbahan lokal, promosi yang menonjolkan nilai budaya, serta upaya menjaga proses produksi tradisional. Kreativitas, reputasi merek, dan nilai budaya menjadi modal utama yang mendorong ketahanan dan daya saing usaha tanpa ketergantungan besar pada modal finansial. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa sinergi antara inovasi, budaya, dan kreativitas merupakan kunci keberlanjutan UMKM kuliner tradisional di era ekonomi kreatif. This study aims to analyze the application of the creative economy concept to traditional culinary MSMEs through a case study of the Honey Baked Sweet Potato business. Using a qualitative method with a case study approach, this study explores non-financial factors such as creativity, product innovation, culture-based marketing strategies, and the preservation of traditional values as key elements of business sustainability. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, then analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model. The results show that Honey Baked Sweet Potato successfully implemented the creative economy concept through product innovation using local ingredients, promotions that emphasize cultural values, and efforts to maintain traditional production processes. Creativity, brand reputation, and cultural values are the main assets that drive business resilience and competitiveness without heavy dependence on financial capital. This study concludes that the synergy between innovation, culture, and creativity is the key to the sustainability of traditional culinary MSMEs in the creative economy era.

title: Autonomous AI agents discover reverse transcriptases with tandem repeat arrays
abstract: Metagenomic databases hold vast quantities of unexplored genetic material that can seed tools for biotechnology and medicine, but discovery is limited by our ability to examine sequence data at scale. Here, we show that large language models (LLMs) in an autonomous harness can alleviate this bottleneck and surface novel molecular systems. We deployed Claude Code instances to survey reverse transcriptase (RT) loci across 1.9 billion protein clusters. Among the top candidates were array-associated RTs (ART), a novel family of jumbo-phage RTs coupled with an array of ~200-nucleotide units and a dedicated partner gene. Session transcripts show that Claude identified the ART family by directly examining its DNA sequences and recognizing the atypical repeats, a behavior attributable to specific Mythos 5 internal signals that respond to repeated DNA. ART arrays are highly expressed and appear as discrete units during Staphylococcus phage infection, suggesting an RT system directed by a repertoire of distinct RNAs. These findings indicate that LLMs can autonomously detect anomalies and drive analyses to initiate biological discoveries.

title: Clinical utility of plasma APOE proteotyping for Alzheimer's disease risk and prognosis
abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder strongly influenced by genetic factors, with apolipoprotein E (APOE) {epsilon}4 allele being the most established risk variant. Although DNA-based genotyping remains standard, plasma proteotyping may provide scalable, isoform-specific alternatives. Methods: Plasma APOE4 protein were quantified using the NULISAseq CNS panel across four cohorts (ADRC, HeartSCORE, LATTICE, and ALPS). DNA-based APOE genotyping was the reference standard. Proteotyping thresholds for APOE {epsilon}4 carrier status and copy number were derived in ADRC and externally validated in the other cohorts. Logistic, proportional-odds, and Cox proportional-hazards models compared genotype- and proteotype-defined groups in relation to amyloid positivity, cross-sectional CDR global scores, and time to CDR-SB worsening, respectively. Results: Plasma APOE4 accurately classified APOE {epsilon}4 carrier status in ADRC (AUC=0.977, 95%CI 0.967-0.985; threshold 5.78 NULISA protein quantification [NPQ] value) and achieved near-perfect external validation in HeartSCORE, LATTICE, and ALPS (all AUCs=1.000, 95%CI 1.000-1.000). Plasma APOE4 also well-differentiated heterozygous from homozygous {epsilon}4 carriers (ADRC AUC=0.879, 95%CI 0.834-0.921; threshold 12.23 NPQ value). Genotype- and proteotype-defined {epsilon}4 carrier status showed similar associations with amyloid positivity (OR=4.40 vs 4.45), higher CDR global scores (OR=1.50 for both), and CDR-SB worsening (HR=1.22 for both). Discussion: Plasma APOE4 proteotyping accurately distinguished genotype-defined APOE {epsilon}4 carrier status and copy number while demonstrating AD-related associations comparable to DNA genotyping.

title: Genetic Variant Burden Rises with BMI: Insights from Rare and Low-Frequency Variants in Obesity
Impact of Prolonged Obesity Across the Lifecourse on Myocardial Stress and Injury in Older Age: Birth Cohort Study
abstract: Background The consequences of prolonged exposure to obesity on biomarkers of myocardial stress and injury remain unclear. We examined associations of duration and cumulative severity of obesity from childhood to later adulthood with concentrations of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI), and growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) at age 62 years. Methods The sample comprised 4,901 participants in the 1958 National Child Development Study who had measurements of NT-proBNP, hs-cTnI, or GDF-15 at age 62 years and at least four BMI assessments between 7 and 62 years of age. Individual BMI trajectories were modelled, from which total duration of obesity and mean excess BMI (area between the trajectory and the age-specific obesity threshold divided by duration) were derived. Associations of ever versus never having been obese, obesity duration, and mean excess BMI with biomarker concentrations were examined using general linear regression models with progressive adjustment for early-life characteristics; contemporaneous cardiometabolic factors; and health behaviours, socioeconomic position, and psychosocial factors. Nonlinear associations of obesity duration were estimated using restricted cubic splines and subsequently approximated using linear splines. Results Overall, 26.3% of participants had ever experienced obesity. There was no evidence of an association between ever versus never having been obese and NT-proBNP. Among men, ever having been obese was associated with 11.00% (95% CI, 4.62-17.37) higher hs-cTnI in the fully adjusted model, whereas there was no evidence of an association among women. Ever having been obese was associated with higher GDF-15, although the association attenuated substantially after adjustment for contemporaneous cardiometabolic factors. Longer obesity duration was associated with higher concentrations of all three biomarkers in fully adjusted models, but the pattern differed by biomarker: hs-cTnI increased approximately linearly with duration, whereas NT-proBNP and GDF-15 remained relatively stable up to approximately 25 years of obesity before increasing with longer duration. In fully adjusted models, each additional year of obesity beyond 25 years was associated with 1.80% (95% CI, 0.54-3.06) higher NT-proBNP and 0.81% (95% CI, 0.25-1.36) higher GDF-15, while each additional year across the full range of obesity duration was associated with 0.41% (95% CI, 0.07-0.76) higher hs-cTnI. Among participants who had ever experienced obesity, each 1 kg/m2 higher mean excess BMI was associated with 4.02% (95% CI, 1.79-6.24) higher NT-proBNP and 2.00% (95% CI, 0.49-3.51) higher hs-cTnI in fully adjusted models; there was no evidence of an association with GDF-15. Conclusions Longer duration of obesity was associated with higher concentrations of biomarkers reflecting myocardial stress, injury, and cellular stress at age 62 years, with associations particularly evident after approximately 25 years of obesity for NT-proBNP and GDF-15. These findings suggest that duration of obesity may provide clinically relevant information beyond current obesity status, supporting its consideration as an additional dimension of cumulative obesity burden in cardiovascular risk assessment.

title: Worldwide diversity and geographic structure of killer-cell immunoglobulin-like receptor (KIR) gene content
abstract: Introduction: Killer-cell immunoglobulin-like receptor (KIR) gene content shapes natural killer-cell responses and varies substantially among populations. We examined whether worldwide KIR diversity reflects regional structure, isolation by distance, serial founder effects, or latitudinal gradients. Data and methods: Carrier frequencies for 11 variable KIR genes were obtained from the Allele Frequency Net Database. The primary analysis included 189 locally sampled, non-diaspora, non-mixed populations from 70 countries, comprising 25,469 individuals; 161 populations had complete 11-gene profiles. Diversity indices, ordination, clustering, permutation-based variance decomposition, Mantel tests, and regression models were used to characterize geographic structure. Serial founder effects were evaluated using four distance measures from East Africa, both globally and within the Old World. Models of latitude incorporated spatial autocorrelation. Prespecified sensitivity analyses evaluated alternative population sets, gene panels, geographic classifications, weighting schemes, and multivariate outlier exclusion. Results: Geographic region explained 53.5% of variation in KIR profiles, substantially exceeding the permutation-null expectation of 6.9%, although multivariate dispersion differed among regions. Twenty-five of 28 pairwise regional comparisons remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. Isolation by distance was modest (Mantel r=0.3003) and weakened after controlling for region (r=0.1557). KIR diversity did not decline with distance from East Africa globally but decreased strongly within the Old World (expected heterozygosity {beta}=-0.0066 and standardized gene content {beta}=-0.0789). B-content decreased nominally with absolute latitude, but latitude was collinear with region and the association survived neither spatial modelling nor sensitivity analyses. Regional differentiation remained robust across analytical specifications, whereas the Old World decline was carried by gene content once standard errors were clustered by country. Conclusion: Worldwide KIR gene-content variation shows pronounced regional differentiation, modest isolation by distance, and no independent latitudinal gradient. Diversity declines with distance from East Africa across the Old World, supporting serial founder effects, but not once the Americas and Oceania are included.

title: Optimization of Irrigation Systems and Ecological Assessment: A Case Study of Andijan Region, with a Forecast to 2032
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive assessment of the economic and ecological efficiency of irrigation-system optimization in Andijan region, Uzbekistan. Key hydro-technical indicators — hydromodule, drainage modulus, irrigation rate, canal efficiency coefficient (CEC), and water-use coefficient (WUC) — were evaluated using statistical and regression analysis. Irrigation norms for six crop types were compared against the national average and across 13 administrative regions. A power-law regression model (Q = 92.453H^0.5328, R² = 0.9975) was derived from field hydro-post certification data to describe the discharge-water-level relationship. Soil salinity (EC) and groundwater-table monitoring across all 14 districts of the region were used to assess ecological impacts within a DPSIR framework. Based on identified modernization trends, a 2026-2032 forecast projects an increase in the overall CEC from 0.65 to 0.80 and a corresponding reduction in conveyance losses from 35% to 20%. The findings confirm that canal lining, installation of metering devices, and rotational irrigation scheduling can reduce water losses by 10-35%, substantially mitigating soil salinization and groundwater-table rise.
journal: Journal of Mathematical Models and Methods in Engineering

title: A Real-Time Machine Learning-Based Intrusion Detection and Prevention System for Decentralized Networks using Random Forest and Isolation Forest
abstract: Decentralized networks—spanning Internet-of-Things deployments, edge computing platforms and peer-to-peer systems—offer improved scalability, resilience and the elimination of single points of failure. At the same time, their distributed structure makes continuous monitoring and timely intrusion response substantially more difficult. Traditional signature-based intrusion detection systems (IDS) are effective only against previously catalogued attacks; they cannot reliably detect zero-day or heavily obfuscated threats and typically require the centralised collection of raw traffic, thereby raising privacy, bandwidth and single-point-of-failure concerns. This paper presents a complete real-time machine-learning-based user detection and intrusion prevention system expressly designed for decentralised environments. A lightweight monitoring agent executes on every registered physical node, continuously captures live network packets, groups them into traffic flows and extracts a compact set of discriminative features: packet rate, bandwidth usage, latency, failed login attempts and connection duration. These features are classified by a Random Forest ensemble that distinguishes authorised from unauthorised activity. Concurrently, an Isolation Forest anomaly detector flags behavioural outliers that may correspond to previously unseen (zero-day) attacks. For every prediction the system computes a continuous risk score, assigns a discrete threat level (Low, Medium, High or Critical), records an immutable event log entry, displays a real-time alert together with an AI-generated explanation on the administrator dashboard, and—when prevention mode is enabled—automatically installs firewall rules that block the offending traffic. Because only summarised detection results are forwarded to the central monitoring dashboard, raw packet data never leave the local node; privacy is preserved and inter-node communication overhead is minimised. Extensive evaluation on labelled network traffic demonstrates an accuracy of 96.80%, precision of 95.40%, recall of 94.20% and F1-score of 94.80%, markedly surpassing a conventional signature-based baseline. The system maintains normal network performance under both typical and elevated traffic loads, confirming that intelligent detection need not be purchased at the expense of operational efficiency.
journal: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology

title: AgroGuard AI: A Trustworthy Adaptive Architecture for Crop Disease Intelligence under Environmental Non-Stationarity
abstract: Deep learning systems for crop disease recognition are routinely reported at above 95% accuracy on curated benchmarks, yet their field performance degrades sharply and silently once deployed. The cause is not a modelling deficiency in the conventional sense but a violation of the stationarity assumption on which supervised learning rests: the agro-climatic environment that generates the data is itself non-stationary. Humidity regimes shift between seasons, pathogen populations evolve, cultivar mixes change, sensor hardware ages, and the relationship between visual symptom and disease label drifts with them. A model frozen at training time therefore decays monotonically, and — more damagingly for trust — it decays while continuing to report high confidence. This manuscript presents AgroGuard AI, a five-layer reference architecture that treats environmental non-stationarity as a first-class design constraint rather than a deployment nuisance. The architecture couples four mechanisms that are usually studied in isolation. A drift detection subsystem monitors input, representation, and label-conditional distributions using a complementary ensemble of ADWIN, KSWIN, and kernel maximum mean discrepancy tests. A continual learning subsystem combines elastic weight consolidation with sparse episodic replay so that adaptation to a new agro-climatic regime does not erase competence in previously encountered ones. A conformal prediction layer converts raw softmax scores into prediction sets with distribution-free marginal coverage guarantees, and gates low-reliability inputs to human review rather than issuing a confident wrong answer. Finally, a temporal explanation engine reports not only why a prediction was made but why it changed, surfacing the shift in feature attribution that accompanies each adaptation event. We formalise the learning problem, specify each subsystem, derive the adaptation trigger policy, and define a trust metric suite covering calibration error, explanation fidelity, backward transfer, and selective risk. We further specify an edge deployment profile for low-connectivity rural contexts and a privacy-preserving federated aggregation scheme. The manuscript closes with a complete evaluation protocol — datasets, baselines, ablations, and acceptance thresholds — designed to falsify the architecture's central claims. All quantitative values reported herein are design targets and illustrative simulations under explicitly stated generative assumptions; no field trial has been conducted, and this limitation is treated as a defining boundary of the present contribution rather than a caveat.
journal: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology

title: Predicting CSI 800 Sector Index Returns in China ——A Multifactor Statistical and Regularized Learning Approach
abstract: Industry allocation is critical to asset allocation and a major source of excess returns in active investing. This study explores sector return predictability in China with a multifactor framework. We employ monthly data spanning January 2019 to June 2026 for 11 CSI 800 primary sector indices and build 11 predictors, including macroeconomic indicators, Shibor, technical signals and the market factor. We estimate separate industry-level OLS and Lasso regression models, using January 2025–June 2026 as the out-of-sample test window. Static one-shot estimation generates negative out-of-sample R² for both models, a typical outcome in monthly return forecasting. We then implement rolling-window re-estimation with 72-, 60- and 48-month lookback windows to boost forecasts. The 72-month rolling Lasso attains an average out-of-sample R² of −0.07. Its Top-3 industry rotation strategy achieves 65.45% cumulative return and 48.03% excess return relative to the equal-weight benchmark, while rolling OLS yields only 37.46% cumulative return and 20.04% excess return. Given negative predictiveR², we evaluate cross-sectional ranking performance via monthly Spearman Rank IC. The 72-month rolling Lasso delivers a statistically significant mean Rank IC of 0.215 (t=2.96), whereas OLS’s 0.057 (t=0.60) lacks significance. Rolling estimation enables models to adapt to dynamic markets. Lasso demonstrates superior out-of-sample ranking power, consistent with its stronger industry rotation excess returns.

Silicate Biomaterials-Stimulated Vascularized Callus Organoids for Bone Tissue Regeneration.
abstract: Organoids that recapitulate native fracture callus can form spontaneous ossification centers within a bone defect, offering substantial promise for rapid bone regeneration. However, existing callus organoids generally lack a functional vascular network and an appropriate mechanical microenvironment, and their production limits scalability and uniformity. Here, we established a droplet-based microfluidic platform for the high-throughput generation of morphology-dependent magnesium silicate-engineered composite hydrogel microspheres, enabling the uniform construction of vascularized callus organoids. Importantly, morphology-dependent magnesium silicate could regulate both the bulk mechanical performance and internal stress distribution of the composite hydrogels. In vitro, callus organoids modulated by magnesium silicate nanotubes significantly promoted chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation, developed a stable endothelial network and mineralized structure. Furthermore, magnesium silicate nanotube-engineered composite hydrogel (2NT-GM) offered a favorable mechanical microenvironment for callus organoids, thereby activating the mechanotransduction-related pathway for promoting the development of organoids. In a rat femoral condyle critical-sized defect model, the vascularized callus organoids regulated by 2NT-GM were further found to significantly promote vascular network formation, and facilitate bone regeneration at the bone defect center within 6 weeks of implantation. Together, this study suggests a promising strategy for bone tissue regeneration by developing vascularized callus organoids with the stimulation of inorganic silicate biomaterials.

title: Conservation of crop wild relatives in Saudi Arabia: a national checklist and prioritisation
abstract: Crop wild relatives (CWR) contribute to global food security through their value as plant genetic resources and their role in enhancing domesticated crops. Interest in CWR has increased in recent decades due to population growth and the growing challenges posed by climate change, highlighting the need for their effective conservation. In Saudi Arabia, however, no national prioritised inventory has previously been developed to support conservation planning. Hence, this study presents a comprehensive national CWR checklist for Saudi Arabia and a priority inventory to reduce the number of taxa to a manageable size for effective conservation planning. The total CWR checklist includes 487 taxa belonging to 28 families and 104 genera, of which 420 (86.24%) are native, 64 (13.14%) are introduced, and three (0.62%) are endemic. The most species-rich families are Fabaceae with 135 taxa (27.72%), Poaceae with 110 taxa (22.58%), Amaranthaceae with 41 taxa (8.41%), and Brassicaceae with 38 taxa (7.80%). To identify conservation priorities, the checklist was evaluated using two criteria: the socio-economic value of the related crop in Saudi Arabia and the potential utilisation value of the CWR based on the crop gene pool and taxon group concepts. Application of these criteria resulted in a priority inventory of 82 taxa. The priority inventory includes wild relatives of nationally and globally important crops, including wheat ( Aegilops spp.), barley ( Hordeum spp.), and date palm ( Phoenix dactylifera L.). This study provides an essential baseline for future conservation planning and supports the integration of CWR conservation into national strategies for the sustainable management of plant genetic resources in Saudi Arabia.

title: Can AI Solve Eco-Economic Challenges? Simulating the Impact of AI Systems on Seasonality Using Agent-Based Modelling
abstract: As visitors increasingly rely on AI-enabled apps and recommender systems, AI is becoming an important mediator of tourism choice. Tourism decision-making is cognitively demanding, and visitors rarely evaluate all available destinations, attractions, travel periods, and services equally. Consistent with bounded rationality, they simplify complex choice environments through limited information, heuristics, and platform-mediated evaluation. This creates opportunities for AI systems not only to personalise experiences, but also to influence how attention and demand are distributed across attractions and seasons. This research develops and computationally examines a mechanism-based conceptualisation of how AI-enabled information systems mediate visitor choice and how micro-level decision processes accumulate into tourism-system outcomes. Drawing on digital choice architecture, information filtering, platform ecosystem perspectives, and bounded rationality, the research conceptualises AI as a decision-mediating infrastructure. Using an agent-based model of a tourism platform ecosystem, it compares three visitor-facing AI intervention conditions: predictive nudging, a recommender-system filtering, and fairness-oriented visibility enhancement. The model examines how differences in attention, salience, choice-set formation, evaluation, satisfaction, and subsequent behaviour are associated with system-level outcomes. The findings show that AI-mediated interventions can increase visitor activity and spending, but their effects differ across intervention conditions and do not automatically reduce seasonality. The research contributes to Information Systems and smart-tourism research by showing how AI-enabled decision environments can structure attention, consideration, and visibility, while highlighting the limits of digital interventions when destination outcomes are also shaped by wider structural conditions.

Metabolic profiling of retinal organoids reveals conserved core metabolites and alterations in glycolytic and amino acid metabolism
abstract: Retinal organoids have emerged as powerful models of retinal development and disease; however, the extent to which they recapitulate the metabolic landscape of the native retina remains largely unknown. This study aimed to compare the metabolomic profiles of mouse retina and mouse embryonic stem cell-derived retinal organoids and to evaluate metabolic changes during organoid maturation. Untargeted gas chromatography mass spectrometry based metabolomic profiling was performed on intracellular metabolites from mouse retina at postnatal day 3 and mouse retinal organoids (MROs) at differentiation day 28, together with conditioned media collected during organoid maturation. Across mouse retina and retinal organoids, 166 annotated compounds were included in the analysis . Of these, 148 were shared between the two sample types. Using a bidirectional fold-change threshold, differential analysis showed that mouse retinal organoids preserved a substantial metabolic signature shared with mouse retina. However, selective differences were observed in the abundance of glycolysis-associated metabolites and pentose phosphate intermediates including glucose-6-phosphate and ribulose-5-phosphate, as well as tricarboxylic acid-cycle-associated metabolites including citric acid, fumaric acid and oxalic acid. Pathway enrichment analysis identified significant alterations in alanine, aspartate, and glutamate metabolism. Media analysis further revealed stage-dependent changes in extracellular glutamate and glycine abundance during organoid maturation. MRO retains major components of retinal metabolic organization while exhibiting features suggestive of incomplete metabolic maturation compared with native retina. These findings provide valuable insight into MRO metabolic fidelity and guide future optimization strategies.

title: Research on the impact of resource dependence and green finance on the efficiency of green development
abstract: Resource dependence entrenches environmental inefficiency in resource-based cities, yet whether green finance can mitigate this structural lock-in remains unclear. Using a balanced panel of 113 prefecture-level cities in China from 2007 to 2022, we measure green development efficiency via a super-SBM model. We find that resource dependence significantly undermines green development efficiency, but this adverse effect is attenuated by green finance and becomes statistically insignificant at high levels of green-finance penetration. Further analysis highlights industrial-structure adjustment and green technological innovation as two important transmission channels. Heterogeneity analysis reveals substantial variation across city development stages and regions, with the moderating effect particularly evident in mature-stage and declining-stage cities and a comparatively larger estimate in northwestern China. Results remain robust under alternative efficiency indicators, lagged-outcome specifications, and instrumental-variable estimations. Moreover, a comparison with non-resource-based cities confirms that this moderating role is contingent on a highly resource-dependent economic structure. Thus, green finance can be viewed as a targeted structural-corrective tool for resource-dependent contexts, rather than merely a one-size-fits-all environmental subsidy. These insights offer important policy implications for differentiated green finance deployment in resource-based regions.

LGR4 interacts with RhoA to modulate cell survival and epithelial-mesenchymal transition via the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in benign prostatic hyperplasia.
abstract: BACKGROUND Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), a prevalent disorder among elderly men, still has an unclear etiology. Leucine-rich repeat-containing G protein-coupled receptor 4 (LGR4) plays a pivotal role in cellular proliferation, differentiation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in various tissues. This study was designed to investigate the roles of LGR4 in BPH. METHODS Human prostate tissues, cultured human prostate cell (BPH-1 and WPMY-1) were utilized to detect LGR4 expression and localization by immunofluorescence staining, RT-PCR, and Western Blot. LGR4 deficient and overexpression cell models were established. Using these models, the levels of cellular viability, apoptosis, cell cycle were quantified by cell counting kit-8 assay, flow cytometry, respectively. Apoptosis-related proteins, cycle-associated proteins, EMT biomarkers and Wnt/β-catenin pathway were measured by Western Blot. Furthermore, a software, AlphaFold3, was used to perform molecular docking analysis between LGR4 and RhoA. We further studied the interaction between LGR4 and RhoA through Co-Immunoprecipitation assay. RESULTS Our research findings demonstrated that LGR4 was overexpressed in BPH and localized within the stromal and epithelial components of prostate. LGR4 deficiency promoted apoptosis, arrested the cell cycle, inhibited cell growth and EMT. Conversely, overexpression of LGR4 completely reversed the alterations induced by LGR4 deficiency. We further showed that LGR4 regulated the Wnt/β-catenin pathway by interacting with RhoA to control cellular proliferation, apoptosis and EMT, while barely affected cell cycle. CONCLUSIONS Overall, our original data indicate that the upregulated LGR4 could interact with RhoA to exert an inhibitory impact on cell apoptosis while promote cellular proliferation and EMT via Wnt/β-catenin pathway.
