title: Investigation on Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Model Using Sensitivity Analysis
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is challenged by high-dimensional input features that cause redundancy and overfitting. To address this, we propose a short-term PV forecasting model integrating a CNN-LSTM architecture with active subspace-based global sensitivity analysis, which quantitatively evaluates feature influence via gradient information. Using operational data from a PV plant, we compare three feature selection schemes across CNN-LSTM, CNN, and LSTM models. For CNN-LSTM, the baseline yields an average R2 of 0.8769 (RMSE: 134.2 kW), while Pearson-based selection slightly reduces performance (R2 = 0.8646, RMSE: 140.7 kW). In contrast, the active subspace method achieves an average R2 of 0.9341 (RMSE: 83.6 kW), representing improvements of 6.52% and 8.04% over the no-selection and Pearson schemes, respectively. Overfitting is mitigated and convergence accelerates. The method also shows consistent improvements on CNN and LSTM models, confirming its model-agnostic effectiveness. These results demonstrate that the active subspace method is an efficient and interpretable feature engineering tool for PV forecasting.

title: The Impact of Digital Infrastructure on Agricultural Green Total Factor Productivity—An Empirical Study from China
abstract: Agricultural sustainability remains a global priority, but how digital infrastructure accelerates this transition is still poorly specified. Drawing on provincial panel data from 30 Chinese provinces (2010–2023), this study quantifies the effect of digital infrastructure on agricultural green total factor productivity (AGTFP). The empirical strategy combines entropy weighting, a super-efficiency SBM-GML index, two-way fixed-effects panel estimation, and mediation-moderation analysis. Four results stand out. First, digital infrastructure raises AGTFP significantly, and this conclusion survives a series of robustness checks. Second, the effect is context-dependent: it strengthens where environmental regulation is stringent and where digital infrastructure is already well developed, whereas the east–central/west divide fails a formal interaction test. Third, the effect travels through two mediating channels—agricultural technological innovation and the scaling of service provision—rather than through land consolidation. Fourth, rural human capital amplifies the efficiency gains. Taken together, the findings suggest that digital infrastructure does not deliver sustainability dividends automatically; complementary institutions and human capital are required, and scale economies materialize mainly through service provision rather than land aggregation.

title: Digital Inclusive Finance and Agricultural New-Quality Productive Forces: Dynamic Effects, Industrial-Chain Coordination, and Data-Element Thresholds
abstract: This study examines how digital inclusive finance promotes agricultural new-quality productive forces through agricultural industrial-chain coordination, data-element conditions, dynamic accumulation, and spatial spillovers. Based on a balanced panel of 30 Chinese provinces from 2013 to 2023, we estimate two-way fixed-effects, system GMM, mediation, panel-threshold, and spatial Durbin models. The results demonstrate that digital inclusive finance significantly increases agricultural new-quality productive forces. This finding remains robust to lagged specifications, system-GMM estimation, Oster bounds, and an independent agricultural green total factor productivity outcome. Agricultural industrial-chain coordination is positively associated with the outcome and is consistent with a partial transmission channel. Data-element agglomeration generates a double-threshold pattern, with the marginal contribution of digital inclusive finance increasing after the estimated thresholds have been crossed. The spatial estimates indicate positive associations with neighboring provinces under some weight matrices, with stronger associations in eastern China and in regions with greater industrial-chain coordination. By integrating organizational coordination, data factors, temporal dynamics, and spatial dependence, this study provides a unified account of digital financial empowerment in agriculture. The findings indicate the need to develop digital financial inclusion alongside agricultural data infrastructure and cross-stage industrial-chain coordination, which would support sustainable, regionally balanced agricultural modernization.

title: An Exploratory Pilot Study of Cognitive Factors Influencing the Adoption of AI Coding Agents in Agile Development Teams
abstract: This study considers the cognitive factors influencing the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents among software engineers in Agile development environments. In this context, Transparency refers to the degree to which an AI system’s decision processes are clear or understandable to its users, while Trust denotes the confidence developers place in the reliability and correctness of AI-generated code. Specifically, it analyzes the roles of Transparency and Trust as predictors of developers’ Behavioral Intention to deploy AI-generated code. Using a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design administered to 19 Agile software professionals, this study uses descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and simple and multiple linear regression to test a mediation model based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). In this exploratory pilot sample, Trust emerged as the strongest predictor of Behavioral Intention (β = 0.64, p = 0.007), though findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample size. Trust demonstrated the strongest association with Behavioral Intention, while Transparency showed a non-significant positive association with Trust. The observed pattern is consistent with a possible indirect relationship, although mediation was not confirmed in this sample. This evidence suggests that organizations seeking to improve AI adoption in development teams should prioritize the reliability and accuracy of AI tools, conditions that encourage trust, over transparency features alone. This study adds to the cognitive engineering literature on human–AI interaction in high-cognitive-demand work environments.

title: A Systematic Comparison of Differential Metabolites and Functional Pathways in the Gut Contents of Yaks and Plateau Yellow Cattle Across Altitudinal Gradients
abstract: The yak (Bos grunniens) is a crucial species adapted to the extreme high-altitude environment of the Tibetan Plateau. However, a systematic understanding of how gut metabolic homeostasis contributes to this adaptation, particularly across altitudinal gradients and in comparison with sympatric species, remains limited. This study employed untargeted metabolomics to profile the intestinal contents of high-altitude yaks (HYs, 3800 m), low-altitude yaks (LYs, 2500 m), and plateau yellow cattle (PC, 3500 m) from the Gannan region. Multivariate analysis revealed distinct clustering of the three groups, with PLS-DA model validation parameters (R2Y(cum) > 0.997, Q2(cum) > 0.990), confirming significant species-specific and altitude-adaptive differentiation in the gut metabolome. A suite of differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) was identified: HYs were enriched with stress- and inflammation-related molecules (e.g., prostaglandin E2, uric acid-indicative of oxidative stress and inflammatory responses) and steroid metabolites; LYs showed a profile oriented towards basic anabolism and antioxidant defense (e.g., L-galactono-1,4-lactone, allantoin); PC were characterized by unique lipid derivatives (e.g., 5-hexyl-2-furanhexanoic acid) and fungal-origin metabolites. Pathway enrichment analysis pinpointed Linoleic acid metabolism as one of the most significantly enriched pathways, with key hydroxyoctadecadienoic acids (HODEs) and related oxylipins significantly upregulated in HYs. Other significantly enriched pathways included Tryptophan metabolism, ABC transporters, and Protein digestion and absorption. Our findings suggest that high-altitude adaptation in yaks is associated with remodeling of the intestinal metabolic network. The identified signature metabolites and consistently enriched candidate pathways provide novel insights into potential host–microbiome-associated mechanisms and establish a metabolic foundation for the conservation of plateau livestock genetic resources and the development of precision husbandry strategies. However, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating because altitude, species, diet, and environment were not fully decoupled.

title: Study on Spatiotemporal Differentiation of Vegetation NPP and Its Influencing Factors in the Huaihe River Basin Since 2000
abstract: Under the dual stress of climate change and intensive human activities, vegetation dynamics in the Huaihe River Basin, a typical north–south climatic transition zone in China, merit close attention. Net Primary Productivity (NPP) serves as a core metric for characterizing ecosystem carbon-sink capacity and vegetation growth status. Elucidating its spatiotemporal patterns and driving factors is of great significance for regional ecological conservation and adaptive management. Taking the Huaihe River Basin as the study area, this study utilizes MOD17A3HGF NPP datasets and multi-source geospatial data spanning 2000–2024. Integrating trend analysis, the Hurst exponent, residual analysis, and the Geodetector model, this work aims to reveal the spatiotemporal evolution and prospective change trends of vegetation NPP, and to quantitatively identify the independent and interactive effects of climate, topography, and human activities on NPP spatial differentiation. The results show that: (1) Temporally, vegetation NPP exhibits an overall fluctuating upward trend, increasing from 370 gC·m−2·yr−1 to 475 gC·m−2·yr−1, with a multi-year average of 422.9 gC·m−2·yr−1. The period 2013–2014 marks a prominent inflection point for NPP growth. Spatially, NPP follows a distribution pattern of high values in the southeast and low values in the northwest. (2) NPP shows an increasing trend across 94.09% of the basin. Meanwhile, 86.27% of the study area is characterised by anti-persistence, i.e., historical vegetation improvement accompanied by prospective degradation risks, which poses substantial challenges to ecosystem resilience. (3) Climatically, precipitation exhibits strong positive correlations with NPP, followed by temperature. Topographically, the maximum NPP occurs within the elevation band of 500–1000 m and the slope gradient range of 25–35°. Human activities exert positive promotional effects over most parts of the basin, presenting a spatial gradient with high contributions in western mountainous regions, moderate contributions in eastern plains, and low contributions around urban peripheries. (4) Precipitation, elevation, and geomorphic type are the dominant driving factors. Most pairwise factor interactions produce enhanced explanatory power, among which the interaction between elevation and precipitation yields the highest explanatory capacity. This coupling reflects topographic modulation of hydrothermal conditions and the spatial redistribution of precipitation, which creates divergent water availability and vegetation habitats across terrain units. Population density exhibits weak explanatory power when acting independently; nevertheless, its explanatory capacity rises substantially after interacting with precipitation and elevation. This finding indicates that anthropogenic impacts on vegetation are embedded within specific natural environmental contexts.

title: Carbon–Water Coupling Coordination and Its Drivers Along the Water Withdrawal–Use–Discharge Cycle: Evidence from Qinghai Province
abstract: Carbon and water systems exhibit complex synergies and trade-offs and are closely interconnected through the social water cycle. This study examines eight prefecture-level regions in Qinghai Province from 2010 to 2024. A comprehensive carbon–water evaluation system and coupling coordination degree (CCD) model were used to characterize the spatiotemporal evolution of carbon–water coupling coordination, while CatBoost-SHAP was applied to identify the main factors associated with coordination across water withdrawal, use, and discharge processes. The results show that: (1) the carbon–water CCD exhibited an overall fluctuating upward trend, with the comprehensive evaluation index of the carbon subsystem generally higher than that of the water resources subsystem; (2) coordination showed pronounced spatial heterogeneity, characterized by relative stability in high-level regions and gradual improvement in low-level regions; and (3) water resource use within the social water cycle was closely associated with carbon–water coupling coordination, with indicators related to agriculture, the forestry–animal husbandry–fishery sector, and water supply showing relatively high model importance. Accordingly, carbon–water synergistic management should improve water use efficiency in production sectors, strengthen matching between water supply and end-use demand, and implement differentiated management according to regional resource endowments, ecological functions, and socioeconomic development levels.

title: CLASSIFICAÇÃO DA PRODUTIVIDADE DA CANA-DE-AÇÚCAR COM RANDOM FOREST INTEGRANDO ÍNDICES DE VEGETAÇÃO E VARIÁVEIS AMBIENTAIS
abstract: Estimating sugarcane productivity before harvest is important for planning agricultural operations and managing production. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of the Random Forest algorithm for productivity classification using different combinations of spectral, agronomic, and environmental data throughout the harvest season. The study area is located in the municipalities of Pratânia and Lençóis Paulista, São Paulo State, Brazil. Images from the OLI sensor onboard Landsat 8 were used to obtain the NDVI, EVI, and MSAVI2 vegetation indices for periods corresponding to approximately 90 and 180 days before harvest, in addition to the last available image before harvest. Information on soil type, sugarcane variety, crop stage, slope, and aspect was also considered and combined into 12 input configurations. The classifications were performed using 10-fold cross-validation and evaluated based on the percentage of correctly classified instances and the Kappa coefficient. The configuration containing all variables achieved 87.9%, 87.38%, and 82.93% correctly classified instances in the initial, intermediate, and final periods of the harvest season, respectively, with a Kappa coefficient of 0.8. The configuration using vegetation indices obtained approximately 180 days before harvest, together with soil type, variety, crop stage, slope, and aspect, achieved 85.2%, 84.82%, and 81.58% correctly classified instances in the same periods, respectively, also with a Kappa coefficient of 0.8. Thus, using vegetation indices from a single acquisition period maintained results close to those obtained with the complete dataset, including when spectral information was acquired approximately 180 days before harvest.

title: Comparative Analysis of IAE, ISE, and ITSE Performance in IoT-Based ZN-PID Air Heater Temperature Control
abstract: Precise air temperature control remains a critical yet challenging task in modern industrial and agricultural systems due to high thermal inertia and heater non-linearity. Furthermore, implementing intelligent control on low-cost Internet of Things (IoT) devices is often hindered by digital conversion resolution and quantization errors. These limitations can induce thermal oscillations and energy waste if tuning criteria are sub optimally selected. Therefore, this study comparatively evaluates actual thermal performance using Integral Absolute Error (IAE), Integral Squared Error (ISE), and Integral Time Weighted Squared Error (ITSE) as objective functions for Ziegler Nichols (ZN) Type 1 Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) tuning. A key contribution of this work is mitigating quantization errors by integrating a 5x analog amplifier circuit with an LM35 sensor and utilizing high frequency (1000Hz) Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) via a custom-built Solid-State Relay (SSR) on an ESP32. The system was evaluated through physical closed loop testing on a 650 Watt air heater, monitored in real time the MQTT protocol. To ensure robustness, tests were cross validated at 50°C and 60°C setpoints with three replications. Experimental results demonstrate that IAE tuning offers the most balanced performance at the moderate target (50°C), achieving the fastest rise time (5.58s), minimal overshoot (0.42%), high precision (Steady-State Error/SSE: -0.11), and optimal control effort (average PWM: 52.61). Conversely, at the higher target (60°C) which presents a massive initial error deficit ISE tuning proved significantly more robust. It suppressed overshoot to 0.86% while achieving a superior settling time of 15.35 seconds. In conclusion, the IAE criterion is recommended for efficient heating applications with stable loads, whereas ISE is critical for regulating high-inertia thermal loads to prevent extreme overshoot in IoT control actuators.

title: Digital Agriculture and Sector Transformation in South Africa
abstract: Digitalisation is increasingly promoted as a catalyst for agricultural productivity, climate resilience, and market integration. However, there is limited systematic analysis of how digital agricultural transformation unfolds within South Africa’s institutional and socio-economic context. This study examines the trajectory, drivers, and governance implications of digitalisation in South African agriculture. Anchored in an integrated Socio-Technical Systems and Digital Agriculture Ecosystem framework, the study applies a structured qualitative document analysis of 82 academic and policy documents published between 2013 and 2025. The findings reveal highly uneven digital adoption patterns that reflect a structural dualism between capital-intensive commercial agriculture and resource-constrained smallholder systems. While South Africa has developed a relatively advanced digital policy architecture, implementation fragmentation, infrastructure constraints, and limited capacity for extension impede inclusive digital outcomes. The study contributes by integrating socio-technical and ecosystem perspectives to analyse digital transitions in emerging economies and by providing a transparent analytical protocol for document-based research. Policy implications highlight the need for coordinated governance, investment in rural connectivity, and targeted support mechanisms to ensure equitable digital transformation.

title: Enhancing Long-Tailed Macaque Pest Identification Using a Two-Stage YOLO-EfficientNet Pipeline
abstract: Long-tailed macaque (Macaca fascicularis) infestations have reduced corn production from a potential 7–9 tons to only 4–5 tons per growing season (±40%), while conventional deterrence methods such as loud noise and shooting have proven ineffective. This study developed an Internet of Things (IoT)-based pest repellent system using audiosonic waves, an HC-SR501 sensor, and an ESP32-CAM module, incorporating YOLOv8 and EfficientNet-B0 to replace the previously used YOLOv3 Tiny model, with the aim of improving detection accuracy and distinguishing long-tailed macaques from humans. Since population density at the partner's farmland was insufficient to construct an adequate dataset, image data were collected at Kembang Island, South Kalimantan, which serves as a natural habitat supporting a large and observable population of long-tailed macaques, thereby enabling the acquisition of visually representative and diverse training data. A total of 3,083 images were annotated using Label Studio under two classes (human and long-tailed macaque), then divided at an 80:10:10 ratio without augmentation. The YOLOv8n model was trained for 50 epochs, after which validation detections were cropped into 920 images to fine-tune EfficientNet-B0 over 10 epochs. Evaluation results show that YOLOv8 achieved a precision of 0.959, recall of 0.965, mAP50 of 0.979, and mAP50-95 of 0.723, while EfficientNet-B0 reached validation accuracies of 98.4–100% with no significant overfitting. The two-stage detection-classification pipeline was successfully tested end-to-end on 121 field images, demonstrating substantial performance improvements over the prior model and contributing toward IoT and AI-based smart agriculture solutions for effective, sustainable corn field protection.
journal: Best : Journal of Applied Electrical, Science and Technology

title: AI-Powered Personalised Mobile Learning Using Large Language Models: Design, Implementation, and a Simulation-Based Feasibility Evaluation
abstract: The significance of mobile learning (m-learning) has been greatly highlighted by the advent of technology due to its flexibility, accessibility and capability of being used to learn at any time and place. The development of Large Language Models (LLMs) offers great potential for creating adaptive, conversational and content-aware learning experiences via mobile apps. Most existing mobile-learning systems, however, still provide largely static content and shallow personalisation, which limits sustained learner engagement and adaptive support. This paper presents the design and implementation of an Android-based, LLM-powered personalised m-learning platform that integrates four components: a conversational tutoring agent, an Item-Response-Theory (IRT)-based adaptive quiz engine, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) content-recommendation module, and an analytics-driven feedback loop. We describe the system architecture, the prompt-orchestration and knowledge-tracing pipelines, and a rigorous quasi-experimental evaluation protocol (pre-/post-test, System Usability Scale (SUS), and engagement analytics) designed for a controlled classroom deployment. To validate the core algorithmic contributions prior to human-subject trials, we conduct two simulation-based feasibility studies: (i) a synthetic-learner simulation comparing the adaptive difficulty engine against a static item sequence and (ii) a retrieval-precision benchmark comparing RAG-based content recommendation against keyword-matching on a synthetic tagged corpus. The adaptive engine delivered quiz items within the optimal challenge zone (0.4 < P(correct) < 0.8) for 77.8% of interactions, compared with 40.8% for the static baseline, while the RAG recommender achieved substantially higher retrieval precision at every cut-off (P@10 = 0.845 versus 0.483 for keyword matching). These results provide algorithmic evidence that the proposed adaptive and retrieval components behave as intended and motivate the full-scale classroom evaluation described in the protocol. The paper concludes with a discussion of design implications, limitations, and a concrete plan for the human-subject study and future extensions of the platform.
journal: International Journal of Interactive Mobile Technologies (iJIM)

title: Lost in the comments: Social context as a single‐pass jailbreak and defense on agentic platforms
abstract: As LLM‐based agents move onto multiagent platforms, they process direct prompts and surrounding social context—posts, comments, and upvotes—an attack surface that single‐turn alignment never addressed. We built a simulation of Moltbook, a social network for AI agents, and a pipeline turning 100 JailBreakBench goals into platform‐native posts with bystander comments of three valences: aggressive, ethical, and measured. Platform‐context reformatting alone raises the attack success rate (ASR) of GPT‐4o‐mini from 7% to 71%, beating a twenty‐query optimization baseline in one pass. Valence then acts as a bidirectional safety modulator: Ethical comments sharply suppress ASR, aggressive endorsements paradoxically reduce it by exposing intent, and measured, intellectually toned comments prove most dangerous, sustaining or elevating ASR. An ablation identifies valence rather than volume as key—a 35‐fold rise in upvotes leaves ASR unchanged—and every finding reproduces under an independent safety classifier with human adjudication. Ambiguous social context thus poses a greater threat than explicit pressure, while safety‐valenced signals offer a deployable defense for agentic platforms.

title: Design and Implementation of a Telegram-Based Conversational AI Agent for Automated Personal Expense Management Using Large Language Models and Google Sheets
abstract: Manual logging of day-to-day personal expenses is often abandoned by users because it requires them to open a dedicated spreadsheet or application and enter data in a rigid, structured format. This paper presents the design and implementation of a conversational Artificial Intelligence (AI) agent that allows a user to record and retrieve personal expenses simply by chatting in natural language through the Telegram messaging platform. The system is built using the n8n low-code automation platform and combines a Telegram Trigger node, an AI Agent powered by an OpenAI Chat Model, a Simple Memory module for conversational context, and two Google Sheets tools, namely Read Expenses and Add Expense, that allow the agent to write new expense records to, and retrieve existing records from, a connected Google Sheet. When a user sends a message such as "I spent Rs.231 for Medicine today," the agent extracts the expense description, amount, and date, appends the entry to the spreadsheet, and returns a natural-language confirmation. The agent can also generate an on-demand categorized daily summary. The proposed system was implemented and tested with real conversational data, and the results demonstrate that the agent accurately parses free-form expense statements, updates the backend spreadsheet correctly, and produces coherent, human-readable summaries, thereby lowering the friction traditionally associated with manual expense tracking.
journal: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)

title: COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering
abstract: Knowledge distillation aims to train a smaller student model to mimic a larger teacher model for resource-constrained environments. However, the process of distillation is typically data-intensive and computationally expensive, particularly for generative tasks. Few-shot distillation offers an alternative by transferring teacher knowledge using limited training samples. However, we observe that few-shot distillation performance is heavily dependent on the choice of these training samples. In fact, we demonstrate that using more uncertain samples near the teacher's decision boundary can significantly deteriorate distillation performance. Motivated by this observation, we propose Counterfactual-guided Few-shot Distillation in Open-book Question Answering (COFFEQA), a novel strategy that aptly uses counterfactuals to provide additional supervision around challenging factual samples. In the generative QA setting, we define a counterfactual as a minimally modified context that induces the teacher to change its response to an alternative answer. We provide geometric insights on how factual-counterfactual pairs can constrain the deviation between the teacher's and student's decision boundaries. We further introduce a new metric, Context Following Difficulty (CFD) that further validates counterfactuals prior to distillation based on agreement with the intended alternative answer and dependence on the modified context. COFFEQA uses CFD-validated factual-counterfactual pairs for few-shot distillation. Experiments across five in-domain and three out-of-domain QA benchmarks using T5 and Qwen2.5 families show that COFFEQA outperforms factual-only distillation baselines under the same few-shot budget. For instance, on TriviaQA, COFFEQA improves over the factual-only baseline by 8.77 average EM points and 9.98 average F1 points under the T5 setting with 32 few-shot pairs.

title: Neural networks are more modular than single neurons suggest
abstract: Neural networks routinely develop representations in which individual neurons contribute to multiple distinct functions, leading to the widespread view that such networks lack modular organization. We challenge this conclusion by introducing a formally nested hierarchy of modularity: unit-level, which requires distinct computations to occupy disjoint neurons; orthogonal, which asks whether a rotation reveals functionally independent subspaces; and linear, which asks whether a bounded linear map can separate task-relevant computations into independent subspaces. We develop a unified framework for learning decompositions at each level and evaluating them causally through selective ablation. Across vision models, language models and multi-task Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), we find that networks which lack unit-level modularity nonetheless often exhibit clear functional modularity at the subspace level. In vision and language models, content versus style and syntax versus semantics respectively dissociate under subspace ablation despite sharing overlapping populations of neurons. These learned subspaces also align differentially with brain data, with content and style subspaces predicting higher and lower visual cortex respectively, and semantic subspaces outperforming syntactic ones in predicting language cortex activity. In RNNs trained on multiple cognitive tasks and previously shown to lack modular structure, our decomposition recovers sharp double dissociations between tasks. The absence of unit-level modularity frequently coexists with clear subspace-level modularity across domains, enabling targeted intervention on specific computations even in networks where no individual neuron is specialized, with broad implications for mechanistic interpretability and for understanding functional organization in both biological and artificial neural systems.

title: Co-Modifying Application Code and Deployment Infrastructure: A Causal Study of AI Agent Pull Requests
abstract: Current software engineering agents are evaluated predominantly inside isolated sandboxes against synchronous local tests. However, deploying features in collaborative repositories requires modifying continuous integration (CI/CD) pipelines, containers, and provisioning manifests alongside application logic. Because agents lack deployment awareness, attempting cross-domain modifications introduces unverified dependencies into asynchronous integration pipelines. To isolate the causal integration overhead of dual-scope pull requests (PRs)-modifying both application code and deployment infrastructure-we evaluated 26,999 PRs across two large datasets (AIDev v5 and MOSAIC-3M) encompassing six agent architectures and an aligned human baseline. Using a deterministic four-tier file taxonomy and an exact 4D strata-matching framework, we isolated integration metrics under conditional exchangeability while controlling for application volume. We find agents operate primarily as application coders or chore workers, with maintenance tasks capturing 17.70% to 25.41% of agent PRs. Dual-scope modifications represent only 4.48% to 4.55% of agentic PRs, yet trigger bimodal integration outcomes. In the first mode, explicitly reviewed contributions experience protracted delays, adding a median penalty of +13.13 hours and multiplying time-to-merge by 3.24x, driven mechanically by CI/CD and provisioning manifests. In the second mode, maintainer gatekeeping exhibits a structural bypass: even for external contributors lacking repository write access, agent identity reduces the odds of human review by 63.7% compared to human peers. Consequently, 43.1% to 56.2% of dual-scope PRs bypass inspection to merge silently in a median of under 31 minutes. These uninspected modifications compromise build verification, demonstrating the need for deployment-aware benchmarks and strict path-based access controls.

title: Time Delay System for Sequence Modeling
abstract: Existing sequence models share a critical limitation: they lack an explicit, interpretable mechanism for content-aware temporal recall. LSTMs compress everything into a single hidden state, thereby losing information about specific past events. Transformers attend to all tokens indiscriminately at quadratic cost, while state-space models like Mamba compress history into a fixed-dimensional state without explicit content-addressable memory. To address this gap, we introduce a novel framework grounded in nonlinear time-delay systems, in which the effective delay is dynamically estimated based on the semantic similarity between current and historical inputs. Our approach features three key innovations: (i) a differentiable semantic lag estimator that computes content-aware soft attention weights over history, producing a weighted historical context and similarity score; (ii) a diagonal state space with closed-form cumulative sum solution, achieving O(1) per-step complexity with no sequential loops; and (iii) an interpretable fuzzy semantic modulation mechanism that learns context-dependent rules for balancing instantaneous processing versus historical recall, where rule centers correspond to prototypical semantic contexts. Experimental results on text classification and generation outperform state-of-the-art methods.

title: Generalized Determinantal Point Processes for Attraction and Repulsion with Distinct Interaction Kernels
abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) model subset selection probability with repulsion, but many applications also exhibit attraction arising from pairwise relations or shared latent structures. Nonsymmetric DPPs (NDPPs) capture both effects, but their kernels are difficult to interpret and specify. We propose the determinant-ratio point process (DRPP), which models repulsion and attraction via a ratio of the determinants of two symmetric positive-definite kernels. This formulation preserves the feature-based interpretation of standard DPPs while allowing the two effects to be specified separately. Furthermore, we introduce an auxiliary-variable representation that enables efficient MCMC sampling and yields tractable expectation formulas for key statistics including the normalizing constant, which together facilitate maximum-likelihood learning. We theoretically characterize the interaction structures well suited to DRPPs: for clustered attraction with $C$ latent groups, DRPPs exactly realize the target pairwise interactions with an attraction rank $C$, whereas NDPPs can require a rank that grows with the number of items given the same repulsion component. Conversely, nontransitive pair-specific attraction may require compensation through the DRPP repulsion kernel. Experiments support these predictions, showing that DRPPs fit transitive attraction with substantially fewer parameters than NDPPs.

title: Controlled-Minimax: Stabilizing Adversarial Optimization via Control Theory
abstract: Minimax optimization is fundamental to adversarial learning yet suffers from severe stability challenges, often manifesting as persistent limit cycles or divergence. This paper investigates these instabilities through the lens of continuous-time dynamical systems. By modeling training dynamics as a second-order Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE), we rigorously identify the root cause of non-convergence: the problematic eigenstructure of the loss function's Hessian near equilibrium points. To address this, we introduce Controlled-Minimax, a novel stabilization framework that reformulates the optimization trajectory as a controllable physical system. Unlike heuristic regularization techniques, our approach derives a specific feedback controller that provides theoretical guarantees of local exponential stability, regardless of the underlying Hessian spectrum. Consequently, our method stabilizes general minimax problems where traditional gradient descent-ascent methods fail. Extensive experiments on pathological benchmarks including the Dirac-GAN, 2D Gaussian mixtures, and Swiss Roll datasets, as well as high-resolution image synthesis with StyleGAN2-ada, demonstrate that Controlled-Minimax effectively suppresses oscillatory behavior while ensuring fast and robust convergence.

title: DeFiRank: Federated Pairwise Ranking for Governance in Decentralized Financial Networks
abstract: Existing governance approaches in decentralized financial networks rely on manual review processes conducted by human committees, which introduces subjective bias, creates a scalability bottleneck under high network volume, and fails to capture complex behavioural patterns and evolving network dynamics. To address these limitations, we propose \name, a federated learning-based pairwise ranking framework in which multiple institutions collaboratively train a ranking model without sharing their private transaction data. This collaborative learning enables the model to capture network-wide behavioural patterns that signify strong network participation and directly contribute to the network effect, including diversity of counterparties, usage of multiple applications, and frequency of transactions. The proposed system ranks providers based on the authenticity of their actions, promoting genuine contributors and demoting those exhibiting suspicious behaviour. We evaluate \name\ on a real-world blockchain transaction dataset. Results demonstrate that the federated approach achieves ranking performance modestly below the centralized baseline (NDCG@15: $\approx$0.87 vs.\ $\approx$0.92) while preserving data privacy and matching its ranking stability (Kendall $τ$: $\approx$0.70 for both regimes), producing reliable governance decisions, including provider promotion and demotion (648 and 39 unique providers, respectively), without requiring centralized access to sensitive transaction data.

title: Collaborative Learning and Reasoning over Model Slices
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel across diverse tasks, benefiting from knowledge priors, in-context reasoning, and test-time computation. Despite these strengths, single-model reasoning remains vulnerable to error propagation, as later steps depend on the model's earlier outputs, leaving reasoning blind spots difficult to independently reassess. To address this limitation, we develop \textit{collaborative learning}, encompassing the construction of heterogeneous collaborators and the learning of effective cross-model collaboration. Specifically, \textit{model slicing} replaces a large model with smaller, heterogeneous models under a comparable parameter budget, enabling prior reasoning to be reassessed across distinct model parameterizations. \textit{Pyramid supervision} combines protocol distillation with step-level supervision to refine reasoning and interaction decisions throughout collaboration. We evaluate our approach across four task categories: multi-hop question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and open-ended constrained generation. The trained heterogeneous models achieve comparable or better task performance than the original large model and established multi-agent baselines, including reinforcement-learning-based methods, while also achieving higher inference efficiency than the multi-agent baselines and exhibiting differentiated collaboration patterns across tasks. These findings show that learned collaboration turns model heterogeneity into complementary reasoning capabilities.

title: Network Topology Shapes AI Intervention Effectiveness on Deception: Truth-Telling vs. Investigative Agents
abstract: Deploying AI agents to combat dishonest communication is an intuitive response to deception in hybrid human-AI societies. However, the efficacy of such interventions in realistic networked settings remains unclear. We study this problem using an evolutionary game-theoretic model of the Deceiver's Game by extending it to structured networks, where agents can adopt deception, truth-telling, and investigation strategies. We introduce committed AI agents (zealots) fixed to either truth-telling or investigative strategies and conduct agent-based simulations across three network topologies. Our key findings are: (1) passive committed truth-telling agents can amplify adaptive deception by creating exploitable honest partners, whereas investigative agents increase adaptive truth-telling in the oscillatory regime; (2) intervention effects are non-monotonic in deployment density because committed agents reshape rather than simply suppress the underlying oscillatory dynamics; and (3) response peaks depend on topology, with sampled scale-free populations showing sharp low-density responses and fully connected populations requiring larger committed fractions. Overall, the results highlight the need to distinguish passive truth-telling from active investigation when using committed agents to influence networked deception dynamics.

title: AgentValve: Sybil-Resilient Payment Authorization for Permissionless AI Markets
abstract: AI agents increasingly select and pay service providers without human review. In emerging permissionless markets, however, adversaries can create inexpensive identities and fabricate feedback to inflate provider reputation, making reputation-based payment authorization vulnerable to Sybil attacks and exposing clients to unbounded financial loss. This paper presents AgentValve, a protocol for Sybil-resilient payment authorization in permissionless AI markets. AgentValve builds on a trust network that represents reputation as finite capacity in a directed graph and authorizes payments through trust paths with sufficient available capacity. A smart contract atomically reserves the capacity supporting each admitted payment, bounding honest agents' payment exposure by the capacity they extend into the adversarial region, and thus creating identities or interactions entirely within that region cannot increase this bound. To limit capacity depletion by malicious senders, AgentValve combines payment-backed capacity creation with bounded route length, preventing attackers from depleting honest capacity without incurring corresponding payment costs. AgentValve further decouples off-chain route discovery from on-chain verification and introduces a witness-commit mechanism that reduces route verification to linear work while requiring only constant persistent state per admitted payment. We implement a AgentValve prototype and evaluate it using six months of Ethereum data and synthetic workloads. Experimental results show that under attacks with up to 10,000 synthetic Sybil identities and with chosen attackers, the payment exposure and capacity depletion remain bounded. Regarding practicality, the witness-commit mechanism lowers admission cost by up to 40.8% compared with baselines, and admitting common payments costs approximately \$0.04-\$0.21.

title: Video Codec-Guided Training-Free Token Compression for Video Large Language Models
abstract: Video large language models (VLLMs) rely on long visual token sequences to understand complex temporal content, which makes visual token compression important for efficient inference. Existing training-free compression methods mainly reduce the number of tokens sent to the language model, but the compression process itself can still require many visual feature comparisons, especially for intra-frame token protection and inter-frame temporal token merging. This paper proposes a video codec-guided training-free token compression method for VLLMs that uses coding information already available in compressed video as a low-cost search prior. The method aligns reference-frame dependencies, motion vectors, and residuals with the visual token grid. Residual information forms compact candidate pools for token protection, while motion information is propagated along reference-frame chains to construct localized candidates for temporal token merging between sparsely sampled frames. Local visual feature similarity comparison is then used within these candidates to make the final compression decisions, without modifying the base VLLM. Experiments on three representative VLLMs and four video-understanding benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to the state-of-the-art training-free baseline FlashVID, and in some settings surpasses it, while substantially reducing the feature comparisons required by token protection and temporal matching. These results demonstrate that codec information can effectively improve the accuracy-complexity tradeoff of video token compression.

title: Spatial Prediction with Guided Diffusion
abstract: Spatial prediction is a critically important task in data analyses that involve spatially or spatio-temporally-referenced data. It is commonly carried out using hierarchical models, which comprise a process model describing the latent process of interest, and a data model describing how the process is observed. The target quantity is the predictive distribution, which is the conditional distribution of the latent spatial process given the observed data. Unfortunately, the predictive distribution is rarely available in closed form and can be difficult to sample from. Here, we show how recent developments in guided diffusion modelling from machine learning can address a wide class of problems in spatial prediction when the likelihood function derived from the data model is known and differentiable, possibly after relaxation. To show the versatility of the approach, we apply it to both Gaussian and non-Gaussian process models and a variety of data models that describe direct partial observations, linear and areal aggregates, counts, right censoring, and area-exceedance functionals. Where possible, we validate the framework against exact and Markov-chain-Monte-Carlo (MCMC)-derived predictive distributions. We demonstrate our approach on several simulation studies and in a controlled experiment of methane-flux inversion over the UK and Ireland. We show that guided diffusion can sample from the correct predictive distribution in a variety of settings, that it can be applied to models where MCMC is intractable, and that it scales well with the dimensionality of the latent process.

title: Scan-Parallel Variational Inference for event-driven Latent Jump Models
abstract: Continuous-time latent state-space models are widely used for irregularly observed time series, typically representing uncertainty through a random initial state followed by smooth ordinary differential equation (ODE) dynamics, or Brownian perturbations accumulated by a stochastic differential equation (SDE). While these constructions are natural for smooth or diffusive systems, they do not directly encode a finite set of unobserved shocks whose timing, magnitude, and effect on memory are themselves uncertain. We instead introduce latent jump models (LJMs): the latent state follows closed-form deterministic dynamics between Poisson-driven event times and undergoes a learned instantaneous jump at each event, with state-dependent intensity and mark distributions. This defines a time-homogeneous Markov process whose jumps are intrinsic state transitions rather than numerical integration steps. For training, we derive a tractable event-augmented path-space evidence lower bound (ELBO) and introduce Scan-Parallel Variational Inference (SPVI): an observation-conditioned variational posterior samples the complete latent event configuration before the state recurrence is evaluated using triangular affine scans. This enables fast and scalable training for LJMs in logarithmic temporal depth. Across synthetic stochastic systems and real irregular time series, LJMs remain competitive with continuous-time latent baselines in forecast accuracy, often with fewer latent updates than numerical solver evaluations, while training one to two orders of magnitude faster than the sequential baselines.

title: Quantum geometric inflation
abstract: Geometric Inflation adds an infinite tower of curvature invariants to the Einstein-Hilbert action while preserving certain key features such as leading to second order modified Friedmann equations for FRW backgrounds. Sourcing them with a perfect barotropic fluid can easily produce a slow-roll inflationary regime, no inflaton field is required. In this work, we perform the Wheeler-DeWitt quantization of minisuperspace Geometric Inflation models. First, we construct an effective 1D FRW action and perform the Hamiltonian formulation using both Ostrogradsky's approach and Dirac's algorithm for constrained systems. The Lagrangian and Hamiltonian treatment of the perfect fluid is based on Schutz's formalism. Second, we postulate the Wheeler-DeWitt equation and investigate its solutions both analytically and numerically. For radiation we are led to a system of fractional differential equations for which we use Caputo fractional derivative operator. We construct wave packets in momentum space, with the fluid's variable acting as external time parameter.

title: Linear and entropy-stable scheme for the dynamic van der Waals model of non-isothermal liquid-vapor flows
abstract: In this paper, we propose a linear and decoupled fully discrete scheme that preserves the entropy production property for the dynamic van der Waals model. This model provides a thermodynamically consistent diffuse-interface framework for describing non-isothermal phase transitions in single-component liquid-vapor systems, containing the coupled conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy. We first introduce an equivalent reformulation of the governing equations that avoids the use of chain-rule identities, which generally fail under discrete differentiation. Further, a component-wise convex-splitting method is employed to calculate the discrete chemical potential and temperature. This treatment provides a discrete entropy-stable inequality without a time step restriction. Based on the explicitly treated velocity, the scheme allows the three conservation equations to be solved linearly and sequentially in a decoupled manner. Since the momentum equation does not directly affect the entropy-stability analysis, we use a classical linear semi-implicit scheme to solve it. Numerical experiments verify the expected numerical accuracy. Simulations of droplet evaporation and two- and three-dimensional Leidenfrost effects further demonstrate the proposed method can capture complex non-isothermal phase-transition dynamics while numerically reproducing the discrete entropy production behavior.

title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
abstract: Recurrent-depth language models improve inference-time reasoning by repeatedly applying a shared network to refine internal representations, but the additional recurrent computation also increases inference cost. This overhead is particularly pronounced during long-context prefill, where the full input sequence is repeatedly processed across recurrent depth. Weight-and-activation quantization offers a natural way to accelerate this computation through lower-precision arithmetic, yet repeatedly applying quantized computation introduces numerical perturbations that accumulate along the recurrent trajectory. We systematically analyze how such errors propagate across recurrent depth and show that quantization errors introduced earlier are attenuated by more subsequent recurrent steps and therefore have a smaller effect on the final representation. Matched-budget experiments strongly support this prediction, showing that placing quantized computation earlier in recurrent depth consistently yields the best fidelity. Based on this insight, we introduce RAMP (Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision), which performs early recurrent refinement using low-precision weight-and-activation computation and restores high precision for terminal refinement. Across context lengths up to 4K, RAMP preserves near-full-precision prefill quality while achieving up to 1.16x end-to-end first-prefill speedup on an NVIDIA H100, corresponding to a 13.9% latency reduction.

title: NOFACE3D: NOise-scheduled Focused Anchoring and Controlled Enhancement for 3D Generation
abstract: Recent image-to-3D models generate complete, high-quality assets from a single image, with global shape and appearance that are already convincing; what remains is the fine scale, where small, thin, elongated, or detail-rich regions are reconstructed softly and under-resolved. This gap can arise in generators with fixed-resolution spatial grids: the same spatial sampling density is used for a large, smooth, low-curvature surface and for a thin, high-curvature structure that carries most of the perceived detail. To this end, we introduce NOFACE3D, a training-free framework that refines these detail-critical regions while preserving the rest of the asset. Given a generated mesh, its input image, and a refinement box, NOFACE3D extracts the selected submesh, scales it up to fill the generator's input volume, and re-encodes it into the full-resolution latent grid. Conditioned on the image crop, it refines the region through flow-based sampling with a spatially varying noise schedule that anchors boundary latents. The refined region is then integrated back into the original asset, preserving the surrounding geometry and appearance. We implement NOFACE3D on TRELLIS.2 and its sparse voxel representation; all of it operates purely at inference time on the frozen pretrained generator. We evaluate NOFACE3D on PAniC-3D, TexVerse and BigDetail, a new benchmark of 339 assets with annotated detail-critical regions. On all three, it generates sharper geometry and finer texture detail than the baselines. Project page: https://idkcouscous.github.io/NoFACE3D/

title: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows
abstract: AI agents depend on repeated decisions to accomplish tasks, with large language models (LLMs) commonly serving as their core decision makers. The recent emergence of Jev offers an opportunity to make these decisions faster and at lower cost. However, it remains unclear whether such local savings can be translated into efficient and reliable task completion. In this paper, we investigate this efficiency transfer across five agents in two representative application settings, embodied tasks in ALFWorld and mobile app use in AndroidWorld. Across 4,500 task executions, we jointly evaluate task effectiveness, decision-level and task-level resource use, and execution behavior. Experimental results show that Jev integration substantially reduces decision cost and latency across all five agents, with task-level gains varying by workflow. Task success remains close to baseline levels on ALFWorld and declines more substantially in two mobile agents. Auxiliary reasoning and additional interactions absorb decision savings, while failed recovery and premature completion limit successful delivery. Mean cost per successful outcome increases in one agent even as spending per attempt falls. These findings highlight the importance of preserving progress, supporting recovery, and verifying completion when integrating efficient decision models into agent workflows. Their practical value should be assessed through successful task delivery, recovery behavior, and resources per delivered outcome.

title: VETR: Execution-Grounded Self-Improving Agent for Symbolic Graphics Reasoning
abstract: Visual agents for symbolic graphics reasoning depend on executable world representations, yet continued improvement remains bottlenecked by ambiguous supervision from final renders. Recent agentic systems refine scenes through repeated interaction, but they lack mechanisms to recursively extract actionable evidence from execution traces, overlooking which proposed symbolic edits survived, disappeared, or interfered during program execution. To address this, we propose VETR (Verified Execution Trajectories for Refinement), a framework that enables agentic recursive self-improvement over executable world representations for symbolic graphics reasoning. Within each task, VETR retains aligned program/render records with bounded runtime observations and introduces an execution refiner that compiles observed writes and state changes into constrained alternative programs. The refiner validates their endpoints and preservation conditions against captured runtime state; the ordinary visual verifier then assesses goal relevance. Repair construction makes no additional language-model calls, but can require additional executions. Evaluations on BlenderGym (280 tasks) and BlenderBench (27 released tasks) with GPT-5.6-luna and Qwen3.8-27B show that VETR consistently outperforms existing refinement strategies, including BlenderAlchemy and VIGA. Controlled ablations evaluate the contributions of execution refinement and role-asymmetric evidence organization under fixed generator-interaction caps.

title: Locate, Judge, Read: Role-Specialized Tool Agents over a Knowledge-Point Index for Open-Domain Multimodal Document QA
abstract: Question answering over large heterogeneous document collections requires first finding the right passages and then reading them, yet current retrieval-augmented agents give one model both kinds of tools and let it schedule itself. We present KnowForge, a pipeline separated by job: a hybrid-retrieval knowledge-point index; a Locator agent that can only search; a code-scheduled bridge judge that forces the missing second hop; a typed, size-bounded evidence pool that merges every search's ranking; a Deep Reader agent that can only read text, images and tables; and a synthesizer with a format checker. With a self-hosted Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (3B active), KnowForge reaches F1 47.5 on the full open-domain M3DocVQA (2,441 questions, 3,368 PDFs), +11.0 over the published M3DocRAG system and +7.1 over one-shot retrieve-and-answer on the same index and model, and 53.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash. On MultiHop-RAG it reaches 73.5 accuracy, above the strongest published RAG and GraphRAG results (71.2); on the single-document MMLongBench-Doc it lifts the same model from 34.8 to 47.0, level with GPT-4o reading page images (46.3). Per-job ablations on the full benchmarks attribute the gain: the Deep Reader is worth 3.8, 9.8 and 0 points on the three corpora, tracking how visual each is; merging both agents into one with all tools and twice the rounds loses 1.9 F1 because it keeps searching instead of reading; a round-budget sweep shows a step at four Locator rounds and a plateau beyond; query latency scales with model calls rather than corpus size. We serve the three indexed benchmarks as read-only knowledge bases (free registration) and release all prompts and the runner code: https://github.com/metask-ai/knowforge-bench

title: PCM: Programmable Congestion Management for Terabit RDMA NICs
abstract: Datacenter congestion control (CC) and load balancing (LB) evolve rapidly as workload demands change, but deployment depends on RDMA hardware and transport interfaces. Emerging programmable RDMA engines tie policy code to vendor APIs. Operators must therefore port each policy for every platform they deploy. We address this with PCM, a programming model that separates portable congestion management from platform integration on datacenter NICs. Developers write event-driven handlers that they can debug in simulation and reuse on real hardware. PCM exposes flow telemetry as signals and uses triggers to support per-event reactions and coarser responses to accumulated feedback. Vendors provide optimized backends that map signals and output controls to native NIC mechanisms with defined feedback and control semantics. We demonstrate PCM's expressivity by implementing eleven well-known datacenter CC and LB algorithms. We deploy PCM across four distinct datapaths: an Ultra Ethernet simulator, CPU-based UCCL, and on-NIC offloads on NVIDIA ConnectX-8 and Microsoft 1P. On CX-8, PCM-Swift achieves processing capacity equivalent to one reaction per three 4 KiB packets at 800 Gbit/s, using one-fifth of the NIC's hardware threads. In UCCL, it matches native Swift's 1.56 Tbit/s goodput with 64 KiB chunk-level control. PCM's design informed ongoing Ultra Ethernet work toward a portable congestion management interface.

title: DP-MIND: Differentially private memory-guided Long context Inference
abstract: LLM-as-a-Service has become a dominant paradigm for accessing large language models without requiring local deployment. However, the process raises severe privacy concerns when user queries may include sensitive or confidential contexts. Differential privacy (DP) provides a principled approach to protecting such inputs, but existing DP inference methods are primarily designed for short- or moderate-context settings and struggle with million-token-scale inputs due to limited context capacity and severe utility degradation under DP perturbation. In this paper, we propose DP-MIND, a memory-guided framework that scales differentially private inference to million-token contexts. DP-MIND enables private long-context inference by locally perturbing the input and processing it chunk by chunk with a compact memory that preserves task-relevant information across the sequence. To make this memory robust to DP noise, we optimize the memory construction policy directly on perturbed inputs using reinforcement learning, guided by both final answer correctness and memory consistency. We further recover perturbation-corrupted answer spans through a local denoising module without exposing the original context to the external model. We provide theoretical privacy analysis of DP-MIND and further conduct extensive empirical analysis across multiple long-context benchmarks with context lengths up to the million-token scale, demonstrating that DP-MIND consistently outperforms existing DP and long-context inference baselines in both scalability and utility.

title: The Limits of Manipulation within Personalized Incentive Policies
abstract: Demand management policies aim to shift individual behavior toward sustainable choices (e.g., goods, transport modes). Personalized incentive policies tailor subsidies to agents' needs and constraints, but personalization also exposes the regulator to agents' strategic manipulative behavior. The extent to which agents can profitably manipulate such policies remains poorly understood, which limits their applicability. This paper establishes analytically the conditions under which manipulation benefits the agent. We formalize a Stackelberg game in which an agent may simulate a different profile to extract higher incentives from a regulator. Previous work typically assumes that the regulator would instantaneously classify agents into the simulated user profile. In contrast, we explicitly model the regulator's process of learning the agent profile, based on observed past behavior. This makes manipulation harder, since it forces the agent to consistently behave according to a simulated profile, thus renouncing following their true preferences. Manipulative agents thus incur a Cost of Manipulation, which has typically been neglected. By accounting for it, we get a counterintuitive finding: although classification uncertainty reduces personalization accuracy, it may benefit the regulator by deterring manipulation. We establish an upper bound on the agent's gain from manipulation, which becomes stricter as profiles become harder to distinguish for the regulator. Simulations on the London Passenger Mode Choice dataset illustrate this deterrence effect. The framework can therefore be used to stress-test the robustness of personalized incentive policies before deployment.

title: Representing the Non-dominated Set of Multi-objective Optimization Problems with Polyhedral Ordering Cones
abstract: In the literature, research on representing the non-dominated set has focused almost exclusively on multi-objective optimization problems with Pareto-dominance. However, general ordering cones are used to incorporate preferences of decision makers into the optimization process and to model other specific types of optimization problems, such as ordinal optimization problems. In this work, we consider several representation approaches based on representation relations in the context of multi-objective optimization problems with polyhedral ordering cones. Our main research question is whether existing theory and solution approaches developed for the Pareto case can be used to address the more general setting.

title: Quality, Not Just Outcome: A Structural Scoring Framework for Selecting Coding-Agent Trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning
abstract: Open coding agents are commonly trained through supervised fine-tuning on interaction trajectories whose final patches pass the benchmark test suite. However, this outcome-level filtering criterion ignores process quality: trajectories that eventually succeed may still contain inefficient interaction patterns such as repetitive file inspection, unstable tool usage, or delayed modification behavior, all of which become part of the imitation target. We propose TQS (Trajectory Quality Score), a structural scoring framework for coding-agent trajectories that operates directly on trajectory structure, requires no LLM judge, and runs in linear time. TQS characterizes trajectory quality through structural signals organized around structured convergence: information focus, intent--action alignment, and policy dynamics. Using 155,144 successful trajectories from a public open-license corpus, we rank trajectories by TQS and fine-tune coding agents on filtered subsets. Models trained on top-ranked trajectories consistently outperform those trained on random or bottom-ranked subsets on SWE-Bench-Verified. Our results suggest that process-level trajectory quality is an important factor in coding-agent supervision and that structural trajectory filtering provides an effective and scalable alternative to LLM-based data selection.

title: Morphology-based retrieval of local wave parameters and phase shifts in satellite-observed atmospheric disturbances
abstract: Currently available methods for processing atmospheric wave disturbances are often based on integral wavelet transform techniques, which efficiently estimate spectral data but are fundamentally limited by the uncertainty principle. To address this limitation, this work proposes a novel morphological approach based on partitioning spatial disturbance profiles into separate, well-defined wave segments. By focusing exclusively on the local waveform morphology of a central half-wave and its two adjacent out-of-phase counterparts, and taking the modified Morlet wavelet as a primary example of a model wave packet, we successfully reconstruct the complete set of local wave parameters directly from the amplitudes and positions of these three dominant half-waves. Consequently, the theory demonstrates good agreement with observations, confirming the high accuracy of the proposed waveform morphology approach in reconstructing the localized structure of atmospheric disturbances. When applied to evaluating the phase shift between different wave field components, the method reveals that this shift is a weighted combination of the classical monochromatic phase difference and a morphological one determined by the internal symmetry of the underlying wave packets. Although the classical factor yields the dominant contribution, the symmetry-related factor provides a moderate correction to it. The applicability and accuracy of the approach are verified using observational data gathered over several orbits of the low-Earth-orbit satellite Dynamic Explorer 2 as it passed over Earth's polar caps. The obtained results confirm that the observed disturbances correspond to medium-scale acoustic-gravity waves propagating at a small angle to the horizontal plane, demonstrating the broader methodological potential of the proposed technique for analyzing a wide range of wave phenomena.

title: Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence
abstract: Terminal agents are moving beyond local operations toward completing real-world professional tasks. Short trajectories can demonstrate commands and tool calls, but they do not fully show how agents accumulate evidence through exploration, use it to inform judgments, continually adjust strategies based on feedback, and turn intermediate results into final deliverables. High-quality long-horizon trajectories capture these agentic behavioral patterns and their connections within a single problem-solving process, providing richer experience for sustained autonomous work. However, environment synthesis may complete or simplify the key work underlying these patterns in advance and thus remove the need for exploration, implementation, and verification that the agent was meant to perform. To address this, we introduce TerminalHorizon, a fully automated data synthesis engine for long-horizon terminal agents. Starting from real-world professional work, it uses independent execution to identify key work omitted during construction and uses the resulting evidence to guide environment reconstruction. To extend these patterns across stages, it progressively expands tasks under the same goal, introducing new requirements that build on prior results and call for further exploration and improvement. Using this engine, we construct 1.5K task environments and perform supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-27B on the resulting dataset to obtain TerminalHorizon-27B. We achieve substantial performance gains on all 12 benchmarks spanning coding-agent tasks, agentic tasks in real-world production settings, and general reasoning. Multiple RSI case studies, each with a 12-hour research budget, further demonstrate the model's ability to continue experimenting beyond an initial solution, improve its methods based on feedback, and retain effective improvements in its final deliverables.

title: Enhancing credit risk scorecards with transactional-based behavioural features
abstract: Background: Credit risk modelling is fundamental in financial institutions, typically using credit history, repayment behaviour, income, and outstanding debt to estimate a borrower's probability of default. Although transactional data are sometimes incorporated through aggregated measures such as recency, frequency, and monetary indicators, behavioural information embedded in raw transaction narratives remains largely unexplored due to its unstructured nature. This limits opportunities to extract richer behavioural insights. Aim: This research investigates payment narratives from transactional data as an alternative data source for credit risk modelling. Setting: The study uses transactional data from a large South African financial institution focused on small and medium enterprises. Method: Techniques such as natural language processing and regular expressions are used to transform unstructured transaction descriptions into meaningful, explainable behavioural features by categorising transactions into interpretable spending categories. A novel categorisation algorithm was developed and evaluated for classification accuracy. The extracted features are incorporated into a credit risk scorecard to assess their predictive value. Results: The categorisation algorithm demonstrates high classification accuracy. Using these features in the scorecard resulted in a significant increase in Gini compared to a scorecard without them. Conclusion: Text-based transactional information can be systematically extracted, categorised, and operationalised to enhance credit risk model performance. Contribution: The study develops a novel, integrated, explainable methodology for transforming transactional text into behavioural features, introduces a structured RegEx-based categorisation approach, and demonstrates their predictive value within traditional scorecard frameworks.

title: Understanding and Mitigating Cross-Session Attacks via Persistent Artifacts in Agent Skill Composition
abstract: Agent skills extend the capabilities of AI agents by bundling instructions, code, and resources into reusable packages. During skill execution, agents may produce or modify artifacts, such as files, configurations, and cached data, that are reused by other skills in later sessions. Since these artifacts can persist across sessions and later be accessed by other skills, they introduce a new attack surface that can be exploited to influence subsequent executions. However, the security risks arising from such cross-session skill interactions remain largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate cross-session composition attacks in skill-based AI agents and develop a runtime defense against them. Specifically, we characterize three attack mechanisms, namely Instruction Propagation (IP), Data Boundary Violation (DBV), and Evidence Poisoning (EP), through which malicious effects propagate across skill executions via persistent artifacts. To evaluate whether existing agents can resist these attacks while completing legitimate tasks, we construct SkillRelayBench, a benchmark of 270 adversarial cases drawn from 30 cross-session skill-composition scenarios across ten domains. Our evaluation of seven models across Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and Claude Code reveals attack success rates (ASR) ranging from 46.7% to 77.4% and attack chain success rates (ACSR) ranging from 35.6% to 61.1%. Successful attack chains cover all five target security consequence categories, highlighting the broad impact of these attacks. To mitigate these risks, we propose SkillRelayGuard, which restores artifact provenance context and provides pre-execution advisory review while leaving the final execution decision to the agent. Evaluation across three agent settings shows that SkillRelayGuard reduces overall ASR from 69.5% to 10.9% and ACSR from 54.8% to 10.0%, while increasing legitimate task completion from 79.6% to 87.5%.

title: Percolation of Data Constraints and Reorganization of Boolean Function States in Parity Learning
abstract: We study how a neural network reorganizes its learned function as training proceeds and as previously unseen parity data accumulate. The trained model is itself a Boolean function on binary strings of finite length. We then evaluate it on all data, inside and outside the training set, and read off its complete sign table. Its $\pm1$ entries are the amplitudes of a normalized state, dubbed the function-state, whose inverse subsystem purity $K_f=1/\textrm{Tr}(\rho_A^2)$ is an effective Schmidt rank. We find that small data additions broaden the Schmidt spectrum, whereas larger additions reconcentrate it in the target mode. The former is called differentiation because the model distinguishes inputs more sharply. The latter is called target-selective recoherence, where the model settles on the single rule shared by the added data. As the dataset grows, the connectivity of the constraint graph defined by the training set increases monotonically, whereas the learned inverse purity changes nonmonotonically. On a fixed connected dataset, as learning proceeds, the Schmidt spectrum begins to reorganize, followed by gains in target alignment and later by improvement in predictive accuracy. This ordering distinguishes three aspects of learning: constraint identifiability, function-state organization, and predictive accuracy. At fixed data size, a function that has already been learned can re-differentiate, an event we call retreat, without changing graph connectivity. Recovery reconcentrates the Schmidt spectrum in a similar target-selective pattern, without exact recurrence of the Boolean state. Thus the percolation of data constraints fixes the identifiable support, while the reduced state produced by training continues to reorganize even after that support stops changing.

title: Jag: Direct Box Prediction for Efficient Visual Grounding
abstract: Visual grounding combines image--language understanding with geometric prediction, yet autoregressive multimodal models often express a box as a coordinate sequence. Sequential decoding adds computation to the multimodal processing needed for localization. Adapting these representations to box geometry offers a route to direct prediction. We present Jag, which adapts a compact pretrained multimodal model for direct continuous box prediction. A lightweight regression head reads the last valid input-token state, conditioned on the image and referring expression, and predicts all four box coordinates together. Geometric supervision jointly adapts the language backbone, visual merger, and regression head, allowing localization losses to shape both the multimodal representations and the coordinate mapping. Inference retains image--language processing and returns the box in one forward pass, without coordinate generation or text parsing. Across benchmarks, Jag consistently improves grounding accuracy over its base model across the observed target sizes and expression groups. Component ablation show that jointly adapting the representations and head substantially improves accuracy over training the head alone. Against existing specialized grounding models, it achieves competitive accuracy with lower single-request latency and GPU memory use. These results show how supervision tailored to the geometric answer can specialize a compact pretrained multimodal model for accurate grounding and efficient direct prediction. Project page: https://xyzzzh.github.io/Jag/

title: The origin of amplitude chaos and strings
abstract: We analytically study the peak statistics of an amplitude ensemble to identify the local mechanism responsible for peak repulsion. Our analytical approaches show that a smooth, nondegenerate ensemble of sufficiently differentiable amplitudes exhibits quartic nearest-neighbor repulsion, $p_{\rm nn}(S)\sim S^4$, where $S$ is the spacing between adjacent peaks. We verify this prediction numerically for the tree-level highly excited string scattering amplitudes. Interestingly, we find the quartic repulsion to be robust by varying both the underlying ensemble and the amplitude functions, whereas a tunable cusp model shows that weakening differentiability changes the strength of the repulsion. Peak repulsion therefore defines a local universality class that is not unique to string theory and may occur in amplitude ensembles in other theories.

title: Beyond a Single Crop: Contextualized Embeddings for Player Re-Identification
abstract: Person re-identification is typically addressed by learning identity-discriminative embeddings from individual person crops. However, player re-identification in broadcast sports videos presents a unique challenge: players from the same team often share similar appearances, while video sequences provide repeated observations of the same players under different viewpoints and surrounding contexts. Existing crop-based approaches largely ignore this contextual information, which can be critical for resolving visually similar identities. Here, we propose ContextReID, a contextualized embedding framework that represents a player by jointly considering other players in the same frame and observations from different frames of the broadcast sequence.
